Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

(The Sixth Point): The story of the apostasy after the death of the Prophet ﷺ. Whoever hears it, not a speck of a mustard seed’s weight of doubt remains in his heart regarding the sophistries of the devils who call themselves “ʿulamāʾ.” Their claim is: “This is shirk, but they say Lā ilāha illā Allāh — and whoever says it does not disbelieve because of anything.”

Even greater and more explicit than this is their statement that the desert dwellers have not a hair of Islām with them — yet they say Lā ilāha illā Allāh, and thus, by this word, they are considered people of Islām, and their wealth and blood are inviolable, while admitting that they have abandoned Islām entirely. And knowing that they deny the resurrection, that they mock those who affirm it, that they ridicule and prefer the religion of their forefathers opposed to the religion of the Prophet ﷺ.

And with all this, these rebellious devilish ignoramuses declare that the Bedouins are Muslims, even if all of this occurs from them, simply because they say Lā ilāha illā Allāh. The necessary implication of their statement is that the Jews are Muslims, since they also say it. Moreover, the kufr of these - the Bedouins who possess the qualities we mentioned - is far graver than the kufr of the Jews many times over.

What clarifies this from the story of the apostasy is that the apostates divided in their apostasy: among them were those who denied the Prophet ﷺ, returned to the worship of idols, and said: “If he were a prophet, he would not have died.” And among them were those who remained upon the two shahādahs but affirmed the prophethood of Musaylima, thinking that the Prophet ﷺ had shared with him in prophethood, since Musaylima brought false witnesses who testified for him — and many people believed them. Yet despite this, the scholars unanimously held that they were apostates, even if they were ignorant of the matter, and whoever doubts their apostasy is a kāfir.

So once you know that the scholars unanimously held that those who denied and returned to idol worship, and those who reviled the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ, and those who affirmed the prophethood of Musaylima, are all the same in one condition — even if they remained upon the rest of Islām. And among them were those who affirmed the two shahādahs but believed Ṭulayḥa in his claim of prophethood, and among them those who believed al-ʿAnsī, the claimant from Ṣanʿāʾ. And all of these, the scholars unanimously held, are alike.

Then these rebellious ignorant ones issue fatwās that such people are Muslims, even if they explicitly did all of that, so long as they say Lā ilāha illā Allāh. Glory be to You, this is a tremendous slander!

And how excellent is the statement of one of the Bedouins who came to us and heard something of Islām, when he said: “I bear witness that we are kuffār” — meaning himself and all of the Bedouins — “and I bear witness that the pretentious worshipper who calls us ‘people of Islām’ is a kāfir.”

And all praise is due to Allāh, Lord of the Worlds. And may blessings and peace be upon Muḥammad, his family, and his Companions.

[Majmūʿat Rasāʾil fī al-Tawḥīd wal-Īmān (within the collected works of Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb 1/360-362]

Shaykhs Ḥusayn and ʿAbd Allāh, the sons of Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb — may Allāh have mercy on them — said:

Whoever among the people of shirk died before this daʿwah reached him, the ruling regarding him is as follows: if he was known for committing shirk, adhered to it as his religion, and died upon that, then outwardly he is judged to have died upon kufr. No supplication is made for him, no sacrificial offering is made on his behalf, and no charity is given on his behalf.

As for the reality of his condition, that is left to Allāh, the Exalted. If the ḥujjah had been established against him in his lifetime and he was obstinate, then he is a kāfir both outwardly and inwardly. But if the ḥujjah had not been established against him, then his matter is with Allāh, the Exalted.

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 10/142]

Sheikh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbdul-Wahhāb said:

So when they saw me commanding the people with what their Prophet (ﷺ) commanded them—to worship none but Allāh—and that whoever calls upon ʿAbd al-Qādir is a disbeliever, and ʿAbd al-Qādir is free from them; and likewise, whoever seeks help from the righteous, or the prophets, or wails for them, or prostrates to them, or makes vows to them, or directs any form of worship to them—worship that is the exclusive right of Allāh over His servants—then every person who knows the command of Allāh and His Messenger will not deny this matter but will rather affirm and acknowledge it.

As for the one who denies this, he falls into one of two categories:

If he says that calling upon the righteous, seeking their aid, making vows to them, and dedicating oneself as their devotee is a good thing—even if Allāh and His Messenger have stated that it is disbelief—then he is insisting on denying Allāh and His Messenger. There is no ambiguity in his disbelief, and we have no discussion with him.

Rather, our discussion is with a man who believes in Allāh and the Last Day, loves what Allāh and His Messenger love, and hates what Allāh and His Messenger hate—but he is ignorant, and the devils have confused him about his religion. He assumes that having faith in the righteous is correct; yet, if he knew that it was an act of disbelief leading its doer to the Hellfire, he would not have done it.

We clarify this matter for him, saying: A Muslim must follow the command of Allāh and His Messenger and inquire about it. Allāh, the Exalted, revealed the Qurʾān, in which He mentioned what He loves and what He detests, making our religion clear and complete. Likewise, Muḥammad (ﷺ), the best of prophets, had no one on earth more beloved to his companions than him. They loved him more than themselves and their children, recognized his status, and also understood shirk and īmān.

If any Muslim during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) had called upon him, made vows to him, wailed for him, or if any of his companions had gone to his grave after his death to ask him for something, wail for him, or seek refuge by his grave—then know that this is a correct and good practice, and do not follow me or anyone else in rejecting it.

However, if upon inquiry, you find that the Prophet (ﷺ) disavowed those who held such beliefs about the prophets and the righteous, fought them, took their women and children captive, seized their wealth, and ruled them as disbelievers—then know that the Prophet (ﷺ) speaks only the truth and commands only what is right. It is obligatory for every believer to follow what he brought.

In summary, what I reject is placing belief in anything other than Allāh in a way that is not permissible for any but Him. If I said this from my own opinion, then discard it. If I took it from a book that has no practical basis, then discard it as well. If I conveyed it from the scholars of my school of thought, then discard it. But if I have said it based on the command of Allāh and His Messenger and in accordance with the consensus of scholars across all schools of thought, then it is not befitting for a man who believes in Allāh and the Last Day to turn away from it—just because the people of his time or his country have turned away from it, or because most people in his era have ignored it.

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 1/75-76]

Ash-Shaykh Ḥusayn and ash-Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh, the two sons of ash-Shaykh Muḥammad (ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb) said in the course of their answer:

Issue eleven: A man entered this dīn and loved it, but he does not show enmity to the mushrikīn, or he shows enmity to them but does not declare them kuffār, or he says: “I am a Muslim, but I am not able to declare takfīr upon the people of lā ilāha illā Allāh, even if they did not know its meaning.” Or a man entered this dīn and loved it, but he says: “I will not oppose the domes (over the graves). I know they neither benefit nor harm, but I will not oppose them.”

The answer: Such a man is not a Muslim except if he knows tawḥīd, adheres to it, acts according to its requirement, believes the Messenger ﷺ in what he informed, obeys him in what he forbade and commanded, and has īmān in him and what he brought. Whoever says: “I do not show enmity to the mushrikīn,” or shows enmity but does not declare them kuffār, or says: “I will not oppose the people of lā ilāha illā Allāh even if they committed kufr and shirk and opposed the dīn of Allāh,” or says: “I will not oppose the domes”—such a person is not a Muslim.

Rather, he is of those whom Allāh said regarding them: “And they say, ‘We believe in some and we disbelieve in some,’ and they wish to adopt a way in between. Those—they are the disbelievers in truth.” (al-Nisāʾ 4:150–151) And Allāh, subḥānahu wa-taʿālā, has made obligatory showing enmity to the mushrikīn, opposing them, and declaring them kuffār. He said: “You will not find a people who believe in Allāh and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose Allāh and His Messenger…” (al-Mujādilah 58:22) And He, taʿālā, said: “O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, driving out the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allāh your Lord…” (al-Mumtaḥanah 60:1)

And Allāh knows best.

[ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 10/139–140]

### Abā Buṭayn against making every ignorant person a Muslim
<!-- evidence-id: 000148 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="embedded-quotation">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: عبد الله أبا بطين، *الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية*، 12/69.</p>
<p>واحتج بعض من يجادل عن المشركين بقصة الذي قد أوصى أهله أن يحرقوه بعد موته، على أن من ارتكب الكفر جاهلًا لا يكفر، ولا يكفر إلا المعاند.</p>
<p>والجواب عن ذلك كله: أن الله سبحانه وتعالى أرسل رسله مبشرين ومنذرين، لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل؛ وأعظم ما أرسلوا به ودعوا إليه: عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له، والنهي عن الشرك الذي هو عبادة غيره؛ فإن كان مرتكب الشرك الأكبر معذورًا لجهل، فمن الذي لا يعذر؟!</p>
<p>ولازم هذه الدعوى: أنه ليس لله حجة على أحد إلا المعاند، مع أن صاحب هذه الدعوى لا يمكنه طرد أصله، بل لا بد أن يتناقض، فإنه لا يمكنه أن يتوقف في تكفير من شك في رسالة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أو شك في البعث، أو غير ذلك من أصول الدين، والشاك جاهل؛ والفقهاء يذكرون في كتب الفقه حكم المرتد: أنه المسلم الذي يكفر بعد إسلامه، نطقًا أو فعلًا أو شكًّا أو اعتقادًا، وسبب الشك الجهل.</p>
<p>ولازم هذا: أنا لا نكفر جهلة اليهود والنصارى، والذين يسجدون للشمس والقمر والأصنام لجهلهم، ولا الذين حرقهم علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه بالنار، لأنا نقطع أنهم جهال؛ وقد أجمع المسلمون على كفر من لم يكفر اليهود والنصارى، أو شك في كفرهم، ونحن نتيقن أن أكثرهم جهال.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

> Some who argue on behalf of the mushrikīn cited the account of the man who instructed his family to burn him after his death as evidence that a person who commits disbelief in ignorance is not declared a disbeliever and that none is declared a disbeliever except an obstinate rejector.
>
> The answer to all of that is that Allāh, Glorified and Exalted, sent His Messengers as bearers of glad tidings and warners so that people would have no argument against Allāh after the Messengers. The greatest matter with which they were sent and to which they called was the worship of Allāh alone without partner and the prohibition of shirk, which is the worship of other than Him. If the one who commits major shirk is excused because of ignorance, then who would not be excused?
>
> The necessary implication of this claim is that Allāh has no proof against anyone except an obstinate rejector. Yet the proponent of this claim cannot consistently apply his own principle and must contradict himself. He cannot refrain from declaring a disbeliever one who doubts the message of Muḥammad ﷺ, doubts the Resurrection, or doubts another foundation of the religion, although the doubter is ignorant. The jurists mention in their books of jurisprudence that an apostate is a Muslim who disbelieves after his Islam through speech, action, doubt, or belief, while the cause of doubt is ignorance.
>
> Another necessary implication is that we would not declare the ignorant Jews and Christians disbelievers, nor those who prostrate to the sun, moon, and idols because of their ignorance, nor those whom ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allāh be pleased with him, burned with fire, since we are certain that they were ignorant. Yet the Muslims have unanimously agreed upon the disbelief of one who does not declare the Jews and Christians disbelievers or doubts their disbelief, while we are certain that most of them are ignorant.

Source: ʿAbd Allāh Abā Buṭayn, *al-Durar al-Saniyyah fī al-Ajwibah al-Najdiyyah*, 12/69.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1677 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000149 -->

A doubt the Murjiah bring to excuse Shirk

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

Some who argue in defense of the polytheists cite the story of the man who instructed his family to burn his body after his death as evidence that someone who commits an act of disbelief out of ignorance is not deemed a disbeliever—only the stubborn rejecter is.

The response to this is that ALLĀH (ﷻ) sent His messengers as bearers of glad tidings and warnings so that people would have no excuse before Him after the messengers had been sent. The greatest message they conveyed and called people to was the worship of ALLĀH (ﷻ) alone, without any partner, and the prohibition of associating others with Him in worship.

If someone who commits major polytheism is excused due to ignorance, then who is not excused? The implication of this claim is that ALLĀH (ﷻ) has no argument against anyone except the stubborn rejecter. However, the proponent of this argument cannot remain consistent in their reasoning; they will inevitably contradict themselves. For instance, they cannot refrain from declaring as disbelievers those who doubt Muḥammad’s (ﷺ) prophethood, the resurrection, or other fundamental tenets of faith—yet the doubter, too, is ignorant.

he then goes on to say:

The one who claims that a person who commits kufr (disbelief) due to ta’wīl (misinterpretation), ijtihād (independent reasoning), khata’ (mistake), taqlīd (blind following), or jahl (ignorance) is excused is in clear opposition to the Kitāb (Qur’an), the Sunnah, and the Ijmāʿ (scholarly consensus) without a doubt. Moreover, such a person must inevitably contradict their own principle, for if they were to apply it consistently, they would inevitably fall into kufr themselves—just as one would if they hesitated in declaring as kāfir someone who doubts the Risālah (prophethood) of Muḥammad ﷺ.

As for the man who instructed his family to burn his body and whom ALLĀH (ﷻ) forgave despite his doubt regarding one of the attributes of the Almighty Lord, He forgave him because the message had not reached him—this is what several scholars have stated.

For this reason Ibn Taymiyyah رحمه الله, said: "Whoever doubts one of the attributes of the Lord, and such doubt is in something that one like him should not be ignorant of, is a disbeliever. However, if it is something that one like him could be ignorant of, he is not deemed a disbeliever." He further stated: "This is why the Prophet (ﷺ) did not declare the man who doubted ALLĀH’S power to be a disbeliever,because such disbelief only applies after the message has reached a person." Ibn ʿAqīl also held this view, interpreting the case as one where the man had not received the message.

Shaykh Taqi Ad-Dīn's stance regarding ALLĀH’S attributes was that ignorance does not render a person a disbeliever. However, when it comes to polytheism and similar matters, he did not hold the same view, as will be shown later,إن شاء الله. We have already mentioned some of his statements regarding the Ittihadiyyah (a sect that believed in the unity of existence) and others, and his ruling that whoever doubts their disbelief is himself a disbeliever.

The author of Al-Ikhtiyarat stated: "Apostasy applies to anyone who associates others with ALLĀH (ﷻ), hates the Prophet (ﷺ) or what he brought, fails to reject wrongdoing in his heart, believes that some of the Companions fought alongside the disbelievers or deems such an act permissible, denies a matter upon which there is definitive consensus, or places intermediaries between himself and ALLĀH (ﷻ) relying on them, calling upon them, and seeking from them—this is unanimous disbelief."

He further stated: "Whoever doubts one of ALLĀH’S attributes in a way that one like him should not be ignorant of is an apostate. However, if it is something one like him could be ignorant of, he is not an apostate. This is why the Prophet (ﷺ) did not declare the man who doubted ALLĀH’S power to be a disbeliever."

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1919 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000150 -->

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

So, whoever receives the message of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur’an has had the evidence established against them. They are not excused for disbelief due to ignorance of Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, or the Last Day. After that, there is no excuse for ignorance.

Allah, the Exalted, has informed us about the ignorance of many disbelievers while explicitly stating their disbelief. He described the Christians as being ignorant, even though no Muslim doubts their disbelief. We assert the disbelief of most Jews and Christians today, acknowledging their ignorance and imitation. We also believe in the disbelief of those who have any doubt about their disbelief.

The Qur’an indicates that doubt in the fundamentals of religion is disbelief. Doubt is the hesitation between two things, like one who is unsure of the truth of the Prophet or his falsehood, or of the occurrence of resurrection (whether it will happen or not), and similar doubts. This includes someone who does not believe in the obligation of prayer or in its non-obligation, or who does not believe in the prohibition of adultery or in its non-prohibition.

This is disbelief according to the consensus of scholars, and there is no excuse for someone in this state, claiming that they did not understand the proofs and clear signs of Allah. This is because there is no excuse for them after the message has reached them, even if they did not understand it.

[Masʾalah fīman Yukaffiru Ghayrahū min al-Muslimīn - by Sheikh Abdullāh Abā Buṭayn p.20-21]

Shaykh ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn [d. 1282 AH] said:

"What Ibn Taymiyyah mentioned, that whoever does this is a kāfir by the consensus of the Muslims, is exactly what is practiced today at the well-known shrines across most of the lands of Islam. Rather, they have gone far beyond that, adding to it slaughtering and making vows for them, and some have even gone further to the point of prostrating to them on the ground.

So we say: whoever today commits these acts at these shrines is a mushrik, a kāfir, without the slightest doubt, by the proof of the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus. And we know that those who fall into this, while claiming Islam, were only driven into it by ignorance. Had they known that it distances a person from Allah to the furthest extent, and that it is from the very shirk Allah has forbidden, they would never have dared to approach it.

Yet despite this, all of the scholars declared them disbelievers and did not excuse them with ignorance, contrary to what some of the misguided assert, claiming that such people are excused because they are ignorant. This claim is nothing but speaking about Allah without knowledge."

[Al-Durar al-Saniyyah, vol. 10, p. 404]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3728 -->

The rebuttle of the doubt of the Murji’ah and their usage of the Burning man Hadith

al-ʿAllāmah Abā Buṭayn said:

Some of those who argue on behalf of the mushrikīn cite the story of the man who instructed his family to burn him after his death, as evidence that whoever commits kufr out of ignorance does not become a disbeliever, and that only the one who is obstinate is deemed a disbeliever.

The reply to all of this is that Allāh, exalted is He, sent His messengers as bringers of glad tidings and warners, so that people would have no argument against Allāh after the messengers. The greatest matter they were sent with and called to was the worship of Allāh alone with no partner, and the prohibition of shirk — which is the worship of other than Him.

So if the one who commits shirk al-akbar is excused due to ignorance, then who is there that would not be excused?

The necessary consequence of this claim is that Allāh would have no argument against anyone except the obstinate one. Yet the very person who makes this claim cannot remain consistent with his own principle, for he must inevitably contradict himself. It is impossible for him to refrain from declaring disbelief upon one who doubts the messengership of Muḥammad ﷺ, or doubts the resurrection, or any of the other fundamentals of the religion — and the doubter is, in fact, ignorant.

The fuqahāʾ — may Allāh have mercy on them — mention in their books of jurisprudence the ruling on the apostate, saying: “The Muslim who disbelieves after his Islām — whether by word, or by action, or by belief, or by doubt.” And the cause of doubt is ignorance.

[Majmūʿ Fatāwā wa-Rasāʾil by Shaykh al-ʿAllāmah Abā Buṭayn p.679]

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn transmits the ijmāʿ of the ulema and said:

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1898 -->

Sheikh ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn said:

And the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever dies knowing that there is no deity worthy of worship but Allah will enter Paradise.”

The scholars have used these verses and similar ones to prove that the first obligation upon a person is to know Allah.

These verses indicate that the most important duty is understanding the meaning of “There is no deity but Allah”, and the greatest ignorance is the lack of understanding its meaning. Understanding this is one of the most crucial obligations, and ignorance of it is the most severe and detestable ignorance.

It is astonishing that some people, when they hear someone speak about the meaning of this statement, both in negation and affirmation, criticize it, saying, “We are not required to speak about people and their beliefs!”

To them, it should be said: No, you are required to know the concept of Tawḥīd, for Allah created jinn and humans for this purpose, and sent all the messengers calling to it, as well as to know its opposite, which is shirk that is unforgivable. There is no excuse for a person who is required to know this.

It is not permissible to follow blindly in this matter because it is the foundation of all foundations. Whoever does not recognize what is right and deny what is wrong will be doomed, especially in the case of the greatest right, which is Tawḥīd, and the greatest wrong, which is shirk.

[al-Intiṣār li-Ḥizb Allāh al-Muwaḥḥidīn wa ar-Radd ʿalā al-Mujādal ʿan al-Mushrikīn by Sheikh ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn p.10-11]

### Abā Buṭayn on reaching of the message
<!-- evidence-id: 000155 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="embedded-quotation">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: عبد الله أبا بطين، *الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية*، 10/365.</p>
<p>فَمَنْ بَلَغَتْهُ رِسَالَةُ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَبَلَغَهُ الْقُرْآنُ، فَقَدْ قَامَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْحُجَّةُ، فَلَا يُعْذَرُ فِي عَدَمِ الْإِيمَانِ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ، فَلَا عُذْرَ لَهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ بِالْجَهْلِ.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**


“Whoever has been reached by the message of Muḥammad ﷺ and the Qurʾān, the proof has been established against him. He is therefore not excused for failing to believe in Allāh, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. After that, ignorance is not an excuse for him.”

Source: ʿAbd Allāh Abā Buṭayn, al-Durar al-Saniyyah, 10/365.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages.html#message502 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000156 -->

Shaykh ʿAbdullāh ʾAbā Buṭayn (رحمه الله) stated:

"The Almighty (Allāh) said: «And when it was said: 'Indeed, the promise of Allāh is true and the Hour [is coming] - no doubt about it,' you said: 'We do not know what is the Hour. We assume only assumption, and we are not convinced.'» [al-Jāthīyah: 32], and Allāh ‎(تعالى) said regarding the Christians: «They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allāh, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Maryam» [al-Tawbah: 31].

ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim said to the Prophet ‎(ﷺ): 'We did not worship them.'

He said: 'Do they not permit what Allāh has forbidden, so you permitted it? And forbid what Allāh has permitted, so you forbade it?'

He said: 'Yes.'

The Prophet ‌‎(ﷺ) said: 'That is their worship.'

Therefore, Allāh (سبحانه) condemned them and called them Mushrikīn, even though they did not know that their actions that they were doing were acts of worship, so they were not excused for ignorance."

[Ad-Durar as-Sanīyyah, Vol. 10, Pg. 393].

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

Moreover, the scholars of every madhhab have mentioned many statements, actions, and beliefs—far too many to count—whose doer is considered a disbeliever, and they did not restrict this ruling to only the muʿānid (the one who stubbornly resists the truth).

So, whoever claims that someone committing an act of kufr while being a muʾawwil, or mujtahid, or muqallid, or jāhil (ignorant), is excused—such a person is undoubtedly opposing the Qur’ān, the Sunnah, and the ijmāʿ. Moreover, this person is forced to contradict his own principle. [al-Intiṣār li-Ḥizb Allāh al-Muwaḥḥidīn wa ar-Radd ʿalā al-Mujādal ʿan al-Mushrikīn p.26]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message3063 -->

Is the blind follower of shirk excused?

al-ʿAllāmah Abā Buṭayn said:

The Qur’ān refutes the claim that a muqallid (blind follower) in shirk is excused — for such a person has fabricated a lie against Allāh. Allāh said about the followers among the people of Hell:

“Indeed, we obeyed our leaders and elders, and they led us astray from the path.” (al-Aḥzāb: 67) And He, Exalted is He, said, conveying the words of the disbelievers: “Indeed, we found our forefathers upon a religion, and we are rightly guided upon their footsteps.” (az-Zukhruf: 22) And in another verse: “Indeed, we found our forefathers upon a religion, and we are following in their footsteps.” (az-Zukhruf: 23)

The scholars have used these verses and others like them as evidence that taqlīd (blind following) is not permissible in matters of tawḥīd, risālah, and uṣūl ad-dīn (the fundamentals of the religion). It is obligatory upon every mukallaf (legally accountable individual) to know tawḥīd with its proof, as well as risālah and all other fundamentals of the religion — because the evidences for these fundamentals are clear and, all praise is due to Allāh, not exclusive to scholars alone.

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 10/394]

<details class="source-panel scan-source" data-origin="telegram-attachment">
<summary>Show attached source scan</summary>
<p><img class="source-scan" src="assets/scans/4c7944b772fe3c3578e8.jpg" alt="Attached Arabic source scan" loading="lazy"></p>
</details>

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message3033 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000159 -->

al-ʿAllāmah Abā Buṭayn said:

His statement: “and disbelieves in all that is worshipped besides Allah” — the apparent meaning is that this is an additional clarification, because lā ilāha illa-llāh already includes the rejection of all that is worshipped besides Him.

Whoever says lā ilāha illa-llāh yet still commits al-shirk al-akbar — such as invoking the dead or the absent, asking them to fulfill needs or relieve distress, and seeking closeness to them through vows and sacrifices — then he is a mushrik, whether he likes it or not. Allah does not forgive shirk. Indeed, “Whoever associates partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden Paradise for him, and his abode is the Fire” (al-Māʾidah: 72). And despite this, it remains shirk, and whoever commits it is a kāfir.

However — as the Shaykh said — one should not declare an individual as kāfir until the message brought by the Messenger has been made clear to him. If, after clarification, he persists, then a judgment of disbelief is passed on him, and his blood and wealth become permissible. Allah says: “And fight them until there is no more fitnah” (al-Anfāl: 39) — meaning shirk — “and the religion is entirely for Allah” (al-Anfāl: 39). So if in any land there is an idol that is worshipped besides Allah, then the people are to be fought over that idol — that is, to remove and destroy it, and to abandon shirk — until religion belongs entirely to Allah.

Duʿāʾ is an act of dīn. Allah named it “dīn,” as in His saying: “So when they board a ship, they call upon Allah, making their dīn purely for Him” (al-ʿAnkabūt: 65) — meaning duʿāʾ. And the Prophet ﷺ said: “I was sent with the sword before the Hour so that Allah alone would be worshipped with no partner.” So whenever any act of ʿibādah is directed to other than Allah, the sword is unsheathed against it.

And Allah knows best. May peace and blessings be upon Muḥammad, his family, and his companions.

[Majmūʿ Fatāwā wa-Rasāʾil al-Shaykh al-ʿAllāmah ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Abā Buṭayn p.507-508]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message3080 -->

al-ʿAllāmah Abā Buṭayn said:

And those who committed shirk by worshipping idols, or any of the angels, or the devils, or the sun, or the stars, or fire, or anyone other than Allah — whether from the mushrikūn of the Arabs, or the people of India, or Africa, or others — or who claimed that there is a creator or disposer of the universe besides Allah, then all of that is kufr by the ijmāʿ of the Muslims.

So reflect on this transmission of ijmāʿ by the Muslims upon the disbelief of those who worship anyone besides Allah, whether angels or others. This is clear, and all praise is due to Allah. And the verses of the Qur’an on this matter are many. So whoever says that one who has uttered the two shahādahs, and prays and fasts, cannot be declared a disbeliever — even if he worships other than Allah — then he himself is a kāfir. And whoever doubts his kufr [by calling him muslim] is also a kāfir.

[Majmūʿat al-Rasāʾil wa-al-Masāʾil al-Najdiyyah 1/660]

---

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3684 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000161 -->

al-ʿAllāmah Abā Buṭayn said:

Allāh — Exalted is He — said: “Indeed, Allāh does not forgive that partners be associated with Him” (Sūrat an-Nisāʾ: 48), and He said: “Then kill the mushrikīn wherever you find them” (Sūrat at-Tawbah: 5). This is general, applying to every individual among the mushrikīn.

All the ʿulamāʾ, in the books of fiqh, mention the ruling on the apostate. The first among the types of kufr and apostasy they list is shirk. They say: Whoever commits shirk with Allāh has disbelieved, and they do not make an exception for the jāhil. Whoever claims that Allāh has a companion or a child has disbelieved, and they do not make an exception for the jāhil. Whoever slanders ʿĀʾishah (may Allāh be pleased with her) has disbelieved, and whoever mocks Allāh, His messengers, or His books has disbelieved by ijmāʿ— as He, Exalted is He, said: “Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after your belief” (Sūrat at-Tawbah: 66).

They also mention many kinds of acts upon which are agreed upon regarding the disbelief of the one who commits them, and they do not differentiate between the muʿayyan (specific individual) and the general case.

Then they say: Whoever apostasizes from Islām is to be killed after being offered istītābah (a chance to repent). Thus, they ruled him an apostate before even issuing the call to repentance — for istītābah comes after the judgment of apostasy, and istītābah applies only to the specific individual.

[Majmūʿ Fatāwā wa-Rasāʾil by Shaykh al-ʿAllāmah Abā Buṭayn p.599]

<details class="source-panel scan-source" data-origin="telegram-attachment">

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3889 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000162 -->

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

It is said: The naming of something has no bearing on its reality, and the true nature of a thing does not change merely because its name is altered. As the Prophet ﷺ said: “A time will come when people from my Ummah will call wine by another name.”

Similarly, if someone were to call fornication “marriage,” that would not change its legal ruling or its actual nature. Likewise, a person who engages in usurious transactions remains a Murābī (Usurer), even if he does not explicitly call himself one.  In the same way, whoever commits acts of Shirk is a Mushrik, even if he calls it Tawassul or Tashaffu‘ or any other Misleading term.

What confirms this is that everyone acknowledges that worshipping other than Allāh is shirk. We have already presented the definition of ʿibādah: whoever directs any type of ʿibādah to other than Allāh has committed shirk, even if he does not think it is shirk, does not intend deification, and calls it by whatever name he wishes.

So the mushrik is a mushrik—whether he accepts it or refuses it—just as the murābī (usurer) is a murābī, whether he accepts it or refuses it.

[Ta'sīs al-Taqdīs fī Kashf Talbīs Dāwūd bin Jirjīs wa Yalīhi Daḥḍ Shubuhāt ʿalā al-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn p.99-100]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2422 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000163 -->

Shaykh Al-Mujaddid ʿAbd Ar-Raḥmān bin Ḥasan said:

Ibn al-Qayyim also said regarding the levels of people from this Ummah and others:

The seventeenth level is that of the blind followers  and the ignorant among the disbelievers and their followers — their donkeys — who merely say, “We found our forefathers upon a religion and we follow in their footsteps.”

He said: The Ummah has unanimously agreed that this category are disbelievers, even though they were ignorant and mere followers of their leaders and imams, except for what is narrated from some innovators who did not judge them to be in the Fire, equating them with those whom the message did not reach. But this is a view not held by any of the Imāms of the Muslims — neither the Ṣaḥābah, nor the Tābiʿūn, nor those after them.

It is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah; then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian.” He informed us that it is the parents who shift the child from the fiṭrah to Judaism, Christianity, or Magianism, and he did not consider any other factor beyond the upbringing and education by the parents.

It is also authentically reported from him ﷺ that he said: “No soul will enter Paradise except one that is Muslim.”

This follower is not a Muslim; he is a rational, legally accountable being. A rational accountable person is either a Muslim or a kāfir — there is no third category.

He said: Islam is to affirm the tawḥīd of Allah and worship Him alone with no partner, to believe in His Messenger and follow him in what he came with. Whoever does not bring these essentials is not a Muslim — even if not out of obstinacy — but is a disbeliever out of ignorance.

The utmost one can say about this category is that they are ignorant disbelievers, but their ignorance does not remove them from the ruling of kufr.

The disbeliever is one who rejects the tawḥīd of Allah and belies His Messenger, whether through obstinacy or ignorance or blind following those who are obstinate.

[Al-Adillah wa Al-Barāhīn ʿalā ʿAdam Al-ʿUḏhr bil Jahl fī Uṣūl Ad-Dīn by the Shaykh Al-Mujaddid ʿAbd Ar-Raḥmān bin Ḥasan Āl Ash-Shaykh p.27-28]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2391 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000164 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān Ibn Ḥasan said:

He (Ibn Qayyim) said: “Islam is the monotheism of Allah and worshipping Him alone with no partner, believing in His Messenger, and following what he brought. If a person does not fulfill this, he is not a Muslim. Even if he is not oppositional, he is an ignorant disbeliever. The nature of this category is that they are ignorant disbelievers, not oppositional. Their lack of opposition does not take them out of disbelief. The disbeliever is the one who denies the oneness of Allah and denies His Messenger, either out of opposition or ignorance, or following the traditions of their forefathers out of stubbornness.”

Allah has informed us in the Qur’an, in several places, of the punishment for those who blindly follow their ancestors from the disbelievers. They will dispute in Hell, and the followers will say: “Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray, so give them double the punishment in the Fire.” Allah will say: “For each there is double, but you do not know.” (Al-A’raf: 38) This is a summarized explanation, and this verse has many similar instances in the Qur’an. Praise be to Allah for the clarity of the explanation.

The clear verses also show the disbelief of those who associate others with Allah in His worship. Allah says: “When man is touched with harm, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him alone. But when He grants him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he had been calling to Him before, and he makes equals to Allah to mislead others from His way. Say: ‘Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire.’” (Az-Zumar: 8)

[Taḥqīq Madhhab Ibn Taymiyyah fī Masʾalatay al-ʿUdhr bil-Jahl wa Takfīr al-Muʿayyan By Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān Ibn Ḥasan Āl ash-Shaykh p.32]

Shaykh Al-Mujaddid ʿAbd Ar-Raḥmān bin Ḥasan said:

For the people of shirk, you have already learned what Allah has said about them, and what this Imam and other scholars have established regarding their being declared disbelievers due to associating partners in divinity and opposing the Shariah. The religion of shirk is a religion of disbelief, as Allah said: {Indeed, those who have believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associated partners} (Al-Ḥajj 22:17).

Thus, the people of faith are the people of truth, and all others among the five religions are religions of definite disbelief. Whoever does not recognize and understand this distinction is an ignorant and misguided person:

{And whoever Allah wants to put in trial, never will you possess for him [power to do] a thing against Allah} (Al-Māʾidah 5:41).

Shaykh al-Islām, may Allah have mercy on him, also said in al-Fatāwā al-Miṣriyyah: Some people said that when one ‘achieves essentialization’ (tajawhar), obligations fall from him, and commands and prohibitions are mere regulations for the common folk. They claimed that the essence of prophethood boils down to wisdom and benefit, meant to govern the masses, and that they themselves, having achieved tajawhar, are not subject to religious obligations.

These individuals are more disbelieving than the Jews and Christians. Indeed, the Jews and Christians believed in part and disbelieved in part, whereas these have disbelieved entirely and reject adherence to any portion of the truth. He said: Whoever denies an apparent, well-known obligation, or denies an apparent prohibition like immorality, oppression, intoxicants, fornication, or usury, or denies the permissibility of apparent lawful matters like bread, meat, and marriage — then he is a disbeliever and an apostate who must be asked to repent, and if he does not, he is to be executed.


[Al-Adillah wa Al-Barāhīn ʿalā ʿAdam Al-ʿUḏhr bil Jahl fī Uṣūl Ad-Dīn by the Shaykh Al-Mujaddid ʿAbd Ar-Raḥmān bin Ḥasan Āl Ash-Shaykh p.20]

Shaykh ʿAbd Ar-Raḥmān bin Ḥasan said:

So consider—O you whom Allah has granted knowledge of the religion of the messengers, and awareness of what contradicts it from the religion of the polytheists—how the devil has played with most of the ignorant. He stripped them of the light and nobility of knowledge, and made it seem pleasing to them to lose the true meaning of lā ilāha illa Allāh. They became satisfied with its mere wording, without the meaning for which it was revealed: the rejection of shirk with Allah, and the exclusive devotion of all acts of worship to Allah alone.

Through this ignorance and delusion, they fell into the gravest of sins and the most dangerous of prohibitions. They directed the greatest part of their love, and the core essence of worship, to the lords of the graves. Worse still, they went beyond mere shirk, believing those buried had power to manage affairs and the ability to influence events.

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 11/491]

Shaykh Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan Āl ash-Shaykh said:

And neither the scholars of the Salaf nor the Khalaf ever stated that shirk is an area in which ijtihād is permissible, and that its perpetrator is excused because of his ijtihād.

Rather, this is a lie against the Kitāb, the Sunnah, and the ijmāʿ of the scholars of the Ummah.

Rather, all acts of disobedience are such that no one who commits them is excused by claiming that he was a mujtahid, while the threat of punishment from Allah remains upon the one who commits them.

And even if it were assumed that some of them had an interpretation, then everything that opposes the ruling of Allah and His religion is not permissible.

And if that were permissible, then the divine laws and prescribed punishments would be nullified.

And with what Allah has clarified of His religion, which His Messengers called to, from the first of them to the last of them, there remains no excuse for anyone.

[ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 11/548-549]

Shaykh ʿAbd Ar-Raḥmān bin Ḥasan said:

They have been content with merely pronouncing the phrase of tawḥīd, believing it to be beneficial even if they do not believe in its meaning or act according to it. But anyone with the slightest sense knows that lā ilāha illa Allāh indicates tawḥīd, and there is no doubt that shirk contradicts tawḥīd, as has been mentioned—that it nullifies deeds, even if the deeds were sound to begin with. So how is it when the foundation of those deeds is disbelief in the meaning of lā ilāha illa Allāh or shirk itself?

If you understand this, then know that the core difference between the messengers and their nations was precisely over the meaning of lā ilāha illa Allāh in its full and direct sense. The phrase lā ilāha denies shirk and divinity from anything besides Allah. The phrase illa Allāh affirms divinity with all its inward and outward implications for Allah alone. This is made clear repeatedly in the Qur’ān.

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 11/487-488]

Sheikh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf said:

His statement: “By testifying that there is no god but Allah.”

This applies to a person whose disbelief was due to their refusal to say it. If, in their state of kufr, they did not acknowledge this statement, then upon saying it, they become Muslim, and their Islam is recognized. However, as for a person who says it while being an apostate , or a Jew  who says it, they both remain in their original state.

An example of this is those who say “Lā ilāha illa Allāh” yet engage in actions that nullify it—such as those who worship al-Badawī or al-Jīlānī, or those who venerate the graves of the Prophet’s family and similar sites among the Rāfiḍah. The one who asks them to fulfill needs or seeks their help in times of distress has nullified “Lā ilāha illa Allāh.” His tongue says it, but his actions and words affirm that he acknowledges another deity alongside Allāh.

It is not required that he explicitly call it a deity using that exact wording and meaning together. If he perceives it as merely an intermediary, the mushrikūn also called their objects of worship, intermediary . In their terminology, the one to whom such requests are directed is the god, whether the request is directed at the entity itself or through its mediation.

The Prophet came with the statement of tawḥīd that invalidates all of this.

This clarifies the reality of those who claim to belong to Islam. It is common among the youth today that some never pray at all, yet they believe themselves to be Muslim.

Q: What if they are ignorant?

A: “There is no ignorance in tawḥīd. This is not something that can be unknown. Rather, this is someone who has turned away from religion. Can a person be ignorant of the sun? Their scholars are ignorant, and none are more ignorant than the mushrik. In the Qurʾān, jahl is only attributed to those who worship other than Allāh. They are ignorant, yet the ḥujjah (proof) against them is complete.

Thus, two things coexist: knowledge to the extent that the ḥujjah has been established against them, and ignorance to the extent that they have turned away from it.”

A debate once took place between him and the Shaykh al-Azhar, who eventually said: “These people have taken on the appearance of kuffār.” So he replied: “Then should we not take on the appearance of those who declare them mukaffirīn ?”

[Fatāwā wa Rasāʾil by Sheikh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf 12/197-198]

### ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl ash-Shaykh: neither category is ruled Muslim
<!-- evidence-id: 000171 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: عبد اللطيف بن عبد الرحمن آل الشيخ، <em>منهاج التأسيس والتقديس في كشف شبهات داود بن جرجيس</em>، ص. 99.</p>
<p>وَالشَّيْخُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ مِنْ أَعْظَمِ النَّاسِ تَوَقُّفًا وَإِحْجَامًا عَنْ إِطْلَاقِ الْكُفْرِ، حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَجْزِمْ بِتَكْفِيرِ الْجَاهِلِ الَّذِي يَدْعُو غَيْرَ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُبُورِ أَوْ غَيْرِهِمْ إِذَا لَمْ يَتَيَسَّرْ لَهُ مَنْ يَنْصَحُهُ وَيُبَلِّغُهُ الْحُجَّةَ الَّتِي يَكْفُرُ تَارِكُهَا.</p>
<p>قَالَ فِي بَعْضِ رَسَائِلِهِ: وَإِذَا كُنَّا لَا نُقَاتِلُ مَنْ يَعْبُدُ قُبَّةَ الْكَوَّازِ حَتَّى نَتَقَدَّمَ بِدَعْوَتِهِ إِلَى إِخْلَاصِ الدِّينِ لِلَّهِ، فَكَيْفَ نُكَفِّرُ مَنْ لَمْ يُهَاجِرْ إِلَيْنَا وَإِنْ كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا مُوَحِّدًا؟ وَقَالَ: وَقَدْ سُئِلَ عَنْ مِثْلِ هَؤُلَاءِ الْجُهَّالِ، فَقَرَّرَ أَنَّ مَنْ قَامَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْحُجَّةُ وَتَأَهَّلَ لِمَعْرِفَتِهَا يَكْفُرُ بِعِبَادَةِ الْقُبُورِ.</p>
<p>وَقَدْ سَبَقَ مِنْ كَلَامِهِ مَا فِيهِ الْكِفَايَةُ، مَعَ أَنَّ الْعَلَّامَةَ ابْنَ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ جَزَمَ بِكُفْرِ الْمُقَلِّدِينَ لِشُيُوخِهِمْ فِي الْمَسَائِلِ الْمُكَفِّرَةِ إِذَا تَمَكَّنُوا مِنْ طَلَبِ الْحَقِّ وَمَعْرِفَتِهِ وَتَأَهَّلُوا لِذَلِكَ، فَأَعْرَضُوا وَلَمْ يَلْتَفِتُوا. وَمَنْ لَمْ يَتَمَكَّنْ وَلَمْ يَتَأَهَّلْ لِمَعْرِفَةِ مَا جَاءَتْ بِهِ الرُّسُلُ فَهُوَ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ جِنْسِ أَهْلِ الْفَتْرَةِ مِمَّنْ لَمْ تَبْلُغْهُ دَعْوَةُ رَسُولٍ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ.</p>
<p>وَكِلَا النَّوْعَيْنِ لَا يُحْكَمُ بِإِسْلَامِهِمْ وَلَا يَدْخُلُونَ فِي مُسَمَّى الْمُسْلِمِينَ، حَتَّى عِنْدَ مَنْ لَمْ يُكَفِّرْ بَعْضَهُمْ، وَسَيَأْتِيكَ كَلَامُهُ. وَأَمَّا الشِّرْكُ فَهُوَ يَصْدُقُ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَاسْمُهُ يَتَنَاوَلُهُمْ، وَأَيُّ إِسْلَامٍ يَبْقَى مَعَ مُنَاقَضَةِ أَصْلِهِ وَقَاعِدَتِهِ الْكُبْرَى: شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ؟</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

“Shaykh Muḥammad, may Allāh have mercy upon him, was among the people most restrained and hesitant concerning an unrestricted declaration of disbelief. He did not definitively declare disbeliever the ignorant person who calls upon other than Allāh among the occupants of graves or others when no one was available to advise him and convey to him the proof whose rejection entails disbelief.

He said in one of his letters: ‘If we do not fight one who worships the dome of al-Kawwāz until we first call him to make the religion sincerely for Allāh, how could we declare disbeliever one who did not emigrate to us while he is a believing muwaḥḥid?’ He was asked about ignorant people of this kind and explained that one against whom the proof has been established and who is capable of understanding it is declared disbeliever for worshipping graves.

Enough of his words on this has preceded. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allāh have mercy upon him, decisively declared disbelievers those who blindly follow their shaykhs in matters that entail disbelief when they were able and qualified to seek and recognize the truth but turned away and paid no attention. The one unable and unqualified to recognize what the Messengers brought is, according to him, of the category of Ahl al-Fatrah to whom the call of a Messenger did not reach.

Neither category is ruled to be Muslim, nor do they enter under the designation of Muslims, even according to those who do not declare some of them disbelievers. As for shirk, its description applies to them and its name encompasses them. What Islam remains alongside the contradiction of its foundation and greatest principle, the testimony that none is worthy of worship except Allāh?”

Source: ʿAbd al-Laṭīf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Āl ash-Shaykh, *Minhāj al-Taʾsīs wa al-Taqdīs fī Kashf Shubuhāt Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs*, p. 99.

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message626 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000172 -->

Shaykẖ ʿAbd Al-Laṭīf said:

Even he did not decisively declare takfīr for the jāhil who invokes others besides Allah—whether from the awlīyā’ of the graves or others—if no one is available to advise him and deliver the proof that, if rejected, would make one a kāfir. He said in some of his rasā’il:

“And if we do not fight those who worship the dome of the kāwiz, until we advance the invitation to purity of religion from Allah, then how could we declare kāfir one who has not migrated to us, even if he is a believer and muwaḥḥid?”

And he was asked about such ignorant people. He clarified that whoever has received the ḥujjah and is capable of understanding it becomes kāfir by worship of graves. Previously, he had spoken sufficiently on this matter.

Meanwhile, ʿAllāmah Ibn al-Qayyim decisively declared the kāfir status of muqallidīn (blind followers) of their shuyūkh in matters that entail takfīr, if they were capable of seeking the truth and understanding it, and yet neglected it.

For those who are unable or unprepared to understand what the messengers brought, they are considered like the ahl al-fatrah who were not reached by the da‘wah of any messenger. Both types are not judged as Muslim nor included in the category of Muslims, even according to those who do not declare some of them kāfir, as will be explained later.

As for shirk, it applies to them, and its name encompasses them. And what Islam remains with someone who contradicts its very origin? Its greatest principle is the shahādah that there is no god but Allah, and the persistence of Islam and its name, along with some of what the fuqahā’ mentioned regarding the ruling on the murtad, is clearer than its persistence among righteous servants and their du‘ā’.

But al-Iraqī (Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs) avoids calling this worship or du‘ā’, claiming it is tawassul and nida’ (calling), and he considers it recommended. Far, far is he from the truth!!

Where is the escape, and the God to be sought… yet one is trapped between hardship and desire.

All of this is by the grace of Allah, through His Book al-‘Azīz in which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it—tanzīl (revelation) from a Wise, Praiseworthy One. And by what Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah brought as wisdom, guidance, and clarification, to the extent Allah revealed to him.

And Allah continues to plant in this dīn a seed whose proof is established among His servants, who strive in clarifying His dīn and sharī‘ah, while those who deviate in His Book and dīn, and turn it from its intended purpose, are left astray.

[Minhāj at-Taʾsīs wat-Taqdīs fī Kashf Shubuhāt Dāwūd Ibn Jirjīs by Shaykẖ ʿAbd Al-Laṭīf p.99]

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl ash-Shaykh mentions:

He (Shaykh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb) said: the category of these mushrikūn and those like them—those who worship the awliyāʾ and the righteous—we judge that they are mushrikūn, and we affirm their disbelief when the prophetic proof has been established upon them (meaning they are judged as disbelievers inwardly after the proof is established).

As for what is besides that from sins which are lower in rank and corruption, we do not make takfīr because of them, nor do we judge anyone from Ahl al-qiblah—those who have distinguished themselves from the worshippers of statues, idols, and graves — to be kāfir merely for a sin they committed or a grave offense they carried out.

And the extreme groups of the Jahmiyyah, the Qadariyyah, the Rāfiḍah, and others whom the Salaf declared kuffār—we do not go beyond the statements of the imāms of guidance and fatwā from the Salaf of this Ummah regarding them. And we declare ourselves free to Allah from what the Khawārij brought and said concerning the people of sins from the Muslims.

[Minhāj at-Taʾsīs wa at-Taqdīs fī Kashf Shubuhāt Dāwūd ibn Jirjis by Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl ash-Shaykh p.166]

<!-- evidence-id: 000176 -->

Shaykh Isḥāq Āl al-Shaykh said:

And this matter of ours — worshipping Allāh alone without any partner, disavowing the worship of anything besides Him, and holding that whoever worships along with Allāh another has committed shirk al-akbar that takes one out of the religion — is the foundation of all foundations. It is for this that Allāh sent the messengers, revealed the scriptures, and established the proof against mankind through the Messenger and the Qur’ān.

Thus, you will find the response of the a’immah ad-dīn (imāms of the religion) regarding this principle — when declaring as kāfir one who associates partners with Allāh — that he is to be asked to repent; if he repents, then fine, and if not, he is to be killed. They did not mention the need for definition in issues of the fundamental principles. Rather, they only mentioned defintion in subtle matters whose evidences may be hidden from some Muslims — such as issues disputed by certain innovators like the Qadariyyah and Murji’ah, or in obscure matters such as certain linguistic forms of disbelief.

So how could they claim that the worshippers of graves are Muslims and enter under the name of Islam? Can any deed remain alongside shirk? Allāh the Exalted says: “They will not enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle.” (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf:40)

And He says: “Whoever associates partners with Allāh, it is as though he had fallen from the sky, and the birds snatch him away, or the wind blows him into a distant place.” (Sūrat al-Ḥajj:31) And: “Indeed, Allāh does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.” (Sūrat an-Nisāʾ:48) And: “Whoever associates partners with Allāh, his deeds have become worthless.” (Sūrat al-Mā’idah:72) — and many other āyāt.

But this corrupt belief — that the proof has not been established upon this ummah through the Messenger and the Qur’ān — leads to an ugly consequence. We seek refuge in Allāh from the evil understanding that caused them to neglect the Book and the Messenger.

As for the ahl al-fatrah — those whom the message and the Qur’ān did not reach and who died in jāhiliyyah — they are, by ijmāʿ, not called Muslims, nor is forgiveness sought for them. The scholars only differed regarding whether or not they will be punished in the Hereafter.

[Takfīr al-Muʿayyan by Shaykh Isḥāq Āl al-Shaykh p. 9]

Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Saḥmān said:

And these fools generalized the issue and made every ignorance an excuse, and they did not differentiate, and they equated the clear and manifest matters and that which is known from the religion by necessity with the hidden matters whose evidence may be hidden from some people. Likewise, whoever is among the more apparent Muslims—such as someone who grew up in a remote desert or is newly entered into Islām—he may go astray and mislead others and deviate from the straight path.

If you know this, then the issue of Allāh’s ʿuluww over His creation, His istiwā over His Throne, and affirming the attributes of His perfection and the qualities of His majesty are from the clear and manifest matters and from what is known from the religion by necessity. For Allāh has clarified them in His Book and upon the tongue of His Messenger. Whoever hears the Qurʾānic verses and the Prophetic ḥadīths, the proof has been established upon him, even if he does not understand them. If he is one who recites the Qurʾān, the matter is greater and more serious—especially if he is obstinate and claims that what he is upon is the truth, and that the Qurʾān did not clarify this with sufficient and complete explanation—then his disbelief is clearer than the sun at noon.

The one who knows Islām, its rulings, and its principles does not hesitate regarding his disbelief. In summary, whoever follows a religion other than Islām and this description that makes him a disbeliever applies to him, he is a disbeliever. But we do not judge a specific individual to be in the Fire; rather, we leave his affair to Allāh and to His knowledge and judgment regarding the inward reality of his matter. This concerns the rulings of reward and punishment. As for worldly rulings, they proceed according to what is apparent.

If you know and verify this, you understand that this man is disguised in his denial of disbelief upon those who established it, describing kufr. And yet, the daʿwah reached them, the proof was established upon them, but none of the barriers that prevent the establishment of proof took effect. His intent was to criticize the brothers regarding what they did and said about declaring the Jahmīs, the grave worshippers, and the Ibāḍīs of this time. He obliges them with the consequences that do not apply to them, while they absolve themselves to Allāh from saying them.

[Kashf al-Awhām by Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Saḥmān p.117-118]

And I presented this introduction to you so that you understand that many of the religious people in this time do not know the kufr that expels from the millah and the kufr that does not expel from the millah, especially those who claim knowledge and awareness among them who go out to the desert, calling people to Allāh while not knowing the details clarified by the ‘ulamāʾ regarding masāʾil al-takfīr (issues of takfīr), what expels from the millah and what does not expel from the millah.

These hidden matters do not make someone a kāfir if they act upon or say them—according to the correct opinion of the ‘ulamāʾ—until the prophetic proof is established against them.

[Minhāj Ahl al-Ḥaqq wal-Ittibāʿ fī Mukhālafat Ahl al-Jahl wal-Ibtidāʿ by Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Saḥmān p.10]

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Laṭīf and Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Suḥmān said:

And when it is established that duʿāʾ is ʿibādah (worship), then directing it to other than Allāh is shirk. So whoever calls upon along with Allāh anyone from the creation has committed shirk with Him—whether he wills it or refuses. Like if he says: “O Messenger of Allāh,” “O Kaʿbah of Allāh,” “O Station of Ibrāhīm,” or if he supplicates to one of the prophets, or the awliyāʾ, or the righteous—then he is a mushrik with shirk akbar that expels from the religion.

And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them, and they will be disbelievers in their worship.” [Sūrat al-Aḥqāf, 46:5–6] And He said: “And the masājid are for Allāh, so do not call upon anyone along with Allāh.” [Sūrat al-Jinn, 72:18] And besides these, other verses that have come in this meaning.

Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī said:

Allāh declared disbelievers those who spoke a word of disbelief in jest and mockery while traveling, even though they testified that lā ilāha illā Allāh and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah. They came apologizing to the Rasūl ﷺ and swearing oaths, yet Allah revealed about them: “Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after your īmān.” And the inner states are left to Allāh.

The explicit wording of one who calls upon other than Allah, seeks refuge in him, do istaghātha with him, or requests his shafā‘a (intercession) after his death, is greater in kufr than that of one who uttered such words concerning the Rasūl ﷺ and his companions in jest or mockery. For supplication to other than Allah and asking for what only Allah can do is the very foundation of the world’s shirk — none who has even smelled the fragrance of dīn would doubt this. The proof is clear, and the sign is evident.

And whoever says that the one who does such a thing is still a Muslim is among those who have fabricated lies against Allāh. For Allah has declared disbelievers those who made with Him another god, and He has stated explicitly that a person does not enter Islām except by worshipping Allah alone with no partner and by disavowing everything that is worshipped besides Him, as mentioned previously.

However, this objector is either among the most foolish of people, the dullest of mind, and the most ignorant of Allāh, His dīn, and His shar‘ (law); or else he deliberately lies and cares nothing for it.

[as-Sayf al-Maslūl ʿalā ʿĀbid ar-Rasūl by Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī p.126]

Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī said:

And his statement, “Allāh will hold His servants accountable for what they believe inwardly and for their intentions, in accordance with the ḥadīth: ‘Actions are only by intentions’” does not prevent us from affirming the shirk of one who sets up another ilāh alongside Allāh. For judgment in this worldly life is based on outward actions and on what the explicit wording indicates. This is a well-known principle: rulings are applied according to outward matters, while Allāh alone handles what lies within the hearts.

People of sound intellect have stated that it is extreme foolishness to deny what the eye clearly sees and to believe instead what is mere conjecture. So how can we accept this claim from you, when ʿUmar said: “Revelation has ceased, and now we hold you accountable only for what appears to us from your actions. Whoever displays goodness to us, we trust him and draw him near. What is in his inner self is not our concern; Allāh will judge him for his inner self. And whoever displays evil, we do not trust him nor believe him — even if he claims that his inner self is good.” And upon this is the ijmāʿ of the Muslims.

And this noble ḥadīth that you used as evidence is in fact a great foundation among the foundations of the religion — rather, the foundation of every action. It is among the clearest proofs against the one objecting, demolishing what he has established from its very root. For whoever sets up another ilāh alongside Allāh has removed the bond of the religion from himself and nullified his īmān in the Lord of all the worlds.

[as-Sayf al-Maslūl ʿalā ʿĀbid ar-Rasūl by Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī p.136]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1872 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000188 -->

Sheikh Bin Bāz was asked:

Q: Is ignorance an excuse in Tawḥīd ar-Rubūbiyyah (Oneness of Lordship) and Tawḥīd al-Ulūhiyyah (Oneness of Worship), or not? And is the issue of excusing ignorance subject to variation depending on time and place?

A: In matters of creed, there is no excuse for ignorance in Tawḥīd ar-Rubūbiyyah, Tawḥīd al-Ulūhiyyah, or Tawḥīd al-Asmā’ waṣ-Ṣifāt (Oneness of Allah’s Names and Attributes). A believer must hold the correct creed, affirm the oneness of Allāh جل وعلا, believe that He is the Lord of the worlds, the Creator, the All-Knowing, the Sole Lordship, and that there is no creator besides Him. He must also believe that Allah alone deserves worship, that He possesses the most beautiful names and highest attributes, that He has no equal or counterpart.

One who understands this has no excuse for negligence in this matter—except if he is in a distant land where no revelation reaches him. In such a case, he is excused, and his fate is left to Allah. He falls under the ruling of Ahl al-Fatrah (those who lived in a time of disconnection from revelation). Their judgment is deferred to the Day of Judgment, where they will be tested: if they respond correctly, they will enter Paradise; if they respond incorrectly, they will enter Hell.

Thus, the ruling varies: if a person is in a remote location, where he has never heard the Qur’ān or Sunnah, he is like Ahl al-Fatrah, and scholars hold that such individuals will be tested on the Day of Judgment. Whoever obeys will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys will enter Hell.

However, if someone is among Muslims, hears the Qur’ān and Sunnah, yet persists in shirk or denies Allah’s attributes, he is not excused. We seek refuge in Allah from such misguidance.

The issue of excusing ignorance is not a matter of subjective judgment that changes with time and place. Ignorance is not an excuse when it comes to ‘Aqīdah, unless the person is in a location where the message of Islam—the Qur’ān and Sunnah—has not reached him.

On the other hand, in jurisprudential matters, ignorance can be an excuse—for example, if a person is unaware of a particular legal ruling, or if there are intricate details of Allah’s attributes that might be unclear. In such cases, ignorance is excused.

However, regarding fundamental matters—such as belief in the Oneness of Allah, that He is the Creator, the All-Knowing, the One deserving of worship, the Perfect in His Names and Attributes, and belief in what has been revealed in the Qur’ān and authentic Sunnah—there is no excuse for ignorance if the message has reached the individual.

We ask Allah for safety and guidance.

[Fatāwā Nūr ʿalā ad-Darb by Sheikh Ibn Bāz 1/245-246]

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Ibn Bāz رحمه الله was asked:

Question:

Is it permissible to eat the slaughtered animals of those who hold polytheistic beliefs, such as making vows, offering sacrifices, and supplicating to those they claim to be saints (awliyā’)—while knowing that the conclusive proof (ḥujjah) has not been fully established against them to remove their doubts?

Answer:

Whoever is known for holding a corrupt, polytheistic belief, his slaughtered animal is not permissible to eat. If he lives among Muslims, then he has no excuse because he neither inquired nor cared. If it is known that he worships other than Allah—such as those who worship al-Badawi, al-Husayn, al-Hasan, ‘Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), Ibn ‘Arabi, or others whom they call saints—then such people are disbelievers, and their slaughtered animals are impermissible to eat. The same applies to anyone who worships other than Allah, makes vows for them, offers sacrifices to them, or seeks their intercession.

This is major shirk; it is the practice of Jāhiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance)—the same as what Quraysh did with Hubal, al-Lāt, and al-‘Uzza, and what the people of Nūḥ did with Wadd, Suwā‘, and others like them. Such individuals are considered among those upon whom the proof (ḥujjah) has been established, because they live among Muslims, and the Qur’an, Sunnah, and the words of scholars have reached them. If someone has not received any of this knowledge, it is only due to his negligence and lack of concern .

However, those who live in distant lands, away from Muslims, and belong to Ahl al-Fatrah (people who have not received the message and have never heard the words of Allah or His Messenger), they are considered disbelievers in worldly rulings, but their ultimate judgment is left to Allah in the Hereafter. In this world, their slaughtered animals are not permissible to eat as long as they practice the ways of the disbelievers. Their ultimate judgment is left to Allah on the Day of Judgment. On that day, they will be tested. If they obey the commands, they will enter Paradise, and if they disobey, they will enter Hellfire. This is the correct view regarding Ahl al-Fatrah.

Source: [Official Ibn Bāz fatwa, “The ruling on eating the slaughtered animals of those who hold polytheistic beliefs”](https://binbaz.org.sa/fatwas/8613/حكم-اكل-ذباىح-اصحاب-العقاىد-الشركية).

Sheikh Bin Bāz رحمه الله was asked:

Q: “Your Eminence Sheikh! Please kindly answer my question, an Egyptian working in Jordan, asks: Is ignorance an excuse in matters of faith (Lā ilāha illa Allāh)? If ignorance is not an excuse, what is the ruling—according to your esteemed opinion—on someone who only performs some of the prayers? Can we eat from his slaughtered animal? And if an imam believes in the inhabitants of graves, saying that they were righteous people and that visiting them is not considered shirk , is a person deemed Muslim merely by pronouncing the Shahadah? Please provide us with guidance, may you be rewarded.”

A: There is no excuse for ignorance in these matters—matters of faith, monotheism, and associating partners with Allah—for those living among Muslims. Rather, such a person must learn, understand, and be cautious. Ignorance is not an excuse in this case. If someone supplicates to the dead, seeks their aid, or makes vows to them, this constitutes major shirk.

Merely pronouncing the two testimonies is not sufficient while a person engages in such acts, worshiping the dead, seeking their help, or making vows to them—this is major shirk, and they are not excused. They must dedicate worship to Allah alone, avoid shirk, and be wary of it in all its forms.

Abandoning prayer is disbelief. The one who does not pray is a disbeliever, as the Prophet ﷺ said: “Between a man and disbelief and polytheism is the abandonment of prayer.” He also said: “The covenant that distinguishes us from them is prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved.”

Source: [Official Ibn Bāz fatwa, “The issue of excuse due to ignorance in matters of creed”](https://binbaz.org.sa/fatwas/14751/مسالة-العذر-بالجهل-في-مساىل-العقيدة).

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Ibn Bāz was asked:

Question: Some contemporary individuals have stated that anyone who says or does something that constitutes kufr (disbelief) should not be declared a disbeliever until the proof (hujjah) is established against them, and they have included those who worship graves in this category?

Answer: This is due to their ignorance. Grave worshippers are disbelievers, as are the Jews and the Christians. However, when it comes to execution, they should be given the opportunity to repent. If they repent, fine; if not, they should be executed.

Question: But is it necessary for the proof (hujjah) to be established against them?

Answer: The Quran has reached them: “This is a message for the people” [Ibrahim: 52]. They have been informed that they are among the Muslims: “And it was revealed to this Qur’an, to warn you by it, and whomsoever it reaches” [Al-An’am: 19], “This is a message for the people” [Ibrahim: 52], “O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you” [Al-Ma’idah: 67]. The Messenger has delivered it, and the Quran is in front of them, being heard in broadcasts and other places, but they do not care or pay attention. And when someone from outside their circle warns them, they excuse themselves.

[Sharḥ Kashf ash-Shubuhāt by Sheikh Ibn Bāz p.114-115]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1706 -->

Sheikh Bin Bāz was Asked:

Question:

“Your Eminence, in our country, many have gone astray due to Sufi orders, as they worship graves and invoke beings other than Allah. Among them are memorizers of the Qur’an and imams of mosques. My question consists of several parts, Your Eminence: Are these individuals considered disbelievers due to committing shirk (associating partners with Allah) and their lack of knowledge about tawḥīd (Islamic monotheism), if they are ignorant of the meaning of “Lā ilāha illa Allāh” (There is no god but Allah)? Are they excused due to ignorance, or are they deemed disbelievers? Please guide us in light of this question. I still have additional parts to my question—please proceed, Your Eminence.

Answer:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

All praise is due to Allah, and may peace and blessings be upon the Messenger of Allah, his family, his companions, and those who follow his guidance.

The Noble Qur’an and the purified Sunnah have clarified the oneness of Allah—Glorified and Exalted is He—and have also explained the various forms of major shirk. If a person commits shirk while living among Muslims and having access to the Qur’an and Sunnah, then they are judged as committing shirk. Allah—Glorified and Exalted—is He says: “And this Qur’an has been revealed to me so that I may warn you thereby, and whomever it reaches.” (Al-An‘ām 6:19)

Allah also says: “O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord.” (Al-Mā’idah 5:67)

And He says: “Your duty is only to convey the message, and the reckoning is upon Us.” (Ar-Ra‘d 13:40)

So, whoever receives the message of the Noble Qur’an and the purified Sunnah and still engages in shirk is judged accordingly due to their negligence and failure to fulfill their obligation of seeking knowledge and understanding in religion.

If a person invokes the dead, seeks their intercession, or calls upon stars, trees, stones, idols, or jinn—making supplications to them, seeking their help, or offering vows to them—this constitutes major shirk. Such a person must be called to repent by the authorities. If they repent, they are accepted back into Islam; otherwise, they are subject to capital punishment for committing shirk against Allah. As the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever changes his religion, kill him.”

Allah sent His Prophet ﷺ to call people to tawḥīd and to strive against the mushrikīn. Thus, if a person lives among Muslims or in a land where the Qur’an and Sunnah have reached, yet remains negligent and continues in their acts of shirk, they are to be judged as a mushrik.

Source: [Official Ibn Bāz fatwa, “The ruling on grave worshippers and whether they are excused due to ignorance”](https://binbaz.org.sa/fatwas/11713/حكم-عباد-القبور-وهل-يعذرون-بالجهل).

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2853 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000193 -->

Shaykh Bin Bāz was Asked:

A message from the questioner “Ḥā’” from Banī Mālik:

She says: Your Eminence, I would like to ask a question that has been on my mind. What is the ruling on someone who died associating others with Allah – may Allah protect us from shirk – but did not know the seriousness of this matter? He was one of the ignorant people of the villages in that time, unaware that shirk is among the gravest of major sins, and he died in that state. My question is: Is it permissible for us to supplicate for his mercy and forgiveness? Is it allowed to perform ḥajj or ʿumrah on his behalf? Would such acts benefit him? Please advise us in detail. May Allah reward you.

Answer by His Eminence Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Bāz (may Allah have mercy on him):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah. May peace and blessings be upon the Messenger of Allah, his family, companions, and those who follow his guidance. To proceed: Shirk with Allah is the greatest sin and the gravest of all major sins. As the Prophet ﷺ said in the authentic ḥadīth: “Shall I not inform you of the greatest of major sins?” They said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He said, “Associating others with Allah.”

And Allah the Exalted says: {Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills} [al-Nisāʾ: 48].

So, shirk is the gravest sin and the most hideous offense. Whoever dies upon it will not be forgiven, and he will be among the inhabitants of Hell, abiding therein eternally. No ḥajj should be performed on his behalf, nor prayer offered for him, nor supplication made for him, nor charity given on his behalf, because of Allah’s statement: {And it was already revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate [anything] with Allah, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers} [al-Zumar: 65], and His statement: {But if they had associated others with Allah, then worthless for them would be whatever they were doing} [al-Anʿām: 88], and His statement about the polytheists: {Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them. And they are never to emerge from the Fire} [al-Baqarah: 167].

Shirk is directing worship to other than Allah, or any part of it — such as calling upon the dead, or the stars, or the prophets, or the angels; seeking their help, vowing to them, or offering sacrifices to them — this is shirk.

Likewise, the one who denies what Allah has made obligatory — matters that are known necessarily in religion and agreed upon by all Muslims — such as denying the obligation of prayer, zakāh, fasting in Ramaḍān, or ḥajj when able, or who makes lawful what Allah has forbidden from well-known matters like claiming that zinā, wine, or disobedience to parents is ḥalāl — this is major kufr. He is not to be prayed over, nor is forgiveness to be sought for him, nor is ḥajj or charity to be performed on his behalf, because he died outside of Islam.

As long as such a person lived among Muslims, heard the Qurʾān, saw the Muslims and their practices, then the proof has been established against him, as Allah says: {And this Qurʾān was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches} [al-Anʿām: 19].

That is, whoever the Qurʾān reaches, then the proof has reached them. And if he turned away, did not seek knowledge, and did not investigate, then his matter is with Allah — but in terms of the ruling in this world, he is like the disbelievers of Quraysh who were killed at Badr or died in Makkah, and like the general disbelievers among today’s Christians and Jews. All of them have had the proof established against them, because they did not submit to what Muḥammad ﷺ brought, nor did they pay heed to it, so they became disbelievers. We ask Allah for safety and wellbeing.
