Shaykh ibn Bāz was asked:

Ruling on many of the common people falling into serious violations of tawḥīd

Question: Many common people fall into serious violations of tawḥīd. What is their ruling? Are they excused by ignorance? What is the ruling on marrying them and eating their slaughtered meat? Is it permissible for them to enter Makkah al-Mukarramah?

Answer: Whoever is known for praying to the dead, seeking help from them, making vows to them, or similar types of worship, he is a mushrik kāfir. It is not permissible to marry him, nor to enter the Masjid al-Ḥarām, nor to treat him as a Muslim, even if he claims ignorance until he repents to Allah from that.

Allah says in Surat al-Baqarah: “Do not marry the mushrikāt until they believe; and a believing slave woman is better than a mushrikah, even though she may please you. And do not marry the mushrikīn until they believe; and a believing slave is better than a mushrik, even though he may please you.” (Al-Baqarah 2:221)

And in Surat al-Mumtahanah: “O you who believe! When believing women come to you as emigrants, test them. Allah knows best their faith. If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are those disbelievers lawful for them.” (Al-Mumtahanah 60:10)

And in Surat at-Tawbah: “O you who believe! Indeed the mushrikīn are impure, so let them not approach the Masjid al-Ḥarām after this year.” (At-Tawbah 9:28)

It is not acceptable to excuse them by ignorance; rather they must be treated like disbelievers until they repent to Allah from that.

Allah also says about their excuse: “And when they commit a foul deed, they say: ‘We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say: ‘Indeed, Allah does not command foulness. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?’ Say: ‘My Lord has commanded justice. Establish worship and pay attention to your faces at every mosque, and call on Him sincerely, as you began, so you shall return.’” (Al-Aʿrāf 7:28-29)

“And some He guided and some deserved error. Indeed, they took the devils as allies instead of Allah and think that they are rightly guided.” (Al-Aʿrāf 7:30) Regarding the Christians and their likes, Allah says: “Say: ‘Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in worldly life, while they think that they do good work.’” (Al-Kahf 18:103-104) There are many such verses in this meaning.

[Tuḥfat al-Ikhwān bi-Ajwibah Muhimmah Tataʿallaq bi-Arkān al-Islām p.37-39]

Shaykh Ibn Bāz was asked:

Q: Some people argue and say: ‘It is true that seeking intercession is shirk akbar, but it is from the masāʾil khafiyyah (hidden matters).’ He agrees with you that it is major shirk, but he does not agree with making takfīr. He says: ‘This is from the hidden issues.’”

A: No, it is not hidden. The most obvious thing in existence is shirk akbar. If someone prays to other than Allāh, or fasts for other than Allāh, or says: ‘O my master al-Badawī, forgive me, have mercy on me, heal my sick person, return my absent one, I am in your protection and I am sick — grant me healing’ — what could be clearer than this?”

Q: Then your view is that the one ignorant of tawḥīd is not excused for his ignorance?”

He replied: No, he is not excused — if he knows, or if he is among the Muslims. But if he is far away (from the muslim living in a remote land), then his ruling is the ruling of ahl al-fatrah. We treat him with the treatment of the kuffār, but his affair is with Allāh. We do not pray over him, the Muslims do not inherit from him, and his affair is with Allāh.

[Subul as-Salām Sharḥ Nawāqiḍ al-Islām by Shaykh Ibn Bāz p.263-264]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3471 -->

Shaykh Bin Bāz said:

Directing any part of worship to the awliyāʾ, or to the prophets, or to the sun and the moon, or to the jinn, or to the angels, or to idols, or to trees, or to anything else, all of this nullifies the tawḥīd of Allah and invalidates it.

And when it is known that Allah — exalted is He — sent His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, and the prophets before him, to peoples who worshipped other than Allah — some of them worshipped prophets and the righteous, some worshipped trees and stones, some worshipped carved idols, and some worshipped celestial bodies, and the like — they all called their peoples to the tawḥīd of Allah, to believe in Him alone, to declare lā ilāha illa Allāh, to renounce whatever contradicts it, to renounce those who worship other than Allah and the objects of their worship.

For whoever directs part of worship to other than Him has not truly made Him one, as Allah said: “And indeed, We sent into every nation a messenger, [saying]: Worship Allah and avoid Ṭāghūt.” [al-Naḥl 16:36]

From this, it is understood that what is practiced around graves that are worshipped besides Allah — such as the grave of al-Badawī, al-Ḥusayn in Egypt, and the like — and what occurs from some of the ignorant pilgrims and others at the grave of the Prophet ﷺ — asking him for aid, seeking victory over enemies, calling upon him for relief, and presenting complaints to him — all of this is worship of other than Allah, and it is the shirk of the first Jāhiliyyah. Likewise, what is practiced by some Ṣūfīs who believe that certain awliyāʾ govern the cosmos and manage this world — we seek refuge in Allah — this is major shirk in rubūbiyyah.

And likewise what occurs from the belief of some people — that some created beings have a connection with the Lord such that they can dispense with following the Messenger Muḥammad ﷺ, or that they know the unseen, or that they control the created realities — and the like of this: it is kufr akbar  in Allah, clear shirk, which removes its possessor from the millah islāmiyyah (Islamic religion), if he claims affiliation to it.

Thus, there is no tawḥīd, no Islām, no īmān, and no salvation except through singling out Allah in worship, believing that He is the Owner of Sovereignty, the Disposer of affairs, and that He is perfect in His Essence, His Attributes, His Names, and His Acts. He has no partner, no likeness, and cannot be compared to His creation. To Him belongs absolute perfection in His Essence, His Attributes, and His Acts. He alone is the Manager of the dominion — exalted and majestic — without partner, and none can reverse His decree.

[Majmūʿat Rasāʾil fī at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Bin Bāz p.14-15]

Shaykh Ibn Bāz was asked:

Q: What is the ruling on those who call upon other than Allāh from among the Muslims due to ignorance of the reality of tawḥīd?

A: This is their ruling: their action is kufr. Calling upon the dead and directing supplication to the dead is kufr.

The scholars differed concerning the ruling on the individual himself: does he become a kāfir automatically, or is it necessary that he first be made to know?

There are two views:

The first: that it is necessary he be informed, because the matter may have become confused for him due to the callers to falsehood and because of corrupt scholars, so the issue became unclear to him. Therefore, he must be taught and alerted before disbelief is ruled (meaning the punishment being applied) upon him. This is the view of a group of scholars.

The second: that it does not require clarification, because the matter is clear and all of it is manifest shirk. This is the Sunnah, and the Messenger clarified it and explained it. Thus, his kufr does not depend on clarification; rather, he is a kāfir by this action.

However, it is understood that if there were an Islamic state that holds him accountable, it would not execute him until he is asked to repent to Allāh and abandon this shirk. If he repents and desists, then praise is due to Allāh. If he persists, then the matter remains grave.

In any case, the view that he is a kāfir merely by these actions is a strong view. But the more cautious approach is not to hasten in this ruling (of punishment) until he is informed, directed to good, and taught, so that perhaps he may be guided if that becomes possible.

As for his ruling in this world: his ruling is the ruling of a kāfir in worldly matters — he is not prayed over, not washed, and the Muslims do not treat him as one of them.

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Ibn Bāz was asked:

Question: May Allah bless your deeds! The author said: “He may say it while being ignorant, yet he is not excused for his ignorance?”

Answer: Because he is among Muslims, and he has access to the Book and Sunnah—it is near to him. This implies a form of negligence.

Question: Should this be applied to someone who is negligent (mufarriṭ)?

Answer: Yes, because he is a negligent person who has the ability to learn but did not care.

Answer: This is a great matter, and the principle is that one who is among Muslims and has received the Book and the Sunnah is not excused. Allah, the Almighty, said: “This (Qur’an) is a clear message for the people” [Ibrahim: 52], and He also said: “And this Qur’an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches” [Al-An‘am: 19]. Whoever has received the Qur’an and Sunnah is not excused; rather, he is at fault due to his negligence and lack of concern for learning.

Interjection: But can it be said that this is a disputed issue?

Answer: No, it is not a disputed issue, except in subtle cases that may be unclear, such as the story of the man who told his family to burn his body.

[Sharḥ Kashf ash-Shubuhāt by Sheikh Ibn Bāz p.26-27]

Shaykh Ibn Bāz said:

Q: What is the ruling on one who says: “Those who call upon the righteous awliyāʾ are Muslims”?

A: The ruling is that it clarifies to him that this is kufr and misguidance. If he insists, then he becomes a kāfir like them. It is explained to him their kufr and misguidance, with the evidences for that. Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, says: “So do not call upon anyone along with Allāh” (al-Jinn 18).

And He, the Exalted, says: “And whoever calls upon another god alongside Allāh, for which he has no proof, then his reckoning is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will never succeed” (al-Muʾminūn 117).

He named them disbelievers. And He, the Exalted, says: “And those whom you call upon besides Him do not own even the thin membrane of a date seed. If you call upon them, they do not hear your call, and if they were to hear, they could not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will disown your associating them with Allāh” (Fāṭir 13–14).

He called their du‘ā shirk. It should be explained to them that their du‘ā from them and istighāthah from the dead is shirk, the very shirk of the mushrikīn. This was the shirk of Quraysh with al-Lāt and others among the righteous, and with the angels. We ask Allāh for safety and well-being.

[Fatāwā Nūr ʿalā al-Darb by Shaykh Ibn Bāz 2/96]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3417 -->

Shaykh Ibn Bāz Advice to the student of knowledge in the matter of ʿUdhr bil Jahl

Shaykh Ibn Bāz said:

It is obligatory upon the Muslim to have insight and to be upon clarity regarding his religion. A mushrik is a mushrik, even if he says “lā ilāha illā Allāh,” and a kāfir is a kāfir, even if he says “lā ilāha illā Allāh,” until he believes in its meaning and fulfills its right. As the Prophet ﷺ said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say lā ilāha illā Allāh. When they say lā ilāha illā Allāh, their blood and wealth are protected from me, except by its right.”

And likewise, if he calls upon the angels and seeks help from them, or from the jinn, he has disbelieved, even if he says lā ilāha illā Allāh. And in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar: “Except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is with Allah.” So there must be the right of Islam and the right of lā ilāha illā Allāh, which is adherence to the religion of Allah and caution against whatever leads to shirk or denial of Allah and His Messenger.

Even if a person performs every act of worship and believes in everything Allah made obligatory, but then says, for example: “There is no resurrection, no gathering, no Paradise, no Hellfire,” he has disbelieved according to all. Even if he prays and fasts and is among the most devout of people.

Likewise, if he believes in everything but says: “Zinā is ḥalāl,” or “khamr is ḥalāl,” or “ṣalāh is not obligatory,” or “fasting Ramaḍān is not obligatory,” or “ḥajj is not obligatory despite having the ability,” then he has disbelieved according to all.

Therefore, it is obligatory to be alert to these matters, and for the student of knowledge to be upon insight, and not to be deceived by the words of these apostates—these ignorant misguiders who worship graves and seek aid from the dead, while claiming, “We are Muslims.” We ask Allah for safety. May Allah grant everyone success and guidance.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message3046 -->

Shaykh Bin Bāz was Asked:

Question: Is there disagreement on the issue of excuse due to ignorance?

Answer: It is a great issue, and the original ruling is that there is no excuse if among the Muslims there are those who have received the Qurʾān and the Sunnah. They are not excused. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, said: “This is a message for the people” [Ibrāhīm: 52], and He said: “And this Qurʾān has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches” [Al-Anʿām: 19]. Whoever receives the Qurʾān and the Sunnah is not excused; rather, they are held accountable for their negligence and carelessness.

Question: But is it correct to say this is a matter of disagreement?

Answer: No, it is not a matter of disagreement, except in subtle details that may be hidden, like the story of the one who said to his family: “Burn me.”

Source: [Official Ibn Bāz fatwa, “Is the issue of excuse due to ignorance a disputed issue?”](https://binbaz.org.sa/fatwas/31405/هل-مسالة-العذر-بالجهل-من-المساىل-الخلافية).

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1890 -->

Sheikh Bin Bāz was asked:

Q: Are those who worship graves excused due to ignorance, even though there are callers to Tawḥīd among them?

A: It has already been clarified that they are not excused. They are obligated to seek knowledge, understand their religion, and ask about what confuses them. If they remain silent and persist in worshiping the dead, trees, stones, prophets, angels, or jinn, then they are considered disbelievers due to their acts—such as invoking these beings, seeking their intercession, asking them to heal the sick, or bring back the lost.

Q: Is it permissible to pray behind someone known to invoke others besides Allāh? What is the ruling on the prayer of those who follow him?

A: Whoever prays behind someone who commits shirk, their prayer is invalid, as long as that person calls upon other than Allāh, seeks aid from other than Him, or makes vows to other than Him. It is not permissible to pray behind a disbeliever, and the prayer behind a disbeliever is invalid according to the scholars. The only debate exists regarding the sinful Muslim (fāsiq), but as for the disbeliever, there is no difference of opinion.

[Aqwāl ash-Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Ibn Bāz fī al-ʿUdhr bil-Jahl p.26]

Shaykh Ibn Bāz said:

It may also be said that the people of jāhiliyyah are treated like kuffār in worldly rulings: they are not supplicated for, nor is forgiveness sought for them, because they perform the actions of the disbelievers, so they are treated according to those actions. Their affair, however, is with Allah in the Hereafter.

As for the one upon whom the ḥujjah has not been established in this world, he is not punished until he is tested on the Day of Resurrection. For Allah, Exalted is He, said: “We do not punish until We send a messenger.” [al-Isrāʾ: 15] Thus every person who lived in a fatrah — to whom the da‘wah of a prophet did not reach — will be tested on the Day of Resurrection. If he responds correctly, he will enter Paradise; and if he disobeys, he will enter the Fire.

Likewise the very elderly person to whom the da‘wah never reached, and the insane whose minds never perceived the da‘wah, and others similar to them — such as the children of the disbelievers — for when the Messenger ﷺ was asked about them, he said: “Allah knows best what they would have done.” So the children of the disbelievers will be tested on the Day of Resurrection like the people of the fatrah: if they answer correctly, they will be saved, and if not, they will be among those who perish.

[Majmūʿ Fatāwā wa Maqālāt ash-Shaykh Ibn Bāz 5/181-182]

Al-Ṭaḥāwī said in his ʿAqīdah:

We fear for them but do not cause them to despair. Amn (safety from Allah’s punishment) and iyās (despair of His mercy) both remove one from the millah of Islām, and the path of truth lies between the two for the people of the qiblah. A servant does not leave īmān except by juḥūd (denial) that which brought him into it.

Shaykh Ibn Bāz said regarding this: “This limitation is questionable! For the disbeliever enters into Islam by the two testimonies of faith if he is able to pronounce them. If he cannot pronounce them, he enters Islam by repenting from that which caused his disbelief.

And one may exit Islam not only through denial, but through many other reasons clarified by the scholars in the chapter of the ruling on the apostate (bāb ḥukm al-murtadd), such as: reviling Islam, or the Prophet, or mocking Allah, His Messenger, His Book, or any part of His Sharīʿah—due to His saying:

“Say: Is it Allah and His signs and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse—you have disbelieved after you had believed.” [al-Tawbah: 65–66]

Among the causes of apostasy is also worshipping idols, calling upon the dead, seeking aid from them, asking them for help or provision, and the like. These acts contradict the statement lā ilāha illā Allāh, which affirms that worship is the sole right of Allah—including supplication, seeking aid, bowing, prostration, sacrifice, vows, and the like.

Whoever directs any of these acts to other than Allah, whether idols, statues, angels, jinn, or the dead, has committed shirk and nullified lā ilāha illā Allāh. These matters expel one from Islam by the consensus of the scholars, and they are not classified as juḥūd (denial).

Their evidences are well known from the Qur’ān and Sunnah, and there are many other matters that invalidate one’s Islam which are not called juḥūd—these are detailed by the scholars in the chapter on the apostate. Refer to them if you wish. And Allah grants success.”

[Majmūʿ Fatāwā Ibn Bāz 2/83]

Who are Ahl al-Fatrah?

Shaykh Ibn Bāz was asked:

Q: Who are Ahl al-Fatrah? And is it correct that there are some of them today?

A: Ahl al-Fatrah are those to whom the Message did not reach. These are Ahl al-Fatrah: they did not hear of the Qurʾān, nor of the Messenger ﷺ. These are called Ahl al-Fatrah. As for one to whom the Qurʾān reached, or the news of the Messenger ﷺ reached him—that Allāh sent him to the people, calling them—and he was negligent, then he is not from Ahl al-Fatrah. Rather, whoever was not reached by that is said to be from Ahl al-Fatrah.

And the correct view regarding them is that they will be tested on the Day of Resurrection. Allāh will test them on the Day of Resurrection: whoever responds enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys enters the Fire. We ask Allāh for well-being.

[Fatāwā Nūr ʿalā ad-Darb by Shaykh Ibn Bāz 1/262-263]

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn said:

These common people — who have this innovation and other that have been mislead into believing it? What is their ruling? As long as they were intending the truth and did not know it, then their sin is upon the one who gave the fatwā and upon the one who misled them. As for them — there is nothing upon them. Yes.

Q: Should we apply to them the same ruling as the mushrikīn, given that it is the common people who perform ṭawāf around the grave being deceived by their scholars

A: The sin is written upon those who issued it (I.e the fatawa).

Q: And they are not mushrikīn?

A: No. Their action is that of a mushrik, but they are not judged with the ruling [of apostasy] of the mushrik because of their ignorance.

Q: if they die upon that, what are they called?

A: If they die, then as long as their action is the action of shirk, it is judged (I.e the Label is applied) that they are mushrikūn — meaning, they are treated with the treatment of the mushrik. But with Allah, exalted is He, the punishment is lifted from them because of their ignorance.

And for this reason, now there are people in the remote parts of Africa, in the remote parts of distant lands, who do not know anything about Islam. If they died, we do not say of these that they are Muslims, nor do we pray over them, nor seek mercy for them, even though the proof has not been established upon them. Rather, we say: outwardly, we treat them in this world according to what is apparent. But in the Hereafter — their affair is to Allah.


This is one of the clear fatawas of Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn differentiating between the Ism of Mushrikeen being applied even if one is ignorant, and the ruling of the Mushrikeen (check video I linked above for the clear fatawa clarifying this distinction) is only after the proof is established. This is a principle the people of knowledge have applied.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2455 -->

[Ruling on Vowing to a Saint and Its Consequences]

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

A woman vowed to give a sheep to a deceased saint every time she gave birth, whether to a boy or a girl. The Shaykh asked: “To whom does she give it?” The questioner replied: “To the walī.” The Shaykh asked: “And he is deceased?” The questioner said: “Yes, she slaughters [the sheep for him].”

She has already fulfilled two such vows and has two remaining. The sheep is given to someone referred to as khalīfah—a supposed representative of the deceased walī—who does with the sheep as he pleases: he may slaughter it for those present or sell it in the market and keep the proceeds.

The questioner asked:

Can her husband give her money to fulfill this vow, or should he refuse? It is worth noting that the wife holds firm to the belief that the deceased walī can cause benefit and harm. What is the ruling on the husband remaining with her in this state? He requested that the response be recorded if possible to share it with others who hold the same belief. If not, then a written answer is requested. He also asked for recommendations for recorded lectures addressing such issues. May Allah reward you and guide you to all that is good. Submitted by: Your brother, Sudanese by nationality.

Answer:

This question has two parts:

First: Does the husband have to give her money to fulfill this vow? We say: No, the husband is not obligated to give her anything to fulfill such a vow. In fact, it is not even permissible for him to do so. If she insists on the belief mentioned by the questioner—that this walī can bring benefit or harm—then she is a mushrikah, and it is not permissible for him to remain married to her. He must separate from her, for it is not lawful for a Muslim man to remain married to a polytheist woman.

Second: We say to this woman: your vow is invalid because it is a vow to commit a sin, and there is no vow in disobedience. She must offer the kaffārat yamīn (expiation for an oath) for this vow and repent to Allah from such beliefs. She must know that only Allah can bring benefit or harm.

Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—who is the greatest of all saints: {Say: “Indeed, I do not possess for you [the power of] harm or guidance.” Say: “No one can protect me from Allah, nor can I find any refuge besides Him.”} [Sūrat al-Jinn: 21–22]

Meaning: If Allah wills something for me, no one can shield me from it—so how could I shield others? If this applies to the Prophet ﷺ—then how much more so for those below him?

Therefore, we say: awliyāʾ cannot bring benefit or harm. Slaughtering animals in their name is shirk, which expels one from Islam. If she were to die holding this belief, she would be among the inhabitants of Hell. Allah said: {Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah—Allah has forbidden Paradise to him, and his abode is the Fire. And there are no helpers for the wrongdoers.} [Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 72]

So now tell the brother:

1. He must separate from her until she repents from this shirk. If she repents, she must offer expiation for her vow as a kaffārat yamīn.

2. He must admonish her and instill fear of Allah in her. He should tell her that her actions are major shirk, and if she dies upon it, she will die destined for Hell—may Allah protect us.

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

Question: What is the fate of a Muslim who fasts, prays, and gives zakāh, but believes in the awliyāʾ with the belief that in some Islamic countries is called a “good belief” — namely, that they can harm and benefit — and he also makes duʿāʾ to this walī, saying: “O so-and-so, you will have such-and-such if my son or daughter recovers,” or says, “By Allāh, O so-and-so.” What is the ruling on such statements, and what is the fate of such a Muslim?

Answer: "Calling this man — who vows to graves and awliyāʾ and calls upon them — a Muslim is ignorance on the part of the one naming him. In reality, he is not a Muslim, because he is a mushrik. Allāh the Most High said: “And your Lord said, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud for My worship will enter Hell humiliated.’” [Ghāfir: 60].

Duʿāʾ is only to Allāh alone, for He is the One who removes harm and brings benefit, as He said: “Is He [not best] who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth? Is there a deity with Allāh? Little do you remember.” [al-Naml: 62] So this person, even if he prays, fasts, and gives zakāh, if he calls upon other than Allāh, worships him, and vows to him, then he is a mushrik. Allāh has forbidden Paradise for him, and his abode is the Fire, and the wrongdoers will have no helpers."

[Fatāwā Nūr ʿalā al-Darb by Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ al-ʿUthaymīn 4/2]

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

(355) The questioner M.M.H. from ʿAmman, Jordan, says:

We have an imam in our mosque, a ḥāfiẓ of the Qur’ān, proficient in its recitation, and seemingly righteous. In addition to his regular observance of prayer, he fasts every other day. However, he regularly holds dhikr gatherings after ʿishā’, which extend late into the night. In them, they repeat certain phrases such as: “Maddad yā Sayyidī yā Rasūl Allāh” and “Maddad yā Sayyidī ʿAbd al-Qādir,” and similar invocations. Is this permissible and are they rewarded for it or not? Does this affect the validity of our prayer behind him? And if so, what should we do regarding our past prayers behind him?

He replied – may Allāh have mercy on him: In truth, what the questioner has mentioned is deeply saddening!

This imam—who has been described as maintaining prayer and fasting every other day, and whose outward appearance is one of uprightness—has been deceived by Shayṭān, leading him to exit Islām through shirk, whether he realizes it or not. Calling upon other than Allāh is major shirk (shirk akbar) that expels a person from the religion, whether he calls upon the Messenger ﷺ or anyone else. And anyone besides the Messenger has even less status and rank before Allāh than him. So if supplicating to the Messenger ﷺ is considered shirk, then doing so to others like ʿAbd al-Qādir—or anyone else—is even worse and more repugnant.

[Fatāwā Nūr ʿalā al-Darb by Ibn ʿUthaymīn 1/419]

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ al-ʿUthaymīn said:

His statement: “Except the One who created me” combines both negation and affirmation. The negation is: “I am disassociated from what you worship,” and the affirmation is: “Except the One who created me.” This indicates that tawḥīd is not complete except with disbelief in everything besides Allah and īmān in Allah alone. As Allah says: “Whoever disbelieves in al-ṭāghūt and believes in Allah has grasped the firmest handhold” [al-Baqarah: 256].

These people worship Allah and also worship others besides Him — because He said: “Except the One who created me.” The default assumption for exception is that it is connected unless there is evidence otherwise, and yet he [Ibrahim] still disassociated himself from them.

Likewise, in some Muslim countries, people pray, give zakāt, fast, and perform ḥajj, yet they go to graves, prostrate to them, and bow before them. They are kuffār, not muwaḥḥidīn (monotheists), and no deeds are accepted from them. This is among the gravest dangers facing Muslim societies — that disbelief in everything besides Allah is treated as insignificant. This stems from ignorance and negligence on the part of their scholars, because the common person only takes from his scholar. But some people — may Allah protect us — are scholars of the state, not scholars of the religion.

[al-Qawl al-Mufīd ʿalā Kitāb al-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn 1/150]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1562 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000215 -->

The Claim of Some Affected by the Murjiʾah Notion in Our Time That Prostrating to Something Other Than Allah, Such as Idols, for Worldly Reasons Does Not Constitute Kufr:

It has already been mentioned that there is a consensus among the Salaf that kufr can occur through actions just as it can through belief and speech. Whoever utters words of kufr commits kufr and is judged based on the apparent nature of what he has expressed, even if he claims that he did not intend to choose kufr. The same applies to actions—whoever performs an act of kufr, even if he claims it was for worldly reasons or similar motives, he is still judged accordingly. This is explicitly stated by Allah ﷻ in His Book:

Whoever disbelieves in [i.e., denies] Allāh after his belief except for one who is forced [to renounce his religion] while his heart is secure in faith. But those who [willingly] open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allāh, and for them is a great punishment; That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter and that Allāh does not guide the disbelieving people.

(An-Naḥl 106–107)

This serves as a refutation of certain self-proclaimed intellectuals who differentiate between prostrating to an idol and prostrating toward it. They claim that prostrating to an idol is unequivocal kufr that expels one from Islam, while prostrating toward it—meaning before it but not directed to it—is not kufr, in their view. They consider prostration before idols to be a matter requiring further clarification before judgment.

The origin of this statement lies in the doctrine of the Murjiʾah, who assert that there is no disbelief (kufr) except through belief. What led them to make this distinction is that prostration to an idol necessarily involves deliberate intent, purpose, and knowledge, thus they made the ruling of disbelief dependent on what is in the heart, i.e., the intent to disbelieve with knowledge and choice. As for prostration to it or in front of it, they argue that this could involve ignorance or lack of choice.

This is an innovated ideology and a heretical Irjaʾ, and if we were to accept it, we would not consider many clear acts of disbelief as kufr, under the pretense that they are open to interpretation.

Anyone who prostrates to an idol or before an idol without coercion is judged based on the outward appearance of his action, in accordance with the texts of the Qurʾān, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the scholars.

Such principles, which come from those influenced by the misconception of Irjaʾ in our time, are used to deceive Muslims, to undermine the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah, and to trivialize the causes of apostasy. These are among the most dangerous things in destroying the creed of the Salaf and destabilizing the beliefs and practices of Muslims.

The Shaykh Muhammad ibn Ṣāliḥ al-‘Uthaymīn, may Allah have mercy on him, said (in Sharḥ al-Arbaʿīn al-Nawawīyah p. 142-143):

“Then we say, what is the measure of disbelief? For some may view this as disbelief while others do not. Therefore, the Prophet ﷺ specified this by saying: ‘A clear disbelief, with no ambiguity, such as when you see him prostrating to an idol, or hear him curse Allah or His Messenger, or something similar.’

Thus, he, may Allah have mercy on him, explicitly stated that prostration to an idol is major disbelief (kufr akbar) and also included cursing Allah and His Messenger.

He رحمه الله , said: “Some students of knowledge today are confused and say: ’If you see someone who does not pray, do not declare him a disbeliever personally. How can we not declare him a disbeliever?!” They also say: ‘If you see someone prostrating to an idol, do not declare him a disbeliever personally, because perhaps his heart is at peace with faith!’ It is said: This is a great mistake. We judge by the apparent actions. If we find someone not praying, we say: This person is a disbeliever, openly and clearly.

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked: Is it permissible to declare a specific individual (muʿayyan) a disbeliever if he commits an act of kufr?

He replied:

If the conditions of takfīr are fulfilled in his case, then it is permissible to apply kufr to him specifically. If we did not allow for that, the description of apostasy (riddah) would not apply to anyone. Such a person is treated in this world as a murtadd — this applies to worldly rulings.

As for the rulings of the Hereafter, they are stated in general terms, not specifically. This is why Ahl al-Sunnah say: We do not testify that anyone is in Paradise or in Hellfire except those about whom the Prophet ﷺ testified specifically.

[Majmūʿ Fatāwā wa-Rasāʾil Faḍīlat al-Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ al-ʿUthaymīn 2/125]

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

Fatwa No. 376 – Ruling on an Imam Who Calls to Seeking Help from the Dead

Question: The questioner says: In our village, there is a mosque imām who calls people to seek help from other than Allah—from the dead—and believes this practice brings people closer to Allah. What is Islam’s ruling regarding this man? And what is the ruling on praying behind him?

Answer: This man who calls to istighāthah from other than Allah is a mushrik, a caller to shirk, and it is not valid for him to serve as an imām for the Muslims. Prayer behind him is invalid. He must repent to Allah – Exalted is He – before death overtakes him.

Istighāthah is only permissible with Allah alone. It may only be directed to a living person who is capable of saving the one calling for help from harm, such as in the verse: “So the one from his faction called for help against the one from his enemy.” (Al-Qaṣaṣ: 15) As for seeking help from the dead, this is shirk akbar that removes one from the fold of Islam.

And from this platform, I call upon this man to repent to Allah – Exalted is He – and to realize that istighāthah from the dead does not bring one closer to Allah. Rather, it distances a person from Him. Whoever seeks help from the dead falls under the ruling in the verse: “Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah – Allah has forbidden Paradise for him, and his abode is the Fire. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers.” (Al-Mā’idah: 72)

[Fatāwā Nūr ʿalā al-Darb by Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ al-ʿUthaymīn 1/444-445]

Shaykh Muqbil was asked:

Q: Is everyone who falls into major shirk while not knowing, or while being a mutaʾawwil (one acting based on interpretation), considered a mushrik who has exited the religion?

A: Shirk itself differs. The one who prostrates to an idol is considered a mushrik, committing Shirk al-Akbar, and this is up to Allah: if he was ignorant, then if Allah wills He excuses him, and if He wills He punishes him.

And we also say excuse due to ignorance (al-ʿudhr bil-jahl), but we judge him according to the outward of his action (i.e we call him a mushrik). And if the action was Shirk al-Akbar, such as vowing to other than Allah and slaughtering for other than Allah while he does not know, then we hope that Allah forgives him and excuses him due to his ignorance.

Source: [Official Muqbil ibn Hādī al-Wādiʿī fatwa](https://www.muqbel.net/fatwa.php?fatwa_id=3751).

Shaykh Zayd al-Madkhalī said:

In reality what is obligatory is precaution and serious effort so that the person does not fall into shirk al-aṣghar; because shirk al-akbar is clear: the directing of an ʿibādah to other than Allāh. But shirk al-aṣghar has forms; outward actions and inward actions, and the people are lenient regarding it.

So the Muslim person gives importance to protecting themselves from it, and the protection is attained by the bounty of Allāh and His aid, then by studying the types of Tawḥīd in a detailed manner, and by studying the types of Shirk in a detailed manner, so that he does not fall into a type from the types of shirk al-aṣghar while he does not know; otherwise he would be one who has fallen short in knowledge which Allāh made obligatory, and He made it individual obligation upon every mukallaf (morally responsible person).

So the mushrik is not excused in his shirk; for those who are excused are the common folk of the people in the fine details of subsidiary issues and rulings, but they are not excused in Tawḥīd and Shirk.

For this, look to Aṣḥāb al-Fatarāt (the people of didn’t receive the message) who were before the sending of the Prophet ﷺ; when they were upon shirk, Allāh did not excuse them; rather He tests them on Yawm al-Qiyāmah; so the obedient one is saved and the disobedient one perishes.

[Fatḥ wat-Tasdīd fī Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Zayd al-Madkhalī p.70]

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Luḥaidān said:

Q: Some people among us say: Whoever commits shirk al-akbar—such as making duʿāʾ to other than Allāh, or sacrificing and vowing to other than Allāh—is still considered a Muslim as long as he did that out of ignorance. Is this statement correct?

A: No, this is not correct. Did Allāh—glorified and exalted—excuse those who died upon shirk al-akbar on the basis that they were ignorant and that no messenger had previously come to them calling them? Can it be said that such a person is excused?

No. shirk al-akbar —there is no excuse for anyone in it. Either he repents, and repentance—praise be to Allāh—is accepted. Even if he committed shirk extensively and for a long time, then repented sincerely, Allāh would erase all of his shirk.

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Iftāʾ was asked:

Fatwa No. 17626

Question: What is the ruling on takfīr al-muʿayyan (declaring a specific individual to be a disbeliever)?

Answer: Whoever does an act, makes a statement, or holds a belief that necessitates kufr, is judged to be a kāfir and is to be treated as such — whether he is a specific individual or not — due to the generality of the evidences. For example, whoever supplicates to other than Allah, or slaughters for other than Allah, or utters words of kufr, such as insulting Allah or His Messenger, or mocking any aspect of the religion — then he is judged to be a kāfir and is to be asked to repent. If he repents, all is well; but if he does not, then it becomes obligatory upon the Muslim ruler to execute him as an apostate.

And with Allah is success. May peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muḥammad, his family, and his companions.

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Fatwa

President: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bāz

Member: Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān

Member: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Āl ash-Shaykh

Member: Bakr Abū Zayd

They were also asked:

Fatwa No. 17749

Question:

We, a group of students, have disagreed regarding the matter of establishing the ḥujjah (proof) upon the one who opposes the truth in matters of uṣūl ad-dīn (fundamentals of the religion). Some of us said that every ignorant person is excused due to ignorance in all matters, making no distinction between uṣūl (fundamentals) and furūʿ (branches), between the apparent and the hidden. Another group said that a person is excused by ignorance only in hidden matters, but not in the fundamentals — since there is no excuse for the one who commits shirk with Allah, Exalted is He, and worships others such as graves, stones, or trees.

They argued that no Muslim can be unaware of this, and that if one commits such acts, he is not a Muslim. However, in the hidden matters, ignorance is excused until the ḥujjah is established. What is the truth and correct opinion in this issue? Please give us a ruling, may Allah reward you.

Answer: The correct view is that no one is excused for ignorance regarding the uṣūl and principles (qawāʿid) of Islam — among those to whom the Qur’an has reached and to whom the Messenger ﷺ was sent — due to the statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “And this Qur’an has been revealed to me that I may warn you with it, and whomever it reaches.” [Surat al-Anʿām: 19] And His statement, Exalted is He: “This is a message for mankind so that they may be warned by it.” [Surat Ibrāhīm: 52] — and other verses with similar meaning.

As for masāʾil farʿiyyah (subsidiary issues) whose rulings may be obscure, one is excused in such matters due to ignorance until the ḥujjah is established upon him, as many aḥādīth have been reported in this regard. And with Allah is all success. May peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muḥammad, and upon his family and companions.

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Fatwa

President: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bāz

Member: Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān

Member: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Āl ash-Shaykh

Member: Bakr Abū Zayd

[Fatāwā Al-Lajnah Al-Dāʾimah 1/418-419]

Question 2 from Fatwā No. 4400:

Q: There are those who claim: Anyone who adheres to the message of Muḥammad ﷺ and prays facing the Qiblah, even if he prostrates to his shaykh, is not to be declared a disbeliever nor called a mushrik. Some even say that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb erred when he spoke about the eternity of the polytheists in Hell if they do not repent. They claim the polytheists in this ummah will be punished but will eventually enter Paradise, and that none from the ummah of Muḥammad will remain in Hell forever.

A: Everyone who believes in the message of our Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) and all that he brought in the Sharīʿah — if he then prostrates to other than Allāh, whether to a saint, a grave occupant, or a ṭarīqah shaykh — is considered a disbeliever, an apostate from Islam, and a mushrik who has associated others with Allāh in worship. This is the case even if he pronounces the two shahādahs at the time of his prostration, because his act contradicts his declaration.

However, he may be excused due to ignorance, so no punishment is enacted upon him until he is informed and the ḥujjah (proof) is established against him. He is to be given three days’ respite as a warning, in the hope that he repents. If he persists in prostrating to other than Allāh after clarification, he is to be executed for apostasy, as the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever changes his religion, kill him.” [Reported by al-Bukhārī from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما]

This clarification and establishment of the proof is to remove the excuse before punishment — not in order to call him a disbeliever only after the proof. He is already called a disbeliever because of what he has done — such as prostrating to other than Allāh, or making a vow, or sacrificing an animal for other than Allāh — and the Qur’ān and Sunnah have shown that whoever dies upon shirk will not be forgiven and will abide eternally in Hell, as Allāh says: “Indeed, Allāh does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.” [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 48]

And He says: “It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allāh while bearing witness against themselves of disbelief. For such their deeds are worthless, and in the Fire they shall abide forever.” [Sūrat al-Tawbah: 17] And Allāh is the source of success. May peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muḥammad, his family, and companions.

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Iftāʾ

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qaʿūd – Member

ʿAbd al-Razzāq ʿAfīfī – Deputy Head

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bāz – Chairman

[Fatāwā al-Lajnah al-Dāʾimah – al-Majmūʿah al-ʾŪlā 1/334-335]

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Iftāʾ was asked:

Question What is the ruling on meat sold in markets in countries where the people are not free from shirk, despite claiming to be Muslims, due to the prevalence of ignorance and bidʿah-based paths like the Tijāniyyah?

Answer : If the matter is as described in the question — that the slaughterer claims Islam, yet is known to be from a group that permits seeking help from other than Allah in matters that none can resolve except Allah, and they seek aid from the dead such as Prophets or those they believe to be awliyāʾ — then his slaughtered meat is like the meat of the mushrikūn who worshipped al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, Manāt, Wadd, Suwaʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, and Nasr. It is ḥarām for a true Muslim to eat such meat; it is considered maytah (carrion).

In fact, his condition is more severe than theirs because he has apostatized from the Islam he claims, due to his resorting to other than Allah in matters that only Allah can fulfill — such as guiding the lost, healing the sick, and other matters related to what is beyond normal causes, attributing these to the “mysteries” or “blessings” of the dead or to those absent who are treated like the dead.

These ignorant ones call upon them believing that they possess barakah (blessing) and certain attributes that enable them to hear the supplication of one who seeks their help — even if the caller is in the farthest East and the one being called upon is in the farthest West. Those from Ahl al-Sunnah living in such lands must advise them and guide them to pure tawḥīd. If they respond positively, then al-ḥamdu lillāh. But if they refuse after the truth has been made clear, then they have no excuse.

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Fatwā

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: Tell us about the virtue of monotheism (Tawḥīd). If someone unknowingly engages in major shirk throughout their life and dies upon it, are they excused due to ignorance? What is the criterion for ignorance that warrants an excuse?

A: The virtue of Tawḥīd is immense, as it removes a person from disbelief and shirk to the worship of Allāh alone. A Muslim who upholds Tawḥīd lives in the light of Allāh’s guidance, and every good deed they perform is rewarded. However, for a mushrik, no good deed is accepted or beneficial as long as they remain in shirk. This highlights the great virtue of Tawḥīd: it saves a person from Hell and grants them entry into Paradise on the Day of Judgment. In contrast, a mushrik is condemned to Hell, as Allāh says:

“Indeed, whoever associates others with Allāh, Allāh has forbidden him Paradise, and his abode will be the Fire. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers.” (Sūrat al-Mā’idah: 72)

After the Prophet ﷺ was sent, the Qur’ān was revealed, and the Sunnah was preserved, alongside the presence of scholars and widespread knowledge, ignorance has been eliminated—Alḥamdu lillāh. Anyone living among Muslims, reading the Qur’ān, listening to aḥādīth, sermons, lessons, and lectures cannot claim ignorance about shirk. Shirk is a manifest and clear matter that Allāh has strongly warned against.

Someone who lives among Muslims, hears the Qur’ān and the aḥādīth, listens to religious programs, and has access to Islamic knowledge has received the message, and the proof has been established against them. They are not excused for remaining ignorant or persisting in shirk regarding such an evident and fundamental issue.

However, a person who has lived entirely isolated from Muslims, never heard the Qur’ān, and had no access to Islamic knowledge—such a person may be excused due to ignorance, similar to those classified as Ahl al-Fatrah (people who lived in a time or place where the message did not reach them). Their fate is left to Allāh.

Nonetheless, such cases are extremely rare today, especially with the advancements in media and communication, which have spread Islam to the farthest corners of the world. Today, everyone has access to religious teachings. This is part of Allāh’s wisdom in establishing proof against His servants. In the past, Islam spread through daʿwah and jihād, but as these efforts declined, media became a means through which the message of Islam reached people everywhere.

Now, no one can claim ignorance about shirk, Tawḥīd, Paradise, or Hell. No one is unaware that zinā is forbidden, that shirk is prohibited, that ribā (usury) is ḥarām, that alcohol and intoxicants are forbidden, and that killing innocent lives is impermissible. These are clear and universally known prohibitions.

Thus, a person cannot claim ignorance about them. How long will they remain ignorant? They have every opportunity to ask, learn, and remove their ignorance. If they neglect this duty, they are to blame for their own shortcomings.

Source: [Official Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān fatwa](https://www.alfawzan.af.org.sa/ar/node/13595).

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message3100 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Among the questions that have reached us is what the questioner asks: “If someone commits al-shirk al-akbar out of ignorance, and he did that throughout his life and died upon it — is he excused due to ignorance? And what are the conditions for the excuse of ignorance?”

Answer: If he lived cut off from the Muslims, not hearing the Qur’an, nor anything about al-Islām, nor about al-shirk, then this remains his ruling until he dies: he is treated like Aṣḥāb al-Fatrah — those to whom the Qur’an did not reach, nor the call of the Messenger ﷺ. He is thus considered one of Aṣḥāb al-Fatrah.

The scholars have differed about their ruling, but the closest view — and Allah knows best — is that a prophet will be sent to them on Yawm al-Qiyāmah; whoever obeys him will enter al-Jannah, and whoever disobeys him will enter the fire. As for their ruling in this worldly life: if they died upon kufr disbelief and shirk, then they are to be treated as kuffār and mushrikūn — this is their worldly ruling. Their ruling in the Hereafter is left to Allāh ʿazza wa-jall.

But whoever lives among the Muslims, hears the Qur’an, listens to the aḥādīth, attends lectures and lessons — especially with the emergence of Qur’an radio stations and similar means — then the ḥujjah (proof) has been established upon him, and he is not excused due to ignorance.

Because Allāh jalla wa-ʿalā said to the Messenger ﷺ: “And this Qur’an has been revealed to me so that I may warn you with it and whomever it reaches.” (al-Anʿām: 19)

That is, whoever the Qur’an reaches, and he understands the Arabic language in which it was revealed — then the proof has been established against him, and he has no excuse, nor is he considered ignorant. The Qur’an is in Arabic, and it forbids shirk, forbids kufr, and warns that the mushrikūn will remain in the fire, and that they will not be forgiven.

So how could someone not know what shirk is, or not ask about it, or not investigate this immense danger? He is the one who is negligent — and thus, he is not excused by ignorance in al-umūr al-ẓāhirah (clear and apparent matters). As for al-umūr al-khafiyyah (subtle matters) that are only known to the scholars, if someone falls into one of these, he may be excused due to ignorance — until he asks the people of 'ilm.

Fatawa Date:  24 Jul 2024

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: When do we concern ourselves with the establishment of the ḥujjah upon a Muslim who falls into some acts of shirk? And do we say: ‘He is not declared a kāfir until the ḥujjah is established upon him’?

A: Firstly: calling him a Muslim while shirk occurs from him is incorrect. The one from whom shirk al-akbar occurs is not called a Muslim. We say: he is a mushrik. As for if the shirk is shirk aṣghar, such as swearing by other than Allah, or saying: ‘Were it not for Allah and you,’ and similar expressions of minor shirk, then this person is a Muslim.

But the one from whom major shirk occur, we do not say he is a Muslim. We say: he is a mushrik. And he is not excused due to ignorance if he lives among the Muslims, hears the Qurʾān, hears the aḥādīth, hears the speech of the people of knowledge, yet does not accept that and continues upon what he is upon. This person has no proof and no excuse. The ḥujjah has been established upon him.

Yes, and shirk is from the outwardly apparent matters; it is not from the hidden matters. Shirk is from the outwardly apparent matters: making duʿāʾ to other than Allah, sacrificing to other than Allah, making vows to other than Allah,  these are apparent matters, not hidden ones.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Question: May Allāh reward you with goodness. This questioner says: “O teacher of Tawḥīd, I ask you by Allāh to clarify for us the matter of al-ʿudhr bil-jahl?”

Answer: My brother, we have already explained this matter. Do you not understand? complaint is to Allāh.

We say: the one who is excused by ignorance is the one who has never heard anything of Islām, in a secluded place—he has not heard the Qurʾān, he has not heard the ḥadīth, the daʿwah has not reached him.

But a person who lives among Muslims, in the lands of the Muslims, hearing the adhān at every time, and seeing people pray to his right and left—can it be said that such a one is excused by ignorance? This is the one who is ignorant of himself; he does not want knowledge, he does not want the truth. Such a one is not excused. Yes.

Follow-up Question: If a person grew up in the desert, or is new to Islām—recently entered—would he be excused by ignorance if he supplicates other than Allāh while being affiliated with Islām?

Answer: The one who supplicates other than Allāh we judge him as a kāfir and treat him like the kuffār. As for if he is as described—that nothing has reached him—then his affair is with Allāh. But we, outwardly, judge him by the religion he is upon: kufr, shirk, worship of graves. If he has an excuse with Allāh, that is between him and Allāh. He would be among aṣḥāb al-fatrah (those who lived in a period where the message did not reach them). Yes.

But today, as you know, nothing is hidden. Media is widespread. The Qurʾān is heard everywhere in the world now. The Sunnah is heard, the duʿāt are speaking. Islām is widespread—there is hardly a country on earth that Islām has not entered, is there or not? There is no country without masājid, no country without Islamic centers, no country without Muslim minorities. Islām is widespread now, and its rituals are practiced even in the lands of disbelief. The proof has been established, and to Allāh belongs all praise. Yes.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Questioner:

May Allah be good to you, noble Shaykh. This questioner says: “Does the one who falls into shirk out of ignorance enter under the statement of Allah, ‘Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him’?”

Answer: If he is ignorant, and no daʿwah has reached him, and the call of any messenger from among the messengers has not reached him—he is living in isolation from the world—then his matter is with Allah. His matter is with Allah. He is considered from Ahl al-Fatrah, and his matter is with Allah. That is in regard to the Hereafter. As for us, we treat him with the treatment of the mushrikīn—in his funeral, in inheritance—we treat him with the treatment of the mushrikīn. But what is between him and Allah—we do not interfere in that.

Questioner: May Allah grant you success, the questioner says: “If I see a person committing acts of shirk, such as supplicating to the dead or seeking shafāʿah (intercession) from them—how do I treat him? As a Muslim or as a kāfir?”

Shaykh: You treat him as a mushrik. You hear him committing shirk, calling upon other than Allah—do you treat him as a Muslim? No, treat him with the treatment of the mushrik. But call him to Islam. Clarify to him that this is shirk akbar (major shirk), and clarify the danger of shirk. The gate of daʿwah to Allah and sincere advice remains open.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said:

With an ṣaḥīḥ chain from Qatādah: ‘partners in His obedience, not in His worship.’ And shirk in obedience is minor shirk which does not take one out of the religion, especially since the two of them did not do this intending that meaning; rather, they did it out of love for the child and for his safety only. Yet despite that, Allāh called it shirk, so it is shirk even if a person does not intend it.

So this indicates that whoever speaks with shirk or does shirk is called a mushrik, even if he did not intend it or have it as his intention. Thus it is judged upon him that this action of his is shirk, whether it is from minor shirk or major shirk.

And for this reason, the Messenger ﷺ said to the one who said to him: ‘What Allāh wills and you will’: ‘Have you made me a rival to Allāh?’—even though the speaker did not intend to make a rival for Allāh. However, this wording is not permissible, so it is shirk even if he did not intend it—so how then if he did intend it?

So in this is a refutation against the one who says that whoever says a statement of shirk or does shirk is not judged to be a mushrik until he believes it in his heart, as is the saying of the Murjiʾah of this era.

[Iʿānat al-Mustafīd bi-Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān 2/275]

Are the statements of udhr bil jahl, general or do they apply to specific individuals?

Shaykh al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: What do you say about one who claims, among contemporaries, that declaring takfīr of a specific individual from among the grave worshippers is a matter of disagreement, and he claims that they are not kuffār aṣliyyīn (original disbelievers)?

A: This is a corrupt statement, the consequence of which is ignorance in this matter.

And I say, and I repeat, that it is not permissible for anyone to speak in these dangerous matters except after he learns, gains clear understanding, and studies ʿaqīdah — a sound study— upon the people of knowledge.

Then after that, if the situation compels him to speak, he speaks; and if he is not compelled to this, then he should not enter into it. This is what I say and repeat: that this matter is extremely dangerous

Whoever commits shirk, commits shirk, and judgment of shirk is passed upon him. And whoever commits kufr, the judgment of kufr is passed upon him according to what appears to us, and we apply to him the rulings of kuffār.

So if he dies, we do not bury him in Muslim graveyards, and his relatives who are Muslims do not inherit from him. The rulings of the kuffār are applied to him by virtue of his action — by virtue of his action and his statement.

This is what we have been commanded with. We have nothing except outward appearance. We judge based on what is apparent.

As for what is between him and Allah, then Allah is  more seeing and knowing regarding them; if he is excused, Allah knows that he is excused — then his affair is left to Allah. We do not judge the hearts; rather, we judge what appears to us.

So whoever manifests kufr and shirk, we judge him with kufr and shirk, and we apply to him the rulings of shirk and the rulings of kufr— whether he is specific individual or not.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1484 -->

Sheikh Ṣāliḥ ibn Fawzān said:

“The second type: Apostasy ( kufr ridda ) from the religion of Islam. This occurs when a person who was Muslim commits one of the nullifiers ( nawāqiḍ ) of Islam, thereby leaving the religion and becoming an apostate ( murtadd ). Such a person is considered a disbeliever due to apostasy.

The nullifiers of Islam are well known and defined by scholars. Among them: whoever associates partners with Allah ( shirk ), calls upon other than Allah, seeks aid from other than Him, or offers sacrifice to other than Him— such a person is deemed an apostate from Islam because he has committed major shirk, even if he continues to profess the shahādatayn .

Likewise, among the nullifiers of Islam is reviling Allah or His Messenger, or mocking anything from the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of the Messenger. Whoever mocks Allah, His Book, His Messenger, or His Sunnah becomes a disbeliever—whether doing so seriously or in jest—based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

“ If you question them, they will certainly say, “We were only talking idly and joking around.” Say, “Was it Allah, His revelations, and His Messenger that you ridiculed? Make no excuses! You have lost faith after your belief. (Surah At-Tawbah: 65-66)”

“So what was the statement they uttered? They said: ‘We have never seen people like our reciters—more lying tongues, more gluttonous stomachs, and more cowardice in battle.’ They were referring to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions. Thus, Allah revealed their disbelief in His Book in a verse that will be recited until the Day of Judgment, as a warning to Muslims against falling into such actions.

Likewise, learning or teaching sorcery ( siḥr ) is disbelief in Allah. Claiming knowledge of the unseen through divination ( kihāna ), magic, astrology, or fortune-telling is also disbelief that expels one from the religion. This is what is judged as kufr .

Similarly, if a person declares ḥalāl (permissible) something that has been unanimously agreed upon as ḥarām (forbidden), or vice versa, they commit disbelief. The same ruling applies to denying any essential matter of the religion that is known by necessity—such as rejecting the obligation of prayer, zakāh , fasting, or ḥajj . In such cases, the person is judged as a disbeliever.”

“As for the one who has not committed a nullifier ( nāqiḍ ) of Islam, he is not judged as a disbeliever. Even if he commits a major sin ( kabīrah ), he is deemed sinful ( fāsiq ), but not a disbeliever. If he commits an error, a sin, or a violation, he is described as mistaken, disobedient, or something similar—according to what he has done. Justice requires that we weigh matters by their proper shar‘ī standards and not label every person who commits a violation or a sin as a disbeliever.

For example, if someone consumes ribā (usury), we judge him as a fāsiq who has committed a major sin. However, if he deems ribā permissible—meaning he says it is ḥalāl —then we say he is a disbeliever because he has declared lawful what is unanimously agreed upon as forbidden. But if he consumes it without believing it to be ḥalāl , he is a fāsiq and does not leave the fold of Islam; rather, he is treated as a sinful believer.”

[Ẓāhirat al-Tabdīʿ wat-Tafsiq wat-Takfīr wa Ḍawābiṭuhā - al-Sheikh Ṣāliḥ ibn Fawzān p.22-24]

Shaykh al-Fawzān said regarding the statement:

“And the servant does not exit from īmān except by denying that which caused him to enter into it.”

This statement contains an objection, because restricting kufr to denial (juḥūd) is the madhhab of the Murjiʾah. The nullifiers of Islam are many: among them is juḥūd, among them is associating partners with Allah, among them is mocking the religion or anything from it—even without denial—and they are many nullifiers mentioned by the scholars and jurists in the chapters of apostasy. Among them also is making the unlawful, lawful and making the lawful, unlawful.

Shaykh al-Islām Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb mentioned ten of them, and they are the most important, otherwise the nullifiers are many. So restricting the nullifiers of Islam to denial alone is an error.

Some of the mutaʿālimūn (pseudo-scholars) today try to promote this madhhab so that people become lenient in the religion. As long as he has not denied, then according to them he is a Muslim: even if he prostrates to an idol and says, “I did not deny, and I affirm tawḥīd—it is only a sin from the sins.” Or if he sacrifices to other than Allah, or reviles Allah, or reviles the Messenger, or reviles the religion—they say: this is a Muslim because he did not deny.

This is a great error, and it completely destroys the religion, leaving no religion remaining. So it is obligatory to beware of this great danger.

[At-Taʿlīqāt al-Mukhtaṣarah ʿalā Matn al-ʿAqīdah aṭ-Ṭaḥāwiyyah p.144]

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Question:

May Allah bless you, esteemed scholar. A questioner asks: Is this statement a view of the people of Sunnah, that every action or statement that causes the person to be declared a disbeliever (kafir) is only because it indicates disbelief in the heart?

Answer:

This is not what the people of Sunnah and the Jamāʿah have said. They do not say this. We rule based on what is apparent. We have no knowledge of the unseen, only the visible. So, if someone commits shirk by saying or doing something openly, such as slaughtering for other than Allah, making vows to other than Allah, or prostrating to other than Allah, we declare them a disbeliever based on their actions. If they speak words of disbelief, we judge them as disbelievers based on their words. We do not judge what is in the heart. Likewise, if someone accepts Islam and outwardly demonstrates Islam, we judge them as Muslim based on their appearance. We only judge by outward appearances, not by what is hidden.

Source: [Official Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān fatwa](https://alfawzan.af.org.sa/ar/node/9646).

Shaykh al-Fawzān was asked:

Question: What is the criterion for declaring a specific individual to be a disbeliever (takfīr al-muʿayyan)? Some say: “Do not declare a specific person to be a Jew, for example, until it is confirmed to us that what he has done constitutes disbelief.”

Fatawa of Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān

The Host said:

If you say: “Those who hold beliefs about the dead don’t know that what they are doing is shirk. In fact, if one of them were faced with the sword, he would not admit that he is a mushrik or that he committed something that constitutes shirk. If he knew even the least bit that this was shirk, he would not have done it.”

I say: Yes, what you said is true. However, it should not be hidden from you what has been established in the chapter on riddah — that its occurrence does not require knowledge. Whoever makes a kufr-based statement or commits an act of kufr, the ruling applies to him.

In any case, it is obligatory on everyone who becomes aware of these statements or actions—performed by those who venerate the dead—to convey to them the ḥujjah sharʿiyyah, and to clarify what Allah commanded to be clarified, and what He took a covenant upon the people of knowledge to convey.

The Shaykh says:

This does not mean they are excused in their ignorance—because shirk is not obscure, and neither is tawḥīd. The issue is due to their turning away and blind taqlīd, which caused their vision to become blind.

They believe these things are not to be abandoned, and once someone clings to something and sees it as important, they won’t give attention to anything opposing it. If you were to debate them or speak to them, most would not accept it. This is the norm—not that none of them ever returns, for many who are invited and addressed do return to the truth through daʿwah.

Still, we say: this is not an excuse for them. They are not excused in shirk just because they say “We didn’t know this was shirk” or “We didn’t know the meaning of Lā ilāha illa Allāh” or “We didn’t understand the meaning of worship.” These are clear matters. Their ignorance stems from negligence and deliberate turning away, so the blame is upon them, and establishing the ḥujjah for Allah’s sake is required at all times. Arguments must be presented.

As for takfīr, that is another matter. Declaring a specific individual a kāfir can only be done after establishing a personal ḥujjah upon him, and removing the doubts he clings to. After that, judgment is passed. But before that, it is impermissible. Even so, it does not prevent one from saying he is a mushrik, even if we do not declare takfīr that removes him from the religion just based on the action. He may be ignorant—and that’s common among those who fall into this. So there is no necessary link between takfīr and a person being a disbeliever in Allah’s sight, since Allah did not provide mankind with excuses after giving them intellects and abundant signs in His creation.

The essential matter is attachment to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. Allah has removed all excuses by sending down His Book and His Messenger. So if someone says, “I’m ignorant,” it is said to him: You turned away from what was wājib upon you—seeking the truth—and you didn’t search for it. You are accountable for this. No one is going to come to your home saying, “This is the word of Allah, this is what the Prophet said.” This responsibility lies with you. As long as you know there is a Book from Allah and a Messenger, it is wājib upon you to seek what Allah has obligated. If you turn away, the blame is upon you. You are not excused by your ignorance. This is not a case where ignorance is an excuse.

Shaykh ʿAbdullāh Al-Ghunaymān said:

Now, among the problems that people are facing today is that there are students of knowledge and shaykhs who say that if a mushrik performs ṭawāf around a grave, and worships the occupant of the grave, but is ignorant, then we do not call him a mushrik.

Rather, we call him a Muslim. And they say: his action is shirk, but he himself is not a mushrik. This is a strange matter. They say: his action is shirk, yet he is not a mushrik; rather, he is a Muslim. And if he dies upon that, he is in Paradise, because he is excused—excused in his ṭawāf around the grave and in his ʿibādah of it.

This is what the shaykh says: that this is something not known among the earlier generations nor the later ones. It is something uttered only by ignorant scholars—may Allāh grant safety. Meaning: ignorance has taken firm hold in their hearts, and they have become people who do not accept the truth. They argue about such matters.

Then regarding someone like this: does the statement of the shaykh apply to him—his saying, “Whoever does not declare the kāfir to be a kāfir is himself a kāfir”? Because this is shirk and kufr against Allāh, exalted and majestic, and yet he did not declare him a kāfir; rather, he judged him to be a Muslim.

Meaning: as for people like these, the existence of doubts must be removed before judging them to be disbelievers. But we say: this is ignorance—ignorance that no one preceded them in. If a mushrik falls into shirk, then he is a mushrik. Shirk does not exist independently such that the action is called shirk while its doer is called a Muslim. A person is held accountable for what he does.

<div class="video-source" data-origin="telegram-attachment">
<video class="source-video" controls preload="metadata" src="assets/videos/dar-messages5-4278.mp4"></video>

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4347 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000265 -->

Shaykh ʿAbdullāh Al-Ghunaymān said:

The meaning of the verse is that Allāh informed that He does not forgive the mushrik. Therefore, since shirk is unforgivable, it becomes obligatory for the servant to research its types, causes, and means, and to avoid them so that he does not fall into it unknowingly.

Many people, including the intelligent and even scholars, have fallen into shirk al-akbar because of ignorance, carelessness, and leniency, as is still occurring in many Muslim lands. People go to graves, ask their occupants, and think this is not shirk, but rather permissible tawassul. This is among the calamities.

Shirk that Allāh does not forgive may, in some cases, be treated by some people as an act of obedience to draw near to Allāh but the verse indicates that sins other than shirk do not render a Muslim a kāfir.

The verse also shows that if a mushrik dies upon his shirk, he is not forgiven. However, if he repents, Allāh may accept his repentance if He wills. Confidence in Allāh and hope in His acceptance is encouraged; He rejoices most at the repentance of the one who turns back.

Allāh does not benefit from the obedience of the obedient nor from the repentance of the repentant, for He is self-sufficient over all else. Yet, due to His generosity and bounty, He does not wish to punish His servants, and when a servant repents, He rejoices.

This is why Allāh sent the messengers and revealed the books, so that no one has an excuse before Him. The sending of the messengers and revelation of the books is sufficient as guidance. Allāh has given humans reason and thought to discern benefit; thus, if a person  knows that the Messenger came with the truth and guidance from Allāh, it is obligatory for him to seek what the Messenger ﷺ brought.

If he does not, he is blameworthy, and the proof stands against him. There is no excuse for saying, “I was ignorant and did not know,” because that will not help him. Once he knows that Allāh sent His Messenger and revealed His Book, it is incumbent upon him to seek the truth himself.

[Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh ʿAbdullāh al-Ghunaymān 1/157-158]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1876 -->

Sheikh ar-Rājiḥī said:

Q: Is a person ignorant of Tawḥīd excused for their ignorance regarding the matter of invoking others besides Allah and worshiping graves?

A: Such a person is not excused for their ignorance. Allah says: “And We never punish until We have sent a messenger.” (Al-Isrā’: 15). The messenger has been sent, and Allah also says: “And it has been revealed to me that this Qur’an is to warn you thereby, and whomever it reaches.” (Al-An‘ām: 19). Thus, whoever receives the Qur’an has had the evidence established against them.

The excuse for ignorance applies only to those of the Fatrah (the time before the sending of the messenger), but after the messenger was sent, there is no excuse. The messenger was sent with the message of Tawḥīd and the Qur’an, calling to the Oneness of Allah and prohibiting shirk. Therefore, no one has an excuse regarding this issue.

However, a person may be excused in matters that are subtle or obscure, which are not clear to them, similar to the people of Fatrah who never heard the Qur’an.

Source: [ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī, *Sharḥ Kitāb al-Sunnah*](https://shamela.ws/book/35083/148).

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3493 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000268 -->

Question to Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī:

“May Allah be good to you, our virtuous shaykh. In the matter of al-ʿudhr bil-jahl, here among us there are those who worship graves and seek help from them. Is this an excuse for them?”

Answer: “It is not an excuse. The one who makes ṭawāf around graves, worships graves, and calls upon them besides Allah is not excused, while living among Muslims after the Qurʾān has been revealed. Allah the Exalted says: ‘And We never punish until We have sent a messenger’ [al-Isrāʾ 17:15]. And indeed, the Messenger ﷺ has been sent. And He says: ‘This Qurʾān has been revealed to me so that I may warn you by it, and whomever it reaches’ [al-Anʿām 6:19]. Whoever the Qurʾān reaches, the proof has been established against him.

The one excused is the ignorant person in fine, hidden matters that someone like him may not know. But as for clear matters, which Allah revealed the Qurʾān concerning, then a person is not excused to commit shirk with Allah or worship graves. Nor is he excused not to ask about what confuses him. If he wants to buy a car or a house, he asks and consults people of expertise—yet when it comes to his religion, he does not ask! This is the very matter for which Allah sent His Prophet ﷺ. He is not excused now, while the Qurʾān is being recited. As for one who claims he has not heard the Qurʾān, turns away, pretends to be blind and deaf, rejects those who advise him and call him to tawḥīd, then says: ‘I am excused’—he is not excused. Excuse only applies in subtle, hidden issues that someone like him may genuinely not know.”

Another Question:

“We want from your excellency a detailed explanation of al-ʿudhr bil-jahl in matters of ʿaqīdah.”

Answer: “The correct view is that a person is not excused in clear, obvious matters. Someone who lives among Muslims, then commits shirk with Allah, or deals in ribā—and then it is said: ‘He is excused’—no, he is not excused.

But if it is a subtle, hidden matter that someone like him may not know, then he is excused. For example, a man converts to Islam in America, in a society that deals in ribā. He becomes Muslim and then deals in ribā. If asked: ‘Why did you do this?’ he says: ‘I did not know, I was ignorant.’ This is indeed true, and he is excused. But someone who lives among Muslims and deals in ribā, and when asked why, says: ‘Because I was ignorant’—this is not accepted from him. The closer and stronger position is that excuse is only in subtle, hidden matters that someone like him may not know.”
