<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2654 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000269 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī was asked:

“Is the one who performs ṭawāf around graves or commits acts of shirk out of ignorance—meaning he does not know that what he is doing is shirk—to be excused? Please provide detail.

The Shaykh said: "The scholars have 2 opinions on this after the mission/prohethood (بعثة) of Prophet ﷺ — Ahl Al-Fiṭrah after the prophethood/mission of Prophet ﷺ, regarding them their is a scholarly discussion.

But after the Prophet ﷺ was sent and the Qur’ān was revealed—Allah says: “And We never punish until We have sent a messenger”—and indeed Allah has sent the Messenger and revealed the Qur’ān.

So is the mushrik excused if the matter has been confused for him—if he was performing ṭawāf around graves and calling upon them—and he did not perceive the truth, nor recognize it, because of the deception of corrupt scholars who distort things for him and beautify shirk in his eyes?

Some scholars have said he is excused in such a case, but he is treated in this world as a mushrik: he is not washed, not prayed over, not buried among Muslims, and no pilgrimage is performed on his behalf, nor is mercy invoked for him. In the Hereafter, his matter is left to Allah.

This is the position adopted by Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله. He said that no one is declared a kāfir until the ḥujjah (proof) is established against him.

Other scholars said no one is excused after the Prophet ﷺ, because Allah says: “And We never punish until We have sent a messenger”—and the Messenger has been sent and the Qur’ān revealed, and the Qur’ān is recited and the texts are clear regarding the prohibition of shirk. Therefore, they are not excused. These are two views held by scholars.

In any case, those who say he is excused also say that in this world he is treated as a mushrik: he is not washed, not prayed over, not buried in the Muslim cemeteries, pilgrimage is not performed for him, and mercy is not invoked for him. As for the Hereafter, his matter is with Allah.

Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah رحمه الله said a profound statement. He said:

There are two types of shirk: greater and lesser. Whoever is free from both dies upon tawḥīd. Whoever is free from both dies upon tawḥīd and enters Paradise. Whoever is free from the greater enters Paradise.

Whoever dies upon the greater shirk enters the Fire. And whoever dies upon the lesser shirk—if his good deeds outweigh his bad—enters Paradise. That is because of the abundance of tawḥīd alongside a small amount of shirk. But if his bad deeds outweigh his good, he will be punished for this lesser shirk. Shirk is accounted for whether it is greater or if it is extensive in amount.

If it is small in comparison to much sincerity, this is the view of Shaykh al-Islām رحمه الله: shirk is held accountable in both of its forms—greater and abundant in quantity. If someone dies upon greater shirk, he dies from among the people of the Fire.

As for lesser shirk, it depends on whether his good deeds outweigh the bad or the opposite. If the bad deeds outweigh, then his good deeds are nullified and shirk overcomes them. But if the good deeds, especially tawḥīd, are abundant, they may outweigh the shirk.”

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2635 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī was asked:

Question: Is a person excused due to ignorance if he performs acts of shirk, such as circumambulating a grave, without knowing that what he is doing is shirk against Allah Almighty?

Answer: Those who committed such acts before the sending of the Prophet ﷺ are referred to as Ahl al-Fatrah (people of the interval between prophets), and there is scholarly discussion concerning them. As for after the sending of the Prophet ﷺ and the revelation of the Qur’ān, Allah says: “And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger.” [al-Isrāʾ: 15]

So, Allah has sent the Messenger and revealed the Qur’ān. Is the mushrik then excused if he is misled into believing that circumambulating graves, invoking them besides Allah, or sacrificing to them is permissible, due to the deception of evil scholars who disguise and beautify shirk for him—so much so that the truth becomes obscured and he no longer recognizes it? Some scholars have said: Yes, he may be excused in such a case, but he is treated in this world like a mushrik—i.e., he is not washed, not prayed over, and not buried in Muslim cemeteries—just as Ahl al-Fatrah are treated.

This view was adopted by Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, may Allah have mercy on him, who said:

“We do not declare anyone a disbeliever until the proof has been established upon him.” Other scholars, however, held that no one is excused after the sending of the Messenger ﷺ, since Allah says: “And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger.”, and indeed, the Messenger has been sent, and the Qur’ān has been revealed and is recited. Its texts are clear in warning against shirk and in defining it. Therefore, they are not excused.

These two positions are both attributed to the scholars, and were mentioned by Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah and others. May Allah grant everyone success in obeying Him, bless all with righteous deeds and beneficial knowledge, and may peace and blessings be upon Muḥammad, his family, and his companions.

Source: [ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī, source text in Shamela](https://shamela.ws/book/37010/193).

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Āl al-Shaykh was asked:

Q: Whoever worships other than Allāh, such as the one who supplicates to and sacrifices for the awliyāʾ, is it said that he is excused due to his ignorance and that the proof must first be established against him?

A: His action is kufr without doubt. His worship of other than Allāh, his supplication to other than Allāh, is kufr. So we say: this action of his is kufr, and by it he is a disbeliever.

As for the matter of the Hereafter—whether the proof was established against him or whether the message reached him—that is a matter with Allāh, Who has knowledge of it.

But in this worldly life, we deal with him as a mushrik disbeliever. We judge that his action is disbelief and that he, in his very person, is a disbeliever. However, his final outcome is left to Allāh. We hold the belief that whoever meets Allāh as a polytheist, then the Fire will be his abode, because Allāh says: “Indeed, whoever associates others with Allāh – Allāh has forbidden him Paradise” (Al-Māʾidah: 72).

But Allāh knows best the state of His servants on the Day of Resurrection.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āsh-Shaykh said:

This is an issue in which the scholars have differed. The aʾimmah of the Daʿwah — may Allah have mercy on them — said: Merely hearing about the call of Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb is not sufficient — except in the Arabian Peninsula (al-jazīrah) — because during their time, the Daʿwah had spread, the conquests had occurred, and it had been clarified to the people throughout the region.

As for other lands, if someone had not heard of the Daʿwah, then the ḥujjah must be established. Here arises the question: If the ḥujjah has not been established, are the grave worshippers to be declared kuffār or not?

The answer: Yes. Whoever commits shirk is a mushrik, specifically major shirk. Whoever is guilty of it is a mushrik. The establishment of the ḥujjah is a condition only for the obligation of punishment. Just as we call the Jews and Christians kuffār, even if they have never heard of the Prophet ﷺ, likewise those who worship idols or graves and similar things — whoever commits shirk is a mushrik, and the rulings of the mushrik apply to him in this world.

As for the Hereafter, if the ḥujjah has not been established, then he is not definitively judged to be among the people of Hell. Rather, his affair is suspended until the ḥujjah is established before Allah. Thus, a distinction must be made between conditioning for the punishment and refraining from calling someone a mushrik.

Whoever commits major shirk is a mushrik, and the worldly consequences follow: one does not seek forgiveness for him, his slaughtered animals are not lawful to eat, one does not offer sacrifices on his behalf, and other similar rulings. However, judging him to be a kāfir inwardly and outwardly is suspended until the ḥujjah is established. If the ḥujjah is not established, his matter is left to Allah. This is the clarification of the statements of the scholars on this issue — a well-known and precise matter — known as the issue of ʿudhr bil jahl.

[al-Ajwibah wa-al-Buḥūth wa-al-Mudārasāt al-Mushtamilah ʿalayhā al-Durūs al-ʿIlmiyyah 1/41-42]

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āsh-Shaykh said:

And once this has been established, we come to the matter in which most people today have fallen — ignorance of this matter. This relates to judging the current reality, and is tied to what we discussed earlier concerning the foundational principles: that kufr can arise from turning away and ignorance, or from arrogance and prideful rejection.

As for the practical side — judging people in reality — then whoever commits shirk is to be called a mushrik, whether he is knowledgeable or ignorant. However, the ruling of kufr applied to him varies.

If the prophetic proof is established upon him — meaning by someone knowledgeable and skilled in delivering it, to remove the doubts and make him understand the bounds of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger concerning tawḥīd and the clarification of shirk — and despite that, he rejects it after the proof has been made clear, then he is to be considered a kāfir both outwardly and inwardly.

As for the one who turns away, he is treated outwardly as a disbeliever, but inwardly we do not pass judgment of internal kufr upon him until the proof is established. This is because it is a well-known principle among the scholars that:

Whoever commits zinā, he is a zānī, but he may or may not be held accountable. If he knows that zinā is ḥarām and commits it, then he is held accountable. But if he is a new Muslim and commits zinā not knowing it is prohibited, the name “zinā” still applies, but he is not held accountable due to his ignorance.

This is how we reconcile the various statements reported in this area of belief.

[Sharḥ Kashf ash-Shubuhāt by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āsh-Shaykh p.136]

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āl ash-Shaykh said:

Here, if the ḥujjah (proof) has not been established, are the grave-worshippers takfired or not? The answer: yes, whoever commits shirk, then he is a mushrik; shirk al-akbar, whoever commits it is a mushrik. Establishing the ḥujjah is only a condition for the obligation of punishment. Just as the Jews and Christians, we call them kuffār; they are kuffār, even if they never heard of the Prophet ﷺ at all. Likewise the people of idols and graves and the like: whoever commits shirk is a mushrik, and the rulings of the mushrikīn apply to him in the wordly ruling.

As for if the ḥujjah has not been established upon him, then it is not decisively stated that he is in the Fire if he dies; rather, his matter is suspended until the ḥujjah is established upon him before Allah. So there is a difference between making the establishment of the ḥujjah a condition, and refraining from judging shirk: whoever commits shirk al-akbar is a mushrik, and the worldly rulings follow from that—such as not seeking forgiveness for him, his slaughter not being eaten, not offering sacrifice on his behalf, and the like.

As for judging him with kufr outwardly and inwardly, then this is suspended until the ḥujjah is established upon him; and if it is not established upon him, then his affair is with Allah. This is the precise verification of the speech of Ahl al-ʿilm in this issue, and it is a well-known and subtle matter.

Q: As for the last question, we conclude with it. It says: those who perform ṭawāf around graves or fall into some forms of shirk—do we treat them as kuffār, or are they excused due to ignorance?

Sheikh Ṣāliḥ Ibn Muḥammad as-Suwaiḥ said:

The Sixth Issue: The Statement of Some Affected by the Doubts of Irjāʾ in Our Era Regarding Excusing the Grave Worshippers Due to Ignorance

The statements of the great scholars have already been cited in sufficient detail to clarify this matter. The people of Irjāʾ have used caution in takfīr as a pretext to excuse those who worship at graves. Furthermore, they have gone even further by labeling those who declare grave worshippers to be disbelievers as Khārijites!

And we say: Glory be to You! This is a great slander. The distinction between declaring Muslims as disbelievers and declaring idol worshippers as disbelievers is clear and evident. The former is the path and approach of the Khārijites, while the latter is the path and methodology of the Salaf.

Issue Seven: The Extremism of Some Who Have Been Affected by the Misconception of Irjāʾ in Our Time Regarding the Understanding of the Proof

Some individuals, influenced by the misconception of Irjāʾ, have gone to extremes in the issue of understanding the proof. You find some of them excessively excusing grave worshippers, defending them and arguing that polytheists should not be declared disbelievers even if the Qurʾān has reached them and even if they understand the truth. They say:

“Sufficient understanding is the one that removes any excuse from a person for not accepting knowledge, by eliminating the obstructing doubt. But if some level of understanding occurs without removing the doubt, then the intended goal of convincing the individual with the knowledge has not been achieved.”

Reflecting upon this statement is enough to refute and invalidate it. How much more so when the texts of the Qurʾān and Sunnah, as well as the consensus of the Salaf, clearly indicate that this claim is among the most corrupt, misguided, and farthest from the truth!

[Al-Furūq bayna ʿAqīdat al-Salaf wa ʿAqīdat al-Murjiʾah fī al-Īmān by Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad al-Suwaiḥ p.161-162]

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Suwayyiḥ said:

The scholars have unanimously agreed that whoever equates Islam with any other religion, or permits practicing a religion other than Islam, is a kāfir who has left Islam. His kufr is known necessarily from the religion. Such a call is an atheistic, kufr-based call that nullifies Islam, as proven by the Qurʾān, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the scholars. Allah the Exalted has declared kāfir those who worship anyone besides Him and do not believe in His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, even if they were upon a religion that originally had some truth, such as one who prays, fasts, and performs ḥajj, and says “lā ilāha illā Allāh,” yet worships graves and shrines.

There is no religion except Islam, and no law accepted by Allah except that which He revealed to His Messenger, with whom He sealed the messages and abrogated all previous religions. Whoever does not submit to Allah is a kāfir, whose enmity is evident and clear, and there can be no reconciliation between him and the Muslims except with tawḥīd. The kufr of those devoted to graves, and of whoever does not follow Islam, is known by necessity from the religion. It is obligatory to show enmity toward him, to disassociate from him, and to declare him kāfir, as indicated by the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the scholars.

Allah the Exalted says: “Indeed they have disbelieved who say, ‘Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary.’” [al-Māʾidah 5:17]

And He says: “They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘Allah is the third of three.’ But there is no deity except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment.” [al-Māʾidah 5:73]

And He says: “They say, ‘Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided.’ Say, ‘Rather, the religion of Ibrāhīm, inclining to truth; and he was not of the polytheists.’” [al-Baqarah 2:135]

And He says: “Never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their way. Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the only guidance.’ If you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have no protector or helper against Allah.” [al-Baqarah 2:120]

And He says: “Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam.” [Āl ʿImrān 3:19]

And He says: “Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter.” [Āl ʿImrān 3:85]

And He says: “The religion of your father Ibrāhīm. It is He who named you Muslims.” [al-Ḥajj 22:78]

And He says: “You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. Those—He has written faith in their hearts and supported them with a spirit from Him. And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. They are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah—they will be successful.” [al-Mujādilah 58:22]

And He says: “O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection, while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, driving out the Messenger and yourselves only because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have come out for jihād in My cause and seeking My approval, you confide affection to them, but I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the straight path. If they gain dominance over you, they would be your enemies and extend against you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve.” [al-Mumtaḥanah 60:1–2]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3191 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000281 -->

what is the response to the one who uses the Qu'ran being created as a evidence to excusing the Mushrik - Answered by Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Jarbūʿ

I asked the Shaykh:

Some of the Murjiʾah in our time use statements from some of the salaf as proof, where the salaf said that whoever claims the Qur’an is created has committed shirk. Then these people argue: “If there is an excuse (i.e., a valid excuse for ignorance) for someone who says that the Qur’an is created, then excusing someone in other matters—like worshiping other than Allah or slaughtering for other than Him—should be even more appropriate, since both are forms of shirk.” So what is the correct way to clarify this to someone who is unaware and hears this kind of argument?

The Shaykh Responded:

Worshiping other than Allah is kufr; such a person is not a Muslim at all—he is not considered a Muslim to begin with. But if someone affirms the oneness of Allah and becomes a Muslim, then falls into an act of kufr, we ask: Is this kufr definitive (qaṭʿī)—i.e., has its ruling been made clear in the Qur’an and Sunnah? If its clarification is definitive, then such a person becomes a kāfir, even if he did not realize that clarification.

However, regardless of these details, shirk —one is not considered a Muslim unless he disavows himself from shirk. No one says that a person cannot be a Muslim unless he affirms that the Qur’an is the uncreated Speech of Allah. But when it comes to shirk, there are many, many verses—decisive and conclusive—that clearly establish that one cannot be a Muslim while worshiping others besides Allah. How can such a person be judged to be Muslim?

If someone affirms tawḥīd but then falls into an act of kufr, then that is a separate matter. As for these individuals—they do not leave the people (i.e., alone); they do not back off—they continue to fight (i.e., argue), they do not stop. Don’t engage them—they will mislead you from the path of Allah. They are blind in their insight. They are blind of inner sight.

They do not distinguish between the Muslim who is muwaḥḥid and the mushrik who is najis (impure), the one who commits filthy acts of shirk. Indeed, the mushrik is impure. And Allah says: “If you commit shirk, surely your deeds will be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers.” (Surah az-Zumar 39:65) If you commit shirk, then it’s over—your matter is finished. Don’t be deceived by these people—those who do not distinguish, who blur the lines.

As for the claim that a person is excused due to ignorance (ʿudhr bil-jahl), then yes—someone might fall into shirk out of ignorance, and the Messenger has not yet reached him. They say: “We fell into it due to ignorance.” But does that mean the one who worships the ṭāghūt is a Muslim? Or that he is not a kāfir? No. The one who worships the ṭāghūt is a kāfir, not a Muslim, but behind this is fear [i.e., someone might say this out of fear]. But ʿudhr bil-jahl means: he is not punished until he is tested. But he is still not a Muslim. The one who commits shirk is not a Muslim. Islam is tawḥīd. Islam is tawḥīd. Islam is tawḥīd.

Fatawa date: 29th Jul 2025

Shaykh Abī al-ʿAlā ar-Rāshid said:

His saying, the Exalted: “And if any one of the mushrikīn seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allāh. Then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.” (al-Tawbah 9:6)

The implication of this verse is that Allāh, Blessed and Exalted, commanded His Messenger ﷺ that if a person from the mushrikīn seeks protection with him, he should grant it until the person hears the words of Allāh, so that the ḥujjah is established against him. After hearing, no excuse remains. This aligns with what the prominent scholars have stated: the ḥujjah in tawḥīd is established once the Qur’ān reaches a person and is heard.

Thus, the verse clearly indicates that ḥujjah is established by hearing the Qur’ān. In our time, the people of shirk are constantly exposed to the recitation of the Qur’ān, which contains the command to uphold tawḥīd and the prohibition against shirk.

[al-Mulakhkhaṣ al-Mufīd li-ʿĀriḍ al-Jahl wa Atharuhu ʿalā Masāʾil al-ʿAqīdah wa at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Abī al-ʿAlā ar-Rāshid p.120]

Shaykh Abī al-ʿAlā ar-Rāshid said:

His saying, Exalted is He: “And so to many of the Mushrikūn, their "partners" have made fair-seeming the killing of their children, in order to lead them to their own destruction and cause confusion in their religion. And if Allāh had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them alone with their fabrications.” [al-Anʿām: 137]

The point of indication in this verse is that it speaks in the context of the kuffār and mushrikīn presenting their children as vows and offerings to idols and images besides Allāh, Blessed and Exalted. And there is no doubt that this is al-shirk al-akbar, which is among the gravest sins. Then He, Exalted is His status, informs us that behind this shirk are partners and devils who make it seem attractive, adorn it, and confuse it—meaning: they mix truth with falsehood as a beautification and adornment of shirk.

Yet despite this beautifying, embellishing, and confusing of this falsehood by these partners for their followers, Allāh did not make this an excuse for those who obeyed them and followed them out of ignorance of the reality of this embellishment and confusion. Rather, He named the one who obeys these partners a mushrik.

[al-Mulakhkhaṣ al-Mufīd li-ʿĀriḍ al-Jahl wa Atharuhu ʿalā Masāʾil al-ʿAqīdah wa at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Abī al-ʿAlā ar-Rāshid p.118]

Dr. Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar Bāzmūl said:

The statement that whoever bears witness that lā ilāha illā Allāh yet directs worship to other than Allāh — such as slaughtering, making vows to a walī, to a grave or shrine, circumambulating a grave or shrine, or calling upon a dead person — and then saying that this person is a Muslim as long as he acted out of jahl, contains a contradiction. How can he be described as a Muslim when he contradicts tawḥīd at its very foundation and directs worship to other than Allāh? Rather, this action is shirk, and he is a mushrik in essence.

As for judging him to be a Muslim merely because he uttered the shahādatayn while he practices acts of shirk by directing worship to other than Allāh, then this is irjāʾ.

I seek forgiveness from Allāh and repent to Him for any expression that may have come from me contrary to this.

Therefore, it is necessary to distinguish between the rulings of this world and the rulings of the Hereafter with regard to those who fall into shirk out of ignorance and believe that they have not contradicted Islām.

Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar Bāzmūl

Shaykh Muḥammad ad-Dawsarī said:

And irjāʾ continued in the ummah throughout the ages, its fire sometimes dimming—when the light of knowledge increased—and sometimes blazing—when the light of knowledge waned—until its effects became clearly visible in the ummah today. Indeed, it has become a practical reality: many people today suffice with belief in the heart and uttering the shahādatayn, then commit whatever sins they wish and abandon many obligations, if not all; moreover, many frequent graves and shrines, engaging in shirk al-akbar and falsehood, yet still consider themselves within Islam and among the Muslims.

And despite all this, today one sees those defending that corrupt school and supporting it, presenting it as the madhhab of the salaf of the ummah. Whoever denies it is labeled an khārijī takfīrī, speaking about what he does not know, lacking both knowledge and patience, obsessed with declaring Muslims as disbelievers.

And that defender authored parts, books, fatwās, and responses with differing titles but unified goals: the single goal of supporting that disgraceful madhhab. Among those who carried this banner and was fanatic for it is ʿAlī ibn Ḥasan al-Ḥalabī.

[Rafʿ al-Lāʾimah ʿan Fatwā al-Lajnah ad-Dāʾimah by Shaykh Muḥammad ad-Dawsarī  p.73]

## 6. One who calls the mushrik a Muslim or excuses the mushrikīn

### The foundational rule: the third nullifier
<!-- evidence-id: 000289 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: محمد بن عبد الوهاب، <em>نواقض الإسلام</em>، ص. 2 في نسخة المكتبة المحلية؛ وانظر: <em>الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</em>، 2/361 و10/91.</p>
<p>الثَّالِثُ: مَنْ لَمْ يُكَفِّرِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، أَوْ شَكَّ فِي كُفْرِهِمْ، أَوْ صَحَّحَ مَذْهَبَهُمْ، كَفَرَ.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

“The third: whoever does not declare the mushrikīn disbelievers, doubts their disbelief, or considers their way correct, has disbelieved.”

Source: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, *Nawāqiḍ al-Islām*, p. 2 in the local library edition; also *al-Durar al-Saniyyah*, 2/361 and 10/91.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2182 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000290 -->

Sheikh Muḥammad bin ʿAbd al-Wahhāb mentioned some nullifiers of Islam and said:

First: Associating partners with Allah (shirk) in His worship. Allah says: {Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whom He wills} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 48).

And He also says: {Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah, then Allah has forbidden Paradise for him, and his refuge will be the Fire, and the wrongdoers will have no helpers} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 72).

An example of this is slaughtering for other than Allah, such as someone who sacrifices for the jinn or at a grave.

Second: Whoever places intermediaries between himself and Allah, calling upon them, seeking their intercession, and relying on them—he has committed disbelief by ijmāʿ.

Third: Whoever does not declare the polytheists as disbelievers, or doubts their disbelief, or considers their beliefs to be valid—he has committed disbelief.

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 2/361]

### Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb against calling grave worshippers Muslims
<!-- evidence-id: 000291 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="user-supplied-scan">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَالَ: وَهَذَا يَعْرِفُهُ مَنْ لَهُ أَدْنَى إِلْمَامٍ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ وَالدِّينِ، فَتَسْمِيَةُ عُبَّادِ الْقُبُورِ مُسْلِمِينَ، لِأَنَّهُمْ يُصَلُّونَ وَيَصُومُونَ، وَيُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْبَعْثِ، مُجَرَّدُ تَعْمِيَةٍ عَلَى الْعَوَامِّ، وَتَلْبِيسٍ، لِيَنْفُقَ شِرْكُهُمْ، وَيُقَالَ بِإِسْلَامِهِمْ وَإِيمَانِهِمْ، وَيَأْبَى اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: محمد بن عبد الوهاب، نقله عبد اللطيف آل الشيخ، <em>الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</em>، 12/536.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

“This is known to anyone who has even the slightest acquaintance with knowledge and the religion. Thus, calling the grave worshippers ‘Muslims’ because they pray, fast, and believe in the Resurrection is nothing but deceiving the common people and causing confusion, so that their shirk may be promoted and it may be claimed that they are Muslims and believers. But Allāh, His Messenger ﷺ, and the believers reject that.”

Source: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, as transmitted by ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl al-Shaykh, *al-Durar al-Saniyyah*, 12/536.

### The sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb
<!-- evidence-id: 000292 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ حُسَيْنٌ، وَالشَّيْخُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، ابْنَا الشَّيْخِ مُحَمَّدٍ، رَحِمَهُمُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى، فِي أَثْنَاءِ جَوَابٍ لَهُمَا: الْمَسْأَلَةُ الْحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ: رَجُلٌ دَخَلَ هَذَا الدِّينَ وَأَحَبَّهُ، وَلَكِنْ لَا يُعَادِي الْمُشْرِكِينَ، أَوْ عَادَاهُمْ وَلَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُمْ، أَوْ قَالَ: أَنَا مُسْلِمٌ، وَلَكِنْ لَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أُكَفِّرَ أَهْلَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَلَوْ لَمْ يَعْرِفُوا مَعْنَاهَا، وَرَجُلٌ دَخَلَ هَذَا الدِّينَ وَأَحَبَّهُ، وَلَكِنْ يَقُولُ: لَا أَتَعَرَّضُ لِلْقِبَابِ، وَأَعْلَمُ أَنَّهَا لَا تَنْفَعُ وَلَا تَضُرُّ، وَلَكِنْ مَا أَتَعَرَّضُهَا.</p>
<p>الْجَوَابُ: أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَا يَكُونُ مُسْلِمًا، إِلَّا إِذَا عَرَفَ التَّوْحِيدَ وَدَانَ بِهِ، وَعَمِلَ بِمُوجَبِهِ، وَصَدَّقَ الرَّسُولَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِيمَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ، وَأَطَاعَهُ فِيمَا نَهَى عَنْهُ وَأَمَرَ بِهِ، وَآمَنَ بِهِ وَبِمَا جَاءَ بِهِ. فَمَنْ قَالَ: لَا أُعَادِي الْمُشْرِكِينَ، أَوْ عَادَاهُمْ وَلَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُمْ، أَوْ قَالَ: لَا أَتَعَرَّضُ أَهْلَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَلَوْ فَعَلُوا الْكُفْرَ وَالشِّرْكَ وَعَادَوْا دِينَ اللَّهِ، أَوْ قَالَ: لَا أَتَعَرَّضُ لِلْقِبَابِ، فَهَذَا لَا يَكُونُ مُسْلِمًا، بَلْ هُوَ مِمَّنْ قَالَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ: {وَيَقُولُونَ نُؤْمِنُ بِبَعْضٍ وَنَكْفُرُ بِبَعْضٍ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ سَبِيلًا أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ حَقًّا}.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: حسين وعبد الله ابنا محمد بن عبد الوهاب، <em>الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</em>، 10/139–140.</p>
</div>
</details>

Shaykhs Ḥusayn and ʿAbd Allāh, the sons of Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, may Allāh the Exalted have mercy on them, said in the course of one of their answers:

“The eleventh issue: A man has entered this religion and loves it, but he does not show enmity toward the mushrikīn. Or he shows them enmity but does not declare them disbelievers. Or he says, ‘I am a Muslim, but I am unable to declare the people of lā ilāha illā Allāh disbelievers, even if they do not know its meaning.’ Another man has entered this religion and loves it, but he says, ‘I do not oppose the domes. I know that they neither benefit nor harm, but I do not oppose them.’

The answer: A man is not a Muslim unless he knows tawḥīd, embraces it as his religion, acts according to what it requires, believes the Messenger ﷺ concerning what he informed of, obeys him in what he prohibited and commanded, and believes in him and in what he brought. Therefore, whoever says, ‘I do not show enmity toward the mushrikīn,’ or shows them enmity but does not declare them disbelievers, or says, ‘I do not oppose the people of lā ilāha illā Allāh, even if they commit kufr and shirk and oppose the religion of Allāh,’ or says, ‘I do not oppose the domes,’ is not a Muslim. Rather, he is among those concerning whom Allāh said: ‘They say, “We believe in some and disbelieve in others,” and wish to take a path between that. It is they who are truly the disbelievers.’”

Source: Ḥusayn and ʿAbd Allāh, the sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, *al-Durar al-Saniyyah*, 10/139–140.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message5056 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000293 -->

The one who calls a grave worshipper a Muslim, and refrains from takfiring them is also a kāfir like them after proof is established.

Shaykh Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Āl ash-Shaykh was asked:

As for the statement of the questioner: ‘If he is unable to utter their kufr and revile them, what is his ruling?’

Then the answer: this is not free from either him being doubtful regarding their kufr, or ignorant of it, or affirming that they are kuffār, they and those like them, but he is not able to confront them and declare their kufr, or he says: ‘Others besides them are kuffār, but I do not say that they are kuffār.’

So if he is doubtful regarding their kufr or ignorant of their kufr, the evidences from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ concerning their kufr are clarified to him.

Then if he doubts after that or hesitates, then he is a kāfir by ijmāʿ of the scholars: that whoever doubts the kufr of the kāfir, then he is a kāfir.

And if he affirms their kufr, but is unable to confront them by declaring their kufr, then he is compromising with them, and he enters into His statement: ‘They wish that you should compromise (in religion out of courtesy) with them: so they (too) would compromise with you.’ [al-Qalam 68:9] And he has the ruling of his likes from the people of sins.

And if he says: ‘I say others besides them are kuffār, but I do not say they are kuffār,’ then this is a ruling from him that they are muslims, since there is no middle ground between kufr and Islam. So if they are not kuffār, then they are Muslims. Thus, whoever names kufr “Islam,” or names the kuffār “Muslims,” then he is a kāfir, so this one becomes a kāfir.

As for his statement: ‘If you know this from a person, what becomes obligatory upon you?’

Then the answer: it is obligatory upon you to advise him, call him to Allah, and make him know the ugliness of what he has committed. Then if he repents, then this is what is sought.

And if he persists and is obstinate, then he has the ruling of what he committed: if it was kufr, then he is a kāfir; and if it was disobedience or sin, then he is a sinful disobedient person. It is obligatory to condemn him, discipline him, boycott him, and distance him until he repents.

And the Prophet ﷺ boycotted those who stayed behind from a single expedition, and forbade speaking to them and giving salām to them. So how about one who allies with the kuffār  and displays affection toward them?”

[ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 8/160-161]

### Calling the disbelievers Muslims
<!-- evidence-id: 000294 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="embedded-quotation">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: سليمان بن عبد الله، *الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية*، 8/161.</p>
<p>وَإِنْ كَانَ يَقُولُ: أَقُولُ غَيْرَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ، وَلَا أَقُولُ هُمْ كُفَّارٌ، فَهَذَا حُكْمٌ مِنْهُ بِإِسْلَامِهِمْ، إِذْ لَا وَاسِطَةَ بَيْنَ الْكُفْرِ وَالْإِسْلَامِ؛ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُونُوا كُفَّارًا فَهُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ. وَحِينَئِذٍ فَمَنْ سَمَّى الْكُفْرَ إِسْلَامًا، أَوْ سَمَّى الْكُفَّارَ مُسْلِمِينَ، فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**


“If he says, ‘I call others disbelievers, but I do not call these people disbelievers,’ this is a ruling from him that they are Muslims, since there is no middle position between disbelief and Islam. If they are not disbelievers, they are Muslims. Therefore, whoever calls disbelief Islam or calls the disbelievers Muslims is a disbeliever.”

Source: Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, al-Durar al-Saniyyah, 8/161.

The order of this passage matters: the author first distinguishes doubt, ignorance, inability to confront, and an affirmative judgment that the people are Muslims. He directs that evidence be explained to the doubtful or ignorant person before giving the later ruling.

### ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan: the categories that oppose the foundation of Islam
<!-- evidence-id: 000295 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: عبد الرحمن بن حسن، <em>الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</em>، 8/264–265.</p>
<p>وَأَمَّا قَوْلُهُ: وَمَنْ كَفَّرَ مُسْلِمًا فَهُوَ الْكَافِرُ. فَالْجَوَابُ: أَنَّهُ مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا وَهُوَ يَدَّعِي الْإِسْلَامَ لِنَفْسِهِ، وَلِكُلِّ قَوْلٍ حَقِيقَةٌ. وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ شَيْخُنَا رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى تَعْرِيفًا جَامِعًا لِأَصْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ، قَالَ: أَصْلُ دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَقَاعِدَتُهُ أَمْرَانِ: الْأَمْرُ بِعِبَادَةِ اللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَالتَّحْرِيضُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ، وَالْمُوَالَاةُ فِيهِ، وَتَكْفِيرُ مَنْ تَرَكَهُ. الثَّانِي: الْإِنْذَارُ عَنِ الشِّرْكِ فِي عِبَادَةِ اللَّهِ، وَالتَّغْلِيظُ فِي ذَلِكَ، وَالْمُعَادَاةُ فِيهِ، وَتَكْفِيرُ مَنْ فَعَلَهُ.</p>
<p>وَالْمُخَالِفُ فِي ذَلِكَ أَنْوَاعٌ: فَأَشَدُّهُمْ مُخَالَفَةً مَنْ خَالَفَ فِي الْجَمِيعِ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ عَبَدَ اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ، وَلَمْ يُنْكِرِ الشِّرْكَ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ أَشْرَكَ وَلَمْ يُنْكِرِ التَّوْحِيدَ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ أَنْكَرَ الشِّرْكَ وَلَمْ يُعَادِ أَهْلَهُ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ عَادَاهُمْ وَلَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُمْ.</p>
<p>وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ لَمْ يُحِبَّ التَّوْحِيدَ وَلَمْ يُبْغِضْهُ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ أَنْكَرَهُ وَلَمْ يُعَادِ أَهْلَهُ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ عَادَاهُمْ وَلَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُمْ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ كَفَّرَهُمْ وَزَعَمَ أَنَّهُ مَسَبَّةٌ لِلصَّالِحِينَ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ لَمْ يُبْغِضِ الشِّرْكَ وَلَمْ يُحِبَّهُ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ لَمْ يَعْرِفِ الشِّرْكَ وَلَمْ يُنْكِرْهُ.</p>
<p>وَمِنْهُمْ، وَهُوَ أَشَدُّ الْأَنْوَاعِ خَطَرًا: مَنْ عَمِلَ بِالتَّوْحِيدِ وَلَمْ يَعْرِفْ قَدْرَهُ، فَلَمْ يُبْغِضْ مَنْ تَرَكَهُ وَلَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُمْ. وَمِنْهُمْ: مَنْ تَرَكَ الشِّرْكَ وَكَرِهَهُ وَأَنْكَرَهُ وَلَمْ يَعْرِفْ قَدْرَهُ، فَلَمْ يُعَادِ أَهْلَهُ وَلَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُمْ. وَكُلُّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَدْ خَالَفُوا مَا جَاءَ بِهِ الْأَنْبِيَاءُ مِنْ دِينِ اللَّهِ. انْتَهَى كَلَامُهُ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.</p>
<p>فَيُقَالُ لِهَذَا الْمِسْكِينِ: تَفَطَّنْ فِي نَفْسِكَ! هَلْ أَنْتَ دَاخِلٌ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَنْوَاعِ؟ فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِيهَا، فَمَا أَسْلَمْتَ حَتَّى يَثْبُتَ لَكَ الْإِسْلَامُ.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

“As for his statement, ‘Whoever declares a Muslim disbeliever is himself the disbeliever,’ the answer is that there is no one except that he claims Islam for himself, but every claim has a reality.

Our shaykh, may Allāh have mercy upon him, gave a comprehensive definition of the foundation of Islam. He said: ‘The foundation and principle of the religion of Islam consists of two matters. The first is commanding the worship of Allāh alone without partner, encouraging it, showing loyalty upon it, and declaring disbeliever the one who abandons it. The second is warning against shirk in the worship of Allāh, treating it severely, showing enmity because of it, and declaring disbeliever the one who commits it.’

Those who oppose this are of various types. The most severe in opposition is the one who opposes all of it. Among them is one who worships Allāh alone but does not reject shirk; one who commits shirk but does not reject tawḥīd; one who rejects shirk but does not show enmity to its people; and one who shows enmity to them but does not declare them disbelievers.

Among them is one who neither loves nor hates tawḥīd; one who rejects it but does not show enmity to its people; one who shows enmity to them but does not declare them disbelievers; one who declares its people disbelievers but claims that this insults the righteous; one who neither hates nor loves shirk; and one who neither recognizes nor rejects shirk.

Among them, and this is the most dangerous category, is one who acts upon tawḥīd but does not recognize its worth, so he neither hates those who abandon it nor declares them disbelievers. Among them is one who abandons, hates, and rejects shirk but does not recognize its worth, so he neither shows enmity to its people nor declares them disbelievers. All of these have opposed what the Prophets brought of the religion of Allāh.’ End of his words, may Allāh have mercy upon him.

It is said to this unfortunate person: examine yourself carefully. Are you included among these categories? If you are among them, you have not entered Islam until Islam is established for you.”

Source: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan, *al-Durar al-Saniyyah*, 8/264–265.

### ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan: what lā ilāha illā Allāh requires
<!-- evidence-id: 000296 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: عبد الرحمن بن حسن، <em>الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</em>، 2/207.</p>
<p>وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ عَادَاهُمْ وَلَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُمْ؛ فَهَذَا النَّوْعُ أَيْضًا لَمْ يَأْتِ بِمَا دَلَّتْ عَلَيْهِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مِنْ نَفْيِ الشِّرْكِ، وَمَا تَقْتَضِيهِ مِنْ تَكْفِيرِ مَنْ فَعَلَهُ بَعْدَ الْبَيَانِ إِجْمَاعًا؛ وَهُوَ مَضْمُونُ سُورَةِ الْإِخْلَاصِ، وَقُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ، وَقَوْلِهِ فِي آيَةِ الْمُمْتَحَنَةِ: كَفَرْنَا بِكُمْ. وَمَنْ لَمْ يُكَفِّرْ مَنْ كَفَّرَهُ الْقُرْآنُ فَقَدْ خَالَفَ مَا جَاءَتْ بِهِ الرُّسُلُ مِنَ التَّوْحِيدِ وَمَا يُوجِبُهُ.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

“Among them are those who oppose the mushrikīn but do not declare them disbelievers. This type has likewise not fulfilled what lā ilāha illā Allāh indicates of negating shirk and what it requires, by consensus after clarification, of declaring the one who commits it a disbeliever. This is the content of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, Sūrat al-Kāfirūn, and His statement in al-Mumtaḥanah, ‘We reject you.’ Whoever does not declare disbelievers those whom the Qurʾān declared disbelievers has opposed the tawḥīd brought by the Messengers and what it necessitates.”

Source: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan, *al-Durar al-Saniyyah*, 2/207.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3646-message3648 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000297 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī said:

Allah the Exalted says: “and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.” (Qur’ān 18:110) This is the clearest proof that worshipping the prophets or anyone else besides Allah is shirk with Allah. Whoever associates them with Allah in His worship is not from the Ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ — not among the muwaḥḥidīn (monotheists) who respond to Allah and His Messenger.

And whoever prevents or forbids takfīr of one who commits shirk with Allah, equates others with Him, or rejects what has come in this regard from the Kitāb and the Sunnah, and speaks about Allah and His Messenger without knowledge — then it is necessary to judge him by the ruling of the Kitāb and the Sunnah as being a kāfir and mushrik, whether he accepts that or not.

And whoever does not declare a disbeliever the one who associates partners with Allah and equates others with Him — such a person is himself a kāfir by ijmāʿ of the Muslims.

Indeed, every shirk that has appeared in the world has only come about through the opinions of people like you — you are the ones who command shirk, act upon it, and call others to it. And those among you who do not command it, do not forbid it either, nor do they declare disbelievers those who commit it. You have resembled those who invented shirk and introduced into the religion of Allah those wicked foundations whose consequence is to make equals with the Lord of the Worlds, to set others as His equals, to show enmity toward His awliyāʾ and His party, and to ascribe to them what does not befit them.

And this — that very thing — is the essence of filth, impurity, and corruption. Allah the Exalted said: “And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. And We caused to overtake them in this world a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be of the despised.” (Qur’ān 28:41–42).

And his statement — “And your declaring the Ummah of Muḥammad disbelievers without right” — means that he was astonished that we declare as disbelievers those who worship others along with Allah. That, in reality, is the essence of the matter.

He (the objector) falsely portrays them — those who worship alongside Allah other deities — as being part of the Ummah of Muḥammad that has responded and affirmed pure monotheism. This is nothing but deceptive pretense and falsehood, which he fabricates and repeats to divert people from the path of Allah without right, and to confuse the ignorant.

If he possessed sound reason and knowledge — to discern what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was upon — namely, takfīr upon those who worship with Allah others besides Him, and that he (the Prophet ﷺ) disputed with the mushrikūn of the Arabs and their likes, who made with Allah another deity — he would not have exposed this disgrace of his.

We say: This is a tremendous slander. We have not declared the Ummah of Muḥammad to be disbelievers. Rather, we have applied the Qur’ānic verses according to their true indication and necessary implication — declaring as disbelievers those who call upon other than Allah and associate partners with Him.

We have declared them disbelievers only for what Allah and His Messenger have declared disbelief for — in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and in following what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, upon which the people of knowledge have agreed by ijmāʿ.

And whoever does not declare the mushrikīn disbelievers, or doubts their disbelief, or approves of their creed, has himself committed disbelief.

Woe unto him! Where is our “declaring the Ummah of Muḥammad disbelievers”? Rather, the reality of his doctrine is that, according to him, the monotheistic Ummah of Muḥammad consists of the worshippers of graves, the prophets, and the righteous — those who make with Allah other deities, ask them to fulfill their needs, and seek from them relief from their distresses, and who turn to them in times of hardship and affliction.

These are the very people whom the Qurʾān declared to be kuffār, and for whose combat the Messenger ﷺ was sent, a matter upon which the Muslims have an undeniable ijmāʿ.

Source: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī, *as-Sayf al-Maslūl ʿalā ʿĀbid ar-Rasūl*, pp. 98–99.

Lajnah Dā’imah addressed the necessity of establishing proof before declaring as a disbeliever regarding the one who excuses an ignorant Muslim who committed shirk while still regarding them as a Muslim.

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Iftāʾ was asked:

Q: We have, in our area, the widespread phenomenon of grave worship, and at the same time there are those who defend such people and say that they are Muslims excused due to their ignorance. They say that there is no problem in marrying our daughters to them, in praying behind them, and in giving them all the rights of a Muslim over another Muslim.

Not only that, but they label those who say that such people are kuffār as people of innovation, treating them as they would innovators. They even claim that Your Eminence excuses grave worshippers due to their ignorance, saying that you approved a memorandum by a person called al-Ghubāshī in which he excuses grave worshippers.

Therefore, I request from Your Eminence to send a sufficient and complete research clarifying the matters in which ignorance is a valid excuse and the matters in which there is no excuse, as well as indicating the references that can be consulted in this regard.

A: So whoever does istighāthah from the occupants of the graves to repel harm or to remove distress, it is to be made clear to him that this is shirk. The ḥujjah is then to be established against him in fulfillment of the obligation of conveying. If, after clarification, he persists, then he is a mushrik [inwardly] who is to be treated in this world as the disbelievers are treated, and he will deserve the painful punishment in the Hereafter if he dies upon that…

And whoever lives in a land where the call (da‘wah) to Islām and other than it is heard, then does not believe nor seek the truth from its people, he is in the ruling of one to whom the da‘wah of Islām has reached and who has persisted upon kufr…

.. As for the one who lives in non-Islamic lands and has not heard about the Prophet ﷺ nor about the Qur’ān and Islām, then—assuming his existence—his ruling is the ruling of Ahl al-Fatrah (meaning they are treated as disbelievers in the wordly ruling). It is obligatory upon the scholars of the Muslims to convey to him the Sharī‘ah of Islām, in its fundamentals and branches, establishing the proof and as an excuse to him. And on the Day of Resurrection, he will be dealt with like one who was not held legally accountable in the world due to his insanity, stupidity, or young age and lack of legal responsibility (Allah will test them)...

.. And by this it is known that it is not permissible for a group of the muwaḥḥidīn who hold the belief of the kufr of the worshippers of graves to perform takfīr upon their brothers from the muwaḥḥidīn who refrained from making takfīr of them until the ḥujjah is established against them.

For their refraining from making takfīr of them has a shubhah (doubt), which is their belief that it is necessary to establish the ḥujjah upon those grave-worshippers before declaring them disbelievers. This is in contrast to the one whose kufr has no shubhah, such as the Jews, the Christians, the Communists and their likes — for there is no doubt in their kufr, nor in the kufr of the one who does not make takfīr of them.

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Fatwā

President: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bāz

Vice President: ʿAbd al-Razzāq ʿAfīfī

Member: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Quʿūd

Member: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghadayyān

[Fatāwā Al-Lajnah Al-Dāʾimah 3/96-97 & 99]

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said in regards to:

The Third Nullifier: Whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be disbelievers, or doubts their disbelief, or affirms the correctness of their creed — has committed kufr.

This is a very serious matter that many people who affiliate themselves with Islam fall into. A person might say, “As for me, al-ḥamdu lillāh, I do not commit shirk, nor have I associated partners with Allah. But as for the people, I do not declare them disbelievers.”

We say to him: You have not understood the religion. It is obligatory upon you to declare as disbelievers those whom Allah has declared disbelievers, and to declare as mushrikīn those who commit shirk with Allah, even if it be under some pretense or justification. You must also disassociate yourself from them, just as Ibrāhīm disassociated himself from his father and his people when he said: “Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except for the One who created me, for indeed He will guide me.” [al-Zukhruf:26–27]

As for affirming the correctness of their creed, this is even more severe. If someone says about what they are doing, “There is some consideration in this,” or, “These are only means they use to draw nearer to Allah,” or, “They are simply ignorant and fell into this by mistake,” and he defends them—this is even greater kufr than what they [the mushrikīn] have fallen into themselves. He has validated disbelief, affirmed shirk, or expressed doubt about it.

[Sharh Nawāqid al-Islām by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p. 20]

The one who excuses the grave worshipper with ignorance and calls them Muslim is either ignorant or someone that is covering up shirk

Shaykh al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: What is the ruling on one who does not takfir the grave worshippers and says: “They are ignorant and do not intend to worship other than Allah”?

A: Either he is ignorant, or he is covering up for shirk. He is covering up shirk and concealing it. If he is ignorant, then his speech is not given consideration because he is ignorant. His ignorance should be explained to him, and he should be informed that he does not know this matter.

But if he intends concealment and obscuring the truth, then it is obligatory that he be refuted. It is obligatory that he be refuted and that his statement be condemned.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3208 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000306 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said:

Whoever doubts the kufr of the mushrikīn in general — whether they are pagans, Jews, Christians, or those who claim to be Muslim while committing shirk — must hold the belief that they are disbelievers.

Everyone who associates partners with Allah and worships alongside Him others — such as trees, stones, idols, statues, graves, or shrines — is a mushrik kāfir who must be declared as such, even if he claims to be Muslim and says lā ilāha illa Allāh, Muḥammad rasūl Allāh; for shirk nullifies the two testimonies, contradicts Islam, and corrupts tawḥīd.

Therefore, it is obligatory for the Muslim to declare takfīr upon the mushrikīn who worship other than Allah — whether they are Arab or non-Arab, Jew or Christian, or claim to be Muslim. This is a matter of ʿaqīda that is not open to compromise.

So whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be disbelievers becomes an apostate kāfir like them — because to him, īmān and disbelief are the same, and he does not distinguish between them. Thus, he is a disbeliever.

Likewise, whoever doubts the disbelief of the mushrikīn and says, “I don’t know whether they are disbelievers or not,” then he is a kāfir — because he is wavering in his religion between kufr and īmān, and does not differentiate between the two.

[Sharḥ Nawāqiḍ al-Islām by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.80]

Whoever places between himself and Allāh intermediaries — calling upon them, asking them for intercession, and relying upon them — has committed kufr by ijmā‘.

Whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be disbelievers, or doubts their kufr, or believes that their madhhab is correct, has disbelieved.

Whoever believes that the guidance of anyone other than the Prophet ﷺ is more complete than his guidance, or that the judgment of anyone other than him is better than his judgment — such as those who prefer the rule of ṭāghūt over the rule of the Messenger ﷺ, or who prefer man-made laws over the judgment of al-Islām — has committed kufr.

Whoever hates anything that the Messenger ﷺ came with, even if he acts upon it, has committed kufr.

Whoever mocks anything from the religion of the Messenger ﷺ, or its reward or its punishment, has committed kufr. The proof for this is the saying of Allāh, the Exalted: “Say, ‘Was it Allāh, His verses, and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.’” [at-Tawbah:65–66]

[ʿAqīdat at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh al-Fawzān p.51]

### Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān: defending the description of Islam for people who commit shirk
<!-- evidence-id: 000308 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said concerning the third nullifier:

“This is a very serious matter into which many who affiliate themselves with Islam fall. A person might say, ‘As for me, all praise is for Allāh, I do not commit shirk and have not associated partners with Allāh, but I do not declare other people disbelievers.’

We say to him: you have not understood the religion. You must declare disbelievers those whom Allāh declared disbelievers, and declare mushrikīn those who commit shirk with Allāh, even if that occurs under some pretext or justification. You must disassociate yourself from them, just as Ibrāhīm disassociated himself from his father and his people when he said: ‘Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except for the One who created me, for He will surely guide me.’ [al-Zukhruf 43:26–27]

As for affirming the correctness of their way, this is even more severe. If someone says about what they are doing, ‘There is some room for consideration in this,’ or, ‘These are only means they use to draw nearer to Allāh,’ or, ‘They are merely ignorant and fell into this by mistake,’ and he defends them, this is even greater disbelief than what they themselves have fallen into. He has validated disbelief, affirmed shirk, or expressed doubt concerning it.”

Source: Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān, *Sharḥ Nawāqiḍ al-Islām*, p. 20.

### Full statement of Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān
<!-- evidence-id: 000309 -->

“This is the meaning of īmān: that you believe in your heart that Allāh alone deserves worship, and that everything worshipped besides Allāh is false, whether angels, prophets, righteous people, stones, trees, or idols. You must also disbelieve in all of these. This is the meaning of faith in Allāh: that you believe in your heart that no one deserves worship except Him, and that whatever is worshipped besides Him is false. This is required by this creed.

It is not enough to say this with your tongue without believing it in your heart. Nor is it enough to perform outward actions, prayer and fasting, while saying, ‘I worship only Allāh,’ but then saying: ‘I do not know about those who worship graves and shrines. I cannot say they are wrong, because they pray, fast, and say lā ilāha illā Allāh.’

We say: You have not understood the meaning of lā ilāha illā Allāh, nor the meaning of faith in Allāh and kufr biṭ-ṭāghūt. Had you understood properly, you would know that faith in Allāh is not valid except with disbelief in the ṭāghūt, outwardly with the tongue and inwardly with conviction.

This is the meaning of faith in Allāh: that you direct all worship to Him alone and direct none of it to another. A person may perform prayer, fast, and give zakāh, yet seek deliverance from someone besides Allāh, or sacrifice to someone besides Him. Such a person has worshipped Allāh in some things and worshipped others in some things, and is therefore a mushrik.

As for the one who worships Allāh through some acts of worship and worships others through other acts, this person has not truly believed in Allāh. This is like those who fast, perform prayer, perform ḥajj, and pronounce the two testimonies, but then call upon others besides Allāh. They call upon the dead, sacrifice for the dead, make vows to the dead, and circumambulate the graves. These people have not worshipped Allāh; rather, they are mushrikūn.

The worship of Allāh and the worship of others can never unite. Allāh, Majestic and Exalted, says: ‘I am the One most free of need from partners. Whoever performs a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his shirk.’ In another narration: ‘It belongs to the one he associated, and I am free of him.’

Allāh does not accept that anyone be associated with Him in any kind of worship. Rather, all worship must be solely for Allāh. As He says: ‘Fight them until there is no fitnah and the religion, all of it, is for Allāh.’ [al-Anfāl 8:39] Thus, no part of the religion can be for Allāh and another part for idols, graves, or anyone else. The religion must be entirely for Allāh.”

Source: Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān, Sharḥ Maʿnā al-Ṭāghūt, pp. 12–13.

### ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān: the act cannot be called shirk while its doer is called Muslim
<!-- evidence-id: 000310 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān said:

“Among the problems people face today is that some students of knowledge and shaykhs say that if a mushrik circumambulates a grave and worships its occupant but is ignorant, then we do not call him a mushrik. Rather, we call him a Muslim. They say that his action is shirk but that he himself is not a mushrik. This is a strange matter. They say his action is shirk, yet he is not a mushrik but a Muslim. If he dies upon that, he is in Paradise because he is excused for circumambulating the grave and worshipping it.

The shaykh says that this is unknown among both the earlier and later generations. It is said only by ignorant scholars, may Allāh grant safety. Ignorance has taken firm hold in their hearts, and they have become people who do not accept the truth and who argue concerning such matters.

Does the shaykh’s statement, ‘Whoever does not declare the kāfir a kāfir is himself a kāfir,’ apply to a person of this kind? This is shirk and disbelief in Allāh, Mighty and Majestic, yet he did not declare its doer a disbeliever and instead ruled him to be a Muslim.

Concerning people of this kind, their doubts must first be removed before they are judged disbelievers. But we say that this is an ignorance in which no one preceded them. When a mushrik falls into shirk, he is a mushrik. Shirk does not exist independently such that the act is called shirk while its doer is called a Muslim. A person is held accountable for what he does.”

Source: ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān, statement preserved in the Dār as-Salafiyyah ʿUdhr bil-Jahl collection.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3757 -->

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

Whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be disbelievers has not disbelieved in the ṭāghūt; meaning, he has affirmed shirk. And whoever doubts the disbelief of the Jews and Christians, or considers their religion to be correct, has not disbelieved in the ṭāghūt, and therefore is not a believer.

The proof of the disbelief of one who does not declare the mushrikīn to be disbelievers, or doubts their disbelief, or considers their religion valid, is the statement of tawḥīd — Lā ilāha illā Allāh — because such a person has not disbelieved in the ṭāghūt.

And likewise, the saying of Allah the Exalted: “So whoever disbelieves in the ṭāghūt and believes in Allah has grasped the firmest handhold.” [Sūrat al-Baqarah:256]

There is no tawḥīd and no īmān except with two things: disbelief in the ṭāghūt and īmān in Allah. For this reason, the statement of tawḥīd — Lā ilāha illā Allāh — contains both negation and affirmation.

So, if a person were to say, “Allah is the One who is worshipped, and I believe in Allah and worship Him,” he would not thereby be a believer.

We say: This is not tawḥīd. It is not sufficient that you worship Allah; rather, you must also reject the worship of every object of worship besides Allah. That is, you must bring together both negation and affirmation.

The meaning of Lā ilāha illā Allāh is: “There is no deity truly worthy of worship except Allah.” So, if someone were to say, “I worship only Allah — am I not a monotheist (muwaḥḥid)?” we say to him: No — it is not enough that you worship Allah; you must also disbelieve in the worship of anything besides Him. This is kufr biṭ-ṭāghūt and it only occurs through both negation and affirmation: Lā ilāha illā Allāh.

[Shurūḥ Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Mujaddid Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb by Shaykh ar-Rājihī 1/178]

Shaykh Ayman al-ʿAnqarī said:

The Third Nullifier: Whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be kuffār, or doubts their disbelief, or affirms the correctness of their religion — is himself a kāfir.

This nullifier includes three types:

1. That he does not declare the mushrikīn to be kuffār, holding firmly to the view that they are not disbelievers.

2. That he doubts their disbelief — and this is indicated as another type by the author’s saying “أو ” (or), which here is for diversification. Doubt is hesitation between two equal possibilities with no preference for one over the other, such as saying: “I do not know — are they disbelievers or not?”

3. Or that he affirms the correctness of their religion — and this is the worst of the types, for it involves ascribing correctness to their creed. For example, saying: “Their religion is correct,” or “They are upon valid heavenly religions,” or “Their religion is not false.” This also includes the present-day claim of unity and reconciliation between the three religions — as they allege — Islam, Judaism, and Christianity; saying: “They are all true religions, and they are all believers in Allāh, so do not declare them disbelievers.”

It is therefore obligatory to decisively declare as kāfir those whom Allāh and His Messenger have declared kāfir, from Ahl al-Kitāb, the mushrikīn, the atheists, and the apostates. And this is from the necessary requirements of al-tawḥīd — for tawḥīd must include two matters:

The first is al-kufr biṭ-ṭāghūt, which is to believe in the falsehood of worship directed to other than Allāh, to hate it, to show enmity towards it, to declare its people to be disbelievers, and to oppose them.

The second is al-īmān billāh — Glorified and Exalted is He — and this is the meaning of the statement of al-tawḥīd: “Lā ilāha illā Allāh,” meaning: “There is no deity in truth except Allāh.” Allāh, Exalted is He, said clarifying these two matters:

“So whoever disbelieves in the ṭāghūt and believes in Allāh has grasped the firm handhold that will never break” (al-Baqarah 2:256).

Whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be kuffār is to be considered as denying the speech of Allāh and the speech

of His Messenger ﷺ. Likewise, whoever doubts their disbelief is considered not to have affirmed the speech of Allāh and His Messenger that indicates their disbelief.

As for the one who affirms the correctness of their religion — in addition to this being a denial of the speech of Allāh and His Messenger — he is also thereby engaging in istihlāl that which Allāh has made unlawful, for Allāh has invalidated those religions, clarified the distortions of their adherents, and abrogated them through Islām. Affirming them as correct nullifies that.

From the Sunnah is the ḥadīth of Abū Mālik al-Ashjaʿī — may Allāh be pleased with him — in a marfūʿ report:

“Whoever says: ‘Lā ilāha illā Allāh’ and disbelieves in whatever is worshipped besides Allāh — his blood and wealth are inviolable, and his reckoning is with Allāh” (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim)

The point of evidence is that a person’s wealth and blood are not protected until he disbelieves in whatever is worshipped besides Allāh — and from disbelieving in it is declaring its adherents to be kuffār.

[Sharḥ Nawāqiḍ al-Islām by Shaykh Ayman al-ʿAnqarī p.41-43]

### Full statement of Ayman al-ʿAnqarī
<!-- evidence-id: 000316 -->

“The third nullifier is: whoever does not declare the mushrikīn disbelievers, doubts their disbelief, or affirms the correctness of their religion, is himself a disbeliever.

This nullifier includes three types:

1. That he does not declare the mushrikīn disbelievers and firmly holds that they are not disbelievers.

2. That he doubts their disbelief. This is indicated as another type by the author’s use of ‘or,’ which here indicates diversification. Doubt is hesitation between two equal possibilities without preferring either, such as saying, ‘I do not know whether they are disbelievers.’

3. That he affirms the correctness of their religion. This is the worst of the three types because it attributes correctness to their creed. Examples include saying, ‘Their religion is correct,’ ‘They follow valid heavenly religions,’ or ‘Their religion is not false.’ This also includes the present-day claim of unity and reconciliation among the three religions, as they allege, Islam, Judaism, and Christianity, and saying, ‘They are all true religions and all believe in Allāh, so do not declare them disbelievers.’

It is therefore obligatory to decisively declare as disbelievers those whom Allāh and His Messenger declared disbelievers, including the People of the Book, the mushrikīn, the atheists, and the apostates. This is among the necessary requirements of tawḥīd, for tawḥīd must include two matters:

The first is kufr biṭ-ṭāghūt, which is to believe in the falsehood of worship directed to other than Allāh, hate it, show enmity toward it, declare its people disbelievers, and oppose them.

The second is faith in Allāh, Glorified and Exalted, and this is the meaning of the statement of tawḥīd, lā ilāha illā Allāh: there is no deity truly worthy of worship except Allāh. Allāh, Exalted is He, clarified these two matters when He said, ‘Whoever disbelieves in the ṭāghūt and believes in Allāh has grasped the firmest handhold that will never break.’ [al-Baqarah 2:256]

Whoever does not declare the mushrikīn disbelievers is considered to have denied the speech of Allāh and the speech of His Messenger ﷺ. Likewise, one who doubts their disbelief is considered not to have affirmed the speech of Allāh and His Messenger that establishes their disbelief.

As for one who affirms the correctness of their religion, in addition to denying the speech of Allāh and His Messenger, he also treats as lawful what Allāh has made unlawful. Allāh invalidated those religions, clarified the distortions of their adherents, and abrogated them through Islam. Affirming them as correct nullifies that.

From the Sunnah is the marfūʿ report of Abū Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, may Allāh be pleased with him: ‘Whoever says lā ilāha illā Allāh and disbelieves in whatever is worshipped besides Allāh, his wealth and blood are inviolable, and his reckoning is with Allāh.’ [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim]

The point of evidence is that a person’s wealth and blood are not protected until he disbelieves in whatever is worshipped besides Allāh, and part of disbelieving in it is declaring its adherents disbelievers.”

Source: Ayman al-ʿAnqarī, Sharḥ Nawāqiḍ al-Islām, pp. 41–43.

How to deal with the excuser of shirk - Answered by Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Jarbūʿ

I said to the Shaykh: As-salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh, our noble shaykh — may Allāh preserve you and bless you.

We know that whoever excuses the mushrik is a kāfir. But how should one deal with this excuser (ʿādhir)? And what is the ruling concerning one who excuses the excuser? A clarification on this matter would be beneficial, O shaykh.

He replied: Wa ʿalaykum as-salām wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh.

First: this one who excuses the mushrik — if he says he is Muslim, meaning he excuses him due to his ignorance — he is, in reality, Muslim, and it may be that he is a Muslim while committing shirk. Then this statement of his is kufr, and his belief is kufr. So we should alert him and clarify to him. If he persists, we stay away from him — we do not pray behind him, and we do not study from him — except maybe returning the salām.

If there is an issue, then distance yourself from him — distance yourself and increase in distancing — if he insists. And we continue on our path.

And if a person believes in his kufr, he does not speak, he does not say: “So-and-so is a kāfir,” or: “So-and-so declared takfīr,” nor does he cause chaos among people. He proceeds on his way — seeks knowledge, calls to Allāh, learns, remembers Allāh, makes duʿā’, sends ṣalawāt upon the Messenger, and stays away from these people.

Controls and conditions of Takfiring the one who calls the mushrik, Muslim by Shaykh Manṣūr as-Samarī

Shaykh Manṣūr as-Samarī said:

As-salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatullāh. This was sent to me by one of the Indonesian brothers — our brother Shīṭah. I explained that this is, in context, about someone who wanted to declare takfīr on those who do not declare takfīr on the grave worshippers, the mushrikīn. He said: “Those are like them.”

This, however, is takfīr nawʿ (type-based takfīr), not takfīr ʿayn (specific takfīr). Meaning, we do not yet have a specific person — so-and-so, son of so-and-so — who says: “These particular people we know, those who appear to have some Islam,” etc., meaning he has a doubt. When we have a specific individual like this — someone who excuses those people — then we establish the proof upon him. If he does not respond, then we declare him kāfir like them. He becomes a disbeliever like them.

That is the intent — that is what Shaykh Muhammad and others meant. They did not mean that whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be disbelievers is automatically like them in every case. Rather, if someone says: “These are not disbelievers,” then yes — he is like them. That is the Shaykh’s intent. This is the difference between al-ʿayn (the individual) and an-nawʿ (the type).

The Shaykh’s words here concern the type, because he said: those who do not declare takfīr on the grave worshippers. It is like when the Prophet ﷺ said regarding wine: “Allāh cursed ten concerning it — its drinker, its presser, its one who has it pressed,” and so on — he listed them all. Then later, a ṣaḥābī was brought who drank wine. Some said, “May Allāh curse him.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not curse him, for I know he loves Allāh and His Messenger.”

So, the curse itself is not lifted, but when does it apply to a person specifically? It applies when the conditions are fulfilled and the mawāniʿ (preventing factors) are absent. This is the same principle.

When do we say to this ʿādhir (excuser) — the one who excuses these people or those he sees — “You are a kāfir”? We ask him: “Do you excuse everyone who worships graves?” If he says: “No, I excuse only these people I know — so-and-so and so-and-so — because, to me, the daʿwah has not reached them,” then we tell him: “These people are mushrikīn by the proof of Allāh and His Messenger ﷺ.” We clarify it to him. If he persists afterward, then the ruling of takfīr applies to him, because now you have removed his shubhah, fulfilled the conditions, and the mawāniʿ are gone.

This is regarding the specific individual. But before you perform takfīr ʿayn and want to issue the general ruling — takfīr nawʿ — that does not require the fulfillment of conditions or removal of preventers. You simply say: “Whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be disbelievers is like them.”

<!-- authority-death: 241 -->

Shāhīn ibn al-Sumaydaʿ said that he heard Imām Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal say:

“Whoever says that the Qurʾān is created is a disbeliever, and whoever doubts his disbelief is a disbeliever.”

Source: Ibn Abī Yaʿlā, *Ṭabaqāt al-Ḥanābilah*, 1/173, in the biography of Shāhīn ibn al-Sumaydaʿ. Also transmitted in *al-Jāmiʿ li-ʿUlūm al-Imām Aḥmad, al-ʿAqīdah*, 3/572.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">The report has a complete chain in the cited source. No named authentication judgment for this exact chain was found during the present review, so the archive does not grade it.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Full chain</summary>
<p>Ibn Abī Yaʿlā → Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Muhtadī bi-Allāh → Abū al-Ḥusayn ibn Akhī Mīmī → ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Mawṣilī → Mūsā ibn Muḥammad al-Ghassānī → Shāhīn ibn al-Sumaydaʿ → Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="online-primary-text">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَأَنْبَأَنَا أَبُو الْحُسَيْنِ بْنُ الْمُهْتَدِي بِاللَّهِ، عَنْ أَبِي الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَخِي مِيمِي، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْمَوْصِلِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْغَسَّانِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا شَاهِينُ بْنُ السَّمَيْذَعِ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ يَقُولُ: «مَنْ قَالَ: الْقُرْآنُ مَخْلُوقٌ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ، وَمَنْ شَكَّ فِي كُفْرِهِ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن أبي يعلى، <em>طبقات الحنابلة</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">1/173</bdi>، في ترجمة شاهين بن السميذع. ونقله أيضًا <em>الجامع لعلوم الإمام أحمد، العقيدة</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">3/572</bdi>.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Muḥammad ibn Saḥnūn: whoever doubts the disbelief of one who reviles the Prophet is a disbeliever
<!-- evidence-id: 000735 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->
<!-- authority-name: Muḥammad ibn Saḥnūn -->
<!-- authority-death: 256 -->

Muḥammad ibn Saḥnūn said:

“The scholars have unanimously agreed that one who reviles the Prophet ﷺ and disparages him is a disbeliever. The threat of Allāh’s punishment applies to him, and his ruling according to the Ummah is execution. Whoever doubts his disbelief and punishment has disbelieved.”

Source: Ibn Taymiyyah, *al-Ṣārim al-Maslūl ʿalā Shātim al-Rasūl*, p. 513, transmitting the statement of Muḥammad ibn Saḥnūn.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">The consulted text quotes Muḥammad ibn Saḥnūn without a transmission chain at this location. No named authentication judgment for the attribution was found during the present review.</p>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَحْنُونٍ: «أَجْمَعَ الْعُلَمَاءُ أَنَّ شَاتِمَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ الْمُنْتَقِصَ لَهُ كَافِرٌ، وَالْوَعِيدُ جَارٍ عَلَيْهِ بِعَذَابِ اللَّهِ، وَحُكْمُهُ عِنْدَ الْأُمَّةِ الْقَتْلُ، وَمَنْ شَكَّ فِي كُفْرِهِ وَعَذَابِهِ كَفَرَ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن تيمية، <em>الصارم المسلول على شاتم الرسول</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">513</bdi>، ناقلًا قول محمد بن سحنون.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Ḥarb al-Kirmānī: the transmitted creed concerning the Jahmiyyah and those who do not declare them disbelievers
<!-- evidence-id: 000736 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->
<!-- authority-name: Ḥarb al-Kirmānī -->
<!-- authority-death: 280 -->

Ḥarb al-Kirmānī introduced this creed as the doctrine of the leading scholars, the people of reports, and the recognized people of the Sunnah whom he met in Iraq, the Ḥijāz, Syria, and elsewhere. He specifically named Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr al-Ḥumaydī, and Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr. The creed states:

“The Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh, spoken by Him, and is not created. Whoever claims that the Qurʾān is created is a Jahmī and a disbeliever. Whoever claims that the Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh but stops short and does not say that it is uncreated is more disbelieving than the first and fouler in statement. Whoever claims that our utterances of the Qurʾān and our recitation of it are created, while the Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh, is a filthy, innovating Jahmī. Whoever does not declare these people and all the Jahmiyyah disbelievers is like them.”

Source: Ḥarb al-Kirmānī, *Masāʾil Ḥarb al-Kirmānī*, 3/967 and 3/975, ed. Fāyiz Ḥābis.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَالَ أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ حَرْبُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ: هَذَا مَذْهَبُ أَئِمَّةِ الْعِلْمِ، وَأَصْحَابِ الْأَثَرِ، وَأَهْلِ السُّنَّةِ الْمَعْرُوفِينَ بِهَا، الْمُقْتَدَى بِهِمْ فِيهَا، وَأَدْرَكْتُ مَنْ أَدْرَكْتُ مِنْ عُلَمَاءِ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ وَالْحِجَازِ وَالشَّامِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ عَلَيْهَا. وَهُوَ مَذْهَبُ أَحْمَدَ، وَإِسْحَاقَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَخْلَدٍ، وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ الْحُمَيْدِيِّ، وَسَعِيدِ بْنِ مَنْصُورٍ، وَغَيْرِهِمْ مِمَّنْ جَالَسْنَا وَأَخَذْنَا عَنْهُمُ الْعِلْمَ.</p>
<p>وَالْقُرْآنُ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ تَكَلَّمَ بِهِ لَيْسَ بِمَخْلُوقٍ، فَمَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ مَخْلُوقٌ فَهُوَ جَهْمِيٌّ كَافِرٌ، وَمَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ وَوَقَفَ وَلَمْ يَقُلْ لَيْسَ بِمَخْلُوقٍ فَهُوَ أَكْفَرُ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ وَأَخْبَثُ قَوْلًا، وَمَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ أَلْفَاظَنَا بِالْقُرْآنِ وَتِلَاوَتَنَا لَهُ مَخْلُوقَةٌ وَالْقُرْآنُ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ جَهْمِيٌّ خَبِيثٌ مُبْتَدِعٌ. وَمَنْ لَمْ يُكَفِّرْ هَؤُلَاءِ الْقَوْمَ وَلَا الْجَهْمِيَّةَ كُلَّهُمْ فَهُوَ مِثْلُهُمْ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: حرب الكرماني، <em>مسائل حرب الكرماني</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">3/967</bdi> و<bdi dir="ltr">3/975</bdi>، تحقيق فايز حابس.</p>
</div>
</details>
