### ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl ash-Shaykh against Islām by mere affiliation
<!-- evidence-id: 000446 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>الْأَمْرُ الثَّانِي: أَنَّهُ زَعَمَ أَنَّ مَنِ انْتَسَبَ إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ يَكُونُ مُسْلِمًا بِمُجَرَّدِ انْتِسَابِهِ إِلَيْهِ؛ فَعَلَى زَعْمِهِ أَنَّ عُبَّادَ الْقُبُورِ الْيَوْمَ، مِمَّنْ يَدْعُونَ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ وَالْأَوْلِيَاءَ وَالصَّالِحِينَ، وَسَائِرَ مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ وَأَشْرَكَ بِهِ مِمَّنْ يَتَلَفَّظُ بِالشَّهَادَتَيْنِ، أَنَّهُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ بِمُجَرَّدِ انْتِسَابِهِمْ إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ، تَحِلُّ نِسَاؤُهُمْ وَتُؤْكَلُ ذَبَائِحُهُمْ؛ وَقَدْ تَبَيَّنَ لَكَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ فِيهِمْ وَرَسُولُهُ، مِنْ تَكْفِيرِهِمْ وَعَدَمِ إِسْلَامِهِمْ.</p>
<p>الْأَمْرُ الثَّالِثُ: أَنَّهُ زَعَمَ أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَكُونُ مُسْلِمًا بِنَفْسِهِ، لَا بِاعْتِقَادِهِ وَإِرَادَتِهِ وَقَوْلِهِ وَعَمَلِهِ؛ وَزَعَمَ أَنَّ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ لِشَيْخِ الْإِسْلَامِ ابْنِ تَيْمِيَّةَ، وَهُوَ نَقْلٌ مُحَرَّفٌ مُتَصَرَّفٌ فِيهِ كَمَا بَيَّنَّاهُ فِي الرَّدِّ، وَأَنَّ هَذَا لَا يَقُولُهُ عَالِمٌ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: عبد اللطيف بن عبد الرحمن آل الشيخ، <em>الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</em>، 10/493، في الرد على داود بن جرجيس.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl ash-Shaykh says that Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs claimed that anyone affiliated with Islām is Muslim by mere affiliation. On that claim, present-day grave worshippers who call upon prophets, awliyāʾ, and righteous people, and anyone else who disbelieves in Allāh and associates partners with Him while pronouncing the two testimonies, would be Muslims merely because they affiliate themselves with Islām, their women would be lawful in marriage, and their slaughter would be eaten. He responds that Allāh and His Messenger have made clear that they are to be declared disbelievers and are not Muslims.

He then rejects the claim that a man is Muslim “in himself” without reference to his belief, will, speech, and action, and states that the attribution of this claim to Ibn Taymiyyah is a distorted and manipulated quotation that no scholar would affirm.

Source: ʿAbd al-Laṭīf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Āl ash-Shaykh, al-Durar al-Saniyyah, 10/493, in his refutation of Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs.

## 9. Between the two extremes

This section can be built almost entirely from quoted distinctions:

- Major shirk must not be renamed Islam.
- The outward description of an act and its doer must not automatically be confused with the question of punishment in the Hereafter.
- A person unreached by the message is not simply placed in the same category as a Muslim upon tawḥīd.
- A confused Muslim who hesitates because of a scholarly doubt is not automatically treated like the original mushrik before clarification.
- Statements concerning clear major shirk should not be generalized to every obscure theological or subsidiary issue.
- General rulings should not be turned into uncontrolled chains of takfīr.


<a id="other-tawhid"></a>

### Permanent Committee: the confused excuser is not immediately treated like the original disbeliever
<!-- evidence-id: 000447 -->

The Permanent Committee’s answer says that it is not permissible for muwaḥḥidīn to declare their brothers disbelievers merely because those brothers refrain from declaring grave worshippers disbelievers until proof is established against them. Their hesitation may arise from a doubt concerning whether the proof must first be established upon the grave worshipper.

The answer contrasts this with Jews, Christians, Communists, and similar groups, whose disbelief is not treated as doubtful.

Source: *Fatāwā al-Lajnah al-Dāʾimah*, 3/96-97, 99.

### Al-Malaṭī on the Muʿtazilah’s endless chain of takfīr
<!-- evidence-id: 000448 -->

Imām al-Malaṭī said:

“The Muʿtazilah of Baghdād and Baṣrah, and all the people of the qiblah, agree that whoever doubts whether a disbeliever is a disbeliever is himself a disbeliever, because one who doubts disbelief has no faith, since he cannot distinguish between disbelief and faith.

There is therefore no disagreement among the ummah, including the Muʿtazilah and those below them, that one who doubts the disbelief of a disbeliever is a disbeliever.

The Muʿtazilah of Baghdād went further than the Muʿtazilah of Baṣrah. They said that the one who doubts the doubter, the one who doubts the one who doubts the doubter, and so on endlessly, are all disbelievers, following the same path as the first doubter.

The Muʿtazilah of Baṣrah said that the first doubter is a disbeliever because he doubted disbelief. The second, who doubted the first, is not a disbeliever but a sinner, because he did not doubt disbelief itself. He only doubted whether the first doubter became a disbeliever because of his doubt, so his path is not the same as that of the first doubter.

Likewise, according to them, those who doubt the doubter and those who doubt the one who doubts the doubter, continuing endlessly, are all sinners except for the first doubter, who is a disbeliever. Their position is better than the position of the people of Baghdād.”

Source: al-Malaṭī, *al-Tanbīh wa-al-Radd ʿalā Ahl al-Ahwāʾ wa-al-Bidaʿ*, pp. 47–48.

## 10. Other tawḥīd evidence

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2200 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000449 -->

Abū ʿAbdullāh (Imām Aḥmad) said:

There is no deed after the declaration of tawḥīd of Allāh that is better than prayer.

For it begins with tawḥīd and the glorification of Allāh through takbīr, then praise upon Allāh through reciting the Fātiḥah, which is praise, exaltation, and supplication. Likewise, glorification (tasbīḥ) in rukūʿ and sujūd, the takbīrāt at every lowering and rising—all of that is tawḥīd and glorification of Him.

It ends with the testimony of His tawḥīd and the messengership of His Prophet. Its rukūʿ and sujūd are expressions of humility and submission to Him.

Raising the hands in opening and bowing, lifting the head—these are to magnify and venerate Allāh. Placing the right hand over the left while standing expresses humility before Allāh and surrender in servitude.”

[Ta'ẓīm Qadr aṣ-Ṣalāh - Imām  al-Marwazī 1/268]

Imām Aḥmad transmits ijmāʿ on the takfir of the jahmiyyah, mu’tazilah and nothing nullifies ones Islam except shirk.

Imām Aḥmad said in his letter to al-Muṣaddad:

I advise you and myself to fear Allah, the Almighty, and to adhere to the Sunnah. You have witnessed the consequences for those who oppose it and what has been said about those who follow it. It has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said, “Indeed, Allah will enter a servant into Paradise by the Sunnah, for he adheres to it.” Therefore, I command you not to prefer anything over the Qur’an, for it is the speech of Allah, the Almighty. Whatever Allah spoke, it is not created. What He has informed us about the past nations is not created. What is in the Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ, what is in the Mushafs, and how it is recited, and however it is described — all of it is the speech of Allah, and it is not created. Whoever says it is created is a disbeliever in Allah, the Almighty. Whoever does not declare such a person a disbeliever is also a disbeliever.

Then after the Book of Allah, we have the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, the ḥadīth from him, and from the rightly guided companions of the Prophet ﷺ, affirming what the messengers have brought, and following the path of salvation. This path was passed down by the people of knowledge, generation after generation. Beware of the opinion of Jahm, for he is one of opinion, speech, and arguments.

It has been agreed upon by the scholars we have encountered that the Jahmiyyah split into three sects. One group said that the Qur’an is the created speech of Allah. Another group said that the Qur’an is the speech of Allah but remained silent, and they are the cursed al-Wāqifah group. Others said that our words with the Qur’an are created. All of these groups are Jahmiyyah and Kuffār and should be given the opportunity to repent. If they repent, they are spared; if not, they should be killed.

It has been unanimously agreed by the scholars we have encountered that anyone holding these views, if they do not repent, should not be married, their legal rulings are invalid, and their slaughtered animals should not be consumed.

Faith is both speech and action: it increases with good deeds and decreases with bad deeds. A person can leave faith and enter Islam, but nothing removes a person from Islam except associating partners with Allah, the Almighty, or rejecting any of Allah’s obligatory duties out of denial. If one abandons a duty out of laziness or negligence, they remain under Allah’s will. If He wills, He may punish them, and if He wills, He may forgive them.

As for the Mu’tazilah, it has been agreed by the scholars we have encountered that they declare people disbelievers for committing sins. Those among them who hold this view claim that Adam was a disbeliever and that the brothers of Yūsuf were disbelievers when they lied to their father Ya’qūb . The Mu’tazilah also agree that anyone who steals even a single seed is a disbeliever, and they must divorce their wives, and if they had performed Ḥajj, they must start over. Those who hold such views are considered disbelievers, they should not be married, and their testimony is not accepted.

[Ṭabaqāt al-Ḥanābilah 1/342-343]

Imām ʿAbdullāh Ibn Aḥmad reported:

Abū Bakr Saʿīd ibn Yaʿqūb al-Ṭālaqānī narrated to us, saying: Al-Muʾammal ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿUmārah ibn Zādhān say:

“It has reached me that the Qadariyyah will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment alongside the polytheists. They will say, ‘By Allah, we were not polytheists! By Allah, we were not polytheists!’

Then it will be said to them: ‘Indeed, you committed shirk without realizing it.’”

He also said: “It has reached me that on the Day of Judgment, it will be said to them: ‘You are the adversaries of Allah, the Almighty.’”

Footnote

In al-Qadar by al-Firyābī (242), Abū Makhzūm narrated from Sayyār and Abū Hāshim al-Rummānī that they used to say: “Denial of Qadar is shirk.”

Ibn Taymiyyah, in Minhāj al-Sunnah (3/276), while discussing the reason why the Qadariyyah were called mushrikūn, stated:

“It is said: If events occur without being caused by Allah’s action or power, this constitutes clear association (shirk) with Allah. This is why these people were likened to the Magians, who believe that the creator of evil is not the creator of good, thereby making Allah a partner with another.

Whoever considers the actions of people to be independent of Allah’s will, as if they are merely the acts of agents acting under a sovereign, has fallen into clear shirk—one that even the idol worshippers did not approve of, because it is shirk in lordship (rubūbiyyah), not in divinity (ulūhiyyah). The idol worshippers admitted that their idols were owned by Allah, as they said: ‘Here we are, O Allah, You have no partner—except a partner that belongs to You; You own him and all that he owns.’

These people, however, claim that what a person possesses of his actions is his own independent property, separate from Allah. This is why Ibn ʿAbbās said:

‘Belief in Qadar is the foundation of tawḥīd. Whoever affirms Allah’s oneness and believes in Qadar, his tawḥīd is complete. But whoever affirms Allah’s oneness while denying Qadar, his denial nullifies his tawḥīd.

The belief of the Qadariyyah involves both shirk and taʿṭīl. It entails attributing some events to causes other than Allah, removing them from His decree, and affirming an independent creator besides Him. These are two branches of disbelief because the root of all disbelief is either taʿṭīl or shirk.”

[Kitāb al-Sunnah by Imām ʿAbdullāh Ibn Aḥmad p.403-404]

Imām aṭ-Ṭabarī رحمه الله reported:

Bishr ibn Maʿādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, regarding the verse: "And do not eat from that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is disobedience."

Qatādah explained: The enemy of Allah, Iblīs, inspired his allies from among the misguided, saying to them: "Argue with the companions of Muhammad regarding carrion. Say to them: ‘You eat what you slaughter and kill yourselves, but you do not eat what Allah has killed! And yet, you claim to follow Allah’s command?’" So Allah revealed to His Prophet: "And if you obey them, indeed, you would be polytheists."

And by Allah, we do not know shirk to have ever been except in one of three ways: calling upon another god besides Allah, prostrating to someone other than Allah, or dedicates Slaughtered offerings to other than Allah.

[Tafsīr aṭ-Ṭabarī 9/525]

Imām aṭ-Ṭabarī رحمه الله reported:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us. Al-Ḥārith also narrated to me, saying: Al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Waraqāʾ narrated to us—both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the verse: “We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position” (Quran 39:3). Mujāhid said: Quraysh used to say this about their idols, and those before them said it about the angels, ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and ʿUzayr.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah regarding the verse: “And those who take protectors besides Him [say], ‘We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position’” (Quran 39:3). They said: We do not worship them except so that they may intercede for us with Allah.

Regarding the verse: “Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ” (Quran 39:3), Allah, the Almighty, states that He will decide between these groups who took protectors besides Him in this world. On the Day of Judgment, He will settle what they used to dispute over in the world regarding their worship of those they served. He will cast them all into Hell—except those who sincerely devoted their religion to Allah, worshipped Him alone, and did not associate anything with Him.

[Tafsīr aṭ-Ṭabarī 20/157-158]

Imām aṭ-Ṭabarī رحمه الله said:

His saying: “If you invoke them, they do not hear your supplication, and even if they heard, they would not respond to you” (Quran 35:14).

Allah, the Almighty, states: O people, if you call upon these deities that you worship besides Allah, they will not hear your supplication, for they are lifeless objects that do not comprehend what you say.

“And even if they heard, they would not respond to you”—meaning, even if they were able to hear your supplication and understand your words, by being given the ability to hear, they still would not respond to you, as they are not sentient beings. Not everyone who hears a statement is necessarily able to reply to it.

Allah, the Almighty, is addressing the polytheists who associate idols and false gods with Him, saying: How can you worship something that has these attributes—something that can neither benefit you nor harm you? And how can you abandon the worship of the One who holds both your benefit and harm in His hands, the One who created you and bestowed His blessings upon you?

[Tafsīr aṭ-Ṭabarī 19/350-351]

Imām aṭ-Ṭabarī said regarding the verse:

“And whoever calls upon besides Allāh another deity for which he has no proof - then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.” [al-Muʾminūn: 117]

He, exalted is His mention, says: And whoever calls upon, together with the One worshipped — the One for whom ʿibādah (worship) is not fitting except for Him — another maʿbūd (object of worship), having no proof for what he says and does of that, nor any evidence.

And His saying: “Then his reckoning is only with his Lord.” It means: the reckoning for his evil deed is with his Lord, and He will give him his full recompense when he comes before Him. And His saying: “Indeed, the disbelievers will not be successful.” means: the people of kufr in Allāh will not succeed with Him, nor will they attain eternal abiding in bliss.

[Tafsīr aṭ-Ṭabarī 10/82]

Imām Ibn Battāh said:

And it suffices you from that what your noble Master informed you of in His statement: “And they were not commanded except that they should worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, upright, and establish prayer and give zakāh; and that is the correct religion” [al-Bayyinah: 5].

This verse combines speech, action, and intention:

a. Worshipping Allah does not occur except after acknowledging Him.

b. Establishing the prayer and giving zakāh does not occur except through action.

c. Sincerity does not occur except with the resolve of the heart and intention.

[Al-Ibānah al-Kubrā by Imām Ibn Battāh 1/628]

Ibn Ḥazm said:

As for reviling Allāh, there is not a single Muslim on the face of the earth who disagrees that it is kufr mujarrad (absolute disbelief)—except the Jahmiyyah and the Ashʿariyyah, two sects that are not considered reliable. They explicitly state that reviling Allāh and openly declaring kufr is not in itself kufr. Some among them say: it is merely an indication that the person holds kufr in his heart, not that he is certainly a kāfir just for reviling Allāh.

Their foundation in this matter is a corrupt principle that departs from the ijmāʿ of the people of Islām: namely, that īmān is only affirmation in the heart—even if someone openly declares kufr, and worships idols, without coercion or quoting another, but does so by choice—yet is still, according to them, a Muslim?

This is absolute kufr, because it contradicts the consensus of the Ummah, the ruling of Allāh the Exalted and His Messenger, and of all the Companions and those who came after them. No one—neither believer nor disbeliever—disagrees that this Qur’ān is what Muḥammad ﷺ brought, and that it is a revelation from Allāh the Exalted.

Nor have they differed in the fact that it explicitly labels certain speech as kufr, and that it definitively rules kufr upon those who utter certain well-known statements—such as His saying, “Surely they have disbelieved who say, ‘Indeed, Allāh is the Messiah, son of Mary’” [al-Mā’idah: 17], and His saying, “Indeed, they said the word of kufr, and disbelieved after their Islām” [al-Tawbah: 74]. Thus, it is clear that kufr can consist of speech.

[al-Muḥallā by Ibn Ḥazm 12/435]

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

For this reason, among the followers of these people (i.e the Ashāʿirah) are those who prostrate to the sun, the moon, and the stars, and call upon them as they call upon Allāh, fast for them, offer sacrificial rites to them, and seek nearness to them.

Then they say: “This is not shirk. Shirk only occurs if I believe that they are the ones who manage my affairs. If I merely make them a cause or a intermediary, then I am not a mushrik.”

But it is known by absolute necessity from the religion of Islām that this is indeed shirk, So this, and similar matters, belong to the tawḥīd with which Allāh sent His messengers, yet they (the Ashāʿirah) do not include it in the definition of tawḥīd as they understand it. Instead, they include in it the denial of His attributes.

For when they say: “He has no partner, no part, no likeness,”—even if the words are intended in a correct sense—they imply that Allāh is like nothing else. He cannot be divided, corrupted, or rendered impossible; rather, He is One and ṣamad (the Self-Sufficient). Ṣamad means that He has no hollow within Him, and He is the Master whose perfection is complete.

Yet they take this to deny His ʿulūww over His creation and His distinction from what He has made, denying what He actually affirms of His attributes. They claim that affirming these attributes would require Him to be composite, divided, or to have a likeness.

[Darʾ Taʿāruḍ al-ʿAql wa an-Naql 1/287-288]

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

And the meaning here is: that shirk occurs frequently, and likewise shirk with the people of the graves through such actions as their du‘ā’, pleading to them, desiring them, and the like.

[Iqtiḍāʾ aṣ-Ṣirāṭ al-Mustaqīm by Ibn Taymiyyah 2/304-305]

### Ibn Taymiyyah: commanding or praising shirk is apostasy by agreement
<!-- evidence-id: 000466 -->

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>فَمَنْ تَكُونُ هَذِهِ حَالُهُ فِي الشِّرْكِ وَعِبَادَةِ الْأَوْثَانِ كَيْفَ يَصْلُحُ أَنْ يَذُمَّ أَهْلَ التَّوْحِيدِ الَّذِينَ يَعْبُدُونَ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى لَا يُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَلَمْ يَعْبُدُوا لَا شَمْسًا وَلَا قَمَرًا وَلَا كَوْكَبًا وَلَا وَثَنًا، بَلْ يَرَوْنَ الْجِهَادَ لِهَؤُلَاءِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ ارْتَدَّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَبُو مَعْشَرٍ وَالرَّازِيُّ وَغَيْرُهُمَا مُدَّةً؟</p>
<p>وَإِنْ كَانُوا رَجَعُوا عَنْ هَذِهِ الرِّدَّةِ إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ فَإِنَّ سَرَائِرَهُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ، لَكِنْ لَا نِزَاعَ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَنَّ الْأَمْرَ بِالشِّرْكِ كُفْرٌ وَرِدَّةٌ إِذَا كَانَ مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ، وَأَنَّ مَدْحَهُ وَالثَّنَاءَ عَلَيْهِ وَالتَّرْغِيبَ فِيهِ كُفْرٌ وَرِدَّةٌ إِذَا كَانَ مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن تيمية، <em>بيان تلبيس الجهمية</em>، 3/54.</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

Ibn Taymiyyah says that those who worship Allāh alone without associating anything with Him, and who worship neither the sun, moon, stars, nor idols, regard striving against such mushrikīn as one of the obligations.

He then states: “Even if they returned from this apostasy to Islām, their inner affairs are with Allāh. However, there is no disagreement among the Muslims that commanding shirk is disbelief and apostasy when done by a Muslim, and that praising it, commending it, and encouraging it is disbelief and apostasy when done by a Muslim.”

Source: Ibn Taymiyyah, Bayān Talbīs al-Jahmiyyah, 3/54.

<a id="ignorant-major-shirk"></a>

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1560 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000467 -->

Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

Associating partners with Allah in love, worship, supplication, and requests is different from associating partners in belief and acknowledgment. As Allah says:

“And of mankind are some who take (for worship) others besides Allâh as rivals (to Allâh). They love them as they love Allâh. But those who believe, love Allâh more (than anything else).” (Al-Baqarah: 165)

So, whoever loves a created being as they love the Creator has committed shirk, taking equals alongside Allah in love. Even if they acknowledge that Allah is their Creator, they have still fallen into this form of shirk.

[Majmū Fatāwā by Ibn Taymiyyah 10/265]

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

So this intercession (ash-shafāʿah) which the Qur’an negated includes the negation of what the mushrikūn of the Arabs used to say, and those similar to them from the other mushrikīn.

And it is of the same type as the shirk of the Christians and those like them among the misguided who affiliate themselves with Islam, where they believe regarding the angels or the prophets or the shuyūkh that they are intercessors for them with Allāh — just as the intercessors intercede with the kings of the world.

And they strike for Allāh an analogy and say: whoever wants to draw near to a great king should not come to him first, but rather draw near to those close to him, who then raise his needs and bring him near to him.

Allāh the Exalted said: “And those who take Awliyâ’ besides Him (say): "We worship them only that they may bring us near to Allâh."” [az-Zumar: 3] That is, they say: “We do not worship them except that they may bring us near to Allāh.”

He mentioned this after His saying: "The revelation of the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] is from Allāh, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book, [O Muḥammad], in truth. So worship Allāh, [being] sincere to Him in religion. Unquestionably, for Allāh is the pure religion.

And those who take Awliyâ’ besides Him (say): "We worship them only that they may bring us near to Allâh. Indeed, Allāh will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allāh does not guide he who is a liar and disbeliever." [az-Zumar :3]

[al-Radd ʿalā al-Manṭiqiyyīn by Ibn Taymiyyah p.571-572]

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

They believed that the du‘ā’ to the dead, for whom a shrine was built, and doing istighāthah from them was more beneficial than du‘ā’ to Allāh and seeking help from Him in the house built for Allāh ‘Azza wa Jall. So they preferred the house built for the supplication of the created being over the house built for the du‘ā’ of the Creator. And if there is an endowment for this and an endowment for that, then the endowment of shirk is greater in their view, imitating the mushrikīn of the Arabs, whom Allāh described in His words: “And they assign to Allāh a share of what He created of the crops and the cattle, saying, ‘This is for Allāh’—by their claim—and ‘This is for our partners.’ But that which is for their partners does not reach Allāh, and that which is for Allāh reaches their partners. Evil is what they judge.” [Al-An‘ām 6:136]

And when one of them goes to the grave which he venerates, weeps at it, humbles himself, prays, and supplicates, he attains from softness, humility, servitude, and presence of heart  what he does not attain even in the five daily prayers, Jumu‘ah, Qiyām al-layl, or Qur’ān recitation. Is this anything but the state of the innovating mushrikīn and not of the sincere monotheists who follow the Book of Allāh and His Messenger ﷺ?

[al-Istighāthah fī ar-Radd ʿalā al-Bakrī by Ibn Taymiyyah p.381-382]

Ibn Qayyim said:

Among them: that which the Messenger ﷺ legislated regarding visiting graves is only to remember the Hereafter, and to show iḥsān (goodness) to the deceased by making duʿāʾ for him, and praying for mercy upon him, and istighfār (seeking forgiveness) for him, and asking for well-being for him, so the visitor is a doer of iḥsān to himself and to the dead.

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

“The foundation of the dīn of al-Islām and its basis are two matters:

First: The command to worship Allāh alone, without partner, urging toward that, loyalty upon it, and declaring takfīr of whoever abandons it.

Second: The warning against shirk in the worship of Allāh, emphasizing sternness therein, showing enmity in that regard, and declaring takfīr of whoever commits it.

The opponents of this are of various kinds: The most severely opposed are those who oppose in all of it. Among the people are those who worship Allāh alone, yet do not denounce shirk, nor show enmity toward its people. And among them are those who show enmity toward them but do not declare them kāfir. And among them are those who do not love tawḥīd nor hate it. And among them are those who declare them kāfir but claim that it is an insult to the righteous. And among them are those who neither hate shirk nor love it. And among them are those who do not know shirk and do not denounce it. And among them are those who do not know tawḥīd and do not denounce it.

And among them — and this is the most dangerous of the kinds — are those who act upon tawḥīd, but do not know its true worth, nor hate those who abandon it, nor declare them kāfir. And among them are those who abandon shirk and hate it, but do not know its true worth, nor show enmity toward its people, nor declare them kāfir. These have indeed opposed what the prophets came with from the dīn of Allāh, exalted is He. And Allāh knows best.”

[ al-Durar al-Saniyyah 2/22 ]

The importance of affirming the names and attributes of Allah

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

“Whoever denies the Attributes is a muʿaṭṭil, and the muʿaṭṭil is worse than the mushrik. For this reason, the Salaf used to call the works authored on affirming the Attributes ‘Kitāb al-Tawḥīd.’ Al-Bukhārī concluded his Ṣaḥīḥ with that, saying: ‘Kitāb al-Tawḥīd,’ and then he mentioned the Attributes, chapter by chapter.

The crux of the issue is this: the theologians say that tawḥīd is not complete except by denying the Attributes, while Ahl al-Sunnah said: tawḥīd is not complete except by affirming the Attributes. And your tawḥīd is taʿṭīl. For this reason, this statement led some of them to deny the very Lord, Blessed and Exalted, as is the doctrine of Ibn ʿArabī, Ibn al-Fāriḍ, and multitudes of people—none can count them except Allah.”

[al-Durar al-Saniyyah 1/113]

The Reality of the contemporary Murji’ah

Shaykh Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān Āl ash-Shaykh said:

We have heard from a group of those who claim knowledge and religion, and who, in their own estimation, follow Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb — that whoever commits shirk and worships idols should not be labeled as a kāfir or mushrik specifically. That is because some of those who spoke to me directly regarding that heard from some of the brothers that he applied Shirk and Kufr to a man because he Made du‘āʾ to the prophet ﷺ and made Istighāthah with him. The man said to him: “Do not call him a kāfir until you make it known to him.”

Such people and their likes show no concern about mixing with the mushrikīn during travel or in their lands. In fact, they even seek knowledge from those who are among the most disbelieving of the scholars of the mushrikīn. They have pieced together for themselves certain shubuhāt to justify their claims — some of which, In Sha Allāh, will be mentioned later in this treatise. They have deceived with these doubts some of the common folk among their followers — those who have no knowledge or those do not know of their condition, and lacking discernment and understanding. They are physically separated from the brothers, yet separated from the Sheikhs with their hearts, and are flattering towards them. They have become alienated and have caused others to feel alienated from them because of the shubuhāt they display and the gloom that has come upon them through mixing with the sinners and mushrikīn.

When examined closely, they do not declare a mushrik to be a disbeliever except in general terms, and even then they hesitate among themselves. Their bidʿah and shubuhāt gradually spread until they deceived even some of the close companions. And Allāh knows best — this occurred due to their neglect of the kutub al-uṣūl (foundational books), their lack of attention to them, and their absence of fear of deviation.

Anyone with the slightest knowledge, upon seeing the condition of people today and examining the beliefs of these mashāyikh, would be utterly bewildered — and there is no power nor strength except through Allāh. One of those I referred to, when I questioned him about this issue, said: “We say to the people of these tombs — those who worship them and those buried within them — your action is shirk, but you are not mushrik.” So look at this, reflect upon it, praise your Lord, and ask Him for safety.

[Fatāwā al-Aʾimmah an-Najdiyyah 3/116-117]

Shaykh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

And know that Allāh out of His wisdom, did not send any prophet with this tawḥīd except that He appointed for him enemies—just as He, the Most High, said: "And so We have appointed for every Prophet enemies - Shayātīn among mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech as a delusion.” (al-Anʿām: 112)

And the enemies of tawḥīd may possess much knowledge, books, and arguments, as He, the Most High, said: “And when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they [merely] rejoiced in what they had of knowledge” (Ghāfir: 83)

So when you know that, and you know that the path to Allāh must have enemies sitting upon it—people of eloquence, knowledge, and arguments—then it is obligatory upon you to learn from the religion of Allāh that which becomes a weapon for you, by which you fight these devils, about whom their leader and foremost said to your Lord: “ surely I will sit in wait against them on Your Straight Path.” (al-Aʿrāf: 16)

But if you turn to Allāh and listen to the proofs of Allāh and His clear evidences, then do not fear and do not grieve—indeed, the plot of Shayṭān is weak. And the common person from the muwaḥḥidīn will overcome a thousand from the scholars of these mushrikīn.

[Kashf Shubuhāt by Shaykh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb p.26-27]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message4164 -->

Shaykh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbdul-Wahhāb said:

And none may be sought for help except Him, nor may sacrifices be offered to anyone besides Him, nor vows made for any other—neither for a near angel nor a sent prophet. Whoever does Istighāthah from other than Him has committed disbelief, whoever offers a sacrifice to other than Him has committed disbelief, and whoever makes a vow to other than Him has committed disbelief, and the like of these acts.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said regarding this:

Tawḥīd al-Ulūhiyyah encompasses all acts of worship, and none of them may be directed to anyone other than Allah, for He alone is deserving of them. Whoever dedicates any act of worship to other than Allah is a polytheist, even if he says, “Lā ilāha illa Allāh.” In fact, even if he worships Allah through various acts of devotion, as long as he does not devote all of them sincerely to Allah alone, he is not a Muslim.

Whoever does this has committed disbelief, even if he says, “Lā ilāha illa Allāh,” because he has not truly actualized its meaning. This is a contradiction—how can someone say “Lā ilāha illa Allāh” while offering sacrifices to others besides Him? How can he claim “Lā ilāha illa Allāh” while doing Istighāthah with the dead, the absent, the jinn, or the devils? How can he profess “Lā ilāha illa Allāh” while making vows to other than Allah? This is a clear contradiction.

[Sharḥ Tafsīr Kalimat at-Tawḥīd  by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.27-28]

Sheikh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbdul-Wahhāb said:

So, by Allah, my brothers, hold firmly to the foundation of your religion—its beginning and its end, its core and its peak: the testimony that there is no god but Allah. Understand its meaning, love it, and love its people. Make them your brothers, even if they are far away. Disbelieve in the ṭāghūts, oppose them, hate them, and hate those who love them, defend them, refuse to declare them disbelievers, or say, “It is not my concern,” or, “Allah has not commanded me regarding them.”

So, by Allah, my brothers, hold fast to this, that you may meet your Lord without associating anything with Him. O Allah, let us die as Muslims and join us with the righteous.

[Sharḥ Tafsīr Kalimat at-Tawḥīd  by Sheikh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.32-33]

Sheikh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbdul-Wahhāb said:

Know that the Tawḥīd that the messengers called to, from the first to the last, is the exclusive worship of Allah alone, with no rights granted to any close angel, nor any prophet sent, let alone others. From this, no one should be called upon except Allah, as He says:

"And that the mosques are for Allah, so do not call upon anyone with Allah." (Surah Al-Jinn: 18)

So, whoever worships Allah day and night, and then calls upon a prophet or a saint at their grave, has taken two gods. They have not witnessed "There is no god but Allah", because the god is the one who is called upon, just as the polytheists today call upon the grave of Az-Zubayr, or Abdul Qadir, or others, and similarly, they used to call upon the grave of Zayd and others before. Whoever sacrifices a thousand sacrifices for Allah, then sacrifices for a prophet or anyone else, has made two Gods, as Allah says:

"Say, indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds." (Surah Al-An'am: 162)

The rites of sacrifice are part of worship; and so on and so forth. Whoever dedicates all acts of worship to Allah alone, and does not associate anyone else in it, is the one who truly bears witness that "There is no God but Allah."

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 10/61]

Shaykh Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Āl ash-Shaykh said:

And this tawḥīd is the reality of the dīn of Islām, which Allāh does not accept from anyone other than it. As the Prophet ﷺ said: “Islām is built upon five: shahādat an lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa-anna Muḥammadan rasūl Allāh ﷺ; establishing the ṣalāh; giving the zakāh; fasting in Ramaḍān; and making ḥajj to the House.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

So he informed that the dīn of Islām is built upon these five pillars, which are actions. This indicates that Islām is to worship Allāh alone without partner: by performing what is commanded, avoiding what is prohibited, and having sincerity in that for Allāh.

This includes all types of ʿworship, so it is obligatory to devote them purely to Allāh, the Exalted. Whoever associates between Allāh, the Exalted, and others in anything, then he is not a Muslim.

[Taysīr al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥamīd by Shaykh Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Āl ash-Shaykh p.23]

Shaykh Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Āl ash-Shaykh said:

The realization of tawḥīd is knowledge of it, awareness of its reality, and upholding it in knowledge and action. Its reality is the drawing of the soul toward Allāh in love and fear, turning in repentance, reliance, duʿāʾ, sincerity, reverence, awe, magnification, and worship.

In summary: there is nothing in his heart for other than Allāh, no desire for what Allāh has forbidden, and no dislike of what Allāh has commanded. And this is the reality of lā ilāha illā Allāh, for al-ilāh is the maʾlūh (the one who is worshipped).

And how excellent is what Ibn al-Qayyim said:

For the Wāḥid (One), be wāḥid (one), in wāḥid (one)—

Meaning: the path of ḥaqq (truth) and of īmān.

And this is the reality of the two shahādatayn (testimonies). Whoever fulfills them in this manner is among the seventy thousand who will enter Jannah without reckoning and without punishment.

[Taysīr al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥamīd by Shaykh Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Āl ash-Shaykh p.62]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3526 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000492 -->

Shaykh Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Āl ash-Shaykh said:

This tremendous word entails that everything besides Allāh is not a god, and that ascribing divinity to anything else is the most false of falsehoods, and affirming it (for others) is the darkest form of injustice. Thus, none deserves worship except Him, just as ulūhiyyah does not befit any other besides Him. It therefore contains the negation of ulūhiyyah from all besides Him, and its affirmation for Him alone, with no partner.

And this necessitates the command to take Him alone as ilāh, and the prohibition of taking another along with Him as an ilāh. The one addressed understands this from the negation and affirmation — just as if you see a man seeking a fatwā or testimony from one unqualified for it, while neglecting the one who is qualified, and you say: “This is not a muftī nor a witness; the muftī is so-and-so, and the witness is so-and-so.” This in itself is both a command and a prohibition.

And within the meaning of ulūhiyyah enters all types of worship that proceed from the heart’s devotion to Allāh in love, humility, and submission to Him alone without partner. It is obligatory to single out Allāh, Exalted is He, with them — such as duʿāʾ, fear, love, reliance, turning in repentance, repentance, sacrifice, vow, prostration, and all forms of worship. All of these must be devoted solely to Allāh, without partner.

So whoever directs anything of the worship that is befitting only for Allāh to other than Allāh — he is a mushrik, even if he pronounces “lā ilāha illā Allāh,” since he has not acted upon what it necessitates of tawḥīd and ikhlāṣ.

[Taysīr al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥamīd by Shaykh Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Āl ash-Shaykh p.46]

al-ʿAllāmah Abā Buṭayn said:

As for the one who makes the way of the kuffār better than the way of the believers:

If his meaning is regarding the situation of the people of this time, as if he says: indeed the actions of the mushrik of this time at the graves and elsewhere are better than those who call only upon Allah and do not call upon others — then he is a kāfir without doubt.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message2110 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000497 -->

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

Since it is well established among scholars that seeking refuge (istiʿādhah) in Allah is an act of worship, they have ruled that seeking refuge in a created being is impermissible. Based on this principle, they used it as evidence that the Speech of Allah is uncreated, because it is authentically reported that the Prophet ﷺ sought refuge in the perfect words of Allah, both in action and in speech. This is an argument used by Ahl al-Sunnah against the Jahmiyyah, who claim that the Qurʾān is created. They argue that if the Qurʾān were created, it would not be permissible to seek refuge in it.

Since istiʿādhah (seeking refuge) is a form of supplication (duʿāʾ), as explained by Shaykh al-Islām Taqī al-Dīn (Ibn Taymiyyah), this matter is clear. The scholars who prohibited seeking refuge in created beings also maintain that it is impermissible to supplicate to them, since istiʿādhah is, in reality, a type of duʿāʾ. The one seeking refuge in his Lord is, in essence, asking Him to avert or remove harm, and this is the very definition of duʿāʾ.

Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said: “Seeking refuge (istiʿādhah), seeking protection (istijārah), and seeking aid (istighāthah) are all forms of supplication (duʿāʾ), and these terms are closely related. The Prophet ﷺ himself referred to istiʿādhah as duʿāʾ, as recorded in the Sunan where a man asked him: ‘O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication I can make.’ The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, from the evil of my sight, from the evil of my tongue, from the evil of my heart, and from the evil of my desires.’” (Sunan Abī Dāwūd)

Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate, saying: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is a terrible companion, and I seek refuge in You from betrayal, for it is a terrible inner trait.” (Abū Dāwūd, with a ṣaḥīḥ chain).

In the Sunan, ʿĀʾishah (رضي الله عنها) reported that the Prophet ﷺ would supplicate using these words: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Fire and the punishment of the Fire, and from the evil of wealth and poverty.”

In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ would supplicate: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the removal of Your blessing, the loss of Your protection, the sudden onset of Your punishment, and anything that incurs Your displeasure.”

The purpose of citing these aḥādīth is to establish that the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions referred to istiʿādhah as duʿāʾ. Thus, when the scholars ruled that istiʿādhah is not permissible with a created being and is exclusively for Allah, because it is a form of duʿāʾ, then the same applies to all other forms of duʿāʾ. If this is firmly established, it becomes clear that if a person fears an enemy and seeks protection from a living, present person to shield him from harm, this is permissible according to all Muslims. This does not fall under the scholars’ ruling that istiʿādhah with a created being is prohibited.

This is an example of a single act whose ruling changes based on its recipient: Seeking help from a living, present person is permissible, whereas seeking help from anyone else is forbidden. Likewise, supplicating to anyone other than Allah to fulfill needs is impermissible, as Allah says: “So do not call upon anyone along with Allah.” (Sūrat al-Jinn: 18). However, this does not include asking a living, present person for assistance in matters within human capability.

[Ta'sīs al-Taqdīs fī Kashf Talbīs Dāwūd bin Jirjīs wa Yalīhi Daḥḍ Shubuhāt ʿalā al-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn p.87-88]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message2047 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000498 -->

what is Wasīlah?

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

If it is asked, “What is the meaning of wasīlah in the statement of Allah, the Exalted: ‘And seek nearness (wasīlah) to Him’ [Al-Māʾidah: 35], the answer is: The intended meaning of wasīlah is drawing near to Allah, the Exalted, through doing what He has commanded and avoiding what He has forbidden.

Al-Baghawī said: “Wasīlah means nearness.” Al-Bayḍāwī said: “It means that by which you seek closeness to His reward and nearness to Him, through acts of obedience and refraining from sins.” Ibn Kathīr said: “It means to draw near to Him through obedience and doing what pleases Him.” He also stated, “This is the consensus of the commentators.”

Similarly, in another verse: “They seek nearness to their Lord.” [Al-Isrāʾ: 57] Al-Baghawī said: “Wasīlah means nearness.” It has also been said: “Wasīlah is everything by which one draws near to Allah.” Al-Bayḍāwī commented: “They seek to their Lord wasīlah through obedience.” Ibn Kathīr said: “It means that they strive to be closer to Allah through obedience and increasing in goodness.”

Regarding Al-Baghawī’s statement: “They seek out whoever is closer to Allah and use him as a means,” this is his own wording, not from Ibn ʿAbbās. The one who misattributed it to Ibn ʿAbbās has erred. If the meaning of wasīlah is as Al-Baghawī mentioned, then it refers to what the Ṣaḥābah did with the Prophet ﷺ during his lifetime—such as asking him to supplicate for them or seeking rain through him, as reported in many aḥādīth.

This is also what ʿUmar did after the Prophet’s death, when he sought rain through Al-ʿAbbās, saying: “O Allah, we used to seek rain through our Prophet, and You would provide for us. Now, we seek rain through the uncle of our Prophet, so grant us rain!”

Similarly, Muʿāwiyah did this with Yazīd ibn Al-Aswad Al-Jurashī when he sought rain, saying: “O Allah, we seek intercession through our best ones. O Yazīd, raise your hands to Allah!” So Yazīd raised his hands, supplicated, and they were given rain.

This is the correct understanding of wasīlah.

[Ta'sīs al-Taqdīs fī Kashf Talbīs Dāwūd bin Jirjīs wa Yalīhi Daḥḍ Shubuhāt ʿalā al-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn p.119-120]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message2031 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000499 -->

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

If it is said: “These well-known idols of the polytheists are inanimate objects, such as al-Lāt, Manāt, and al-ʿUzzā, while the one buried in a grave is a human—so what is the common factor between them?”

We respond: The Qur’anic texts prohibiting the invocation of anyone besides Allah are general and apply to anyone who is called upon other than Allah, whether they can neither harm nor benefit. Allah, the Exalted, says:

“And do not invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you do so, then you will surely be among the wrongdoers.” (Yūnus: 106) And He says: “So do not invoke anyone with Allah.” (Al-Jinn: 18) And: “Say: Shall we invoke, besides Allah, that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us—like one whom the devils have lured away in the land, bewildered?” (Al-Anʿām: 71) And: “And who is more astray than one who invokes, besides Allah, those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their supplication?” (Al-Aḥqāf: 5)

Al-Bayḍāwī, commenting on this verse, said: “This is a denunciation of the fact that there is no one more misguided than the polytheists, who abandoned the worship of the All-Hearing, the Responsive, the Omnipotent, and the All-Knowing in favor of worshiping those who cannot respond to them—even if they could hear their supplications—let alone know their inner thoughts or attend to their interests. Those whom they call upon are either inanimate objects or subjugated servants preoccupied with their own states.”

Allah, the Exalted, also says: “And those whom you invoke besides Him do not own even a qitmeer (the thin membrane on a date seed). If you invoke them, they will not hear your supplication, and if they were to hear, they would not respond to you.” (Fāṭir: 13–14)

The rebuke in these verses applies to anyone who calls upon those who possess these qualities—whether they are humans, angels, or idols. This includes anyone who neither benefits those who invoke them nor harms those who do not. It also includes those who cannot hear the supplication directed at them, and even if they could, they would be unable to respond—because answering the supplicant is impossible for them. These are the characteristics of the dead.

[Ta'sīs al-Taqdīs fī Kashf Talbīs Dāwūd bin Jirjīs wa Yalīhi Daḥḍ Shubuhāt ʿalā al-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn p.90]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4978 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000500 -->

an important question to ask yourself, do you fall into one of the categories mentioned by Shaykh Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan

Shaykh Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan Āl ash-Shaykh said:

The Answer: It is that there is no one except that he claims Islām for himself, and every statement has a reality.

And our shaykh (Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb) , may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned a comprehensive definition of foundation of Islām, saying: “The foundation of the religion of Islām and its principle is two matters:

The first: the command to worship Allah alone with no partner, to encourage to do so, loyalty to those who adhere to it, and takfīr of whoever leaves it.

The second: warning against shirk in the worship of Allah, being severe regarding it, enmity to those who commit it, and takfīr of whoever commits it.

Those who oppose this are of types: the most severe in opposition is the one who opposes all of it. Among them is one who worships Allah alone but does not reject shirk. Among them is one who commits shirk but does not reject tawḥīd. Among them is one who rejects shirk but does not show enmity to its people. Among them is one who shows enmity to them but does not make takfīr of them.

Among them is one who does not love tawḥīd and does not hate it. Among them is one who rejects it but does not show enmity to its people. Among them is one who shows enmity to them but does not make takfīr of them. Among them is one who makes takfīr of them and claims it is insulting the righteous.

Among them is one who does not hate shirk and does not love it. Among them is one who does not know shirk and does not reject it. Among them, and it is the most dangerous type, is one who acts upon tawḥīd but does not know its value, so he does not hate those who leave it and does not make takfīr of them.

Among them is one who leaves shirk, hates it, and rejects it, but does not know its value, so he does not show enmity to its people and does not make takfīr of them.

And all of these have opposed what the prophets came with from the dīn of Allah.” End of his words.

It is said to this unfortunate one: reflect upon yourself! Are you inside these categories? If you are in them, then you have not entered Islām until Islām is confirmed for you. And it is also said: who is this who declared you a kāfir and confronted you with takfīr? If it is established from a known person, then it is to be examined: did the ruling match the place or not? If it matches, then there is no objection to the one who ruled by the evidence.

[ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 8/264-265]

Shaykh Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan said:

"And they used to say it, but they were ignorant of its meaning which it indicated, of Ikhlāṣ of ʿIbādah for Allāh alone and the leaving of the worship of what is other than Him. So their saying 'La ilaha illa Allāh' was not benefiting them due to their ignorance of the meaning of this word, like the condition of most of the later generations from this Ummah; for indeed they used to say it along with what they used to do of Shirk through the worship of the dead, and the absent ones, and the Ṭawāghīt, and the shrines.

So they come with what contradicts it; so they affirm what it negated of Shirk by their belief, and their speech, and their action, and they negate what it affirmed of Ikhlāṣ likewise. And they thought that its meaning is 'the Ability to Create' in Taqlīd (blind imitation) of the Mutakallimīn (theologians) from the Ashāʿirah and others.

And this is Tawḥīd al-Rubūbiyyah which the Mushrikūn acknowledged, yet it did not enter them into Islām, just as He, the Exalted said: 'Say, [O Muḥammad], "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?"' ... to His saying: "Then how are you deluded?"' And His saying: "Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight ?' ... to His saying: 'and who arranges [every] matter?" They will say, "Allāh," so say, "Then will you not fear Him?' And the likes of these verses in the Qur’ān are many.

And this Tawḥīd, indeed the Mushrikūn of the nations acknowledged it, and the People of al-Jāhiliyyah acknowledged it—those among whom Muḥammad ﷺ was sent—yet it did not enter them into Islām; because they had rejected what this word indicated of Tawḥīd al-Ilāhiyyah, and it is the Ikhlāṣ of ʿIbādah and the negation of Shirk and the disavowal from it, just as He, the Exalted said: 'Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except Allāh and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allāh." But if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].'

So this Tawḥīd is the foundation of Islām, and He, the Exalted said: 'You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them,1 you and your fathers, for which Allāh has sent down no evidence. Legislation is not but for Allāh. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.' And He said: 'So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the correct religion before a Day comes from Allāh of which there is no repelling.'

And He, the Exalted said: '[They will be told], "That is because, when Allāh was called upon alone, you disbelieved; but if others were associated with Him, you believed. So the judgement is with Allāh, the Most High, the Grand.' And He said: ' So worship Allāh, [being] sincere to Him in religion. Surely the religion is for Allâh only.'

And the likes of these verses regarding the clarification of the Tawḥīd to which the Messengers called, and with which the Books descended, in the Qur’ān are many. And we will mention some of that, if Allāh the Exalted wills, in this commentary."

[Kitāb at-Tawḥīd wa Qurrat ʿUyūn al-Muwaḥḥidīn by Shaykh Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb p.36-37]

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

So reflect—may Allah have mercy on you—on the speech of this imām, and his explicit statement that whoever calls upon the dead and turns to them, and seeks istaghāthah from them so that they may intercede for him with Allah, has committed shirk al-akbar, the shirk for whose rejection Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ.

And for Takfiring the one who does not repent from it, and to fight and show enmity toward him—and that this occurred in his time, and that they altered the religion of the Messenger ﷺ and opposed Ahl al-tawḥīd, those who command them with sincerity in worship to Allah alone, with no partner.

And reflect also on his statement: “And how rare is the one who is freed from this!” Rather, how rare is the one who does not show enmity toward the one who condemns it! The matter will become clear to you, if Allah wills.

But reflect—may Allah guide you—on his statement: “And none is saved from the shirk of this shirk al-akbar except the one who shows enmity to the mushrikin” to the end.

It will become clear to you that Islām is not established except by showing enmity toward the people of this shirk; so if he does not show enmity toward them, then he is from them, even if he does not do it (i.e commit shirk), And Allah knows best.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1521 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000503 -->

Sheikh ’Abd ar-Raḥmān ash-Shaykh said:

The author رحمه الله said: “Chapter on the fear of shirk and His (Allah’s) saying: “Indeed, Allah does not forgive that a partner be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.” [An-Nisa: 48, 116].

Explanation:

Ibn Kathīr said: “Allah informs us that He does not forgive shirk (associating partners with Him), meaning He does not forgive a servant who meets Him while being a polytheist. But He forgives what is lesser than that for whom He wills.”

Thus, this verse makes clear that shirk is the greatest of sins, because Allah has stated that He will not forgive it unless one repents from it. Lesser sins are subject to His will—He may forgive them for whom He wills, or He may punish them.

This leads to a great fear of shirk, as it is the most heinous and unjust sin. It involves diminishing the Lordship of Allah, directing His exclusive rights to others, and equating Him with others, as He says: “Then those who disbelieved in their Lord associate others with Him.” [Al-An’am: 1].

Shirk contradicts the purpose of creation and divine commandments in every way. It is the ultimate form of defiance against the Lord of the worlds, arrogance in refusing to obey Him, and the rejection of submission to His commands. The world cannot prosper without this submission to Him.

When it is absent, the world falls into corruption, and the Day of Judgment will come, as the Prophet ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until no one on earth says: ‘Allah, Allah.’” (Reported by Muslim).

And because shirk is the act of likening the created to the Creator – exalted and sanctified be He – in the attributes of divinity, such as the power over harm and benefit, the ability to give and withhold, which leads to dependence in supplication, fear, hope, reliance, and all forms of worship, which are exclusively for Allah, the Exalted. So, anyone who attaches these attributes to a created being has likened them to the Creator and made someone who does not possess the power to harm or benefit, nor life, nor death, nor resurrection, similar to the One who is worthy of all praise, who has created everything, who owns everything, who holds all goodness in His hands, and to whom everything ultimately returns.

The entire outcome of matters is in His hands, and their final decision lies with Him. Whatever He wills, happens; whatever He does not will, does not happen. No one can prevent what He gives, and no one can give what He has withheld. He is the Mighty, the Wise. Thus, the most heinous comparison is the comparison of the helpless and poor by nature, to the self-sufficient and rich by nature.

Among the attributes of divinity is the absolute perfection in every aspect, without any deficiency in any way. This necessitates that all forms of worship—such as veneration, awe, fear, supplication, hope, repentance, reliance, and seeking help—along with the utmost love and utmost humility, should be directed exclusively to Him. All of this is required by reason, law, and innate nature to be for Allah alone, and it is logically, legally, and innately impossible for it to be for anyone else. Anyone who performs any of these actions for someone other than Allah has likened that other to the One who has no equal, no likeness, and no partner. This is the worst and most invalid form of comparison.

For these reasons, among others, Allah, the Exalted, has declared that He will not forgive it, even though He has written mercy upon Himself. This is the meaning of the words of Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him.

[Fatḥ al-Majīd by Sheikh ’Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan ibn ash-Shaykh p.62-63]

Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan said:

The worship of the lords of graves contradicts Islam, for its foundation is tawḥīd and ikhlāṣ (sincerity). Sincerity cannot be established except by negating shirk and disavowing it, as Allah, the Exalted, said: “So whoever disbelieves in al-ṭāghūt and believes in Allah has grasped the firmest handhold” [Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:256]. These deeds, when accompanied by shirk, are “like ashes which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day” [Sūrat Ibrāhīm 14:18], and they become scattered dust, “like a mirage in a desert plain which the thirsty one thinks is water until he comes to it and finds nothing” [Sūrat al-Nūr 24:39].

Lā ilāha illā Allāh — how could this shirk be hidden from him, to the point that he took it as a religion whose defense is obligatory?! The scholars, past and present, from the Companions, the Followers, the Imāms, and all the people of Sunnah, have unanimously agreed that a person is not a Muslim except by freeing himself from major shirk, disavowing it and those who commit it, hating them and opposing them according to one’s ability and capacity, and devoting all deeds solely to Allah — as in the ḥadīth of Muʿādh reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs: “For indeed, the right of Allah over His servants is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him.”

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 11/545]

Sheikh ’Abd ar-Raḥmān ash-Shaykh said:

The Author (Sheikh Muhammad Ibn Abdul Wahhab) رحمه الله said: On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever dies while calling upon a rival to Allah besides Him will enter the Fire. ” Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

Explanation:

Ibn al-Qayyim said: Al-nidd (الند) means a counterpart or equal. It is said: “So-and-so is the nidd of so-and-so” or his equivalent, meaning his equal and counterpart. End quote. Allah Almighty said:

“So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know [the truth].” (Al-Baqarah: 22)

His statement: (Whoever dies while calling upon a rival to Allah besides Him) —meaning: he assigns a rival to Allah in worship, calling upon him, asking him, and seeking his aid— “will enter the Fire.”

Al-ʿAllāmah Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Beware of shirk, for it is evident and clear, This type shall never be forgiven.

It is to set up a rival to the Most Merciful, regardless of who it may be—whether a stone or a human being.

He calls upon it, hopes for it, then fears it, and loves it, just as the love of the Sustainer.

And know that setting up a rival to Allah is of two types:

The first: To make that rival a partner with Allah in any type of worship, or in some of it, as previously mentioned. This is major shirk.

The second: It is the type of minor shirk, such as saying: “What Allah wills and you wills,” or “If it weren’t for Allah and you.” Also, slight showing off (riya). It is confirmed that when a man said to the Prophet ﷺ, “What Allah wills and you wills,” he replied, “Did you make me a partner with Allah? Rather, what Allah alone wills.” This was narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah, al-Bukhārī in his Al-Adab al-Mufrad , al-Nasā’ī, and Ibn Mājah.

In this, it is evident that calling upon others besides Allah for something that only Allah can do is clear shirk, such as seeking intercession from the dead. The right of intercession belongs to Allah alone, and He has control over it, while no one else holds any part of it. It is He who permits the intercessor to intercede for those who meet Allah with sincerity and monotheism, from among the people of major sins.

[Fatḥ al-Majīd by Sheikh ’Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan ibn ash-Shaykh p.65-66]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1531 -->

Sheikh ’Abd ar-Raḥmān ash-Shaykh said:

Whoever sincerely loves Allāh and His Messenger from his heart, this necessitates that he also loves with his heart what Allāh and His Messenger love, and hates what Allāh and His Messenger hate, and that he is pleased with what pleases Allāh and His Messenger, and angered by what angers Allāh and His Messenger, and that he acts with his limbs in accordance with this love and hatred.

If he then acts with his limbs in a way that contradicts this—by committing something that Allāh and His Messenger hate, or neglecting something that Allāh and His Messenger love, while being obligated and able to perform it—this indicates a deficiency in his obligatory love. He must repent from that and return to completing the obligatory love, which, when perfected, constitutes a pillar of worship.

All sins originate from preferring one’s own desires over the love of Allāh and His Messenger. Allāh has described the Mushrikūn (polytheists) as followers of their desires in multiple places in His Book, such as His saying:

“But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allāh?” (Al-Qaṣaṣ 50)

Likewise, Bid‘ah (religious innovations) arise from preferring desires over divine legislation, which is why the people of innovation are called “the people of desires.” Similarly, sins occur because a person prefers his desire over the love of Allāh and the love of what Allāh loves.

As for love of individuals, it is obligatory that it be in accordance with what the Messenger ﷺ brought. The believer must love those whom Allāh loves, from the Angels, the Messengers, the Prophets, the Ṣiddīqūn, the Martyrs, and the Righteous in general. For this reason, among the signs of the sweetness of faith is that a person loves another person, not loving him except for Allāh.

It is therefore prohibited to show allegiance to the enemies of Allāh and to those whom Allāh hates, in general. By this, the entire religion belongs solely to Allāh. And whoever loves for Allāh, hates for Allāh, gives for Allāh, and withholds for Allāh, has perfected faith.

And whoever’s love, hatred, giving, and withholding is for his own desire, then this is a deficiency in his obligatory faith, from which he must repent.

[Fatḥ al-Majīd by Sheikh ’Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan ibn ash-Shaykh p.376]

[Tuḥfat aṭ-Ṭālib wa-al-Jalīs fī Kashf Shubuh Dāwud bin Jirjīs by Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān p.41]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4308 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000511 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl al-Shaykh said:

Yes. If a mushrik says it (The Shahādah) and nothing appears from him that contradicts it, then he is someone from whom restraint is observed merely on the basis of that statement, and he is judged to have entered Islām.

But if it becomes apparent from him, and it is repeatedly seen, that he does not adhere to what it indicates of īmān in Allāh, His tawḥīd, and disbelief in what is worshipped besides Him, then he is not judged to be a Muslim, nor is he given any respect. The texts of the Qurʾān and the Sunnah, and the ijmāʿ of the Ummah, all indicate this.

So whoever truly identifies himself with Islam, loves Muḥammad ﷺ, follows him in his way, loves his noble Companions, and those who followed them from the scholars of the Sharīʿah, affirms decisively and without hesitation the kufr of whoever equates anyone with Allah besides Him, and makes du‘āʾ to others alongside Him from rivals and false gods.

Many people have been afflicted by this doubt and have gone astray because of it, thinking that merely pronouncing the shahādatayn prevents kufr. But Allah, Exalted is He, says: ‘And whoever calls upon besides Allāh another deity for which he has no proof - then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.’ [al-Muʾminūn: 117] his kufr is from making du‘āʾ to other than Allah.

And He, Exalted is He, says: ‘And do not call upon besides Allāh that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.’ [Yūnus: 106].

And He, Exalted is He, says: ‘To Him [alone] is the supplication of truth. And those they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with a thing, except as one who stretches his hands toward water [from afar, calling it] to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it [thus].1 And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error.’ [ar-Raʿd: 14]

And in the ḥadīth as well, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: lā ilāha illā Allāh. If they say it, they protect from me their blood and their wealth except by its right.’ And in another narration: ‘except by the right of Islam.’

And the greatest right of Islam and its fundamental foundation is: worshipping Allah alone, and disbelieving in whatever is worshipped besides Him. This is what the word of sincerity indicates. So whoever says it while worshipping other than Allah, or arrogantly refusing to worship Allah, is contradicting himself, bearing witness against himself to kufr and shirk.

[Al-Ittiḥāf fī al-Radd ʿalā al-Ṣaḥāf by Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl al-Shaykh p. 45-46]

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl al-Shaykh said:

As for if the one who performs takfīr of someone from this ummah bases his takfīr on a text and proof from the Book of Allāh and the Sunnah of His Prophet, and has seen clear kufr bawāḥ (manifest disbelief) — such as shirk with Allāh and worshipping other than Him, or mocking Him — Exalted is He — or His āyāt or His Messenger, or denying them, or hating what Allāh has sent down of guidance and the religion of truth, or rejecting the truth, or denying the attributes of Allāh and the descriptions of His majesty, and the like of that — then the one who performs takfīr with this is correct, rewarded, obedient to Allāh and His Messenger.

Allāh said: "And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [proclaiming]: ‘Worship Allāh and avoid the ṭāghūt.’ Among them were those whom Allāh guided, and among them were those upon whom misguidance was justified." [al-Naḥl: 36].

So whoever is not among the people of worshipping Allāh and affirming His attributes of perfection and the descriptions of His majesty, believing in what His messengers came with, avoiding every ṭāghūt that calls to other than what the messengers came with, then he is among those upon whom misguidance has been decreed, and he is not among those whom Allāh guided to faith in Him and in what His messengers came with from Him.

And takfīr for abandoning these uṣūl (foundations) and not believing in them is from the greatest pillars of the religion, known to everyone who has earnestness in knowing the religion of Islām. And the majority of what is in the Qurʾān is nothing but in establishing His rubūbiyyah (lordship), His attributes of perfection, His descriptions of majesty, the obligation of worshipping Him alone without partner, what He has prepared for His allies who responded to His messengers in the Hereafter, and what He has prepared for His enemies who disbelieved in Him and His messengers and took besides Him false gods and lords. And this is clear, by the praise of Allāh.

[ʿUyūn al-Rasāʾil wal-Ajwiba ʿalā al-Masāʾil by Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl al-Shaykh 2/908-909]

And despite that, al-ʿAllāmah Ibn al-Qayyim firmly stated the kufr of those who blindly imitate their shaykhs in matters that constitute kufr, if they were able to seek the truth and know it, and were qualified for that — yet they turned away and paid no attention. As for the one who was not able and not qualified to know what the Messengers brought, then according to him he is from the category of Ahl al-Fatrah — those to whom the call of a Messenger did not reach.

And both types are not judged to be Muslims, nor do they enter into the Label of “Muslims,” even according to those who did not declare some of them to be kuffār — and his statement regarding that will come to you. As for shirk, it applies to them, and its name includes them. And what Islām remains alongside contradicting its very foundation?

What clarifies this is that the foundation of Islām and its basis is the Shahādah: lā ilāha illā Allāh; and it is the foundation of Īmān in Allāh alone, and it is the best of the branches of Īmān. Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl ash-Shaykh said:

That is clarified as follows: The foundation of Islām and its basis is the shahādah — lā ilāha illā Allāh. It is the foundation of īmān in Allāh alone, and it is the best of the branches of īmān.

This foundation necessarily requires knowledge, action and affirmation, by the ijmāʿ of the Muslims.

Its meaning is the obligation of worshipping Allāh alone, without partner, and disavowing the worship of anything besides Him, whoever it may be. This is the wisdom for which mankind and jinn were created, for which the messengers were sent, and for which the books were revealed.

It includes complete humility and love, and it includes complete obedience and exaltation. This is the religion of Islām, which Allāh does not accept any religion other than it, neither from the earlier ones nor from the later ones.

All of the prophets are upon the religion of Islām. It entails submission to Allāh alone. Whoever submits to Him and to others besides Him is a mushrik, and whoever does not submit to Him is arrogant from His worship.

[Minhāj at-Taʾsīs wa at-Taqdīs fī Kashf Shubuhāt Dāwūd ibn Jirjis by Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl ash-Shaykh p.162]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3821 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000516 -->

Shaykh Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq said:

Shaykh al-Islām (Ibn Taymiyyah) said: “Istighāthah is requesting relief, which means the removal of hardship.” Thus, istighāthah is the duʿāʾ of the distressed one, while duʿāʾ itself is broader in meaning, since it can come from both one in distress and one not in distress.

Duʿāʾ is of two kinds: duʿāʾ al-masʾalah (the supplication of asking) and duʿāʾ al-ʿibādah (the supplication of worship). Duʿāʾ al-masʾalah is asking for what benefits the supplicant, either by gaining some good or by removing some harm. The one who is truly worshipped must therefore have control over benefit and harm. That is why Allāh reproached those who worship other than Him — those who worship what possesses no power to bring benefit or avert harm. This is what the author intended.

As for duʿāʾ al-ʿibādah, it is to worship Allāh through the various acts of worship — such as ṣalāh, zakāh, sacrifice, and others — out of fear and hope: hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment, even if there is no direct wording of request or petition. These two forms of duʿāʾ are inseparably linked: every duʿāʾ al-ʿibādah necessarily implies duʿāʾ al-masʾalah, and every duʿāʾ al-masʾalah inherently contains duʿāʾ al-ʿibādah.

In the Qurʾān, sometimes the term duʿāʾ refers to one of them, sometimes to the other, and sometimes to both together. For example, in His saying: “Call upon Me; I will respond to you.” (Sūrat Ghāfir: 60) — it has been interpreted in both senses: Some said, “Worship Me and obey My command, and I will answer you,” while others said, “Ask of Me, and I will give you.”

And there is ijmāʿ among the scholars that whoever directs any part of either type of duʿāʾ to other than Allāh has committed shirk — even if he says lā ilāha illā Allāh, Muḥammad rasūl Allāh, performs ṣalāh, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim.

[Ibṭāl at-Tandīd by Shaykh Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq p.84-85]

Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Saḥmān said:

As for his statement: ‘The shuyūkh today say such-and-such and such-and-such,’ the answer is that we say: Yes, the shuyūkh today say that we do not make takfīr of the one whose outward appearance is Islām, and they do not apply kufr to all the people of the desert-dwellers who live among the people of Islām.

Rather, they say: whoever among them establishes the description of kufr is a kāfir—such as one who worships other than Allah, associates with Him any of the created beings, or seeks judgment from the ṭawāghīt and believes that their judgment is better and superior to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger, or mocks the religion of Allah and His Messenger, or denies the resurrection.

So whoever establishes this description we mentioned of the mukaffirāt (nullifiers that entail disbelief), and other matters that expel from the religion, whether in the desert or in settled lands, then he is a kāfir. As this was mentioned by Shaykh al-Islām Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb and other scholars—may Allah have mercy on them. And this is what we hold as religion before Allah in whatever desert or settled lands it may be.

Then if we were to begin mentioning what these people have introduced of bidʿah, exaggeration, and transgression of limits in the commands and prohibitions, the answer would become lengthy. The intelligent person proceeds and looks, and guidance and success are in the hand of Allah. Rather, what is required is giving excuse, warning, and clarifying the truth.

And whoever does not have the description of kufr established upon him, while he adheres to the outward laws of Islām, then he is a Muslim, and we do not declare him a kāfir for committing sins and acts of disobedience, nor for actions that do not expel him from the religion.”

[Minhāj Ahl al-Ḥaqq wal-Ittibāʿ by Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Saḥmān p. 20–21]

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nāṣir al-Saʿdī said:

Among its virtues is that it makes it easy for the servant to do good and to abandon evil deeds, and it brings him comfort during calamities. For the one who is sincere to Allah in his īmān and tawḥīd, acts of obedience become light upon him because of what he hopes for of his Lord’s reward and pleasure.

And abandoning sins that the soul desires becomes easy for him because of what he fears of Allah’s anger and punishment.

And among its greatest virtues is that it frees the servant from the slavery of created beings, from attachment to them, from fearing them, hoping in them, and acting for their sake. This is true honor and the highest form of dignity.

Along with that, he becomes devoted and worshipful to Allah alone, hoping in none besides Him, fearing none except Him, and turning in repentance to none but Him. Through this, his success is completed and his ultimate triumph is realized.

[al-Qawl al-Sadīd Sharḥ Kitāb al-Tawḥīd p.24]

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ibrahim said:

“The Islām of the majority is nominal Islam, for most of those affiliated with it in this time are called ‘Muslims’ only by name, in contrast to the Jews and Christians. Whoever is found to have something that nullifies it, then his Islam is merely Islam-in-name, with no love and no honor.
