Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm Āl ash-Shaykh said:

“From ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘“Whoever testifies that lā ilāha illā Allāh”’—knowing its meaning, acting upon what it necessitates, inwardly and outwardly.

The shahādah requires knowledge of what is testified to; if it were out of ignorance, it would not be a testimony (a shahādah).

It requires certainty; if it were out of doubt, it would not be a testimony.

It requires truthfulness; therefore the deeds of those who act differ greatly according to what is in the heart. Whoever’s deeds are lesser, that is according to the deficiency of his affirmation.

It requires acting upon it. The one who does not act upon what he testified to—that is, what he conceives in his heart—his abandonment of action is a witness that he did not testify with his heart. For if he truly testified, he would never abandon it, necessarily.

The mushrikūn say: ‘Lā ilāha illā Allāh,’ while their tongues and actions say: so-and-so is the ilāh. Thus they directed themselves to the soul of the religion and its foundation and nullified it. They say: "we pray, we fast, and we testify lā ilāha illā Allāh, and so on,” yet they opposed the foundation of the religion.

So whoever affirms it verbally and rejects it in meaning—by being contrary to it—he is a apostate, and he is greater than the kāfir aṣlī (original disbeliever). Therefore the grave-worshippers in these times are kuffār murtaddūn (apostate disbelievers), because they knew and rejected its meaning.

Thus it becomes clear that knowledge of it, acting upon it, and truthfulness are necessary.

By knowledge, one is saved from the path of the Christians—which is misguidance. By action, one is saved from the path of the Jews. And by truthfulness one is saved from the path of the hypocrites.”

[Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm 1/221-222]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3725 -->

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

Question: What is shirk al-khafī (hidden shirk)? What is the difference between it and shirk al-asghar (minor shirk)? And how can a Muslim rid himself of it?

Answer: Shirk is divided into three types: shirk al-akbar (major shirk), shirk al-asghar, and shirk al-khafī.

shirk al-akbar is when a person directs any act of worship to other than Allāh, exalted is He. Among the greatest acts of worship is duʿāʾ. So if a person calls upon anyone other than Allāh — such as a prophet, a saint, an angel, the sun, or the moon — seeking benefit or removal of harm, then he has committed shirk al-akbar with Allāh. Likewise, if he bows or prostrates to an idol, the sun, the moon, or the occupant of a grave, he has committed shirk al-akbar that expels him from Islām — we seek refuge with Allāh.

Allāh says: “Indeed, whoever associates others with Allāh — Allāh has forbidden Paradise for him, and his abode will be the Fire. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.” (Sūrah al-Mā’idah, 5:72)

This applies to outward actions. Similarly, if one inwardly believes that anyone shares with Allāh in His creation or has the power to do what only Allāh can do, he too is guilty of shirk al-akbar.

shirk al-asghar is what is less than shirk al-akbar. An example is when a person swears by other than Allāh — not believing that the one sworn by deserves the same reverence as Allāh, but doing so out of veneration or habit. This is shirk al-asghar. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever swears by other than Allāh has committed disbelief or shirk.” It is prohibited — whether one swears by the Prophet ﷺ, Jibrīl, or anyone else among creation — and it constitutes shirk al-asghar.

shirk al-khafī refers to that which lies within the heart and is known only to Allāh. It may be major or minor. If a person associates another with Allāh in his heart, believing that other to be equal to Allāh in His rights or actions, then this is shirk al-akbar— even if hidden from people. If a person performs acts of worship for Allāh but mixes them with riyāʾ (showing off), then this is shirk al-khafī that is asghar, because it is concealed from people yet does not expel one from Islām.

Question: How can a Muslim rid himself of shirk?

Answer: Deliverance from both major and minor shirk is through sincere repentance to Allāh, returning to Him, and adhering firmly to His commands while avoiding His prohibitions. Through steadfastness and sincerity in obedience, Allāh protects His servant from falling into shirk.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2727 -->

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn said:

What the author intends here is Tawḥīd al-ʾUlūhiyyah — the oneness of Allah in worship — and this is the aspect in which the polytheists went astray, those whom the Prophet ﷺ fought, whose blood, wealth, lands, and homes he deemed lawful, and whose women and children he took as captives. This type of tawḥīd is also the one most frequently addressed by the messengers in their dealings with their people. Allah the Exalted said: “And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship Allah and avoid false gods.’” (Surah al-Naḥl, 16:36)

Worship is not valid except when directed solely to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Whoever falls short in this aspect of tawḥīd is a mushrik kāfir, even if he affirms tawḥīd al-rubūbiyyah and tawḥīd al-asmāʾ wa al-ṣifāt.

Suppose, for example, that a man fully affirms Allah’s lordship and His names and attributes, but then goes to a grave and worships the one buried in it, or makes a vow of sacrifice to draw near to him — such a person is a mushrik kāfir, eternally in the Hellfire.

Allah said: “Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah — Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers.” (Surah al-Māʾidah, 5:72) Tawḥīd is the greatest command that Allah has given, because it is the foundation upon which the entire religion is built. For this reason, the Prophet ﷺ began his call to Allah with it, and he instructed those whom he sent to call others to Islam to begin with it as well.

The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever dies while calling upon anything besides Allah as a rival will enter the Fire.” (Narrated by al-Bukhārī) The author, may Allah have mercy on him, cited as evidence Allah’s command to worship Him and prohibition against associating partners with Him, in His statement: “Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him.” (Surah al-Nisāʾ, 4:36) So, Allah the Exalted commands His worship and forbids shirk. This entails affirming worship exclusively for Him alone.

Whoever does not worship Allah is a disbelieving arrogant one; Whoever worships Allah and others along with Him is a disbelieving polytheist; And whoever worships Allah alone is a sincere Muslim.

[Sharḥ Thalāthat al-Uṣūl by Shaykh ibn ʿUthaymīn p.40-42]

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

Q: Is it permissible to give zakāh to a Muslim who supplicates to other than Allāh, swears by other than Allāh, circumambulates graves, and believes that the righteous have the power to bring benefit and harm?

A: rather, the one described in the question is a mushrik, a kāfir. Allāh does not accept ṣalāh, fasting, ṣadaqah, or anything else from him.

Whoever makes du‘āʾ to other than Allāh is a mushrik, and whoever worships graves is a mushrik. Such a person is not to be given zakāh. Rather, he is to be called to Islām and taught tawḥīd. If he accepts it, then that is what is sought; otherwise, it is upon the ruler to carry out concerning him what the Sharīʿah requires.

As for the one who swears by other than Allāh, he may be given zakāh, because swearing by other than Allāh does not expel one from the religion, even though it is shirk. He may be given zakāh, and he should be advised and taught that swearing by other than Allāh is a type of shirk, so that Allāh may guide him.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Luḥaidān said:

When the Companions heard the saying of Allah Most High: “Those who believe and do not mix their belief with Zûlm (injustice) - those will have security, and they are [rightly] guided.” (al-Anʿām 6:82), that was difficult for them, and they thought that what was meant by the verse was that they wrong themselves by actions they commit.

So they said: “O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not wrong himself?” He said: “It is not that. Rather, it is shirk. Have you not heard what Luqmān said to his son while advising him: ‘O my son! Join not in worship others with Allâh. Verily joining others in worship with Allâh is a great Zûlm’ (Luqmān 31:13).”

Thus, the great ẓulm — which, if it enters a righteous act by which Allah is worshipped, corrupts it — is shirk.

For this reason, whoever dies upon Shirk al-akbar has no hope of forgiveness, and it is not valid for one who knows that he died upon Shirk al-akbar to make du‘āʾ to Allah for him, because Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has forbidden that: “It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the Mushrikīn, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire.” (al-Tawbah 9:113).

So if a person knows that someone died upon Shirk al-akbar — even if he was a close relative, even if he was a brother, a close friend, an intimate companion, and so on — it is not permissible for him to seek forgiveness for him.

[Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Luḥaydān p.65]

Shaykh al-Luḥaydān was asked:

Questioner: May Allah be good to you. He says: Is the one who says, “Grave-worshipers are our brothers”, considered a disbeliever?

Shaykh: If the grave-worshipers have become brothers to this person who says so, then there is no polytheist on earth more disbelieving than him. Allah says: “You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger” [al-Mujādilah 58:22].

The opposition to Allah—its highest and most terrible form—is shirk. The Prophet ﷺ was asked: “Which sin is greatest?” He said: “That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you.”

And from the words of Luqmān: “Indeed, shirk is a tremendous wrong.”

So those who worship the graves with acts of worship are not brothers to the Muslim. If someone makes them his brothers, then his religion is corrupted. The issue is not merely that they say, “Lā ilāha illā Allāh.” The bare utterance of Lā ilāha illā Allāh—while openly contradicting it through worship of others besides Him—does not benefit one in the least.

Fatwā no. (10684):

Q: What is the dividing line between kufr and Islam? And does the one who pronounces the shahādatayn, then comes with actions that contradict them, enter among the Muslims despite his ṣalāh and his outward state?

A: The dividing line between kufr and Islam is pronouncing the shahādatayn along with truthfulness, sincerity, and acting according to what they necessitate. So whoever fulfills that is a Muslim believer.

As for the one who commits hypocrisy, then he neither affirmed truthfully nor sincerely, so he is not a believer.

Likewise, the one who pronounces them while coming with what contradicts them from shirk, such as one who seeks istighāthah through the dead in hardship or ease, or one who gives preference to judging by man-made laws over judging by what Allah revealed, or one who mocks the Qurʾān or what is authentically established from the Sunnah of the Messenger of

Allah ﷺ, then this person is a kāfir, even if he pronounces the shahādatayn and prays and fasts.

And with Allah is success. May Allah send prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muḥammad, his family, and his Companions.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3908 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said:

This is the meaning of His statement: “They do not mix their belief with injustice” [al-Anʿām: 82]. That is: with shirk. This is exactly how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained it. When this verse was revealed, it distressed the Companions and they said: “O Messenger of Allah, which one of us has not wronged himself?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied: “It is not the wrong you are thinking of. It is shirk. Have you not heard the words of the righteous servant: ‘ "O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allāh. Indeed, Shirk [with Him] is great injustice." [Luqmān: 13].

As for His statement, “those will have security”: Does this mean complete and absolute security, that they will never be punished at all? Or does it mean general security, that even if they are punished, they will inevitably enter Paradise in the end?

The verse accommodates both meanings. And on either interpretation, it demonstrates the virtue of tawḥīd: that it grants protection from punishment, either total protection or protection from permanent punishment. The verse therefore highlights the excellence of tawḥīd, and that Allah grants its people security in proportion to their level of tawḥīd and their freedom from sins and disobedience.

The verse also implies — through its opposite meaning — that whoever commits shirk with Allah and mixes his tawḥīd with shirk has no security whatsoever. We seek refuge in Allah from that. This makes clear the danger of shirk: a person may worship Allah, yet still invoke others alongside Him, seek aid from the dead, slaughter for graves, or perform ṭawāf around shrines seeking their help. Such a person has mixed his īmān with shirk, and he will have no security at all until he sincerely repents to Allah and purifies his tawḥīd.

Thus, the point is not merely that a person worships Allah; he must also avoid shirk entirely.

[Iʿānat al-Mustafīd bi-Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.77]

Shaykh al-Fawzān said:

And whoever calls to tawḥīd, they call him a Khārijī. Those who promote Islam, they call him a Khārijī. And the kuffār call him extremist, fundamentalist, and other such labels, and they warn against callers to tawḥīd and callers to ‘aqīdah.

Yes, even many of the scholars in these centuries intensified their stance against whoever rejected shirk al-akbar. This is the speech of the Shaykh (Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbd al-Wahāb). He was in the thirteenth century.

In his time, the denunciation of those who are called “scholars” became severe against the callers to tawḥīd. They would call them Khawārij and declare the callers to tawḥīd misguided, and this is present in their books until now.

Meaning, even many of the scholars in those centuries intensified their opposition against whoever condemned shirk al-akbar.

Shaykh al-Fawzān said:

He said: “And do not associate anything with Him,” because a person may worship Allāh, yet mix his worship with shirk. In that case, the worship is not valid until it is purified from shirk, as Allāh said: “Worship Allāh and associate nothing with Him” (al-Nisāʾ: 36).

And He said: “Worship Allāh and avoid the ṭāghūt.” So it is necessary, along with worshipping Allāh, to abandon shirk, because if shirk enters into worship it nullifies it and corrupts it, even if it was originally for Allāh.

This requires that you learn what correct worship is, and what shirk is, so that you may perform worship in its proper manner and avoid shirk.

This is the right of Allāh upon His servants, and it is the first of rights, as Allāh said: “And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. And that you be dutiful to your parents” (al-Isrāʾ: 23). So He began with tawḥīd, which is the right of Allāh.

Shaykh al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: Some people make a distinction between the shirk of the People of the Book and the shirk of those who affiliate themselves with Islam in this era. Is there any difference between the kāfir aṣlī (original disbeliever) and someone who ascribes himself to Islam but then falls into shirk akbar?

A: I do not know of such a distinction. Whenever a person commits shirk, he is a mushrik — whether he is from the People of the Book or from this ummah. Whoever commits shirk is a mushrik, from whatever community he may be.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4264 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000548 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said:

Whoever slaughters for other than Allah—meaning: whoever seeks closeness by slaughtering to other than Allah, such as idols, shrines, trees, stones, the jinn, and the like—then everyone who seeks closeness by slaughtering to other than Allah has indeed been cursed by Allah.

This indicates the severity of this crime, for Allah, does not curse except for a grave offense. Thus it shows the seriousness of the crime of one who slaughters for other than Allah, regardless of whether that slaughter is great or small, significant or insignificant.

That occurs when one mentions over the sacrifice a name other than the name of Allah, or when in his intention, heart, and belief he seeks closeness through this sacrifice to other than Allah; or when he intends by this sacrifice to repel harm from the one for whom it is slaughtered—so he slaughters for the jinn in order to repel their harm and out of fear of them; or he slaughters for an idol believing that the idol brings him benefit.

This is like what some ignorant people do: when rain is delayed, they take a bull or another animal and slaughter it in a specific place, or at a grave, seeking the descent of rain. They may then be tested, and rain may fall, and their need may be fulfilled as a trial and examination from Allah. This does not indicate the permissibility of what they did of shirk and seeking closeness to other than Allah.

Whoever does that is a mushrik and cursed, whether he verbally says, “This sacrifice is for the grave,” or “for al-Badawī,” or “for al-Ḥusayn,” or for so-and-so, or whether he only intends it in his heart. This sacrifice is ḥarām, because it falls under His statement: “that which has been dedicated to other than Allah.” [Baqarah: 173]

This includes what is slaughtered in the name of other than Allah, and it also includes what is slaughtered in the name of Allah while intending an idol, the jinn, or demons. Sorcerers and charlatans today, when sick people come to them, command them to slaughter for other than Allah so that they may be cured of their illness.

Included in slaughtering for other than Allah are several categories: what is slaughtered for other than Allah as an act of devotion, even if “Bismillāh" is said over it—this is forbidden by the ijmāʿ of the Muslims, and it is Shirk with Allah. Also included is what is slaughtered for meat but over which a name other than Allah is mentioned.

Also included is what is slaughtered as a form of greeting and glorification, such as what is slaughtered for kings and leaders upon their arrival—when they disembark from a plane, a car, or an animal, an animal is slaughtered at their arrival. Also included is what is slaughtered at the beginning of a project: some ignorant people, or some who are careless, when they establish a project—such as a factory or the like—slaughter an animal when the machinery is first set in motion.

Likewise, what is slaughtered upon first entering a house out of fear of the jinn—this is shirk, because it is among what is slaughtered for other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As for slaughtering an animal upon entering a house out of joy and happiness, and to invite neighbors and relatives, then there is no harm in that.

[Iʿānat al-Mustafīd bi-Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.224-225]

In this verse, Allāh says to His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ:

“It has indeed been revealed to you” — meaning Allāh revealed to you — “and to those before you” — meaning the prophets — “that if you should associate [anything] with Allāh, your work would surely become worthless” — meaning invalidated — “and you would surely be among the losers. Rather, worship [only] Allāh and be among the grateful.”

So if this is directed to the Messenger ﷺ—that if he were to commit shirk, all of his deeds would be nullified and he would be among the losers—then what about others from the people?

This is by way of warning this ummah from falling into shirk.

This verse does not exclude anyone. Whoever commits Shirk al-Akbar, his deeds are nullified, no matter how much effort he exerts. This is not specific to the people of jāhiliyyah; rather, it is general for anyone who commits shirk until the Hour is established.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: I ask about the meaning of the word Tawhid, what its conditions are, and how a Muslim can hold its meaning in belief without being tested or examined.”

A: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and may Allah bless and grant peace to our Prophet Muhammad, his family, and companions.

The word Tawhid is La ilaha illa Allah. Its meaning is: there is no true object of worship except Allah. It encompasses both negation and affirmation. The negation is in the phrase La ilaha (there is no deity), which nullifies all that is worshiped besides Allah, the Exalted. The affirmation is in the phrase illa Allah (except Allah), which affirms that worship is for Allah alone, because worship is a right of Allah that none may share, as Allah says:

“And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me. Indeed, it is Allāh who is the Provider, the firm possessor of strength.” [Adh-Dhariyat: 56–58]

It is a right of Allah. Tawhid and worship are a right of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, upon His servants. As the Prophet ﷺ said to Mu‘adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him: “The right of Allah upon His servants is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and the right of the servants upon Allah is that He does not punish those who do not associate anything with Him.”

Allah also says: “Worship Allâh and join none with Him (in worship); and do good to parents.” [An-Nisa: 36] This establishes His right as the foremost of rights, which is its meaning.

Its implication is that the servant must single out Allah in worship. If he knows its meaning and pronounces it with understanding, then he must act according to its implications and meaning. That is, he must worship Allah alone, with no partner. If he worships or calls upon anyone besides Allah, this contradicts La ilaha illa Allah, invalidates it, and corrupts the meaning of the phrase. Such pronouncement is of no benefit if coupled with shirk.

Rather, he must act in accordance with it, dedicating his religion, worship, and actions solely to Allah, Glorified and Exalted. His actions must follow the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ, without innovations, fabrications, or superstitions. He worships Allah according to what Allah has legislated, not according to his own desires, whims, or what people do without evidence or support from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said:

It is not enough for a person to worship Allah alone; he must also avoid the ṭāghūt (false deity). If he dies while his worship is mixed with shirk, then that worship becomes invalid.

He must also disassociate himself from shirk and from the mushrikīn, showing enmity toward them for the sake of Allah. If he approves of them in their shirk and does not disassociate from them, then his tawḥīd does not benefit him.

The verse “And avoid the ṭāghūt” encompasses both abandoning the worship of the ṭāghūt and expressing barā’ah (disavowal) from those who worship the ṭāghūt.

[at-Taʿlīq al-Mukhtaṣar al-Mubayyan ʿalā Qurrat ʿUyūn al-Muwaḥḥidīn by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.18]

Shaykh al-Fawzān said regarding the verse:

"And who is more astray than one who calls on besides Allâh, such as will not answer him till the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their calls to them? And when mankind are gathered (on the Day of Resurrection), they (false deities) will become their enemies and will deny their worshipping." (al-Aḥqāf: 5-6)

Allah judged that there is no one more astray than the person who called upon other than Allah from among created beings—those who are not capable of responding to his supplication in this world, nor are they even aware of the one who calls upon them.

And when the Resurrection occurs and they are gathered along with all people, they will show enmity toward the one who used to call upon them and will disassociate themselves from him.  Thus this mushrik is in misery in both abodes: he obtains no response in this world, and in the Hereafter his act of worship will be rejected at the moment he is most in need of it.

The relevance of the two verses to the chapter:

They contain the ruling that whoever calls upon other than Allah is the most astray of the astray, and that duʿāʾ is an act of worship—so whoever directs it to other than Allah is a mushrik.

That duʿāʾ is an act of worship, and so whoever calls upon other than Allah has committed shirk al-akbar.

That idols do not hear the one who calls upon them, nor respond to him—contrary to what the mushrikūn imagine.

[Al-Mulakhkhaṣ fī Sharḥ Kitāb al-Tawḥīd by Shaykh al-Fawzān p.99]

Shaykh al-Fawzān said:

1. The meaning of lā ilāha illā Allāh is to disbelieve in whatever is worshiped besides Allah — such as idols, graves, and other objects of devotion.

2. Mere utterance of lā ilāha illā Allāh without disbelieving in what is worshiped besides Allah does not make a person’s life and property inviolable, even if he understands its meaning and acts upon it outwardly — unless he adds to it disbelief in all that is worshiped besides Allah.

3. Whoever manifests tawḥīd and adheres to its outward obligations must be spared from harm until something contrary to that becomes evident from him.

4. It is obligatory to refrain from harming a kāfir if he enters Islam — even during battle — until something contrary to that becomes clear from him.

5. A person may say lā ilāha illā Allāh yet not disbelieve in what is worshiped besides Allah.

6. Judgment in this world is based on outward actions, while in the Hereafter it is based on intentions and purposes.

7. The life and wealth of a Muslim are sacred and inviolable except with just cause.

Shaykh al-Fawzān was asked:

Question: The one who performs ṭawāf  around a grave — is he considered a mushrik absolutely, or do we need to examine his intention? If it was done as an act of drawing near…?

Answer: This — we have told you — is from the matters of the hearts. We do not look into the hearts. We judge by what is outward. So whoever performs ṭawāf around a grave seeking nearness to the grave itself is a mushrik, because he has directed an act of worship to other than Allāh.

Are we to wait and say, “Let us find out what is in his heart”? When will you ever know what is in his heart? You will never know it. None knows it except Allāh.

If he intends by his ṭawāf to draw near to other than Allāh, then he is a mushrik. If he intends that the ṭawāf is for Allāh, but he performs ṭawāf around a grave, a building, or some shrine, seeking nearness to Allāh and believing that this will benefit him, then we say: this person is a mubtadiʿ (innovator), because he has worshipped Allāh with an act of worship that Allāh did not legislate. Allāh did not legislate ṭawāf around anything except the Kaʿbah.

So whoever performs ṭawāf around other than the Kaʿbah seeking nearness to Allāh through that act is a mubtadiʿ. And whoever performs ṭawāf around other than the Kaʿbah seeking nearness to the one being circumambulated is a mushrik.

As for those who perform ṭawāf around graves, they are seeking nearness to them. Those who performs ṭawāf around them, only do so in order to draw near to them, hoping in them and fearing them.

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān was asked:

Q: 'Is it said that the lack of judgment of Kufr upon the one who said to the dead person at his grave: "Make du‘āʾ to Allah for me" and the likes of it, that it is based upon the dead person hearing whoever is at his grave?'

A: they explained it like this, but it is a weak reason; because the tree hears, and the stone hears, and everything hears.  If, for example, the matter were merely that something hears—even though this hearing is a kind of hearing whose reality we do not know—yet it is certain that it hears. And for this, the stone among the stones used to greet the Messenger ﷺ; it says: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allāh.'

And likewise the trunk upon which he used to give khuṭbah, he used to lean upon it... when he separated from it, and it began to cry -meaning it cried due to the loss of the remembrance that used to be mentioned upon it—and it hears. And He has informed us that everything glorifies with His praise. So the taʿlīl is incorrect.

And this is du‘āʾ to other than Allāh. You call upon him for a thing he has no power over, and is not capable of. As it is known, this is Shirk. And this Shirk of the Mushrikīn. It is not possible that anyone finds a proof that the Mushrikīn believed that their objects of worship share with the Lord of the Worlds in Creation and Origination and Governance and Giving Life and Causing Death and other than that. This is not possible.

So they call upon them so that they be intermediaries to intercede for them. For this reason Allah greatly repeated the refutation against them regarding this very matter of intercession; because the intercession is the Shirk which he calls upon them. "or 'Have they taken intercessor besides Allāh? Say: Even if they possess nothing and do not reason?' then He says: 'Say: To Allah belongs all intercession'.

So Shirk came from this type, all the Shirk of the Mushrikīn. his saying that if one calls upon the buried person so that he may intercede for him, or that he may make du‘āʾ to Allah for him, or the like, that this is merely a bidʿah—this is contrary; this is contrary to the state that the mushrikīn were upon, and contrary to what Allah has informed us of. So it is not correct.


عَنْ النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمْ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ

3247 سنن الترمذي

al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Duʿāʾ  is worship". Then he recited: “And your Lord said: ‘Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too arrogant for My worship will enter Hell, humiliated.’”

[al-Tirmidhī in Sunan al-Tirmidhī 3247]

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān said:

And his statement: “lā sharīka lahu (there is no partner to Him)” is an emphasis of negation; meaning that devotion to Him negates any sharing with Him in anything of devotion .

And there is no partner to Him in turning to Him or ʿibādah (worship), so it is necessary for the servant to be knowing and acting upon its meaning and what it indicates.

From this it becomes clear that those who do not know its meaning fall into apparent contradictions: you find them, for example, saying “lā ilāha illa Allāh” while performing ṭawāf around the graves, seeking istighāthah from their occupants, and calling upon them secretly and openly.

And this is the shirk akbar which this statement nullifies. If they were of those who truly knew its meaning and knew what it signifies, they would not do such actions. Even the kuffār of old used to know its meaning.

[Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān 1/84]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4300 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000566 -->

Does the shahada benefit one who doesn’t know its meaning?

Shaykh ʿAbdullāh Al-Ghunaymān said:

One category is those who do not benefit from saying it, because they did not say it with knowledge, truthfulness, and sincerity; rather, they said it only by imitation and habit. By ijmāʿ, this does not benefit them.

For example, if a man does not know the meaning and does not know the language, but he hears people saying something and then says it with his tongue—meaning, he hears them saying “lā ilāha illā Allāh”, so he says it with his tongue while not knowing its implication or its meaning.

Likewise, he sees people praying ṣalāh, so he prays; sees people fasting, so he fasts; and sees them performing ḥajj, so he performs ḥajj, while not knowing the meaning and not knowing what is intended. Would such a person be considered a Muslim? The answer is that he is not a Muslim. It is necessary that a Muslim be aware of what is in his heart and believe that the religion of Islam is true.

Mere utterance does not benefit. It is well known that people differ in levels of knowledge, and likewise in their utterance of this statement. Thus, the ḥādīth came indicating the differing levels among people, and there is no contradiction between the ḥādīth.

[Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh ʿAbdullāh al-Ghunaymān 1/98]

Shaykh ʿAbdullāh Al-Ghunaymān said:

Abandoning the ṣalāh contradicts the statement lā ilāha illā Allāh. The statement lā ilāha illā Allāh does not combine with abandoning ṣalāh—ever. And likewise it is said regarding the other aḥādīth. Because from the greatest forms of worship is performing ṣalāh—with khushūʿ (humility), raghbah (hope), and rahbah (fear).

As for a person whose heart is devoted to Allah, truthful, certain, and sincere, yet he does not pray—this is not possible. It is not possible at all. It is impossible. And assuming the existence of a person who says lā ilāha illā Allāh while not praying is an invalid assumption, because it combines contradictions, matters that are mutually contradictory.

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Muḥsin al-ʿAbbād was asked:

Q: We have people in our country who go to shrines and graves for duʿāʾ , tamassuḥ (seeking blessings by touching), and request of good. Does this make them kafir in a definite sense?

A: A person who performs Istighāthah with the inhabitants of the grave and asks them to fulfill needs or remove hardships — this is the right of Allah. And the right of Allah is not to be diverted except to Him. It cannot be directed to anyone else. So whoever does this should not be prayed behind if he were an imām.

And his ṣalāh is invalid in the sense that it is not correct to follow him. Whoever worships besides Allah, performs Istighāthah from other than Allah, or asks for fulfillment of needs from anyone other than Allah — this person is kāfir. That is, one does not pray behind him and he is treated like the kuffār.

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

Whoever believes in some of the Book and disbelieves in some; or believes in some of the messengers and disbelieves in some of them; or believes in some of the scriptures and disbelieves in some of them; or believes in some of the Qur’ān and disbelieves in some of it; or believes in some of what the Messenger came with and disbelieves in some of it — then he is a kāfir by ijmā‘, and a kāfir in all of it, and it does not benefit him that he believed in some of it.

And with this is removed the doubt which this person mentioned, which is his statement: “We testify that lā ilāha illā Allāh, and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh, and we believe in the resurrection, and we believe the Messenger, and we perform ḥajj and we fast and we give charity.”

We say to him: this does not benefit you; because if you call upon other than Allāh, your tawḥīd and īmān are nullified. So if you call upon the righteous, and you say: “Yā Sayyidī al-Badawī, help me,” or “Yā Sayyidī yā Rasūl Allāh,” or “Yā ‘Abd al-Qādir, madad madad,” or you slaughter or vow for them — you have committed kufr, and you have committed shirk with Allāh, and you have exited from the millah of Islām, and you have become a mushrik, and your tawḥīd and your īmān have been nullified.

An example of that: a person performs wuḍū’ and perfects the wuḍū’, then urine or feces or wind comes out from him — he is no longer upon purity, rather it has been nullified; the impurity has nullified it. Likewise, a person who says: “I testify lā ilāha illā Allāh, and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh,” and he prays and fasts, then he slaughters for other than Allāh or calls upon other than Him — his tawḥīd is nullified by this shirk and is removed. For shirk nullifies tawḥīd and īmān, just as impurity nullifies purity and corrupts it. We ask Allāh for safety and well-being.

[Shurūḥ Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Mujaddid Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb by Shaykh ar-Rājihī 2/359-360]

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

Al-shafā‘ah (intercession) only occurs under two conditions:

First: permission from Allāh for the shāfi‘ (intercessor).

Second: approval for the one for whom intercession is sought. Allāh does not permit anyone to be taken out of the Fire except for the sinful muwaḥḥidīn, and Allāh only approves of those upon tawḥīd and sincerity.

As for the kāfir, Allāh does not approve of him, and no one can intercede for him. Whoever dies upon shirk without dying upon tawḥīd has no share in al-shafā‘ah. Allāh says: “So no intercession of intercessors will be of any use to them.” [al-Muddaththir: 48].

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message4132 -->

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

“Whoever says: lā ilāha illā Allāh and disbelieves in what is worshipped besides Allāh, his wealth and blood become inviolable …”

This is among the greatest clarifications of the meaning of lā ilāha illā Allāh, for mere utterance of it is not what makes a person’s blood and wealth inviolable; nor is mere knowledge of its meaning along with uttering it; nor mere acknowledgement of it; nor merely that he does not supplicate except to Allāh alone with no partner. Rather, his wealth and blood do not become inviolable until he adds to all of that disbelief in whatever is worshipped besides Allāh.

Meaning: these five matters are required, as previously mentioned:

1. Uttering this statement.

2. Knowing its meaning.

3. Acknowledging it.

4. That he does not worship anyone except Allāh.

5. That he disbelieves in whatever is worshipped besides Allāh, meaning: complete disavowal of every object of worship other than Allāh.

If he hesitates or doubts regarding any one of these five, then he is not a person of tawḥīd. So if he doubts or withholds judgement, then his wealth and blood do not become inviolable.

Meaning: if he doubts the obligation of disavowal from every object of worship besides Allāh, or hesitates concerning whether those objects worshipped besides Allāh are true or not true, or he withholds judgement, then his wealth and blood are not inviolable. What a tremendous issue this is! And what an exceptionally clear clarification it is! And what a decisive proof it is against the one who disputes it!

[at-Tanḍīd Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ar-Rājihī p.100-101]

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

The Prophet ﷺ was sent by Allah to a people who were divided in their acts of worship. Among them were those who worshipped idols, trees, stones, the sun, or the moon.

Among them were those who worshipped the Prophets, the awliyāʾ, and the righteous.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ takfired them, made their blood and wealth lawful, and fought them, as Allah, the Most High, said: “And fight against them until there is no fitnah until the religion, all of it, is for Allāh.” [al-Anfāl: 39]

Fitnah here means shirk. That is, fight them until shirk is removed. He did not differentiate between them.

So whoever worships stones, trees, the sun, the moon, the righteous, or the angels, they are all mushrikūn, they are all to be fought, and they are all upon falsehood.

Therefore, everyone who worships other than Allah is a mushrik and a kāfir.

[Shurūḥ Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Mujaddid Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb by Shaykh ar-Rājihī 1/141]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3763 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000574 -->

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

ʿibādah (worship) is a comprehensive term that includes everything that Allāh loves and is pleased with—of sayings and actions, both outward and inward. It includes everything the Sharʿ commands or forbids. It is the performance of commands and the abandonment of prohibitions out of devotion to Allāh. Thus, duʿāʾ, slaughtering, vows, and ṭawāf of the House are all forms of ʿibādah, and so are other acts. ʿIbādah is of many kinds, and among the greatest of them is duʿāʾ. So if you direct any part of it to other than Allāh, you have fallen into shirk.

And read His saying, the Exalted: “So do not call upon other god along with Allāh, or you will be among those punished.” (ash-Shuʿarāʾ :213) And His saying: “And do not call upon, besides Allāh, that which neither benefits you nor harms you; for if you do so, then indeed you will be among the wrongdoers.” (Yūnus: 106)

And His saying: "And the masājid are for Allāh alone, so do not call upon anyone along with Allāh.” (al-Jinn :18) And His saying: “And those, whom you invoke or call upon instead of Him, own not even a Qitmîr (the thin membrane over the date-stone).  If you call upon them, they hear not your call; and if (in case) they were to hear, they could not grant it (your request) to you. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will disown your worshipping them. And none can inform you (Muhammad ﷺ) like Him Who is the All-Knower (of everything).” (Fāṭir :13–14)

And His saying: "And whoever calls upon another god besides Allāh for which he has no proof - then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.” (al-Muʾminūn :117) The texts are many regarding the prohibition of calling upon other than Allāh, for duʿāʾ is among the greatest acts of ʿibādah.

And you, O mushrik, have not understood the ʿibādah for which Allāh created you, since you claim that seeking refuge in the righteous and calling upon them is not ʿibādah.

In fact, it is ʿibādah itself.  It is narrated from an-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr that he said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say, “Duʿāʾ is ʿibādah.” Then he recited: “And your Lord said: "Call upon Me, and I will respond to you. Verily! Those who scorn My worship they will surely enter Hell in humiliation!’” (Ghāfir :60)¹

[Shurūḥ Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Mujaddid Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb by Shaykh ar-Rājihī 2/318-319]

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī was asked:

Q: Is the ṣalāh valid behind an imām who performs istighāthah from the dead and asks them for aid, or not?

A: This man is a kāfir. Whoever performs istighāthah from the dead and asks them for aid, and asks them for fulfillment of needs and relief of hardships, is a mushrik. The ṣalāh behind him is not valid, and praying behind him is invalid.

Whoever prayed behind him without knowing his condition, then later comes to know it, must repeat the ṣalāh. This is by the ijmāʿ of the Muslims that prayer is not valid behind a mushrik.

The disagreement among the scholars regarding the validity of praying behind a fāsiq (open sinner):

1.    The Ḥanābilah and a group of scholars prohibit praying behind him and say it is not valid.

2.   Others say it is valid but disliked.

The correct view is that it is valid, but praying behind a upright person is better. This is if he is a muwaḥḥid (monotheist) but sinful. As for the mushrik, prayer behind him is not valid by ijmāʿ.

[Asʾilah wa Ajwibah fī al-Īmān wa al-Kufr by Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī p.35]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2545 -->

Ruling by other than Allah

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āsh-Shaykh said:

This issue—namely, the matter of seeking judgment (taḥākum) by other than the law of Allah—is one in which much confusion occurs, especially among the youth in this country and elsewhere. It is one of the causes of division among Muslims, because people have not viewed it through a unified lens. It is incumbent upon the student of knowledge to seek what the evidences indicate, to understand what the scholars have explained from those evidences, and to comprehend the principles of Sharīʿah and tawḥīd that they derived and clarified in these matters.

One of the causes of confusion is that some have treated the matter of ḥukm (judgment) and taḥākum as a single case. That is, they have viewed it as one single form, while in fact, it comprises multiple scenarios. Among these is the scenario in which independent legislation is enacted to rival the law of Allah, exalted is He. The creation of such a code, in and of itself, is kufr. The one who enacts it, legislates it, supports it, attributes it to himself, and issues rulings based on it—this person is a disbeliever, and his disbelief is clear. That is because he has made himself a ṭāghūt, calling people to worship him through obedience, and he is content with that.

Then there is the one who judges by that legislation—this is a second case. So we have the legislator (al-musharriʿ), the judge who rules by it, the one who seeks judgment through it, and the state or entity that enforces it upon its population—making it a fourth case.

Thus, we are faced with four distinct situations. First is the legislator who permits what Allah has forbidden and forbids what Allah has permitted, opposing the Sharīʿah—this is a disbeliever. Whoever obeys him in this has taken him as a lord (rabb) besides Allah.

As for the judge who rules by such legislation, the matter requires detail. If he rules by it once, or even several times, but it is not his regular practice—and he knows that he is sinning by ruling by other than Allah’s law—then he is treated like other sinners. He is not to be declared a disbeliever unless he deems it permissible (istihlāl). That is why some scholars say: the one who rules by other than what Allah has revealed does not become a disbeliever unless he considers it lawful. This is correct. However, this does not apply to the case of codification and legislation.

As Ibn ʿAbbās said: “It is not the disbelief that you imagine. It is kufr dūna kufr (a lesser form of disbelief).” Meaning: the one who rules in one or two matters by desire, rather than by Allah’s law—while knowing that he is disobedient and does not deem it permissible—this is kufr dūna kufr.

As for the ruler who never judges by the Sharīʿah at all, and consistently rules by other than it, and enforces it upon the people—some scholars have said that he is a disbeliever, absolutely, just like the one who legislated such laws. Allah, exalted is He, said: “They wish to seek judgment from the ṭāghūt…” (al-Nisāʾ: 60), thus declaring the one who judges exclusively by other than Allah’s law to be a ṭāghūt, and He also said: “They were commanded to reject it.” (al-Nisāʾ: 60)

Some scholars, however, have said that even this type does not disbelieve unless he deems it lawful, as he may act upon it while believing in his heart that he is sinful. In that case, he is like the habitual sinner who has not repented. But the correct opinion—according to me—is the first one: that whoever consistently rules by other than Allah’s law and obliges the people to follow it, is a disbeliever. This was also the opinion of my grandfather, Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm in his treatise Taḥkīm al-Qawānīn. For such rulings do not come from a heart that has rejected the ṭāghūt—rather, they stem from a heart that reveres the law and glorifies ruling by it.

The third situation is the case of the mutaḥākimīn—those who seek judgment. That is, someone and his opponent go together to be judged by secular law. This also requires clarification.

It is known and established in the Kitāb of Allah and in the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ that Allah, jalla wa-ʿalā, sent all the messengers and dispatched the prophets for the worship of Allah alone, without partner.

And He created the heavens and the earth, He created the celestial bodies, and He created everything — and He did not permit worship of anyone besides Him.

And this is a necessity that does not require from a person a detailed proof, for he perceives it within himself and he perceives it in what surrounds him.

Shaykh Khālid al-Mushayqiḥ was asked:

Q: Is this expression correct or not? Some people say that making takfīr of the mushrikīn and apostates is not from the foundation of the religion, meaning that making takfīr of the grave-worshippers is not from the foundation of the religion. Are these words correct or not?

A: No, no, these words are not correct. Allah, the Most High, declared them as kuffār: “Surely, disbelievers are those who said: "Allâh is the third of the three (in a Trinity)."  [al-Māʾidah: 73]

“Those who disbelieve from among the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and the Mushrikûn, were not going to leave (their disbelief) until there came to them clear evidence.” [al-Bayyinah: 1]

“Surely, in disbelief are they who say that Allâh is the Messiah, son of Maryam” [al-Māʾidah: 17]

Q: They say that making takfīr of the one who associates partners with Allah, meaning the grave-worshippers, is not from the foundation of the religion.

They say it is obligatory, but not from the foundation of the religion. And they say that whoever says it is from the foundation of the religion is from the Khawārij.

A: No, this is not correct. Also, if we say that it is obligatory, then this itself indicates that it is from the foundation of the religion.

Dr. Ayman al-ʿAnqarī said:

The Intended Meaning of the One Who Abandons Tawḥīd

He is the one who falls into a nullifier from the nullifiers of the statement of tawḥīd: Lā ilāha illa Allāh, whether that nullifier is in the domain of rubūbiyyah—such as believing in a god, creator alongside Allāh, or denying the existence of Allāh, or believing that among the awliyāʾ and imāms are those who control the universe, or that Allāh has delegated the management of the affairs of the world to the saints and imāms.

And among that: to believe that the one who brought this child into being is such-and-such saint or the occupant of such-and-such shrine—because in this is attributing creation to other than Allāh, exalted is He.

And among that: the statement of the doctrine of waḥdat al-wujūd—that Allāh and the universe are one entity, and that Allāh—exalted and far above that—is this very universe in itself, with everything in it from among the created beings. Or if it is in the domain of ulūhiyyah — such as calling upon and istighāthah from the Prophet ﷺ or from the saints in matters that no one is capable of except Allāh—such as fulfilling needs, removing hardships, and guiding hearts. Or requesting intercession from the Prophet ﷺ by saying: “O Messenger of Allāh, intercede for me with Allāh.”

Or approaching al-Badawī or al-Dusūqī or al-Ḥusayn or ʿAlī and saying: “Madad, madad” or “Rescue me” or “Cure me of my illness,” or offering a sacrifice to the occupant of the grave out of veneration for him. Or a woman who cannot conceive goes to those called awliyāʾ and requests from them to become pregnant, saying: “O Master so-and-so, grant me a child.” Or seeking blessings from the graves of the saints with the belief that they elevate needs to Allāh, exalted is He, Or performing ṭawāf around the graves of the awliyāʾ out of glorification and drawing near to them, Or making a vow to other than Allāh. This is what is meant here by abandoning tawḥīd.

[Taḥrīr qawl al-shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿUthaymīn fī tārik al-tawḥīd by Dr. Ayman al-ʿAnqarī p.16-17]

Fatawa of Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Jarbūʿ on ṭalab al-du‘ā’

I asked: As-salāmu ‘alaykum wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh.

Our respected Shaykh, I hope you are well. I have a question: We know that whoever excuses the mushrik and calls him a Muslim is undoubtedly among the ghulāt al-murji’ah. However, some people have confusion regarding the issue of ṭalab al-du‘ā’ due to a misunderstanding of Ibn Taymiyyah’s words when he referred to it as a bid‘ah. How should we deal with them? Should they be treated the same as in the first issue, or is this dealt with differently?

We know that if something is a bid‘ah, it can lead to excusing the mushrik in his shirk, and this is one of the doubts used by the murji’ah to justify excusing the mushrik. But how do we deal with those who fell into this doubt because of some statements from the scholars on this matter, where they claim that there is khilāf (difference of opinion) about it?

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Jarbūʿ responded:

Wa ‘alaykum as-salām wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh.

It is a bid‘ah and it is shirk — it is both a bid‘ah and shirk. When speaking with people who claim it is obligatory and legislated, the response is: it is not legislated, but rather a bid‘ah. When Shaykh al-Islām discussed the rulings concerning it, he said: such a person is a kāfir, and if he repents, then it is accepted, but if not, he is to be executed. At another time, he said: it is kufr by the consensus of the Muslims. So it is both a bid‘ah and kufr.

As for those people, they should be taught. Tell them to learn and to gather the strongest statements of Shaykh al-Islām on the issue.

Saying it is a bid‘ah does not mean it is not shirk. No—it is a bid‘ah that is shirk.

I asked Shaykh Manṣūr as-Samarī:

Q: as-Salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh

We hope you are well, Shaykh. This question was raised by some brothers: The matter of ṭawāf around graves: is the act of ṭawāf kufr by itself, or must the intention of drawing near be taken into account?

For example, may Allāh preserve you: if we see someone performing ṭawāf around a grave, should we call this person mushrik, or should we refrain from applying the label of shirk until their intention is known — whether it was to draw near to Allāh or just for another reason?

Scholars have stated that a person may be a mubtadiʿ if their intention in the circumambulation is to draw near to Allāh, and may be kāfir if their intention is to draw near to the deceased. We would like to know: should a person like this be judged as mushrik before their intention is known, or is the correct approach to say they are Muslim until their intention is known?

A: Wa ʿalaykum as-salām wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh.

The one performing ṭawāf around  the grave, meaning that he does ṭawāf  around the grave while knowing it is a grave — that is, he intentionally wants to perform tawāf around this grave. If this is done as an act of seeking nearness to the owner of the grave, then he is a mushrik. And if it is not for the sake of Allāh, they say he is kāfir, because he has fallen into a bidʿah mukaffirah.

Because tawāf is only valid around the Kaʿbah for Allāh, and this person performed tawāf around a place other than the Kaʿbah, claiming nearness to Allāh. They say this is a bidʿah, and it is a bidʿah that takes one out of Islām according to some scholars. In the words of Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah, the principle is that the qiblah before the Kaʿbah was Bayt al-Maqdis, then it changed to the Kaʿbah. As for tawāf, there is no tawāf except around the Kaʿbah, before and after.

So he says: whoever innovates tawāf around anything other than the Kaʿbah — like someone facing a qiblah other than the Kaʿbah — it is even more severe. And it is more severe than facing a qiblah other than the Kaʿbah in Ṣalāh. If someone faces something other than the Kaʿbah intentionally, he is an mubtadiʿ.  Some say he is not declared kāfir, others say he is. This is because he deliberately intends to set a qiblah other than the Kaʿbah. And this is what they call a bidʿah mukaffirah. Even if he claims it is all for the sake of Allāh, it is still considered a bidʿah that takes him out of the fold of Islam according to these scholars.


A side benefit: this opinion is held by shaykh al-Fawzān amongst few others. Shaykh Ibn Bāz, Shaykh Al-Jarbū and others held the position that the persons intent should be clarified first regarding ṭawāf. This was narrated to me Shaykh Al-Jarbū himself on 13th Rmdn 1447AH.

Although as the mashaykh have also said, the majority of those who perform ṭawāf around the grave are those who wish to draw closer to the grave and rare exception has no ruling. This was mentioned to me by Shaykh ʿAbd Al-Latīf al-Rawī. Allahu A'lam

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Sindī said:

Take care—may Allāh guard you—to understand five issues with a precise understanding; for indeed you will be, by the permission of Allāh upon great goodness and knowledge of the truth regarding Tawḥīd and its opposite.

First: That you know what is the Tawḥīd to which the Prophet ﷺ called.

And second: That you know what is the Shirk which the Prophet ﷺ used to warn against.

And third: That you know the state of the Mushrikīn among whom the Prophet ﷺ was sent. How did they perform worship? And with what thing did they perform worship with? And what were their conditions with their gods? There must be a deep understanding of the state of the Mushrikīn among whom the Prophet ﷺ was sent. Indeed there—perhaps there was—a mistaken concept with some people, so this led him to the fact that he did not understand the proof with a correct understanding.

The fourth matter: That you know what is the ʿIbādah upon which [the matter] revolves... that you know the ʿIbādah. What is the thing which Allāh commanded us with often? 'And worship Allāh and do not associate anything with Him.' Understanding the meaning of ʿIbādah is of great importance. The defect in understanding 'What is ʿIbādah?' will lead to the defect in understanding the reality of Tawḥīd and the reality of Shirk.

The fifth matter: That you grasp the difference between the two Tawḥīds: al-Rubūbiyyah and al-Ulūhiyyah. And that you know: Is there a correlation between them? And what is the reality of this correlation? Is it a correlationfrom the aspect of necessity andinference? Or is it a correlation in reality?

This matter is of great importance, and much of the deception of the Mushrikīn—of old and of new—comes from the direction of this issue between the two Tawḥīds: al-Rubūbiyyah and al-Ulūhiyyah. And the author—raḥimahu Allāh—will guide you to great principles related to this subject. Therefore, the knowledge of Tawḥīd and the knowledge of Shirk, and the grasping of that—O Muwaḥḥid —is by the Tawfīq of Allāh, through the knowledge of four Qawāʿid derived from the Kitāb of Allāh and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ."

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3228 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000593 -->

Shaykh Abdullah Ibn Zayd said:

These two great verses, or this great verse, indicate a profound matter, which is exactly what the author—who speaks the truth—intends to clarify and explain. It contains a response to the doubt raised by those mushrikīn , the worshippers of graves and saints, who are many in our time. We see them performing pilgrimage and ʿumrah , yet they say: “O so-and-so, heal me. O so-and-so, grant me health. O so-and-so, remove this from me. I come to you in supplication, fearful and anxious; remove the affliction and disease from me.”

This is a greater shirk because they call upon and seek help from other than Allah. Even if they perform Hajj, fast, and give zakah, it benefits them nothing, because they have associated others with Allah, the Most High. Whoever associates anyone with Allah, Allah does not forgive him; He will nullify all his deeds of prayer and worship: “But if you associate others with Me, surely your deeds will become worthless, and you will surely be among the losers.” [Quran 39:65]

This verse and the following one are perfectly suited to refute this great doubt and misguidance of these people, because the strongest doubt they hold onto is this one. You always find those who worship graves nowadays—those who visit saints, light candles by their graves, circumambulate them, seek help from them, and slaughter for them. If you ask them why they do this, they say: “They are intermediaries with Allah, interceding for us; we have sins and faults, and we cannot reach the door of Allah, so we make them intercessors to intercede on our behalf.”

This response firmly closes the door on this great doubt. The verses respond strongly to this great doubt which these people cling to. True shafāʿah (intercession) is only for those who are from the people of tawḥīd , from the people of faith, whose deeds please Allah. Allah only accepts the deeds of the muwaḥḥidīn (monotheists), the believers, the Muslims. As for the mushrik , Allah does not accept his deeds: “They do not intercede except for one whom He approves.” [Quran 2:255]

Those servants, those graves, those idols, those prophets, angels, righteous people, and others do not benefit or harm, do not intercede, and do not possess any intercession. They cannot benefit themselves nor intercede for others. All intercession belongs to Allah alone, and they only intercede by His permission. This verse, as mentioned earlier, refutes the mushrikīn who think that intercession is taken from creatures or sought from these saints, righteous people, angels, or others. It clearly indicates that intercession is for Allah alone, and if it is for Allah, then one should ask only Him.

They unanimously agreed on the leadership (Imamate) of Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali (peace be upon them). And they give precedence to the first two caliphs (Abu Bakr and Umar). They also unanimously agreed that the ten who were promised Paradise are certainly and undoubtedly in Paradise.

This, and similar matters, which would be lengthy to explain, has been unanimously agreed upon by people since Allah sent His Prophet ﷺ until our time, in the East and West, on land and sea, in plains and mountains. It is transmitted by scholars, hadith transmitters, and those who record historical accounts, known by the learned and the wise, and accepted by men and women, the elderly and the young, the adults and the children, in both urban and rural areas, among Arabs and non-Arabs. No one opposes this, denies it, or deviates from the consensus except a wicked, deviant, innovator, despicable, abandoned, and accursed person, whom the scholars shun, and the wise avoid. How is tashrīʿ (legislation) understood in the above?

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āl-Shaykh was asked:

Question 123: What is the criterion for tashrīʿ (legislation)? Is it legislating a single matter, or up to 50%? Some people may legislate within their own homes and impose things upon their families — is this considered tashrīʿ and a replacement of Allah’s religion?

Answer: No, this is not tashrīʿ. What is the meaning of tashrīʿ (legislating)? Tashrīʿ, as mentioned, is to make ḥarām something that is ḥalāl, and to believe in its prohibition. Declaring something that is ḥalāl to be ḥarām — this is tashrīʿ. This is kufr.

But if someone says, “This isn’t your concern,” or “Don’t say it’s ḥarām,” or “It’s not ḥarām — we will do it, and you stay out of it,” then what he has done is merely impose his desire upon others. He hasn’t legislated. A legislator (musharriʿ) is someone who changes a ruling and says, “This is not such-and-such — it is instead this.” That’s tashrīʿ — changing the agreed-upon ruling of Allah while knowing what Allah’s ruling is, and then stating otherwise.

But all sinners — except those whom Allah guides — act arrogantly. They are too proud even to be reasoned with. Even, for example, a man in his home may be debating with his son, and the son may provoke his father to say something terrible. This is not birr (righteousness or dutifulness). That is why Allah said to His believing servants: “And do not insult those they invoke besides Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge.” (Sūrat al-Anʿām, 6:108)

[al-Ajwibah wa-al-Buḥūth wa-al-Mudārasāt al-Mushtamilah ʿalayhā al-Durūs al-ʿIlmiyyah 2/178]

## 11. Istighāthah, Ṭalab al-Duʿāʾ, and Tawassul

Every unique substantive statement from the personal Istighatha/Tawasul Telegram topic and the relevant Dār as-Salafiyyah #tawḥīd posts is included below. <!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message3161 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000597 -->

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

One of the gravest forms is that a person calls upon other than Allāh — while the one being called is either dead or absent — whether he be from the prophets, the righteous, or anyone else. He says things like: “Yā Sayyidī Fulān, help me,” or “I seek refuge with you,” or “I seek your aid,” or “Support me against my enemy,” and similar expressions. This is shirk with Allāh.

As for the one who seeks istighāthah from created beings, the shayṭān may fulfill his need, or part of it, and may appear to him in the form of the one whom he sought help from. The person then assumes that what occurred was a karāmah granted to the one he called upon, but it is only a shayṭān who entered and misled him because he committed shirk with Allāh — just as the shayṭān speaks through idols, or through the possessed, and so on. Such events are widespread in our time and in others.

I personally know of many such cases — too numerous to describe — where people sought istighāthah from me or from others, and later reported that someone came to them in my likeness or the likeness of another person, fulfilled their needs, and they believed that this was from the blessing of istighāthah. But in reality, it was only a shayṭān who misled and deceived them. This is the very origin of idol worship and of taking partners with Allāh in the earliest generations, as has been clearly established. Such a person has committed shirk with Allāh — we seek refuge in Allāh from that.

And even worse than this is when someone says, “Forgive me” or “Accept my repentance”, as is done by a group of ignorant mushrikīn.

[Majmū al-Fatāwa 1/350-351 by Ibn Taymiyyah]

Shaykh Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad said:

Know that tawassul through the essence (dhāt) of a created being, or through their rank, is not the same as asking them or making duʿāʾ to them. Tawassul through their essence or their jāh is when one says: “O Allāh, forgive me, have mercy on me, admit me to Paradise through Your Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ,” or “through the rank of Your Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ,” and the like. This is an bid‘ah, not shirk.

But asking them and making duʿāʾ to them is when one says: “O Messenger of Allāh, I ask You for intercession,” or “I am in great distress, relieve me,” or “I seek protection with You from so-and-so, help me,” and the like. This is Kufr and shirk al-akbar that takes the person out of the millah, because it diverts the right of Allāh to someone else. Du‘āʾ is an act of worship that is valid only for Allāh. Whoever calls upon another has in effect worshipped them, and whoever worships other than Allāh has committed shirk.

The evidences for this are too many to enumerate. Many people do not distinguish between tawassul through a created being or through their rank, and asking or making duʿāʾ to them. Understand this, and may Allāh guide us and you to follow the best of paths.

[Ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 3/165-166]

Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān Ibn Ḥasan said:

Shaykh al-Islām (Ibn Taymiyyah), may Allāh have mercy on him, said: “Building mosques on graves is prohibited, and even if something other than a mosque is built on them, it is prohibited by the consensus of scholars, as it is a means to shirk and a forbidden act.”

He also said: “Know that the term ‘du’ā’ in the Qur’ān refers to two meanings: the ‘du’ā’ of worship’ and the ‘du’ā’ of asking.’ Every worshipper is a seeker, and every seeker is a supplicant. One term can encompass the other when separated from its context, and when both meanings are combined, it refers to one who asks for the seeking of benefits and the removal of harm through the forms of asking and requesting.”

I (Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān Ibn Ḥasan) say: Look at this contradiction, confusion, and inconsistency. There is no doubt that disbelief opposes faith, invalidates it, and nullifies deeds, as confirmed by the Qur’ān, Sunnah, and the consensus of Muslims. Allāh, the Exalted, says: “And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deeds are invalid, and he is among the losers in the Hereafter.” (Al-Mā’idah: 5).

It is said that every disbeliever is mistaken, and the polytheists have their justifications. They believe that their polytheism towards the righteous is an act of honoring them that benefits them and wards off harm. But Allāh did not excuse them for this mistake or misinterpretation. Allāh says: “And those who take protectors besides Him say, ‘We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allāh.’

Allāh will judge between them concerning what they differ.” (Az-Zumar: 3). And He also says: “Say, ‘Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose efforts have been wasted in this worldly life while they think that they are doing good.’” (Al-Kahf: 103-104). Where is the reason of this person in relation to these and similar clear verses?

The scholars, may Allāh have mercy on them, followed the path of uprightness and discussed the ruling of apostasy. None of them said that if a person commits an act of disbelief or says something of disbelief while not knowing that it contradicts the testimony of faith, he is not considered a disbeliever due to his ignorance.

And Allāh has clarified in His Book that some of the polytheists are ignorant followers, yet their ignorance and blind imitation did not prevent them from facing Allāh’s punishment, as He said:  “And among the people is he who disputes about Allāh without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil … to His saying: ‘The punishment of the Blaze.’” [Al-Ḥajj: 3-4]

Shaykh Ibn Bāz was asked:

Question: Many students understand that shirk is limited to asking the dead to fulfill one’s needs. But if one asks them for intercession, meaning to make Duʿāʾ for them, they think this is not shirk al-akbar, but rather an bidʿah.

Answer: No, this is still shirk al-akbar. The reason is that the dead cannot make Duʿāʾ for anyone, nor can they intercede. All of them are bound by their own deeds. Duʿāʾ and intercession are only valid in life. That is why when ʿUmar and the Companions asked for rain, they did not ask the Prophet ﷺ to intercede for them after his death. Instead, they sought it through ʿAbbās, Yazīd ibn al-Aswad, and by Duʿāʾ. If it were lawful to seek rain or intercession from the Prophet ﷺ in his grave, they would have said: “make Duʿāʾ for us, O Messenger of Allah,” but they did not.

[Sharḥ Kashf ash-Shubuhāt by Shaykh Ibn Bāz p.53]

Ṭalab ad-Duʿāʾ (requesting Duʿāʾ) from the dead is Shirk Akbar

Shaykh Ibn Bāz was asked:

Q: “A person comes to a grave and asks the one in it to make du‘ā’ for him to Allah—what is the ruling?”

A: “The same applies. He (the deceased) does not possess that. If someone says, ‘Intercede for me, or make du‘ā’ for me,’ this is shirk, without any doubt—because the deceased does not possess the ability to do that (i.e. to say) ‘Make du‘ā’ to Allah for me,’ or ‘Intercede for me’.

Q: “If he says to the grave: ‘Make du‘ā’ for me to Allah’?”

A: “This is not permissible. This is shirk, for he is requesting from the deceased what he cannot do. His affair (i.e., his ability to act) has ended.”

Q: “Some people claim this is the statement of Ibn Taymiyyah— is this correct, Shaykh?”

A: “Yes; he did not lie. Ibn Taymiyyah explicitly stated this. Ibn Taymiyyah made it clear that this is shirk akbar.”

[Subul as-Salām Sharḥ Nawāqiḍ al-Islām by Shaykh Ibn Bāz p.84-85]

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

Q: “Some people say: ‘O Muhammad,’ or ‘O ʿAlī,’ or ‘O Jīlānī’ in times of distress. What is the ruling?”

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3723 -->

Some of the Murji’ah use the claim of hidden shirk to excuse the mushrikĩn, they say Istighathā falls into this category, that it is hidden shirk. What did Our Imām’s Ibn Bāz and Ibn ‘Uthaymīn say regarding hidden shirk and what it is?

Shaykh Ibn Bāz was asked:

Question:

Your Eminence, you have mentioned shirk al-akbar (major shirk) and shirk al-asghar (minor shirk) — but what is shirk al-khafī (Hidden shirk), since some scholars have said that shirk is “more hidden than the crawling of a black ant on a smooth black stone”?

Answer:

Hidden shirk is of two types:

The first type is shirk al-asghar — and this is riyāʼ, for its place is in the hearts. It is called hidden shirk because it is subtle and often concealed, and it is also called minor shirk because it does not expel one from Islām, though it diminishes the sincerity of worship.

The second type is another form of hidden shirk, which is the shirk of hypocrisy — and we seek refuge with Allāh from it. This occurs within the hearts, when people conceal disbelief and misguidance, deny Allāh and His Messenger, and believe the message of the Prophet ﷺ to be false. This is major hypocrisy and constitutes shirk al-akbar and apostasy from Islām — we seek refuge with Allāh.

It is the hypocrisy of the munāfiqūn (hypocrites) — their showing off is the riyāʼ of the hypocrites, and their disbelief is the kufr of the hypocrites; outwardly they are with the Muslims, but inwardly they are with the disbelievers through their corrupt beliefs and their denial of Allāh and His Messenger.

Allāh said regarding them: “In their hearts is a disease, and Allāh has increased their disease.” (Sūrah al-Baqarah, 2:10)

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3280 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Question: Is this statement correct? Those who say that if you ask a dead person to pray for you, it is a form of supplication which is bidʿah and not shirk — is this statement correct?

Answer: This is a false statement. Asking the dead for one’s needs is shirk, and no one disputes this. As for asking the living, who are able to fulfill it, there is no harm — this falls under assistance and cooperation in righteousness and piety. But nothing should be asked from the dead. Rather, supplications are made for them: prayers are asked on their behalf, charity is given for them, Hajj or ʿUmrah may be performed on their behalf. They are in need of others’ supplications; nothing should be requested from them, since they are dead.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3965 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āl ash-Shaykh said:

As for the technical usage: al-shafāʿah (intercession) is a general term for every duʿāʾ that the Prophet ﷺ will make for his ummah on the Day of Resurrection. Every supplication he offers to Allāh in the great gathering on that Day is counted as shafāʿah. This is like what has come in the hadith: “Ummati, ummati” (my ummah, my ummah), or “Ummati yā Rabb” (my ummah, O Lord), and similar expressions. All of these are shafāʿah. For this reason, the scholars classified shafāʿah into several types, due to what appears in the narrations and due to the differing wordings regarding it.

Shafāʿah is duʿāʾ, and Ṭalab ash-shafāʿah (requesting shafāʿah) is Ṭalab ad-Duʿā (requesting duʿāʾ). So if someone says: “I seek istishfāʿ (request for intercession),” it is as if he said: “I ask the Messenger ﷺ to make duʿāʾ for me with Allāh.” Shafāʿah is a request; therefore, whoever seeks istishfāʿ is requesting shafāʿah. Shafāʿah is duʿāʾ, and it is also the seeking of duʿāʾ.

For this reason, every proof previously presented—and every proof in the Book or the Sunnah that invalidates calling upon alongside Allāh any being that is treated like an deity—serves as evidence against shafāʿah of the dead, meaning against istishfāʿ with the dead and with those absent from the realm of responsibility. This is because the true nature of the intercessor is that he is one who requests, and the true nature of the one seeking intercession is also that he is one who requests. In the assumption of the seeker, the shāfiʿ is making duʿāʾ, and the seeker is calling upon the one from whom he seeks shafāʿah.

Meaning: if a person comes to the grave of the Prophet ﷺ, or the grave of a walī, or something similar, and says: “I seek shafāʿah through you,” or “I ask for shafāʿah,” he has requested and called upon that being to make duʿāʾ for him.

For this reason, directing shafāʿah toward other than Allāh becomes major shirk, because in reality it is a duʿāʾ to other than Allāh. In reality it is a request from this dead person—a request, a turning with petition and duʿāʾ to other than Allāh. Thus one directs to other than Allāh what is in essence asking, requesting, and praying.

[Sharḥ Fatḥ al-Majīd li-Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āl ash-Shaykh 2/41-42]

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3397 -->

Shaykh Ayman al-ʿAnqarī said:

A very important issue: What is the ruling on requesting shafāʿah (intercession) and duʿāʾ (supplication) from the dead, such as one saying, “O Messenger of Allāh, ask Allāh for me,” or “supplicate to Allāh for me,” or saying, “O ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī, intercede for me”?

Requesting intercession from the dead is shirk akbar (major shirk), whether at the grave of the dead or from afar.

And Imām Abū al-ʿAbbās Ibn Taymiyyah mentioned in his book Qāʿidah ʿAẓīmah fī al-Farq bayna ʿIbādāt al-Islām wa ʿIbādāt al-Shirk (pp. 31–32) that the way of the Ṣaḥābah (may Allāh be pleased with them) was that they considered this shirk—seeking intercession through the angels, the dead, the prophets, and the righteous. And he mentioned that this was the creed of the Ṣaḥābah (may Allāh be pleased with them) by ijmāʿ.

And also, shafāʿah means request and asking. So when you say, “O Messenger of Allāh, intercede for me,” or “ask Allāh for me,” you have directed to him a type from the types of worship, which is duʿāʾ, and duʿāʾ is not directed except to Allāh. You have directed it to other than Him, so you fell into shirk akbar.

And for this reason, he ﷺ said in the ḥadīth of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr with the people of the Sunan: “Ad-duʿāʾ is worship.” And he brought it with the particle of restriction and the separating pronoun to show exclusivity—that worship is confined within duʿāʾ.

And Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allāh have mercy on him, also pointed out in Qāʿidah ʿAẓīmah fī al-Farq bayna ʿIbādāt al-Islām wa ʿIbādāt al-Shirk (p. 136) an important point in this issue: that they believe, by their requesting from the dead and requesting shafāʿah from them, in a spiritual presence for them, and that they have movement and influence. So the souls of those who invoke them from among the grave-worshippers connect with those dead.

And he referred to that in Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā (vol. 1, p. 167), with his statement:

“And a people from the heretical philosophers of naturalism innovated another form of shirk, which they mentioned concerning the visitation of graves, as Ibn Sīnā mentioned that. And regarding the meaning of shafāʿah, he said: the intercession of the prophets and the righteous, according to the foundation of this idolatrous philosophical belief that Ibn Sīnā and others held, is not as the people of īmān know it—that it is a supplication by which the righteous man supplicates and it is answered—but they claim that the influence in the forces of the world or in the events of the world is the force of the soul, or the movements of the celestial spheres, or the natural force. And man, in their claim, if he loves a righteous man who has died, especially if he visits his grave, then his soul attains a connection with the soul of that dead person, in that which benefits from that separated soul from the ‘active intellect’ according to them.” So his words ended.

This explicit text from Ibn Taymiyyah mentioned a reason for this image—requesting shafāʿah and duʿāʾ from the dead—being shirk, and what the heretical philosophers such as Ibn Sīnā were upon: that they believe in a spiritual presence for the dead, so their souls connect with them, and they believe in their influence in raising their needs to Allāh.

Thus it became clear that the form of requesting shafāʿah and duʿāʾ from the dead is shirk akbar, and it is not an innovation as some people claim at his grave. Rather, it is shirk akbar whether at the shrine of the dead or away from it, as Ibn Taymiyyah mentioned that.
