<!-- evidence-id: 000637 -->
Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

It is well known what newly introduced matters have become widespread and with which people have been afflicted. The gravest of them is associating partners with Allāh: turning to the dead and asking them for victory over enemies, the fulfillment of needs, and the relief of hardships that none can accomplish except the Lord of the earth and the heavens; likewise, drawing near to them through vows and sacrificial offerings, seeking their aid to remove calamities and bring benefits, and other forms of worship that are suitable for none but Allāh.

Directing any single form of worship to other than Allāh is like directing all of it to other than Him, because He is completely free of need for partners and accepts no deed unless it is sincerely devoted to Him. Allāh says: “So worship Allāh, making the religion sincerely His. Unquestionably, the sincere religion belongs to Allāh. As for those who take protectors besides Him, saying, ‘We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to Allāh,’ Allāh will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Allāh does not guide one who is a liar and an obstinate disbeliever.” [Az-Zumar 39:2-3]

He informed us that He accepts no religion except that which is sincerely devoted to Him. He also informed us that the polytheists called upon angels, prophets, and righteous people so that they might bring them nearer to Allāh and intercede for them with Him. He declared them liars and disbelievers in this claim. Allāh also says: “They worship besides Allāh that which neither harms nor benefits them, and they say, ‘These are our intercessors with Allāh.’ Say, ‘Are you informing Allāh of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?’ Glorified and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.” [Yūnus 10:18]

Thus, He informed us that whoever places intermediaries between himself and Allāh and asks them for intercession has worshipped them and associated them with Him. This is because all intercession belongs to Allāh, as He says: “Say, ‘All intercession belongs to Allāh.’” [Az-Zumar 39:44] No one intercedes with Him except by His permission, as He says: “Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?” [Al-Baqarah 2:255] And He says: “On that Day no intercession will benefit except that of one to whom the Most Merciful has granted permission and whose word He approves.” [Ṭā Hā 20:109] He approves nothing but tawḥīd, as He says: “They intercede only for those with whom He is pleased.” [Al-Anbiyāʾ 21:28]

Allāh says: “Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim besides Allāh. They do not possess even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any helper among them. Intercession with Him benefits no one except one to whom He gives permission.’” [Sabaʾ 34:22-23]

Intercession is true, but in this world it is sought only from Allāh. Allāh says: “The places of worship are for Allāh, so do not call upon anyone along with Allāh.” [Al-Jinn 72:18] He also says: “Do not call upon besides Allāh that which can neither benefit nor harm you. If you did so, you would then be among the wrongdoers.” [Yūnus 10:106]

The Messenger ﷺ is the master of the intercessors and the possessor of the praised station, with Adam and everyone after him beneath his banner, yet even he will not intercede except with Allāh’s permission. He will not begin interceding on his own. Rather, he will come and fall in prostration, praise Allāh with praises that Allāh teaches him, and then be told: “Raise your head. Speak and you will be heard. Ask and you will be given. Intercede and your intercession will be accepted.” A limit will then be set for him, and he will admit them into Paradise. What, then, of prophets and righteous people besides him?

No Muslim scholar disagrees with what we have mentioned. The righteous predecessors from among the Companions reached consensus upon it.

Source: al-Durar al-Saniyyah, 1/84-86

<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 84</h4>
<p>وقال تعالى: {وَمَا آتَاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانْتَهُوا} [سورة الحشر آية: 7] ، وقال تعالى: {الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الأِسْلامَ دِيناً} [سورة المائدة آية: 3] . فأخبر سبحانه أنه أكمل الدين، وأتمه على لسان رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم.</p>
<p>وأمرنا بلزوم ما أنزل إلينا من ربنا، وترك البدع، والتفرق، والاختلاف فقال تعالى: {اتَّبِعُوا مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ قَلِيلاً مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ} ، [سورة الأعراف آية: 3] ، وقال تعالى: {وَأَنَّ هَذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيماً فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ} [سورة الأنعام آية: 153] . والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أخبر: بأن &quot; أمته تأخذ مأخذ القرون قبلها، شبرا بشبر، وذراعا بذراع &quot; 1 وثبت في الصحيحين، وغيرهما عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: &quot; لتتبعن سنن من كان قبلكم، حذو القذة بالقذة، حتى لو دخلوا جحر ضب لدخلتموه. قالوا: يا رسول الله، اليهود والنصارى؟ قال: فمن؟ &quot; 2 وأخبر في الحديث الآخر: &quot; أن أمته ستفترق على ثلاث وسبعين فرقة، كلها في النار إلا واحدة، قالوا: من هي يا رسول الله؟ قال: من كان على مثل ما أنا عليه اليوم وأصحابي &quot; 3. إذا عرف هذا، فمعلوم ما قد عمت به البلوى، من حوادث الأمور، التي أعظمها الإشراك بالله، والتوجه إلى</p>
<p>1 البخاري: الاعتصام بالكتاب والسنة (7319) ، وابن ماجه: الفتن (3994) ، وأحمد (2/325 ،2/336 ،2/367) .</p>
<p>2 البخاري: أحاديث الأنبياء (3456) ، ومسلم: العلم (2669) ، وأحمد (3/84 ،3/89) .</p>
<p>3 الترمذي: الإيمان (2641) .</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 85</h4>
<p>الموتى، وسؤالهم النصر على الأعداء، وقضاء الحاجات، وتفريج الكربات، التي لا يقدر عليها إلا رب الأرض والسماوات، وكذلك التقرب إليهم بالنذور، وذبح القربان، والاستغاثة بهم في كشف الشدائد، وجلب الفوائد، إلى غير ذلك من أنواع العبادة التي لا تصلح إلا لله؛ وصرف شيء من أنواع العبادة لغير الله كصرف جميعها، لأنه سبحانه أغنى الشركاء عن الشرك، ولا يقبل من العمل إلا ما كان خالصا، كما قال تعالى: {فَاعْبُدِ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَهُ الدِّينَ أَلا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الْخَالِصُ وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَاّ لِيُقَرِّبُونَا إِلَى اللَّهِ زُلْفَى إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ فِي مَا هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَنْ هُوَ كَاذِبٌ كَفَّارٌ} [سورة الزّمر الآيتان: 2-3] ، فأخبر سبحانه أنه لا يرضى من الدين إلا ما كان خالصا لوجهه; وأخبر: أن المشركين يدعون الملائكة، والأنبياء، والصالحين، ليقربوهم إلى الله زلفى، ويشفعوا لهم عنده. وأخبر أنه لا يهدي من هو كاذب كفار؛ فكذبهم في هذه الدعوى، وكفرهم، فقال: {إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَنْ هُوَ كَاذِبٌ كَفَّارٌ} [سورة الزمر آية: 3] . وقال تعالى: {وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ هَؤُلاءِ شُفَعَاؤُنَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قُلْ أَتُنَبِّئُونَ اللَّهَ بِمَا لا يَعْلَمُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلا فِي الأَرْضِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ} [سورة يونس آية: 18] .</p>
<p>فأخبر أن من جعل بينه وبين الله وسائط، يسألهم الشفاعة، فقد عبدهم، وأشرك بهم، وذلك أن</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 86</h4>
<p>الشفاعة كلها لله، كما قال تعالى: {قُلْ لِلَّهِ الشَّفَاعَةُ جَمِيعاً} [سورة الزمر آية: 44] ؛ فلا يشفع عنده أحد إلا بإذنه، كما قال تعالى: {مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَاّ بِإِذْنِهِ} [سورة البقرة آية: 255] . وقال تعالى: {يَوْمَئِذٍ لا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ إِلَاّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلاً} ، [سورة طه آية: 109] ، وهو سبحانه لا يرضى إلا التوحيد، كما قال تعالى: {وَلا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَاّّّّ لِمَنِ ارْتَضَى} [سورة الأنبياء آية: 28] . وقال تعالى: {قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلا فِي الأَرْضِ وَمَا لَهُمْ فِيهِمَا مِنْ شِرْكٍ وَمَا لَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ ظَهِيرٍ وَلا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَاّ لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ} [سورة سبأ الآيتان: 22-23] .</p>
<p>فالشفاعة حق، ولا تطلب في دار الدنيا إلا من الله تعالى كما قال تعالى: {وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُو مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً} [سورة الجن آية: 18] . وقال: {وَلا تَدْعُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لا يَنْفَعُكَ وَلا يَضُرُّكَ فَإِنْ فَعَلْتَ فَإِنَّكَ إِذاً مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ} [سورة يونس آية: 106] . فإذا كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو سيد الشفعاء، وصاحب المقام المحمود، وآدم فمن دونه تحت لوائه، لا يشفع إلا بإذن الله، لا يشفع ابتداء، بل: &quot; يأتي فيخر ساجدا فيحمده بمحامد يعلمه إياها، ثم يقال: ارفع رأسك، وقل يسمع، وسل تعط، واشفع تشفع. ثم يحد له حدا فيدخلهم الجنة &quot; 1 فكيف بغيره من الأنبياء، والأولياء؟!</p>
<p>وهذا الذي ذكرناه لا يخالف فيه أحد من علماء المسلمين، بل قد أجمع عليه السلف الصالح، من الصحابة</p>
<p>1 البخاري: تفسير القرآن (4476) ، ومسلم: الإيمان (193) ، وابن ماجه: الزهد (4312) ، وأحمد (3/247) ، والدارمي: المقدمة (52) .</p>

<!-- evidence-id: 000638 -->

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Laṭīf and Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Suḥmān said:

And when it is established that duʿāʾ is ʿibādah (worship), then directing it to other than Allāh is shirk. So whoever calls upon along with Allāh anyone from the creation has committed shirk with Him—whether he wills it or refuses. Like if he says: “O Messenger of Allāh,” “O Kaʿbah of Allāh,” “O Station of Ibrāhīm,” or if he supplicates to one of the prophets, or the awliyāʾ, or the righteous—then he is a mushrik with shirk akbar that expels from the religion.

Allāh, said: “Indeed, Allāh does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.” [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 4:48] And He, taʿālā, said: “Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allāh—Allāh has forbidden him Paradise, and his abode is the Fire, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.” [Sūrat al-Māʾidah, 5:72] And He, taʿālā, said: “And do not call upon, besides Allāh, that which neither benefits you nor harms you. For if you do so, then indeed you will be of the wrongdoers.” [Sūrat Yūnus, 10:106] And He, taʿālā, said: “And who is more astray than one who calls upon, besides Allāh, those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they of their supplication are unaware. And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them, and they will be disbelievers in their worship.” [Sūrat al-Aḥqāf, 46:5–6] And He said: “And the masājid are for Allāh, so do not call upon anyone along with Allāh.” [Sūrat al-Jinn, 72:18] And besides these, other verses that have come in this meaning.

Source: ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 5/135

<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 135</h4>
<p>إحساناً إلى الميت سؤال الميت، وتخصيص تلك البقعة بالدعاء الذي هو مخ العبادة، بنص رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فعن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: &quot; الدعاء مخ العبادة &quot; 1.</p>
<p>وإذا ثبت أن الدعاء هو العبادة، فصرفه لغير الله شرك؛ فمن دعا مع الله أحداً من الخلق فقد أشرك به شاء أم أبى، كأن يقول: يا رسول الله، يا كعبة الله، يا مقام إبراهيم، أو يدعو أحداً من الأنبياء والأولياء والصالحين، فهو مشرك الشرك الأكبر الذي يخرج من الملة، قال الله تعالى: {إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ} [سورة النساء آية: 48] ، وقال تعالى: {إِنَّهُ مَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَأْوَاهُ النَّارُ وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصَارٍ} [سورة المائدة آية: 72] ، وقال تعالى: {وَلا تَدْعُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لا يَنْفَعُكَ وَلا يَضُرُّكَ فَإِنْ فَعَلْتَ فَإِنَّكَ إِذاً مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ} [سورة يونس آية: 106] ، وقال تعالى: {وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ يَدْعُو مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَنْ لا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ وَهُمْ عَنْ دُعَائِهِمْ غَافِلُونَ وَإِذَا حُشِرَ النَّاسُ كَانُوا لَهُمْ أَعْدَاءً وَكَانُوا بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ كَافِرِينَ} [سورة الأحقاف آية: 5-6] ، وَقَالَ {وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُو مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً} [سورة الجن آية: 18] ، إلى غير ذلك من الآيات الواردة في هذا المعنى.</p>
<p>إذا تحققت ذلك، فقد قال شيخ الإسلام في الرسالة السنية: فإذا كان على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من مرق من الإسلام مع عبادته العظيمة، فليعلم أن المنتسب إلى الإسلام في هذه</p>
<p>1 الترمذي: الدعوات (3371) .</p>

al-ʿAllāmah Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Suḥmān said:

So the happiest people by the intercession of the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ are the people of tawḥīd who have devoted tawḥīd purely for Allāh and have purified it from all attachments of shirk.

These are the ones whom Allāh, Glorified and Exalted, is pleased with, as He says: “And they do not intercede except for those whom He is pleased with”

Source: al-Hadiyyah as-Saniyyah wa at-Tuḥfah an-Najdiyyah by Shaykh Sulaymān ibn Suḥmān p. 65

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3646-message3648 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000640 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī said:

Allah the Exalted says: “and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.” (Qur’ān 18:110) This is the clearest proof that worshipping the prophets or anyone else besides Allah is shirk with Allah. Whoever associates them with Allah in His worship is not from the Ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ — not among the muwaḥḥidīn (monotheists) who respond to Allah and His Messenger.

And whoever prevents or forbids takfīr of one who commits shirk with Allah, equates others with Him, or rejects what has come in this regard from the Kitāb and the Sunnah, and speaks about Allah and His Messenger without knowledge — then it is necessary to judge him by the ruling of the Kitāb and the Sunnah as being a kāfir and mushrik, whether he accepts that or not.

And whoever does not declare a disbeliever the one who associates partners with Allah and equates others with Him — such a person is himself a kāfir by ijmāʿ of the Muslims.

Indeed, every shirk that has appeared in the world has only come about through the opinions of people like you — you are the ones who command shirk, act upon it, and call others to it. And those among you who do not command it, do not forbid it either, nor do they declare disbelievers those who commit it. You have resembled those who invented shirk and introduced into the religion of Allah those wicked foundations whose consequence is to make equals with the Lord of the Worlds, to set others as His equals, to show enmity toward His awliyāʾ and His party, and to ascribe to them what does not befit them.

And this — that very thing — is the essence of filth, impurity, and corruption. Allah the Exalted said: “And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. And We caused to overtake them in this world a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be of the despised.” (Qur’ān 28:41–42).

And his statement — “And your declaring the Ummah of Muḥammad disbelievers without right” — means that he was astonished that we declare as disbelievers those who worship others along with Allah. That, in reality, is the essence of the matter.

He (the objector) falsely portrays them — those who worship alongside Allah other deities — as being part of the Ummah of Muḥammad that has responded and affirmed pure monotheism. This is nothing but deceptive pretense and falsehood, which he fabricates and repeats to divert people from the path of Allah without right, and to confuse the ignorant.

If he possessed sound reason and knowledge — to discern what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was upon — namely, takfīr upon those who worship with Allah others besides Him, and that he (the Prophet ﷺ) disputed with the mushrikūn of the Arabs and their likes, who made with Allah another deity — he would not have exposed this disgrace of his.

We say: This is a tremendous slander. We have not declared the Ummah of Muḥammad to be disbelievers. Rather, we have applied the Qur’ānic verses according to their true indication and necessary implication — declaring as disbelievers those who call upon other than Allah and associate partners with Him.

We have declared them disbelievers only for what Allah and His Messenger have declared disbelief for — in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and in following what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, upon which the people of knowledge have agreed by ijmāʿ.

And whoever does not declare the mushrikīn disbelievers, or doubts their disbelief, or approves of their creed, has himself committed disbelief.

Woe unto him! Where is our “declaring the Ummah of Muḥammad disbelievers”? Rather, the reality of his doctrine is that, according to him, the monotheistic Ummah of Muḥammad consists of the worshippers of graves, the prophets, and the righteous — those who make with Allah other deities, ask them to fulfill their needs, and seek from them relief from their distresses, and who turn to them in times of hardship and affliction.

These are the very people whom the Qurʾān declared to be kuffār, and for whose combat the Messenger ﷺ was sent, a matter upon which the Muslims have an undeniable ijmāʿ.

Source: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī, *as-Sayf al-Maslūl ʿalā ʿĀbid ar-Rasūl*, pp. 98–99.

Shaykh Ibn Bāz was asked:

Q: Some people argue and say: ‘It is true that seeking intercession is shirk akbar, but it is from the masāʾil khafiyyah (hidden matters).’ He agrees with you that it is major shirk, but he does not agree with making takfīr. He says: ‘This is from the hidden issues.’”

A: No, it is not hidden. The most obvious thing in existence is shirk akbar. If someone prays to other than Allāh, or fasts for other than Allāh, or says: ‘O my master al-Badawī, forgive me, have mercy on me, heal my sick person, return my absent one, I am in your protection and I am sick — grant me healing’ — what could be clearer than this?”

Q: Then your view is that the one ignorant of tawḥīd is not excused for his ignorance?”

He replied: No, he is not excused — if he knows, or if he is among the Muslims. But if he is far away (from the muslim living in a remote land), then his ruling is the ruling of ahl al-fatrah. We treat him with the treatment of the kuffār, but his affair is with Allāh. We do not pray over him, the Muslims do not inherit from him, and his affair is with Allāh.

Source: Subul as-Salām Sharḥ Nawāqiḍ al-Islām by Shaykh Ibn Bāz p.263-264

Shaykh Ibn Bāz said:

“And do not call upon besides Allāh that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.” (Yūnus: 106). That is, from the mushrikīn and the kāfirīn, they are the wrongdoers.

Allāh has made clear that whoever calls upon anyone besides Allāh who cannot benefit or harm – and this is a general description for all creations that cannot benefit or harm independently, and whose benefit and harm are only by Allāh alone – whoever calls upon others besides Allāh is a mushrik.

The exception to this is du‘āʾ to the Living, All-Powerful, Present Allāh; this is not considered shirk by the ijmāʿ of the Muslims.

Source: Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Ibn Bāz p.54

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

Question: What is shirk al-khafī (hidden shirk)? What is the difference between it and shirk al-asghar (minor shirk)? And how can a Muslim rid himself of it?

Answer: Shirk is divided into three types: shirk al-akbar (major shirk), shirk al-asghar, and shirk al-khafī.

shirk al-akbar is when a person directs any act of worship to other than Allāh, exalted is He. Among the greatest acts of worship is duʿāʾ. So if a person calls upon anyone other than Allāh — such as a prophet, a saint, an angel, the sun, or the moon — seeking benefit or removal of harm, then he has committed shirk al-akbar with Allāh. Likewise, if he bows or prostrates to an idol, the sun, the moon, or the occupant of a grave, he has committed shirk al-akbar that expels him from Islām — we seek refuge with Allāh.

Allāh says: “Indeed, whoever associates others with Allāh — Allāh has forbidden Paradise for him, and his abode will be the Fire. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.” (Sūrah al-Mā’idah, 5:72)

This applies to outward actions. Similarly, if one inwardly believes that anyone shares with Allāh in His creation or has the power to do what only Allāh can do, he too is guilty of shirk al-akbar.

shirk al-asghar is what is less than shirk al-akbar. An example is when a person swears by other than Allāh — not believing that the one sworn by deserves the same reverence as Allāh, but doing so out of veneration or habit. This is shirk al-asghar. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever swears by other than Allāh has committed disbelief or shirk.” It is prohibited — whether one swears by the Prophet ﷺ, Jibrīl, or anyone else among creation — and it constitutes shirk al-asghar.

shirk al-khafī refers to that which lies within the heart and is known only to Allāh. It may be major or minor. If a person associates another with Allāh in his heart, believing that other to be equal to Allāh in His rights or actions, then this is shirk al-akbar— even if hidden from people. If a person performs acts of worship for Allāh but mixes them with riyāʾ (showing off), then this is shirk al-khafī that is asghar, because it is concealed from people yet does not expel one from Islām.

Question: How can a Muslim rid himself of shirk?

Answer: Deliverance from both major and minor shirk is through sincere repentance to Allāh, returning to Him, and adhering firmly to His commands while avoiding His prohibitions. Through steadfastness and sincerity in obedience, Allāh protects His servant from falling into shirk.

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn was asked:

Q: Is it permissible to give zakāh to a Muslim who supplicates to other than Allāh, swears by other than Allāh, circumambulates graves, and believes that the righteous have the power to bring benefit and harm?

A: rather, the one described in the question is a mushrik, a kāfir. Allāh does not accept ṣalāh, fasting, ṣadaqah, or anything else from him.

Whoever makes du‘āʾ to other than Allāh is a mushrik, and whoever worships graves is a mushrik. Such a person is not to be given zakāh. Rather, he is to be called to Islām and taught tawḥīd. If he accepts it, then that is what is sought; otherwise, it is upon the ruler to carry out concerning him what the Sharīʿah requires.

As for the one who swears by other than Allāh, he may be given zakāh, because swearing by other than Allāh does not expel one from the religion, even though it is shirk. He may be given zakāh, and he should be advised and taught that swearing by other than Allāh is a type of shirk, so that Allāh may guide him.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Luḥaidān said:

When the Companions heard the saying of Allah Most High: “Those who believe and do not mix their belief with Zûlm (injustice) - those will have security, and they are [rightly] guided.” (al-Anʿām 6:82), that was difficult for them, and they thought that what was meant by the verse was that they wrong themselves by actions they commit.

So they said: “O Messenger of Allah, which of us does not wrong himself?” He said: “It is not that. Rather, it is shirk. Have you not heard what Luqmān said to his son while advising him: ‘O my son! Join not in worship others with Allâh. Verily joining others in worship with Allâh is a great Zûlm’ (Luqmān 31:13).”

Thus, the great ẓulm — which, if it enters a righteous act by which Allah is worshipped, corrupts it — is shirk.

For this reason, whoever dies upon Shirk al-akbar has no hope of forgiveness, and it is not valid for one who knows that he died upon Shirk al-akbar to make du‘āʾ to Allah for him, because Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has forbidden that: “It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the Mushrikīn, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire.” (al-Tawbah 9:113).

So if a person knows that someone died upon Shirk al-akbar — even if he was a close relative, even if he was a brother, a close friend, an intimate companion, and so on — it is not permissible for him to seek forgiveness for him.

Source: Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Luḥaydān p.65

Q10: Some of the devout youth of today claim that all or most of those who fall into shirk in the Islamic world today are not considered polytheists; because they are either great scholars who, through their ijtihad, have concluded that seeking help from others besides Allah is permissible, as did al-Suyūṭī, al-Nabhānī, and others. This is said to have two rewards: one if correct, and one if wrong. Alternatively, they are ordinary laypeople, and this is the utmost they are capable of.

A10: The excused mistake is one in theoretical matters of ijtihad, not one in matters that have been established by explicit texts or in what is known to be a part of the religion by necessity.

And Allah grants success. May peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his companions.

‘Abd al-Razzaq ‘Afīfī… ‘Abd al-‘Azīz ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn Bāz

Source: Fatāwā al-Lajnah al-Dā’imah 2/59-60

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4689 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000648 -->

The scholars have two opinions regarding the issue of excuse of ignorance in shirk al-akbar and clear cut disbelief:


❌ There is no third opinion from the scholars stating that a person is excused due to ignorance while still being considered a Muslim. This position is disbelief and is statement of the contemporary Murjiʾah. Any one claiming this, know that he has been inflicted with the doubts of the Murjiʾah.

Regarding this third position, it falls under the third nullifier: whoever does not takfīr a kāfir is a kāfir. However, the scholars of our time have differed regarding the ruling on the one who excuses the grave-worshipper. This does not apply to those who excuse the Christians and Jews.

There are two opinions: one holds that those who excuse them and still consider them Muslim must have the proof established upon them before takfīr is made, due to the widespread doubts in this matter.


As for matters which are obscure. Then the person is excused with ignorance and remains a Muslim unless they persist in such a matter. Then they are also a disbeliever.

Shaykh al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah mentioned in Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā that asking a dead person to make duʿāʾ for you, to ask Allāh on your behalf, is an act of bidʿah.

A: This is a bidʿah shirkīyyah— not merely an innovation, but an innovation involving shirk. Do not assume it is only a prohibited bidʿah; it is a bidʿah shirkīyyah, and shirk is indeed described as bidʿah.

Q: Is this the same issue you pointed out at the beginning of the lesson?

A: Yes, I clarified an understanding — not the wording of the Shaykh himself. I clarified the misunderstanding of the one quoting him. When the Shaykh says “this is bidʿah” he did not mean bidʿah in the simple sense and remain silent; he meant bidʿah shirkīyyah. That is his intent. His explicit statement here is clear, so why take his words in their general sense and ignore his explicit clarification elsewhere?

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message564 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000650 -->

Shaykh al-Fawzān said regarding the verse:

"And who is more astray than one who calls on besides Allâh, such as will not answer him till the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their calls to them? And when mankind are gathered (on the Day of Resurrection), they (false deities) will become their enemies and will deny their worshipping." (al-Aḥqāf: 5-6)

Allah judged that there is no one more astray than the person who called upon other than Allah from among created beings—those who are not capable of responding to his supplication in this world, nor are they even aware of the one who calls upon them.

And when the Resurrection occurs and they are gathered along with all people, they will show enmity toward the one who used to call upon them and will disassociate themselves from him.  Thus this mushrik is in misery in both abodes: he obtains no response in this world, and in the Hereafter his act of worship will be rejected at the moment he is most in need of it.

The relevance of the two verses to the chapter:

They contain the ruling that whoever calls upon other than Allah is the most astray of the astray, and that duʿāʾ is an act of worship—so whoever directs it to other than Allah is a mushrik.

That duʿāʾ is an act of worship, and so whoever calls upon other than Allah has committed shirk al-akbar.

That idols do not hear the one who calls upon them, nor respond to him—contrary to what the mushrikūn imagine.

Source: Al-Mulakhkhaṣ fī Sharḥ Kitāb al-Tawḥīd by Shaykh al-Fawzān p.99

<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: الملخص في شرح كتاب التوحيد</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 99</h4>
<p>وعن طارق بن شهاب: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: &quot;دخل الجنة رجل في ذباب، ودخل النار رجل في ذباب&quot; قالوا: وكيف ذلك يا رسول الله؟ قال: &quot;مر رجلان على قوم لهم صنم لا يجاوزه أحد حتى يقرِّب له شيئاً. قالوا لأحدهما: قَرِّب. قال: ليس عندي شيء أُقرِّب. قالوا: قرب ولو ذباباً. فقرَّب ذباباً فخلّوا سبيله فدخل النار، وقالوا للآخر: قرب. قال: ما كنت لأقرب لأحد شيئاً دون الله عز وجل فضربوا عنقه فدخل الجنة&quot; (1) . رواه أحمد.</p>
<p>ــ</p>
<p>طارق بن شهاب: هو طارق بن شهاب البجلي الأحمسي رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه. فحديثه مرسل، صحابيٌّ. مات طارقٌ سنة 83هـ رضي الله عنه.</p>
<p>في ذباب: أي بسبب ذباب.</p>
<p>صنمٌ: ما كان منحوتاً على صورة.</p>
<p>لا يجاوزه: لا يمرُّ به ولا يتعداه.</p>
<p>يقرِّب: يذبح.</p>
<p>المعنى الإجمالي للحديث: يخبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن خطورة الشرك</p>
<p>(1) أخرجه أحمد في كتاب الزهد &quot;ص22&quot; وأبو نعيم في الحلية &quot;1/203&quot; وابن أبي شيبة في المصنف &quot;6/477 رقم 33028&quot; موقوفاً على سلمان الفارسي رضي الله عنه.</p>

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3743 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000651 -->

Shaykh al-Fawzān said:

Whoever places between himself and Allāh intermediaries — calling upon them, asking them for intercession, and relying upon them — has committed kufr by ijmā‘.

Whoever does not declare the mushrikīn to be disbelievers, or doubts their kufr, or believes that their madhhab is correct, has disbelieved.

Whoever believes that the guidance of anyone other than the Prophet ﷺ is more complete than his guidance, or that the judgment of anyone other than him is better than his judgment — such as those who prefer the rule of ṭāghūt over the rule of the Messenger ﷺ, or who prefer man-made laws over the judgment of al-Islām — has committed kufr.

Whoever hates anything that the Messenger ﷺ came with, even if he acts upon it, has committed kufr.

Whoever mocks anything from the religion of the Messenger ﷺ, or its reward or its punishment, has committed kufr. The proof for this is the saying of Allāh, the Exalted: “Say, ‘Was it Allāh, His verses, and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.’” [at-Tawbah:65–66]

Source: ʿAqīdat at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh al-Fawzān p.51

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said:

This is the meaning of His statement: “They do not mix their belief with injustice” [al-Anʿām: 82]. That is: with shirk. This is exactly how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained it. When this verse was revealed, it distressed the Companions and they said: “O Messenger of Allah, which one of us has not wronged himself?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied: “It is not the wrong you are thinking of. It is shirk. Have you not heard the words of the righteous servant: ‘ "O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allāh. Indeed, Shirk [with Him] is great injustice." [Luqmān: 13].

As for His statement, “those will have security”: Does this mean complete and absolute security, that they will never be punished at all? Or does it mean general security, that even if they are punished, they will inevitably enter Paradise in the end?

The verse accommodates both meanings. And on either interpretation, it demonstrates the virtue of tawḥīd: that it grants protection from punishment, either total protection or protection from permanent punishment. The verse therefore highlights the excellence of tawḥīd, and that Allah grants its people security in proportion to their level of tawḥīd and their freedom from sins and disobedience.

The verse also implies — through its opposite meaning — that whoever commits shirk with Allah and mixes his tawḥīd with shirk has no security whatsoever. We seek refuge in Allah from that. This makes clear the danger of shirk: a person may worship Allah, yet still invoke others alongside Him, seek aid from the dead, slaughter for graves, or perform ṭawāf around shrines seeking their help. Such a person has mixed his īmān with shirk, and he will have no security at all until he sincerely repents to Allah and purifies his tawḥīd.

Thus, the point is not merely that a person worships Allah; he must also avoid shirk entirely.

Source: Iʿānat al-Mustafīd bi-Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.77

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: إعانة المستفيد بشرح كتاب التوحيد</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 77</h4>
<p>الركوع والسجود؛ من أجل أن يوصف بأنه صاحب طاعة، وإذا صلى وحده نقر الصلاة، وخفّفها، والإخلاص: أن الإنسان يقصد بعمله وجه الله، ولا يقصد بذلك طمعاً من مطامع الدنيا، أو مدحاً، وثناءً من الخلق، ولا يستمع إلى لومهم إذا لاموه في طاعة الله. قالوا: فلان متشدّد، فلان كذا، ما دام أنه على الطريق الصحيح، وعلى السنة، فلا يضره ما يقوله الناس، ولا تأخذه في الله لومة لائم.</p>
<p>الصفة الثالثة: {حَنِيفاً} والحنيف من الحَنَف وهو في اللغة: الميل، والمراد به هنا: الإقبال على الله، وأنه مُعرض عن الناس مُقبل على الله سبحانه وتعالى، يطلب الخير أمن الله وحده.</p>
<p>الصفة الرابعة: {وَلَمْ يَكُ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ} وهذا محل الشاهد من الباب، ومعناه: أنه تبرّأ من المشركين، براءة تامة، أي: قطع ما بينه وبين المشركين من المودّة من أجل الله سبحانه وتعالى، لأنهم أعداء الله، والمؤمن لا يحب أعداء الله.</p>
<p>فإبراهيم عليه السلام لم يكن من المشركين لا بقليل ولا بكثير، قطع صلة المحبة بينه وبينهم، أما صلة التعامل الدنيوي في المصالح المباحة فهذا شيء آخر، إنما المراد قطع صلة المحبة والموالاة والمناصرة، هذا هو المطلوب، أما التعاون الدنيوي فيما فيه نفع للمسلمين، فهذا لا بأس به، يوضِّح هذا قوله في الآية الأخرى: {قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ} يعني: من أتباعه {إِذْ قَالُوا لِقَوْمِهِمْ إِنَّا بُرَآءُ مِنْكُمْ وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ كَفَرْنَا بِكُمْ وَبَدَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةُ وَالْبَغْضَاءُ أَبَدًا حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللهِ وَحْدَهُ} ؛ يعني: لا تقارب بيننا وبينكم في المودة والمناصرة والمؤاخاة أبداً، إلَاّ إذا آمنتم بالله وحده، وكفرتم بما يعبد من دون الله عز وجل، وتركتم عبادة الأصنام، فحينئذٍ نكون إخواناً {حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللهِ وَحْدَهُ} ثم قال في الآية التي بعدها: {لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِيهِمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِمَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُو اللهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ (6) } ثم قال بعدها: {لا يَنْهَاكُمُ اللهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوا إِلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ اللهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ (8) } .</p>
<p>فهذه أربع صفات وصف الله بها إبراهيم: وهي:</p>
<p>الصفة الأولى: أنه كان أمة، يعني: قدوة في الخير.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 77</h4>
<p>لا تخفى عليه خافية ولا تخفى عليه أحوالُ عباده أبداً، ولكنه يبتليهم ويمتحنهم ليكفِّر عنهم سيِّئاتهم وليختبر إيمانهم وليعظُم رجاؤهم بالله عز وجل وليتوبوا إلى الله عز وجل. وله الحكمة في ذلك سبحانه وتعالى.</p>
<p>قوله: &quot;رواه عبد الرزاق&quot; عبد الرزاق بن هَمَّام الصنعاني، الإمام الجليل، شيخ العلماء والمحدِّثين، روى عنه: الإمام أحمد بن حنبل، وإسحاق بن راهوَيْه، وغيرهما من كبار الأئمة- رحمهم الله.</p>
<p>وقوّى إسناد هذا الحديث: ابن جرير الطبري.</p>
<p>فهذه النصوص في هذا الباب يُستفاد منها الأحكام التالية:</p>
<p>أولاً: تحريم الأمن من مكر الله والقنوط من رحمة الله، وأنهما ينقِّصان كمال التّوحيد وقد ينافيان التّوحيد.</p>
<p>ثانياً: أنه يجب على المسلم أن يجمع بين الخوف والرجاء، فلا يخاف فقط ولا يرجو فقط، وإنما يكون خائفاً راجياً دائماً وأبداً، هذا هو التّوحيد، وهو صفة أولياء الله.</p>
<p>ثالثاً: في هذه النصوص أن المعلِّم والداعية يبدأ بالأهم فالأهم؛ لأن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لَمّا أراد أن يعلِّم أصحابه الكبائر بدأ بأهمها وهو الشرك بالله عز وجل، لأن الشرك أكبرُ الكبائر فبدأ به، ثمّ ذكر بعده الأمن من مكر الله والقنوط من رحمة الله.</p>
<p>رابعاً: في الحديثين: أن الذنوب تنقسم إلى صغائر وكبائر، وقد عرّف العلماء الكبيرة بأنها: &quot;ما رُتِّبَ عليها حدٌّ في الدنيا، أو وعيدٌ في الآخرة، أو خُتم بغضب، أو لعنة، أو نار، أو تبرّأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من صاحبها، بأن قال: &quot;ليس منا من فعل كذا&quot;، أو نفى عنه الإيمان كقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: &quot;لا يزني الزاني حين يزني وهو مؤمن، ولا يشرب الخمر حين يشربها وهو مؤمن&quot;. هذه ضوابط الكبيرة.</p>
<p>أما الصغائر فهي ما ليس كذلك مما حرّمه الله ونهى عنه، ولم يصل إلى حدّ الكبيرة.</p>
<p>ولكن لا يحمل هذا الإنسان على أنه يتساهل بالصغائر، لأن الصغائر إذا تُسوهِل بها جرَّتْ إلى الكبائر؛ والصغيرة تعظُم حتى تكون كبيرة مع الإصرار؛</p>
</div>
</details>

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3930 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000653 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said:

As for the one who worships Allah but also worships others alongside Him, this person has not truly realized lā ilāha illā Allāh, even if he utters it with his tongue. The one who says lā ilāha illā Allāh but then goes to graves, seeks needs from them, rubs himself with them, seeks help from them, or circumambulates them, has not purified himself from shirk.

Thus, lā ilāha illā Allāh does not benefit him, even if he repeats it with every breath. Lā ilāha illā Allāh is not merely a phrase to be spoken; it has implications, meanings, and requirements that must be realized—worship of Allah alone and disavowal of shirk and mushrikīn.

Whoever does not disavow shirk has not truly realized lā ilāha illā Allāh, even if he utters it or makes for himself morning and evening litanies, carries a rosary of great length to glorify Allah, or repeats litanies containing lā ilāha illā Allāh thousands of times. This does not benefit him until he follows what Ibrāhīm عليه السلام did—purifying himself from shirk.

Source: Iʿānat al-Mustafīd bi-Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.172-173

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: إعانة المستفيد بشرح كتاب التوحيد</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 172</h4>
<p>لهم صنم لا يجوزه أحد حتى يقرِّب له شيئاً، فقالوا لأحدهما: قرِّب. قال: ليس عندي شيء أقرِّبه، قالوا به: قرِّب ولو ذباباً. فقرّب ذباباً، فخلَّوْ سبيله، فدخل النار. وقالوا للآخر: قرِّب. فقال: ما كنت لأقرِّب لأحد شيئاً دون الله عز وجل. فضربوا عنقه، فدخل الجنة&quot; رواه أحمد.</p>
<p>ــ</p>
<p>&quot;لهم صنم&quot; الصنم هو: ما كان على صورة حيوان، أما ما عُبد وهو على غير صورة حيوان، كالشجر والحجر والقبر فهذا يسمى وثناً، فالوثن أعم من الصنم، لأن الصنم لا يُطلق إلَاّ على التِّمثال، وأما الوثن فيُطلق على التِّمثال وغيره، حتى القبر وثن إذا عُبد، قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: &quot;اللهم لا تجعل قبري وثناً يُعبد&quot;، فالوثن كل ما عُبد من دون الله على أي شكل كان.</p>
<p>&quot;لا يجوزه أحد&quot; أي: يتجاوزه ولا يمرّ عليه أحد، &quot;حتى يقرِّب له شيئاً&quot; يعني: يذبح له تعظيماً له.</p>
<p>&quot;فقال لأحدهما: قرّب، قال: ليس عندي شيء أقرِّبه&quot; اعتذر بالعدم، ولم يقل: إن الذبح لغير الله لا يجوز، أو هذا منكر- والعياذ بالله-، وهذا يدلّ على أنه لو كان عنده شيء لقربه.</p>
<p>&quot;قالوا له: قرِّب ولو ذباباً&quot; فقرب ذباباً، يعني: اذبحه للصنم، &quot;فقرِّب ذباباً فخلوا سبيله&quot; سمحوا له بالمرور، &quot;فدخل النار&quot; بسبب الشرك، وأنه ذبح لغير الله، والعبرة بالنيّة والقصد لا بالمذبوح.</p>
<p>والقصد أنه ما استنكر هذا الشيء، ولا تمنع منه، وإنما اعتذر بعدم وجود شيء فلذلك دخل النار- والعياذ بالله.</p>
<p>&quot;وقالوا للآخر: قرِّب. فقال: ما كنت لأقرِّب لأحد شيئاً دون الله عز وجل&quot; امتنع وأنكر الشرك، &quot;فضربوا عنقه&quot; يعني: قتلوه، &quot;فدخل الجنة&quot; بسبب التّوحيد.</p>
<p>فهذا الحديث حديث عظيم، فيه مسائل عظيمة:</p>
<p>المسألة الأولى: هذا الحديث فيه جواز الإخبار عن الأمم السابقة، والتحدّث عنها بما ثبت لأجل العظة والعبرة.</p>
<p>المسألة الثانية: في الحديث دليل على تحريم الذبح لغير الله، ومن ذبح</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 172</h4>
<p>فلما أصبحت أخبرت بها من أخبرت، ثم أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخبرته، قال: &quot;هل أخبرتَ بها أحداً؟ &quot;، قلت: نعم، قال: فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال: &quot;أما بعد: فإن طفيلاً رأى رؤيا أخبر بها من أخبر منكم، وإنكم قلتم كلمة يمنعني كذا وكذا أن أنهاكم عنها، فلا تقولوا: ما شاء الله وشاء محمد، ولكن قولوا: ما شاء الله وحده &quot;.</p>
<p>ــ</p>
<p>&quot;فقلت: إنكم لأنتم القوم لولا أنكم تقولون: المسيح ابن الله&quot; وهو عيسى ابن مريم، سُمِّي بالمسيح لأنّه يمسح بيده على ذي العاهة فيبرأ بإذن الله. فالنصارى غلوا في المسيح كما غَلَت اليهود في عُزير.</p>
<p>ثم رد عليه النصارى بمثل ما قاله اليهود، قال طُفيل: &quot;فلما أصبحتُ أخبرتُ بها مَن أخبرت، ثم أتيتُ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخبرتُه، قال: &quot;هل أخبرتَ بها أحداً؟ &quot;، قلت: نعم، قال: فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال: &quot;أمّا بعد&quot; هذا فيه: دليل على مشروعية حمد الله والثّناء عليه في بداية الكلام، لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: &quot;كلّ أمر ذي بال لا يُبدأُ في بالحمد لله فهو أبتر&quot;، ولهذا افتتح الله كتابه العظيم القرآن بـ {الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (2) } ، وفيه استحباب الإتيان بأما بعد، وهي كلمة يُؤتَى بها للانتقال من أسلوب إلى آخر.</p>
<p>&quot;فإن طُفيلاً قد رأى رؤيا أخبر بها من أخبر منكم، وإنّكم قلتم كلمة يمنعني كذا وكذا أن أنهاكم عنها&quot; قيل: كان يمنع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الحياء، لأنّه لم ينزل عليه وحيٌ في المنع منها.</p>
<p>&quot;فلا تقولوا: ما شاء الله وشاء محمد، ولكن قولوا: ما شاء الله وحده&quot; لَمّا نبّههم على خطأ هذه الكلمة أرشدهم إلى البديل الصالح منها، وهو أن يقولوا: ما شاء الله وحده.</p>
<p>فهذه القصة فيها فوائد عظيمة ودُروس وعِبَر:</p>
<p>الفائدة الأولى: أن الرؤيا حقّ، ولذلك: لا يجوز الكذب في الرؤيا، وجاء في الحديث الوعيد على ذلك.</p>
<p>الفائدة الثّانية: فيه: فهم الإنسان إذا كان له هوى، فهؤلاء اليهود والنصارى لَمّا كان لهم هوى في حق المسلمين؛ لاحظوا هذه المسألة، لا حُبًّا في الخير أو حِرْصاً على التّوحيد، ولكنّهم يريدون بذلك تنقُّص المسلمين، والتماس عيوبهم، وإن كان في اليهود والنصارى عيوب أكثر منها.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 173</h4>
<p>لغير الله فقد أشرك، لأن هذا الرجل الذي ذبح الذباب دخل النار، وحتى لو كان المذبوح شيئاً تافهاً، والرجل الثاني عظّم الشرك، وتجنبه ولو كان شيئاً حقيراً، فدخل الجنة.</p>
<p>المسألة الثالثة: كما قال الشيخ رحمه الله في مسائله: أن المدار على أعمال القلوب، وإن كان الشيء الظاهر تافهاً، لكن المدار على عمل القلب.</p>
<p>المسألة الرابعة: فيه دليل- كما قال الشيخ رحمه الله على قُرب الجنة والنار من الإنسان، كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: &quot;الجنة أقرب إلى أحدكم من شِراك نعله، والنار مثل ذلك&quot;، هذا ضربوا عنقه فدخل الجنة، وذاك خلو سبيله فدخل النار.</p>
<p>المسألة الخامسة: أن هذا الرجل الذي ذبح الذباب كان مؤمناً، فدخل النار بذبحه الذباب، لأنه لو كان كافراً لدخل النار بكفره، لا بذبح الذباب، فدلّ على أنه كان مؤمناً، وهذه مسألة خطيرة جدًّا، فأين الذين يذبحون للقبور وللجن، وللشياطين، وللعفاريت، وللسخرة؟، فدلّ على أن الشرك الأكبر يخرج من الملة ولو كان شيئاً يسيراً، فأمور التّوحيد وأمور العقيدة لا يُتسامح فيها.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 173</h4>
<p>الفائدة الثالثة: قَبول الحقّ ممّن جاء به ولو كان عدوًّا، لأنّ الحق ضالّة المؤمن، والرُّجوع إلى الحقّ فضيلة.</p>
<p>الفائدة الرّابعة: في الحديث دليل: على أنّ من نهى عن شيء أو منع من شيء وكان له بديل صالح أن يأتيَ بالبديل، فالنّبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لَمّا منع من هذه الكلمة &quot;ما شاء الله وشاء محمد&quot; أتى بالبديل الصالح الذي ليس فيه محذور وهو أن يقال: &quot;ما شاء الله وحده&quot;.</p>
<p>الفائدة الخامسة- وهي التي ساق المصنّف الحديث من أجلها-: أنّ كلمة &quot;ما شاء الله وشاء فلان&quot; ولو كان نبيًّا من الأنبياء؛ شركٌ بالله عز وجل يجب تركُه، ولكنّه من الشّرك الأصغر، بدليل قوله: &quot;يمنعني كذا وكذا&quot;، فإذا كان الإنسان لم يقصد معناه؛ فإنّه شركٌ في الألفاظ، فيجب تركُه واجتنابُه والابتعاد عنه.</p>
<p>الفائدة السادسة: أنه لا يجوز الغلو بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإشراكه مع الله في شيء، ودعاؤه، والاستغاثة به من دون الله عز وجل لأنه نهى أن يقال &quot;ما شاء الله وشاء محمد&quot; فما بالك بما هو أشد من ذلك من أنواع الغلو.</p>

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān was asked:

Q: 'Is it said that the lack of judgment of Kufr upon the one who said to the dead person at his grave: "Make du‘āʾ to Allah for me" and the likes of it, that it is based upon the dead person hearing whoever is at his grave?'

A: they explained it like this, but it is a weak reason; because the tree hears, and the stone hears, and everything hears.  If, for example, the matter were merely that something hears—even though this hearing is a kind of hearing whose reality we do not know—yet it is certain that it hears. And for this, the stone among the stones used to greet the Messenger ﷺ; it says: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allāh.'

And likewise the trunk upon which he used to give khuṭbah, he used to lean upon it... when he separated from it, and it began to cry -meaning it cried due to the loss of the remembrance that used to be mentioned upon it—and it hears. And He has informed us that everything glorifies with His praise. So the taʿlīl is incorrect.

And this is du‘āʾ to other than Allāh. You call upon him for a thing he has no power over, and is not capable of. As it is known, this is Shirk. And this Shirk of the Mushrikīn. It is not possible that anyone finds a proof that the Mushrikīn believed that their objects of worship share with the Lord of the Worlds in Creation and Origination and Governance and Giving Life and Causing Death and other than that. This is not possible.

So they call upon them so that they be intermediaries to intercede for them. For this reason Allah greatly repeated the refutation against them regarding this very matter of intercession; because the intercession is the Shirk which he calls upon them. "or 'Have they taken intercessor besides Allāh? Say: Even if they possess nothing and do not reason?' then He says: 'Say: To Allah belongs all intercession'.

So Shirk came from this type, all the Shirk of the Mushrikīn. his saying that if one calls upon the buried person so that he may intercede for him, or that he may make du‘āʾ to Allah for him, or the like, that this is merely a bidʿah—this is contrary; this is contrary to the state that the mushrikīn were upon, and contrary to what Allah has informed us of. So it is not correct.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3763 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000655 -->

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

ʿibādah (worship) is a comprehensive term that includes everything that Allāh loves and is pleased with—of sayings and actions, both outward and inward. It includes everything the Sharʿ commands or forbids. It is the performance of commands and the abandonment of prohibitions out of devotion to Allāh. Thus, duʿāʾ, slaughtering, vows, and ṭawāf of the House are all forms of ʿibādah, and so are other acts. ʿIbādah is of many kinds, and among the greatest of them is duʿāʾ. So if you direct any part of it to other than Allāh, you have fallen into shirk.

And read His saying, the Exalted: “So do not call upon other god along with Allāh, or you will be among those punished.” (ash-Shuʿarāʾ :213) And His saying: “And do not call upon, besides Allāh, that which neither benefits you nor harms you; for if you do so, then indeed you will be among the wrongdoers.” (Yūnus: 106)

And His saying: "And the masājid are for Allāh alone, so do not call upon anyone along with Allāh.” (al-Jinn :18) And His saying: “And those, whom you invoke or call upon instead of Him, own not even a Qitmîr (the thin membrane over the date-stone).  If you call upon them, they hear not your call; and if (in case) they were to hear, they could not grant it (your request) to you. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will disown your worshipping them. And none can inform you (Muhammad ﷺ) like Him Who is the All-Knower (of everything).” (Fāṭir :13–14)

And His saying: "And whoever calls upon another god besides Allāh for which he has no proof - then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.” (al-Muʾminūn :117) The texts are many regarding the prohibition of calling upon other than Allāh, for duʿāʾ is among the greatest acts of ʿibādah.

And you, O mushrik, have not understood the ʿibādah for which Allāh created you, since you claim that seeking refuge in the righteous and calling upon them is not ʿibādah.

In fact, it is ʿibādah itself.  It is narrated from an-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr that he said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say, “Duʿāʾ is ʿibādah.” Then he recited: “And your Lord said: "Call upon Me, and I will respond to you. Verily! Those who scorn My worship they will surely enter Hell in humiliation!’” (Ghāfir :60)¹

[Shurūḥ Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Mujaddid Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb by Shaykh ar-Rājihī 2/318-319]

footnote

¹ It was narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1479); and by at-Tirmidhī (3247) — and this is his wording; and by Ibn Mājah (3828); and by Aḥmad (4/267). At-Tirmidhī said: “This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.”

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

The fifteenth: their explicit statement that they only intended intercession.

Despite that, they fell into kufr. What they are upon today is the very religion of the mushrikīn of old. The Qurʾān has affirmed this meaning, as Allāh says:

“They worship besides Allāh others who can neither harm nor benefit them, and say, “These are our intercessors with Allāh.”” (Yūnus: 18).

So if the grave worshippers today say: “We only intend intercession,” we say to them: Abū Jahl and Abū Lahab only intended intercession as well.

Source: at-Tanḍīd Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ar-Rājihī p.213

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

Whoever believes in some of the Book and disbelieves in some; or believes in some of the messengers and disbelieves in some of them; or believes in some of the scriptures and disbelieves in some of them; or believes in some of the Qur’ān and disbelieves in some of it; or believes in some of what the Messenger came with and disbelieves in some of it — then he is a kāfir by ijmā‘, and a kāfir in all of it, and it does not benefit him that he believed in some of it.

And with this is removed the doubt which this person mentioned, which is his statement: “We testify that lā ilāha illā Allāh, and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh, and we believe in the resurrection, and we believe the Messenger, and we perform ḥajj and we fast and we give charity.”

We say to him: this does not benefit you; because if you call upon other than Allāh, your tawḥīd and īmān are nullified. So if you call upon the righteous, and you say: “Yā Sayyidī al-Badawī, help me,” or “Yā Sayyidī yā Rasūl Allāh,” or “Yā ‘Abd al-Qādir, madad madad,” or you slaughter or vow for them — you have committed kufr, and you have committed shirk with Allāh, and you have exited from the millah of Islām, and you have become a mushrik, and your tawḥīd and your īmān have been nullified.

An example of that: a person performs wuḍū’ and perfects the wuḍū’, then urine or feces or wind comes out from him — he is no longer upon purity, rather it has been nullified; the impurity has nullified it. Likewise, a person who says: “I testify lā ilāha illā Allāh, and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh,” and he prays and fasts, then he slaughters for other than Allāh or calls upon other than Him — his tawḥīd is nullified by this shirk and is removed. For shirk nullifies tawḥīd and īmān, just as impurity nullifies purity and corrupts it. We ask Allāh for safety and well-being.

Source: Shurūḥ Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Mujaddid Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb by Shaykh ar-Rājihī 2/359-360

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āsh-Shaykh was asked:

Question: What is your opinion about those who attribute to Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah that asking the the dead to pray to Allah for you is not shirk akbar but is a bid‘ah?

Answer: This is in the words of Shaykh al-Islām, and it is correct. But by “bid‘ah” he means bid‘ah muḥdatha (a newly introduced innovation), that is, one that occurred in this Ummah. He did not mean by “bid‘ah” that it is an innovation that is not shirk, because among the bid‘ah that occurred in the Ummah, some are kufr-related or shirk-related, and some are not.

So when he said: “And asking the dead to pray for the supplicant is a bid‘ah,” he means this happened in this Ummah. Even the people of Jāhiliyyah did not do this; they did not say: “Pray to Allah for us,” but rather they said: “intercede for us". The matter of asking the dead for prayer is therefore a bid‘ah that even among the polytheists did not exist. Among the people of Jāhiliyyah it did not exist; it occurred in this Ummah.

What existed among the people of Jāhiliyyah was asking in the form of intercession: “intercede for us.” They would come and draw close in order to intercede, or address the deceased by saying: “intercede for us regarding such-and-such.” But saying “Pray to Allah for us” is a bid‘ah that occurred in this Ummah. Shaykh al-Islām’s statement that it is a newly introduced bid‘ah is correct, and the fact that it is a bid‘ah does not mean it is not shirk akbar.

So building domes over graves, asking the occupants of graves, turning to them as seen in some shrines, making ḥajj to these shrines, and establishing rituals for them—all of these are bid‘ah. We say: bid‘ah muḥdatha (an innovation that occurred in this Ummah). Asking them, asking the people of these shrines, or sacrificing for them in this manner did not exist among the people of Jāhiliyyah in this way.

Rather, their worship of the dead was in the form of idols and statues on graves and similar things, but not in this manner. The people of Jāhiliyyah did not perform pilgrimages like the pilgrimage to the house of Allāh, nor did they go to a shrine or grave in this manner. We say this is a bid‘ah. But does this mean it is not shirk akbar? No, because some bid‘ah are mukaffir.

The virtue of Kashf ash-Shubuhāt

Shaykh Abī al-ʿAlā ar-Rāshid said:

O youth, the treatise Kashf al-Shubuhāt — and we said that Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb authored this treatise intending to respond to two groups. The first group is the group of the mushrikīn who present to the muwahḥidīn a number of doubts. The second group is the group of the Murjiʾah, who also present to the callers to tawḥīd a number of doubts.

We said in the previous lesson that the dāʿi (caller), or any reformer — and this is important — the dāʿi and the reformer who renews for the people the matter of the religion, and calls them to tawḥīd, and returns them to the religion of Allah  calling them to single out Allah in worship, singling out Allah in sacrifice, singling out Allah in legislation and judgment, singling out Allah in allegiance — returning the people to the tawḥīd of Allah — this dāʿi must have enemies. This dāʿi will not be safe, he will not be safe. Why? Because he will proclaim the truth openly.

And Allah said to His Messenger ﷺ: “So proclaim openly that which you are commanded, and turn away from the mushrikīn.” And He said: “And so We have appointed for every Prophet enemies - Shayātīn among mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech as a delusion.” So the devils of mankind and the devils of jinn are the enemies of the call to tawḥīd.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages3.html#message2550 -->

How is tashrīʿ (legislation) understood in the above?

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āl-Shaykh was asked:

Question 123: What is the criterion for tashrīʿ (legislation)? Is it legislating a single matter, or up to 50%? Some people may legislate within their own homes and impose things upon their families — is this considered tashrīʿ and a replacement of Allah’s religion?

Answer: No, this is not tashrīʿ. What is the meaning of tashrīʿ (legislating)? Tashrīʿ, as mentioned, is to make ḥarām something that is ḥalāl, and to believe in its prohibition. Declaring something that is ḥalāl to be ḥarām — this is tashrīʿ. This is kufr.

But if someone says, “This isn’t your concern,” or “Don’t say it’s ḥarām,” or “It’s not ḥarām — we will do it, and you stay out of it,” then what he has done is merely impose his desire upon others. He hasn’t legislated. A legislator (musharriʿ) is someone who changes a ruling and says, “This is not such-and-such — it is instead this.” That’s tashrīʿ — changing the agreed-upon ruling of Allah while knowing what Allah’s ruling is, and then stating otherwise.

But all sinners — except those whom Allah guides — act arrogantly. They are too proud even to be reasoned with. Even, for example, a man in his home may be debating with his son, and the son may provoke his father to say something terrible. This is not birr (righteousness or dutifulness). That is why Allah said to His believing servants: “And do not insult those they invoke besides Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge.” (Sūrat al-Anʿām, 6:108)

Source: al-Ajwibah wa-al-Buḥūth wa-al-Mudārasāt al-Mushtamilah ʿalayhā al-Durūs al-ʿIlmiyyah 2/178

### Istighāthah and calling upon the dead or absent
<!-- evidence-id: 000661 -->

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message552 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000662 -->

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

They believed that the du‘ā’ to the dead, for whom a shrine was built, and doing istighāthah from them was more beneficial than du‘ā’ to Allāh and seeking help from Him in the house built for Allāh ‘Azza wa Jall. So they preferred the house built for the supplication of the created being over the house built for the du‘ā’ of the Creator. And if there is an endowment for this and an endowment for that, then the endowment of shirk is greater in their view, imitating the mushrikīn of the Arabs, whom Allāh described in His words: “And they assign to Allāh a share of what He created of the crops and the cattle, saying, ‘This is for Allāh’—by their claim—and ‘This is for our partners.’ But that which is for their partners does not reach Allāh, and that which is for Allāh reaches their partners. Evil is what they judge.” [Al-An‘ām 6:136]

And when one of them goes to the grave which he venerates, weeps at it, humbles himself, prays, and supplicates, he attains from softness, humility, servitude, and presence of heart  what he does not attain even in the five daily prayers, Jumu‘ah, Qiyām al-layl, or Qur’ān recitation. Is this anything but the state of the innovating mushrikīn and not of the sincere monotheists who follow the Book of Allāh and His Messenger ﷺ?

Source: al-Istighāthah fī ar-Radd ʿalā al-Bakrī by Ibn Taymiyyah p.381-382

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">

<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: الاستغاثة في الرد على البكري</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 381</h4>
<p>الذي فيه استهزاء بالله وآياته ورسوله، مع تعظيم شيخهم وغلوهم فيه (1)، وكذلك النصيرية والإسماعيلية ونحوهم وكثير من طوائف متعددة، [يرى] (2) أحدهم أن استغاثته بالشيخ الميت إما عند قبره وإما عند قبر غيره أنفع له من أن يدعو الله في المسجد عند السحر، ويستهزؤون بمن يعدل عن طريقته إلى التوحيد، ومن هؤلاء من يرى أن زيارة قبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل من الحج إلى الكعبة، وأن دعاء النبي والاستغاثة به أفضل من الاستغاثة بالله ودعائه.</p>
<p>وكثير من هؤلاء يخربون المساجد ويعمرون المشاهد، فتجد المسجد الذي بُني للصلوات الخمس معطلاً مخرباً ليس له كسوة إلا من الناس؛ وكأنه خان من الخانات، والمشهد الذي بني على الميت فعليه الستور؛ وزينة الذهب والفضة والرخام، والنذور تغدوا وتروح إليه، فهل هذا إلا من استخفافهم بالله وبآياته ورسوله [وتعظيمهم] (3) للشرك!!.</p>
<p>فإنهم اعتقدوا أن دعاء الميت الذي بني له المشهد والاستغاثة به أنفع لهم من دعاء الله والاستغاثة به في البيت الذي بُني لله عز وجل، ففضلوا البيت الذي بُني (4) لدعاء المخلوق على البيت الذي بُني لدعاء الخالق، وإذا كان لهذا وقف ولهذا وقف كان وقف الشرك أعظم عندهم مضاهاة لمشركي العرب الذين ذكر الله حالهم في قوله تعالى: {وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ الْحَرْثِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ نَصِيبًا فَقَالُوا هَذَا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وَهَذَا لِشُرَكَائِنَا فَمَا كَانَ لِشُرَكَائِهِمْ فَلَا يَصِلُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ فَهُوَ يَصِلُ إِلَى شُرَكَائِهِمْ سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ (136)} [الأنعام: 136]، كما يجعلون لله زرعاً وماشية ولآلهتهم زرعاً وماشية؛ فإذا أصيب نصيب آلهتهم أخذوا من نصيب الله فوضعوه فيه؛</p>
<p>(1) انظر: الكشف عن حقيقة الصوفية لأول مرة في التاريخ، تأليف محمود عبد الرؤوف القاسم ص 603 وما بعدها، الطبعة الثانية 1413 هـ، الناشر المكتبة الإسلامية عمان - الأردن، والمصادر العامة للتلقي عند الصوفية تأليف صادق سليم ص 232 وما بعدها الطبعة الأولى 1415 هـ، الناشر مكتبة الرشد الرياض - السعودية.</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>كذا في (ح) وفي الأصل و (ف) و (د) ترى.</p>
<p>(3)</p>
<p>كذا في (ف) و (د) و (ح) وفي الأصل تعظيم.</p>
<p>(4)</p>
<p>(بنى) سقطت من (ف).</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 382</h4>
<p>وقالوا (1): الله غني وآلهتنا فقيرة (2)، فيفضلون ما يجعل لغير الله على ما يجعل لله، وهكذا (3) الوقوف والنذور التي تبذل عندهم للمشاهد أعظم (مما تبذل) (4) عندهم للمساجد ولعمارة المساجد وللجهاد في سبيل الله.</p>
<p>وهؤلاء إذا قصد أحدهم القبر الذي يعظمه يبكي عنده ويخضع ويدعو ويتضرع، ويحصل له من الرقة والتواضع والعبودية وحضور القلب، ما لا يحصل له مثله في الصلوات الخمس والجمعة وقيام الليل وقراءة القرآن، فهل هذا (إلا من) (5) حال المشركين المبتدعين لا الموحدين المخلصين المتبعين لكتاب الله ورسوله!! ومثل هذا إذا سمع أحدهم سماع (6) الأبيات يحصل له من الخضوع والخشوع والبكاء ما لا يحصل له مثله عند سماع آيات الله، فيخشع عند سماع المبتدعين المشركين ولا يخشع عند سماع المخلصين المتقين، بل إذا سمعوا آيات الله استثقلوا (7) بها وكرهوها واستهزؤوا بها وبمن يقرؤها، مما يحصل لهم به أعظم نصيب من قوله: {وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّمَا كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلْعَبُ قُلْ أَبِاللَّهِ وَآيَاتِهِ وَرَسُولِهِ كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (65)} [التوبة: 65].</p>
<p>وإذا سمعوا القرآن سمعوه بقلوب لاهية وألسن لاغية كأنهم صم وعمي، واذا سمعوا الأبيات حضرت قلوبهم وسكنت ألسنتهم وسكنت حركاتهم حتى لا يشرب العطشان منهم الماء (8).</p>
<p>ومن هؤلاء من إذا كانوا في سماعهم فأذَّن المؤذن قالوا: نحن في شيء أفضل مما دعانا إليه، ومنهم من يقول: هذا في شغله وهذا في شغله، ومنهم من يقول: كنا في الحضرة فإذا قمنا إلى الصلاة صرنا على الباب.</p>
<p>وقد سألني بعضهم عمن قال ذلك من هؤلاء الشيوخ الضلال؟ فقلت: صدق كان في حضرة الشيطان فصار على باب الله، فإن البدع والضلالة فيها</p>
<p>(1) في (ف) إن.</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>في (د) فقراء.</p>
<p>(3)</p>
<p>في الأصل و (ف) (هؤلاء) وهي زيادة ولا حاجة لها في المعنى.</p>
<p>(4)</p>
<p>ما بين القوسين في (د) مبذول.</p>
<p>(5)</p>
<p>ما بين القوسين في (د) الأمر إلا.</p>
<p>(6)</p>
<p>سقطت من (د) و (ح).</p>
<p>(7)</p>
<p>في (د) اشتغلوا.</p>
<p>(8)</p>
<p>انظر: وصف ابن القيم لحالهم في كتابه: إغاثة اللهفان في مصايد الشيطان 1/ 344 - 347.</p>
</div>
</details>

<!-- evidence-id: 000663 -->

Shaykh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbdul-Wahhāb said:

And none may be sought for help except Him, nor may sacrifices be offered to anyone besides Him, nor vows made for any other—neither for a near angel nor a sent prophet. Whoever does Istighāthah from other than Him has committed disbelief, whoever offers a sacrifice to other than Him has committed disbelief, and whoever makes a vow to other than Him has committed disbelief, and the like of these acts.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said regarding this:

Tawḥīd al-Ulūhiyyah encompasses all acts of worship, and none of them may be directed to anyone other than Allah, for He alone is deserving of them. Whoever dedicates any act of worship to other than Allah is a polytheist, even if he says, “Lā ilāha illa Allāh.” In fact, even if he worships Allah through various acts of devotion, as long as he does not devote all of them sincerely to Allah alone, he is not a Muslim.

Whoever does this has committed disbelief, even if he says, “Lā ilāha illa Allāh,” because he has not truly actualized its meaning. This is a contradiction—how can someone say “Lā ilāha illa Allāh” while offering sacrifices to others besides Him? How can he claim “Lā ilāha illa Allāh” while doing Istighāthah with the dead, the absent, the jinn, or the devils? How can he profess “Lā ilāha illa Allāh” while making vows to other than Allah? This is a clear contradiction.

Source: Sharḥ Tafsīr Kalimat at-Tawḥīd  by Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān p.27-28

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh Abā Buṭayn said in his refutation of Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs:

This belongs to the category of ordinary causes. When a man is known for righteousness and for having his supplications answered, and someone asks or instructs him to supplicate, after which he calls upon Allāh and his supplication is answered, the man himself is not the one who produced the answer. Nor was he asked to perform an act that belongs exclusively to Allāh. He was merely asked to do what he himself is capable of doing, namely supplicating and humbling himself before Allāh.

The verse is therefore among the proofs of tawḥīd, of turning faces toward Allāh, and of directing hearts to Him. Āṣif sought a means to Allāh through affirming His oneness and lordship. He intended Allāh alone and did not turn to Sulaymān or anyone else, even though Sulaymān was superior to him because he was a prophet.

The account also shows that prophets are not to be asked or made the object of one’s request. Indeed, their objective may sometimes be attained at the hands of believers who are below them in rank. It shows that the greatest means and the noblest objective is to single Allāh out in worship and to call upon Him alone without partner, as Āṣif did. It also shows that the allies of Allāh disavow any independent might or power, as indicated by the account: he performed ablution, prayed, and supplicated, saying, “O Possessor of majesty and honor,” as Mujāhid related. Al-Zuhrī said that he said: “Our God and the God of everything, the One God, there is no deity except You, bring me her throne.”

After this, what doubt can remain, and what proof is there in the account that anyone besides Allāh may be called upon?

The Iraqi then launched into rambling and lengthy speech whose substance was that a cause does not act independently and that Allāh is the true actor. By this he intended to argue that calling upon dead and absent righteous people is lawful so long as one believes that Allāh is the true actor.

The refutation of this and the demonstration of the ignorance of its advocate and his departure from the way of the Muslims have already preceded. It has also been established that the foundation and governing principle of Islam is to worship Allāh alone without partner and to single Him out as the sole object of intention and request.

Affirming tawḥīd ar-rubūbiyyah and believing that Allāh alone brings acts into existence is not sufficient for happiness and salvation, nor does it make a person Muslim, until he worships Allāh alone and disavows every rival and deity besides Him.

The Prophet ﷺ said to the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays: “I command you with four matters and forbid you from four matters. I command you to believe in Allāh alone. Do you know what belief in Allāh alone is? It is the testimony that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allāh.”

This is clear, by the praise of Allāh, even if it remains hidden from those whose inner sight resembles that of bats, who have not illuminated themselves with the light of knowledge or taken refuge in a firm support.

Source: Tuḥfat al-Ṭālib wa-al-Jalīs fī Kashf Shubah Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs, pp. 49-50

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: تحفة الطالب والجليس</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 49</h4>
<p>وهذا من جنس الأسباب العادية، فإن الرجل إذا كان معروفاً بالصلاح، وإجابة الدعاء، فطلب منه الدعاء، أو أمر به، فدعا الله واستجيب له، لا يكون هو الفاعل للاستجابة، وليس المطلوب منه ما يختص بالله من الفعل، وإنما يطلب منه ما يختص به من الدعاء والتضرع.</p>
<p>فالآية من أدلة التوحيد، وصرف الوجوه إلى الله، وإقبال القلوب عليه، فإن آصف توسل إلى الله بتوحيده وربوبيته، وقَصَدَه وحده، ولم يقصد سليمان ولا غيره، مع أن سليمان أفضل منه لنبوته.</p>
<p>وفيها أن الأنبياء لا يسألون ولا يقصدون، بل ربما صار حصول مقصودهم، ونيل مطلوبهم على يد من هو دونهم من المؤمنين.</p>
<p>وأن أعظم الوسائل وأشرف المقاصد هو توحيد الله بعبادته ودعائه وحده لا شريك له، كما فعل آصف.</p>
<p>وفيها براءة أولياء الله من الحول والقوة، كما دلت عليه القصة، فإنه1 توضأ، وصلى، ودعا، فقال في دعائه: &quot;يا ذا الجلال والإكرام&quot; قاله مجاهد.</p>
<p>وقال الزهري2: يا إِلهَنا وإله كل شيء، إلهاً واحداً، لا إله إلا أنت، ائتني بعرشها&quot;.</p>
<p>فأي شبهة تبقى مع هذا، وأي حجة فيه على أن غير الله يدعى؟</p>
<p>1 في النسخ الخطية: &quot;وأنه&quot;.</p>
<p>2 في طبعة آل ثاني: &quot;الزيادي&quot; وهو خطأ.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 50</h4>
<p>ثم أخذ العراقي في هذيان وإسهاب حاصله: أن السبب لا يفعل، وأن الله هو الفاعل.</p>
<p>ومراده بهذا أن دعاء الأموات والغائبين من الأولياء والصالحين يجوز ويسوغ، إذا اعتُقِد أن الله هو الفاعل.</p>
<p>وقد مَرَّ رد هذا، وتقرير جهل قائله، ومفارقته لما عليه أهل الإسلام، وقد تقدم أن أصل الإسلام وقاعدته: هي عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له، وإفراده بالقصد والطلب.</p>
<p>وأن توحيد الربوبية، واعتقاد الفاعلية له تعالى لا يكفي في السعادة والنجاة، ولا يكون به الرجل مسلماً حتى يعبد الله وحده، ويتبرآ مما سواه من الأنداد والآلهة.</p>
<p>وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لوفد عبد القيس: &quot;آمركم بأربع، وأنهاكم عن أربع: آمركم بالإيمان بالله وحده، أتدرون ما الإيمان بالله وحده؟ شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله&quot; 1.</p>
<p>وهذا ظاهر بحمد الله، وإن خفي على خفافيش البصائر، الذين لم يستضيئوا بنور العلم، ولم يلجؤوا2 إلى ركن وثيق، فهاموا من</p>
<p>1 أخرجه البخاري في &quot;صحيحه&quot;: كتاب الإيمان (1/ 129) ، وفي العلم (1/ 185) عن ابن عباس قال: إن وفد عبد قيس أتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: &quot;من الوفد –أو من القوم.... الحديث&quot;.</p>
<p>وأخرجه مسلم في &quot;صحيحه&quot;: كتاب الإيمان 1/ 46، 47، 48، 49، 50) ، عن ابن عباس وأبي سعيد.</p>
<p>2 في طبعة آل ثاني: &quot;يلجأوا&quot;.</p>
</div>
</details>

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages4.html#message3880 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000665 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ash-Shaykh said:

Among the things transmitted from his companions such as the author of al-Furūʿ, and likewise those after him among the Ḥanbalīs who authored within the madhhab of Aḥmad, such as the author of al-Inṣāf and al-Tanqīḥ, and likewise those after them among later authors, such as the author of al-Iqnāʿ and al-Muntahā: these and others transmitted, in the chapter on the ruling of the murtadd, from Shaykh al-Islām Aḥmad ibn Taymiyyah that he said:

“Whoever places between himself and Allāh intermediaries that he calls upon, asks, and relies upon, has committed disbelief by ijmāʿ. And this is the madhhab of Aḥmad according to all of his companions.” His statement on intermediaries will appear later, if Allāh wills.

Thus the reliance of the Ḥanbalīs and others from Ahl al-Sunnah on the creed mentioned by Shaykh al-Islām concerning ijmāʿ is based on what will be mentioned from the clear verses, if Allāh wills. For this is what the call of the Messengers agreed upon from the first of them to the last of them. And it is the very purpose for which Allāh created creation: the negation of shirk in ʿibādah, that no type of worship be directed to anyone besides Allāh, whoever that may be.

This is what the Qur’ān indicates from beginning to end. And nothing has been transmitted from any of the salaf of the Ummah, nor from its imāms, permitting the calling upon the dead or the absent, nor permitting istighātha or istishfāʿ (seeking intercession) through them. On the contrary, the prohibition of this has come repeatedly in the clear verses, as we will mention some of that, if Allāh wills.

With what we have mentioned of ijmāʿ, and what the Book and the Sunnah indicate regarding restricting all types of ʿibādah to Allāh alone, and that whoever directs any of it to other than Allāh—for example istighātha from the dead or the absent—is a disbeliever: by all this it becomes clear that this al-ʿIrāqī (Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs) has opposed the Book, the Sunnah, and the ijmāʿ. And it is impossible that anything transmitted from the early generations of the Ummah and its imāms contradicts this ijmāʿ.

He has also opposed the scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah from every madhhab. How far removed he is from the religion upon which they unanimously agreed.

Source: Kashf mā Alqāh Iblīs min al-Bahraj wa-al-Talbīs ʿalā Qalb Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs by Shaykh ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ash-Shaykh p.49-50

<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: كشف ما ألقاه إبليس</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 49</h4>
<p>الشيخ رحمه الله (1) نوعي التوحيد بأتم بيان: توحيد المعرفة والإثبات، وتوحيد الطلب والقصد، ورد على من عارض أدلة التوحيد بشبهة أو تحريف، فهذه كتبه موجودة، وكلها متفقة على هذا المعنى، كالاقتضاء والمنهاج (2) ، وكتاب العقل النقل. وكتاب الفرقان بين أولياء الرحمن وأولياء الشيطان، ورده على ابن الأخنائي ودره على السبكي في مسألة الزيارة، ورده على ابن البكري في مسألة الاستغاثة، وسيأتيك جمل منه إن شاء الله تعالى، وكلامه في أصول الدين مطرد في جميع كتُبه لا اختلاف فيه بحمد الله. فمما نقل عنه أصحابه –رحمه الله –كصاحب الفروع، وكذلك من بعده من الحنابلة المصنفين في مذهب أحمد، كصاحب الإنصاف والتنقيح، وكذا من بعده من المصنفين، كصاحب الإقناع والمنتهى، وقد نقل هؤلاء وغيرهم في باب حكم المرتد عن شيخ الإسلام أحمد بن تيمية –رحمه الله – أنه قال: (من جعل بينه وبين الله وسائط يدعوهم ويسألهم ويتوكل عليهم كفر إجماعاً؛ وهذا هو مذهب أحمد عند أصحابه كلهم) (3) ، وسيأتي كلامه هذا في مسألة الوسائط إن شاء الله تعالى. فصار اعتماد الحنابلة وغيرهم من أهل السنة على اعتقاد ما ذكره (4) شيخ الإسلام –رحمه الله –من الإجماع – [مستنده ما ستذكره في الآيات المحكمات إن شاء الله]- (5) ، لأنه هو الذي اتفقت عليه دعوة الرسل من أولهم إلى آخرهم</p>
<p>(1) زاد في &quot;م&quot;: &quot;تعالى&quot;.</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>يريد بالاقتضاء أي: كتاب &quot;اقتضاء الصراط المستقيم لمخالفة أصحاب الجحيم&quot; ويريد</p>
<p>بالمنهاج أي: كتاب&quot;منهاج السنة النبوية في نقض كلام الشيعة القدرية&quot;.</p>
<p>(3)</p>

<p>وهو الذي خلق الله تعالى (1) الخلق لأجله، وهو نفي الشرك في العبادة بأن لا يُصرف شيء من أنواعها (2) لغير الله كائناً من كان، وهو الذي دل عليه القرآن من أوله إلى آخره، ولم ينقل عن أحد من سلف الأمة وأئمتها أنه أجاز دعوة الأموات والغائبين والاستغاثة (3) والاستشفاع/بهم، وقد تواتر النهي عن ذلك في الآيات المحكمات كما سنذكر بعض ذلك إن شاء الله تعالى. وبما ذكرناه من الإجماع، وما دل عليه الكتاب والسنة من قصر العبادة بجميع أنواعها على الله تعالى، وأن من صرف منها شيئاً لغير الله فاستغاث بغيره من الأموات والغائبين (4) فهو كافر، يبين أن هذا العراقي قد خالف الكتاب والسنة والإجماع-، ومن المحال أن يوجد عن سلف الأئمة وأئمتها ما يخالف هذا الإجماع (5) -، وخالف العلماء من أهل السنة من كل مذهب؛ فما أبعده عن هذا الدين الذي أجمعوا عليه كما قال الشاعر:</p>

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

So reflect—may Allah have mercy on you—on the speech of this imām, and his explicit statement that whoever calls upon the dead and turns to them, and seeks istaghāthah from them so that they may intercede for him with Allah, has committed shirk al-akbar, the shirk for whose rejection Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ.

And for Takfiring the one who does not repent from it, and to fight and show enmity toward him—and that this occurred in his time, and that they altered the religion of the Messenger ﷺ and opposed Ahl al-tawḥīd, those who command them with sincerity in worship to Allah alone, with no partner.

And reflect also on his statement: “And how rare is the one who is freed from this!” Rather, how rare is the one who does not show enmity toward the one who condemns it! The matter will become clear to you, if Allah wills.

But reflect—may Allah guide you—on his statement: “And none is saved from the shirk of this shirk al-akbar except the one who shows enmity to the mushrikin” to the end.

It will become clear to you that Islām is not established except by showing enmity toward the people of this shirk; so if he does not show enmity toward them, then he is from them, even if he does not do it (i.e commit shirk), And Allah knows best.

Source: ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 1/432

<p>{وَاجْنُبْنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَنْ نَعْبُدَ الأَصْنَامَ رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ} [سورة إبراهيم آية: 35-36] . وما نجا من شرك هذا الشرك الأكبر، إلا من جرد توحيده لله، وتقرب بمقتهم إلى الله تعالى انتهى كلامه رحمه الله تعالى.</p>

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Laṭīf Āl ash-Shaykh said:

As for making the dead into means by which one seeks Istighāthah from them, Makes du‘āʾ to them, hopes in them, and venerates them as intermediaries, then this is the religion of the idol worshippers.

The one who does that is takfired by the mere belief and action, even if he does not believe in their independence, as the Qurʾān has stated in more than one place. So al-ʿIrāqī (Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs) is opposing the Qurʾān and contradicting its texts.

Shaykh Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq said:

Shaykh al-Islām (Ibn Taymiyyah) said: “Istighāthah is requesting relief, which means the removal of hardship.” Thus, istighāthah is the duʿāʾ of the distressed one, while duʿāʾ itself is broader in meaning, since it can come from both one in distress and one not in distress.

Duʿāʾ is of two kinds: duʿāʾ al-masʾalah (the supplication of asking) and duʿāʾ al-ʿibādah (the supplication of worship). Duʿāʾ al-masʾalah is asking for what benefits the supplicant, either by gaining some good or by removing some harm. The one who is truly worshipped must therefore have control over benefit and harm. That is why Allāh reproached those who worship other than Him — those who worship what possesses no power to bring benefit or avert harm. This is what the author intended.

As for duʿāʾ al-ʿibādah, it is to worship Allāh through the various acts of worship — such as ṣalāh, zakāh, sacrifice, and others — out of fear and hope: hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment, even if there is no direct wording of request or petition. These two forms of duʿāʾ are inseparably linked: every duʿāʾ al-ʿibādah necessarily implies duʿāʾ al-masʾalah, and every duʿāʾ al-masʾalah inherently contains duʿāʾ al-ʿibādah.

In the Qurʾān, sometimes the term duʿāʾ refers to one of them, sometimes to the other, and sometimes to both together. For example, in His saying: “Call upon Me; I will respond to you.” (Sūrat Ghāfir: 60) — it has been interpreted in both senses: Some said, “Worship Me and obey My command, and I will answer you,” while others said, “Ask of Me, and I will give you.”

And there is ijmāʿ among the scholars that whoever directs any part of either type of duʿāʾ to other than Allāh has committed shirk — even if he says lā ilāha illā Allāh, Muḥammad rasūl Allāh, performs ṣalāh, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim.

Source: Ibṭāl at-Tandīd by Shaykh Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq p.84-85
