The Reality of the contemporary Murji’ah

Shaykh Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān Āl ash-Shaykh said:

We have heard from a group of those who claim knowledge and religion, and who, in their own estimation, follow Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb — that whoever commits shirk and worships idols should not be labeled as a kāfir or mushrik specifically. That is because some of those who spoke to me directly regarding that heard from some of the brothers that he applied Shirk and Kufr to a man because he Made du‘āʾ to the prophet ﷺ and made Istighāthah with him. The man said to him: “Do not call him a kāfir until you make it known to him.”

Such people and their likes show no concern about mixing with the mushrikīn during travel or in their lands. In fact, they even seek knowledge from those who are among the most disbelieving of the scholars of the mushrikīn. They have pieced together for themselves certain shubuhāt to justify their claims — some of which, In Sha Allāh, will be mentioned later in this treatise. They have deceived with these doubts some of the common folk among their followers — those who have no knowledge or those do not know of their condition, and lacking discernment and understanding. They are physically separated from the brothers, yet separated from the Sheikhs with their hearts, and are flattering towards them. They have become alienated and have caused others to feel alienated from them because of the shubuhāt they display and the gloom that has come upon them through mixing with the sinners and mushrikīn.

When examined closely, they do not declare a mushrik to be a disbeliever except in general terms, and even then they hesitate among themselves. Their bidʿah and shubuhāt gradually spread until they deceived even some of the close companions. And Allāh knows best — this occurred due to their neglect of the kutub al-uṣūl (foundational books), their lack of attention to them, and their absence of fear of deviation.

Anyone with the slightest knowledge, upon seeing the condition of people today and examining the beliefs of these mashāyikh, would be utterly bewildered — and there is no power nor strength except through Allāh. One of those I referred to, when I questioned him about this issue, said: “We say to the people of these tombs — those who worship them and those buried within them — your action is shirk, but you are not mushrik.” So look at this, reflect upon it, praise your Lord, and ask Him for safety.

Source: Fatāwā al-Aʾimmah an-Najdiyyah 3/116-117

### ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Ibn Bāz: invoking the dead and the worldly ruling on Ahl al-Fatrah
<!-- evidence-id: 000670 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Ibn Bāz was asked whether it is permissible to eat the slaughtered animals of those who make vows, offer sacrifices, and supplicate to those whom they regard as awliyāʾ when the proof has not removed their doubts.

He answered:

“Whoever is known for holding a corrupt, polytheistic belief, his slaughtered animal is not permissible to eat. If he lives among Muslims, then he has no excuse because he neither inquired nor cared. If it is known that he worships other than Allah, such as those who worship al-Badawī, al-Ḥusayn, al-Ḥasan, ʿAlī, Ibn ʿArabī, or others whom they call awliyāʾ, then such people are disbelievers, and their slaughtered animals are impermissible to eat. The same applies to anyone who worships other than Allah, makes vows for them, offers sacrifices to them, or seeks their aid.

This is major shirk. It is the practice of Jāhiliyyah, the same as what Quraysh did with Hubal, al-Lāt, and al-ʿUzzā, and what the people of Nūḥ did with Wadd, Suwāʿ, and others like them. Such individuals are considered among those upon whom the proof has been established because they live among Muslims, and the Qurʾān, Sunnah, and the words of the scholars have reached them. If someone has not received any of this knowledge, it is only due to his negligence and lack of concern.

As for one who is in a distant land away from the Muslims and belongs to Ahl al-Fatrah, to whom the call has not reached and who has not heard the words of Allah or His Messenger, he has the ruling of the disbelievers in this world, while his matter in the Hereafter is left to Allah. His slaughtered animal is not eaten so long as he practices the deeds of the disbelievers. On the Day of Resurrection he will be tested. If he obeys, he will enter Paradise, and if he disobeys, he will enter the Fire. This is the correct view regarding Ahl al-Fatrah.”

Source: [Official Ibn Bāz fatwa, “The ruling on eating the slaughtered animals of those who hold polytheistic beliefs”](https://binbaz.org.sa/fatwas/8613/حكم-اكل-ذباىح-اصحاب-العقاىد-الشركية).

Supplicating to Other than Allah and istighāthah with them

al-Lajnah ad-Dai’ma was asked:

Q: We request your ruling regarding a group of people who sit in circles inside the mosque, remembering Allah and His Messenger, and who — during their adhkār — say things that contradict tawḥīd. For example, they all say together in one voice: “Take my hand, O Messenger of Allah!” And their leader says things like: “O key to the treasures of Allah! — O Kaʿbah of Allah’s manifestation! — O Throne of Allah’s istiwāʾ! — O Kursī of Allah’s descent! Enrich us, O Messenger of Allah! You are the one intended, O Beloved of Allah! You, you, O Messenger of Allah!” and other similar phrases filled with expressions of shirk.

A: Firstly: Remembering Allah in groups with one voice, as practiced by the Ṣūfiyyah, is an bidʿah. It has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: “Whoever introduces into this matter of ours that which is not from it, it will be rejected.”

Secondly: Calling upon other than Allah and seeking help from them to remove distress or hardship is major shirk, and it is not permissible to do so. This is because duʿāʾ and istighāthah are acts of ʿibādah and devotion due solely to Allah. Directing them to anyone besides Him constitutes major shirk that expels a person from Islam — and we seek refuge in Allah from that.

Allah the Exalted said: “And do not call upon, besides Allāh, that which neither benefits you nor harms you; for if you do so, then indeed you will be among the wrongdoers. And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He; and if He intends good for you, none can repel His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills among His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.” (Yūnus :106–107)

And He said: “And the masājid are for Allāh alone, so do not call upon anyone along with Allāh.” (al-Jinn :18) And He said: And whoever calls upon another god besides Allāh for which he has no proof - then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.” (al-Muʾminūn :117) There are many other verses commanding that ʿibādah (worship) be devoted purely to Allah alone. It is also established in the ḥadīth that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah.” And he ﷺ said: “Duʿāʾ is ʿibādah.”

And Allah grants success. May blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muḥammad, his family, and his Companions.

Source: Fatāwā ʿUlamāʾ al-Balad al-Ḥarām p.63-64

Fatwā no. (10684):

Q: What is the dividing line between kufr and Islam? And does the one who pronounces the shahādatayn, then comes with actions that contradict them, enter among the Muslims despite his ṣalāh and his outward state?

A: The dividing line between kufr and Islam is pronouncing the shahādatayn along with truthfulness, sincerity, and acting according to what they necessitate. So whoever fulfills that is a Muslim believer.

As for the one who commits hypocrisy, then he neither affirmed truthfully nor sincerely, so he is not a believer.

Likewise, the one who pronounces them while coming with what contradicts them from shirk, such as one who seeks istighāthah through the dead in hardship or ease, or one who gives preference to judging by man-made laws over judging by what Allah revealed, or one who mocks the Qurʾān or what is authentically established from the Sunnah of the Messenger of

Allah ﷺ, then this person is a kāfir, even if he pronounces the shahādatayn and prays and fasts.

And with Allah is success. May Allah send prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muḥammad, his family, and his Companions.

The Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Fatwā :

Chairman: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Bāz

Vice Chairman: ʿAbd al-Razzāq ʿAfīfī

Member: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghadayyān

Source: Fatāwā al-Lajnah al-Dāʾimah — First Collection 2/45–46

<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: فتاوى اللجنة الدائمة</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 45</h4>
<p>‌</p>
<p>‌الردة تحبط الأعمال إذا لم يتب منها</p>
<p>فتوى رقم (7658) :</p>
<p>س: في العام قبل الماضي نويت أداء فريضة الحج مقرنا، وما إن وصلت إلى بيت الله الحرام حتى أديت فريضة العمرة، وتعتبر طواف القدوم في نفس الوقت، حيث لم أتشرف بزيارة بيت الله من قبل ثم بعدها بيوم واحد أديت فريضة العمرة نيابة عن والدتي المتوفاة ولما كان هناك متسع من الوقت قبل الذهاب إلى منى في يوم التروية أشار علي الأهل الذين أقضي الوقت عندهم بالتحلل من الإحرام ففعلت وعند الذهاب إلى منى أحرمت من جديد ثم صليت ركعتين بنية الإحرام بالحج فقط في مسجد العمرة، وفي هذه الحالة تعتبر نيتي قد تغيرت من القران إلى التمتع، فهل يشوب حجي أي شائبة رغم قيامي بنحر ذبيحة، وهل تعتبر العمرة التي أديتها نيابة عن والدتي في موسم الحج صحيحة أم أنه لا يجوز تأدية عمرتين في موسم حج واحد، هل أي ذنب يرتكبه الإنسان بعد أدائه الفريضة يؤثر عليها؛ لأننا لسنا منزهين عن الخطأ؟</p>
<p>ج: أولا: تعتبر في حجك المذكور متمتعا بالعمرة إلى الحج، وقد أحسنت فيما فعلت من التحلل من العمرة.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 46</h4>
<p>ثانيا: العمرة التي أديتها عن أمك بعد أن اعتمرت عن نفسك صحيحة إذا كنت أديتها بعد التحلل من عمرتك بالحلق أو التقصير بعد الطواف والسعي.</p>
<p>ثالثا: ما كان من الذنوب دون الكفر الأكبر لا يبطل الأعمال الصالحة، ولكن تكون المقاصة بين حسنات وسيئات من خلط عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا ما لم يتب منها أو يعف الله عنه. أما الردة عن الإسلام - والعياذ بالله - فتحبط جميع الأعمال الصالحة إذا مات على ردته. ومن تاب منها توبة نصوحا لم تحبط أعماله الصالحة؛ فضلا من الله ورحمة، قال الله تعالى: {وَمَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَيَمُتْ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُولَئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ} (1)</p>
<p>وبالله التوفيق. وصلى الله على نبينا محمد، وآله وصحبه وسلم.</p>

<!-- evidence-id: 000673 -->

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān said:

This is the meaning of īmān: that you believe in your heart that Allāh alone deserves ʿibādah, and that everything worshipped besides Allāh is false — whether angels, prophets, righteous people, stones, trees, or idols. You must also have disbelief in all of these. This is the meaning of īmān in Allāh: that you believe in your heart that no one deserves worship except Him, and that whatever is worshipped besides Him is false. This is required by this ʿaqīdah.

It is not enough to say this with your tongue without believing it in your heart. Nor is it enough to perform outward actions — ṣalāh, fasting — while saying, “I worship only Allāh,” but then saying: “I don’t know about those who worship graves and shrines; I can’t say they are wrong, because they pray and fast and say lā ilāha illā Allāh.”

We say: you have not understood the meaning of lā ilāha illā Allāh, nor the meaning of īmān in Allāh and kufr biṭ-ṭāghūt. Had you understood properly, you would know that īmān in Allāh is not valid except with disbelief in ṭāghūt — outwardly with the tongue and inwardly with conviction.

This is the meaning of īmān in Allāh: that you direct all ʿibādah to Him alone and direct none of it to another. A person may perform ṣalāh, fast, and give zakāh, yet does Istighāthah from someone besides Allāh, or sacrifice to someone besides Him. Such a person has worshipped Allāh in some things and worshipped others in some things — and is therefore a mushrik.

As for the one who worships Allāh in some ʿibādah, and worships others in other types of ʿibādah, this person has not truly believed in Allāh. Like those who fasts, perform ṣalāh, perform ḥajj, and pronounce the shahādātayn, but then call upon others besides Allāh — they call upon the dead, sacrifice for the dead, make vows to the dead, and circumambulate at the graves. These people have not worshipped Allāh; rather, they are mushrikūn.

Because the worship of Allāh and worship of others can never unite. Allāh - Jalla wa ʿAlā - says: “I am free of partners in shirk, so whoever performs an action in which he associates someone with Me, I leave him and his shirk; and in another narration, "it is for the one who associates, and I am free of him.”

Allāh does not accept that anyone be associated with Him in any type of ʿibādah. Rather, all ʿibādah must be solely for Allāh. As He says: "And fight against them until there is no fitnah [i.e shirk] and [until] the religion [i.e., worship], all of it, is for Allāh." [al-Anfāl: 39]. Thus, no part of the religion can be for Allāh and another part for idols, graves, or anyone else — the religion must be entirely for Allāh.

Source: Sharḥ Maʿnā al-Ṭāghūt by Shaykh al-Fawzān p.12-13

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4906 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000674 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān said:

And his statement: “lā sharīka lahu (there is no partner to Him)” is an emphasis of negation; meaning that devotion to Him negates any sharing with Him in anything of devotion .

And there is no partner to Him in turning to Him or ʿibādah (worship), so it is necessary for the servant to be knowing and acting upon its meaning and what it indicates.

From this it becomes clear that those who do not know its meaning fall into apparent contradictions: you find them, for example, saying “lā ilāha illa Allāh” while performing ṭawāf around the graves, seeking istighāthah from their occupants, and calling upon them secretly and openly.

And this is the shirk akbar which this statement nullifies. If they were of those who truly knew its meaning and knew what it signifies, they would not do such actions. Even the kuffār of old used to know its meaning.

Source: Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān 1/84

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4444 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000675 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Muḥsin al-ʿAbbād was asked:

Q: We have people in our country who go to shrines and graves for duʿāʾ , tamassuḥ (seeking blessings by touching), and request of good. Does this make them kafir in a definite sense?

A: A person who performs Istighāthah with the inhabitants of the grave and asks them to fulfill needs or remove hardships — this is the right of Allah. And the right of Allah is not to be diverted except to Him. It cannot be directed to anyone else. So whoever does this should not be prayed behind if he were an imām.

And his ṣalāh is invalid in the sense that it is not correct to follow him. Whoever worships besides Allah, performs Istighāthah from other than Allah, or asks for fulfillment of needs from anyone other than Allah — this person is kāfir. That is, one does not pray behind him and he is treated like the kuffār.

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4393 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000676 -->

Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī was asked:

Q: Is the ṣalāh valid behind an imām who performs istighāthah from the dead and asks them for aid, or not?

A: This man is a kāfir. Whoever performs istighāthah from the dead and asks them for aid, and asks them for fulfillment of needs and relief of hardships, is a mushrik. The ṣalāh behind him is not valid, and praying behind him is invalid.

Whoever prayed behind him without knowing his condition, then later comes to know it, must repeat the ṣalāh. This is by the ijmāʿ of the Muslims that prayer is not valid behind a mushrik.

The disagreement among the scholars regarding the validity of praying behind a fāsiq (open sinner):

1.    The Ḥanābilah and a group of scholars prohibit praying behind him and say it is not valid.

2.   Others say it is valid but disliked.

The correct view is that it is valid, but praying behind a upright person is better. This is if he is a muwaḥḥid (monotheist) but sinful. As for the mushrik, prayer behind him is not valid by ijmāʿ.

Source: Asʾilah wa Ajwibah fī al-Īmān wa al-Kufr by Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Rājihī p.35

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4248 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000677 -->

Shaykh Abī al-ʿAlā ar-Rāshid said:

Despite all these evidences clarifying the weighty conditions with which this great statement has been bound, many people pronounce this statement without fulfilling its conditions or avoiding its nullifiers, and this is of no benefit to them by ijmāʿ.

The reciter: "He said: this is what benefits the one who says Lā ilāha illā Allāh. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: “he has grasped the firmest handhold”. This is unlike the one who says it while calling upon other than Allah and making istighāthah with them—whether from a dead person or an absent one—who neither benefits nor harms, as is seen among most of creation. These people have said it, yet they have become involved in what contradicts it. Thus it does not benefit the one who says it except with knowledge of its meaning, in negation and affirmation.

The one who is ignorant of its meaning, even if he says it, it does not benefit him due to his ignorance of what it was established for, according to the Arabic usage intended by it—namely, the negation of shirk. Likewise, if he knows its meaning without certainty. So where then is certainty with doubt?"

The Shaykh then said: Yes, here is an affirmation of an important foundational principle by which the shaykh refutes the Murjiʾah and those who followed their path in the era of Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله, such as Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs. They argued against the shaykh, saying: “You declare disbelievers those who say Lā ilāha illā Allāh.” So he established the principle that whoever says Lā ilāha illā Allāh while being involved in a nullifier —such as making duʿāʾ to the dead, making istighāthah with them, or believing that they bring benefit —this statement, along with involvement in a nullifier, does not benefit its speaker.

Likewise, the one who says it while ignorant of its meaning: it does not benefit him due to his ignorance, for one of its foremost conditions is knowledge of its meaning. This is one of the foundational principles that the shaykh established in refutation of those who say: “You declare people disbelievers who say Lā ilāha illā Allāh.”

However, this does not necessarily mean that it is to be used as evidence for the statements of some extremists who test people and harbor evil suspicion toward them. The one who pronounces Lā ilāha illā Allāh: if he pronounces it while not being involved in shirk, it is accepted from him; and if he pronounces it while being involved in shirk, it is not accepted from him.

### Ṭalab al-duʿāʾ and requesting intercession from the dead
<!-- evidence-id: 000678 -->

Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said:

“Whoever takes the angels and prophets as intermediaries, calls upon them, relies upon them, and asks them to bring benefits and repel harms, such as asking them for the forgiveness of sins, the guidance of hearts, the relief of distress, and the fulfillment of needs, is a disbeliever by the consensus of the Muslims.”

[Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā, 1/124]

---

<!-- evidence-id: 000679 -->
Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said:

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="user-supplied-text">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَمَعْلُومٌ أَنَّ هَذَا لَيْسَ مِنْ دِينِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَلَا دِينِ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ، لَمْ يَسُنَّ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ لِلْخَلْقِ أَنْ يَطْلُبُوا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ الْمَوْتَى، وَالْغَائِبِينَ، وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ، دُعَاءً، وَلَا شَفَاعَةً، بَلْ هَذَا أَصْلُ الشِّرْكِ، فَإِنَّ الْمُشْرِكِينَ إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذُوهُمْ شُفَعَاءَ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: {وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ هَؤُلَاءِ شُفَعَاؤُنَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قُلْ أَتُنَبِّئُونَ اللَّهَ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ} [يُونُس: 18].</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">[قَاعِدَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ فِي الْفَرْقِ بَيْنَ عِبَادَاتِ أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَالْإِيمَانِ وَعِبَادَاتِ أَهْلِ الشِّرْكِ وَالنِّفَاقِ، ص. 121]</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

“It is well known that this is neither from the religion of the Muslims nor from the religion of any of the messengers. No prophet ever prescribed for people that they ask the deceased righteous, those who are absent, or the angels for supplication or intercession. Rather, this is the very foundation of shirk, for the polytheists only took them as intercessors. Allāh, the Exalted, said: ‘They worship besides Allāh what can neither harm nor benefit them, and they say, “These are our intercessors with Allāh.” Say, “Do you inform Allāh of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?”’ [Yūnus 10:18].”

[Qāʿidah ʿAẓīmah fī al-Farq bayna ʿIbādāt Ahl al-Islām wa-al-Īmān wa-ʿIbādāt Ahl al-Shirk wa-al-Nifāq, p. 121]

---

<!-- evidence-id: 000680 -->
Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said:

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="user-supplied-text">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَالْمَقْصُودُ هُنَا: أَنَّهُ إِذَا كَانَ السَّلَفُ وَالْأَئِمَّةُ قَالُوا فِي سُؤَالِهِ بِالْمَخْلُوقِ مَا قَدْ ذُكِرَ، فَكَيْفَ بِسُؤَالِ الْمَخْلُوقِ الْمَيِّتِ؟ سَوَاءٌ سُئِلَ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ اللَّهَ أَوْ سُئِلَ قَضَاءَ الْحَاجَةِ، وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ، مِمَّا يَفْعَلُهُ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ، إِمَّا عِنْدَ قَبْرِ الْمَيِّتِ، وَإِمَّا مَعَ غَيْبَتِهِ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">[اقْتِضَاءُ الصِّرَاطِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ لِمُخَالَفَةِ أَصْحَابِ الْجَحِيمِ، 2/330]</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

“What is intended here is this: if the Salaf and the imams said what has already been mentioned concerning asking Allāh by means of a created being, then what of asking the deceased created being himself? This applies whether he is asked to ask Allāh or is asked to fulfill a need, and similar practices carried out by some people, either at the deceased person’s grave or while he is absent.”

[Iqtiḍāʾ al-Ṣirāṭ al-Mustaqīm li-Mukhālafat Aṣḥāb al-Jaḥīm, 2/330]

---

<!-- evidence-id: 000681 -->
Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said:

“If you establish intermediaries between Allāh and His creation like the chamberlains between a king and his subjects, such that they convey the needs of His creation to Allāh, and Allāh only guides and provides for His servants through their intercession, while the creation asks them and they ask Allāh, just as intermediaries before kings ask the kings to fulfill the people’s needs because of their proximity to them, and the people ask those intermediaries either out of respect that prevents them from asking the king directly or because asking the intermediaries is more effective than asking the king, since they are closer to the king than the petitioner, then whoever establishes them as intermediaries in this manner is a disbeliever and a polytheist. He is to be asked to repent; if he repents, that is accepted, and otherwise he is to be killed. Such people have likened Allāh to His creation, likened created beings to the Creator, and established rivals alongside Allāh.”

[Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā, 1/126]

---

<!-- evidence-id: 000682 -->
Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said:

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="user-supplied-text">
<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>فَإِنَّ مُشْرِكِي الْعَرَبِ وَغَيْرَهُمْ مِمَّنْ يُقِرُّ بِأَنَّ الرَّبَّ فَاعِلٌ بِمَشِيئَتِهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ، وَأَنَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَأَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ مَخْلُوقَةٌ لِلَّهِ، لَيْسَتْ مُقَارِنَةً لَهُ فِي الْوُجُودِ دَائِمَةً بِدَوَامِهِ، كَانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ لِيُقَرِّبُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ زُلْفَى، وَيَتَّخِذُونَهُمْ شُفَعَاءَ يَشْفَعُونَ لَهُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ، بِمَعْنَى أَنَّهُمْ يَدْعُونَ اللَّهَ لَهُمْ فَيُجِيبُ اللَّهُ دُعَاءَهُمْ لَهُمْ. وَهَؤُلَاءِ الْمُشْرِكُونَ الَّذِينَ بَيَّنَ الْقُرْآنُ كُفْرَهُمْ وَجَاهَدَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى شِرْكِهِمْ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">[الرَّدُّ عَلَى الْمَنْطِقِيِّينَ، ص. 101]</p>
</div>
</details>

**English**

“The Arab polytheists and others acknowledged that the Lord acts by His will and power, that He is the Creator of everything, and that the heavens and the earth were created by Allāh and were not coexistent with Him in existence or everlasting with His everlastingness. Nevertheless, they worshipped others besides Allāh so that those beings might bring them nearer to Him, and they took them as intercessors to intercede for them before Allāh, meaning that those intercessors would supplicate to Allāh on their behalf and Allāh would answer their supplication for them. These are the polytheists whose disbelief the Qurʾān made clear and whom the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ fought because of their shirk.”

[al-Radd ʿalā al-Manṭiqiyyīn, p. 101]

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message755 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000683 -->

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (رحمه الله) said:

The way of the Companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him) was that they worshipped Allah alone by what their Prophet commanded them. The lawful for them was what he declared lawful, the forbidden was what he declared forbidden, and the religion was what he legislated. They prayed the five prayers as Allah commanded, at their appointed times, in congregation in the mosques. They fasted the month of Ramadan, performed the Hajj to the Ancient House, paid the zakat, commanded the good and forbade the evil, strove in the way of Allah, and worshipped Allah by all else that their Prophet commanded them. They worshipped none but Allah, and called upon none other than Allah, neither from what is in the heavens nor from what is in the earth: not the angels, not the celestial bodies, not the prophets, not their images. Indeed they knew that all of this falls under the polytheism that Allah and His Messenger have forbidden.

They supplicated to no created being, whether angel, jinn, or human, whether prophet or otherwise, neither at his grave nor in his absence. They sought help from none but Allah, sought victory from none but Allah, placed their trust in none but Allah. They did not supplicate to any absent or dead created being, nor did they call upon him in distress, nor complain to him, nor ask him for forgiveness, guidance, or support. Rather they sought all of this from Allah.

They did not do as the Christians do, seeking intercession through angels or through the dead among the prophets and the righteous, whether at their graves or elsewhere. None of them would say: 'O Gabriel, O Michael, intercede for me with Allah,' nor would any say: 'O Ibrahim, O Musa, O Isa, intercede for me with Allah,' as the Christians do. Rather they knew that nothing is to be asked of one who is absent, and nothing is to be asked of one who is dead, and that the angels do not act except by what their Lord commands them, and they do not intercede except for whom He approves, and likewise the prophets and the righteous. However, one may ask any of them during their lifetime for supplication and intercession, just as the Companions used to ask that of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and just as creation will ask him for intercession on the Day of Resurrection, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him.

[A Great Principle on the Difference Between the Worship of the People of Islam and Faith and the Worship of the People of Polytheism and Hypocrisy, pg. 31-32]

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message534 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000684 -->

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

The mushrikūn among these people might say: “We seek ishtishāf (intercession) through them,” meaning we ask the angels and prophets to intercede. So when we approach the grave of someone, we request them to intercede for us. When we depict their statue—whether the statues are three-dimensional or pictured statues as the Christians depict in their churches—they say: “Our intention with these statues is to remember their owners and their lives, and we address these statues with the purpose of addressing their owners to intercede for us with Allāh.”

Then one of them might say: “O my master Fulān" or "O my master Jirjis" or "Butrus" or "the kind Lady Maryam". Or "O my master al-Khalīl" or "Mūsā ibn ʿImrān" or others, intercede for me with your Lord.” They may address the deceased at their grave or address someone alive but absent, just as they would if that person were present. They recite poems in which one of them says: “O my master Fulān! I am under your protection, I am in your vicinity, intercede for me with Allāh, ask Allāh to grant us victory over our enemy, ask Allāh to remove this hardship from us, I complain to you about such and such, so ask Allāh to relieve this distress.” Or someone might say: “Ask Allāh to forgive me.”

These types of addressing angels , prophets, and the righteous after their death at their graves or in their absence, and addressing their statues, is among the greatest forms of shirk found among mushrikūn who are not Ahl al-Kitāb, among innovators of the Ahl al-Kitāb, and Muslims who introduced acts of shirk and worship that Allāh did not permit. Allāh, the Exalted, says (42:21): "Or have they partners with Allâh (false gods) who have instituted for them a religion which Allâh has not ordained?"

Thus, calling upon angels and prophets after their death, seeking them, asking for help through them, seeking intercession from them in this way—and erecting statues of them as a means of requesting intercession—is part of a religion that Allāh did not legislate, that no Messenger was sent to legislate, and that no book was revealed for. It is neither obligatory nor recommended by ijmāʿ of the Muslims.

None of the Ṣaḥābah or the Tābiʿīn performed this in a proper manner, nor did any Imām of the Muslims command it. Even if many people who practice worship and asceticism do this and narrate stories and visions about it, all of this is from Shayṭān. Some even compose poems in the context of supplicating the deceased, seeking intercession or aid, or mention this within praise of the prophets and righteous. All of this is not sanctioned—neither obligatory nor recommended—by the ijmāʿ of the Muslim scholars.

Source: al-Qā‘idah al-Jalīlah fī al-Tawassul wa al-Wasīlah by Ibn Taymiyyah p.23-25

<summary>Show Arabic source text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: قاعدة جليلة في التوسل والوسيلة</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 23</h4>
<p>الجاهل (1) ، فمنهم من يحب شخاً فيتزيّا في صورته ويقول: أنا فلان. ويكون ذلك في برِّية ومكان قفر فيطعم ذلك الشخص طعامًا ويسقيه شراباً أو يدله على الطريق أو يخبره ببعض الأمور الواقعة الغائبة فيظن ذلك الرجل أن نفس الشيخ الميت أو الحي فعل ذلك، وقد يقول: هذا سر الشيخ وهذه رقيقته (2) وهذه حقيقته أو هذا مَلَكٌ جاء على صورته. وإنما يكون ذلك جنيًّا، فإن الملائكة لا تعين على الشرك والإفك والإثم والعدوان. وقد قال الله تعالى (17: 56 - 57) : {قُلْ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ فَلَا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ الضُّرِّ عَنكُمْ وَلَا تَحْوِيلاً أُوْلَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ الْوَسِيلَةَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُ وَيَخَافُونَ عَذَابَهُ إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ كَانَ مَحْذُورًا} .</p>
<p>47 -</p>
<p>قال طائفة من السلف: كان أقوام يدعون الملائكة والأنبياء كالعزير والمسيح، فبين الله تعالى أن الملائكة والأنبياء عباد الله (3) ، كما أن الذين يعبدونهم عباد الله، وبين أنهم يرجون رحمته ويخافون عذابه ويتقربون إليه كما يفعل سائر عباده الصالحين.</p>
<p>48 -</p>
<p>والمشركون من هؤلاء قد يقولون: إنا نستشفع بهم أي نطلب من الملائكة والأنبياء أن يشفعوا، فإذا أتينا قبر أحد طلبنا منه أن</p>
<p>(1) في ز: الجاهل العابد، وفي هذا الكلام إشارة إلى الآية الكريمة: {وأنا منا الصالحون ومنا دون ذلك، كنا طرائق قدداً} (سورة الجن: 11) .</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>أي طيفه. وكل من رق جسده ونفسه يسمى رقيقًا.</p>
<p>(3)</p>
<p>والمسيح عليه السلام يتبرأ من الذين اتخذوه وأمه إلهين، وذلك يوم يسأله الله سبحانه: {أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني وأمي إلهين من دون الله قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق} . (المائدة 116) .</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 23</h4>
<p>وسواع</p>
<p>…</p>
<p>إلخ ولقد قالوا في حماس: {وقالوا لا تذرن آلهتكم ولا تذرن ودًّا ولا سواعًا ولا يغوث ويعوق ونسرًا} سورة نوح، آية (23) .</p>
<p>إن هذا الإمام المجاهد المناضل عن التوحيد والحق قد وقف حياته للدعوة إلى الحق في ميادينه مدافعًا عنه بكل ما منحه الله من طاقات ومواهب، واضعًا نصب عينيه كتاب الله وسنة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وما أُثِر عن السلف الصالح من الصحابة والتابعين لهم بإحسان في مجال العقيدة والعبادة والتشريع وسائر الميادين الإسلامية، وفي هذا الكتاب الجليل قد عالج القضايا الآتية:</p>
<p>1 -</p>
<p>التوسل وأنواعه وأشياء تتعلق وترتبط به.</p>
<p>2 -</p>
<p>الشفاعة بأنواعها وأشياء تجر إليها من لا يفهم.</p>
<p>3 -</p>
<p>الدعاء بأنواعه.</p>
<p>مفرقاً فيها بين الحق والباطل والهدى والضلال بالأدلة الواضحة والحجج الساطعة.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 24</h4>
<p>يشفع لنا، فإذا صورنا تمثاله - والتماثيل إما مجسدة وإما تماثيل مصورة كما يصورها النصارى في كنائسهم - قالوا: فمقصودنا بهذه التماثيل تذكر أصحابها وسيرهم ونحن نخاطب هذه التماثيل ومقصودنا خطاب أصحابها ليشفعوا لنا إلى الله. فيقول أحدهم: يا سيدي فلاناً أو يا سيدي جرجس أو بطرس أو ياستي الحنونة مريم. أو يا سيدي الخليل أو موسى ابن عمران أو غير ذلك، اشفع لي إلى ربك. وقد يخاطبون الميت عند قبره أو يخاطبون الحي وهو غائب، كما يخاطبونه لو كان حاضراً حياًّ وينشدون قصائد يقول أحدهم فيها: يا سيدي فلانا! أنا في حسبك، أنا في جوارك، اشفع لي إلى الله، سل الله لنا أن ينصرنا على عدونا، سل الله أن يكشف عنا هذه الشدة، أشكو إليك كذا وكذا فسل الله أن يكشف هذه الكربة. أو يقول أحدهم: سل الله أن يغفر لي. ومنهم من يتأول قوله تعالى: (4: 64) : {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ ظَلَمُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ جَاءُوكَ فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا اللَّهَ وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمْ الرَّسُولُ لَوَجَدُوا اللَّهَ تَوَّابًا رَحِيمًا} .</p>
<p>49 -</p>
<p>ويقولون: إذا طلبنا منه الاستغفار بعد موته كنا بمنزلة الذين طلبوا الاستغفار من الصحابة، ويخالفون بذلك إجماع الصحابة والتابعين لهم بإحسان وسائر المسلمين، فإن أحداً منهم لم يطلب من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد موته أن يشفع له ولا سأله شيئاً ولا ذكر ذلك أحد من أئمة المسلمين في كتبهم، وإنما ذكر ذلك من ذكره من متأخري الفقهاء وحكوا حكاية مكذوبة على مالك رضي الله عنه سيأتي ذكرها وبسط الكلام عليها (1) إن شاء الله تعالى.</p>
<p>(1) انظر: (ص 121) .</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 24</h4>
<p>‌</p>
<p>‌منهج شيخ الإسلام في هذا الكتاب</p>
<p>إن هذا الإمام واسع الاطلاع، طويل الباع، عميق الفهم فهو الإمام الفذ في التفسير وعلومه، والحافظ الناقد في الحديث وعلومه، وهو الفقيه المبرز والأصولي المتمكن، والمجتهد المطلق، والعالم بالملل والنحل، والمنطق والفلسفة والتصوف والكلام، والعارف بأباطيلها وزيفها وغشها وخداعها.</p>
<p>عرف العلوم المسماة بالعقلية أكثر من أهلها المختصين فيها وعرف عيوبها وزيفها وخطرها وما تؤدي إليه من ضلال وهلاك، فوجه ما حباه الله به من طاقات، فزلزل قواعدها، ودك معاقلها.</p>
<p>وعرف التصوف وما ينطوي عليه من شرور وخرافات وأباطيل واصطلاحات فاسدة ومغالطات تفسد وتدمر الدين والعقل، فثلَّ عروشه ودمر قواعده، وكشف تلك المغالطات بالحجج الواضحة والبراهين الساطعة.</p>
<p>وخرج من معاركه العلمية والجهادية ظافرًا منتصرًا انتصاراً حاسماً فلا ترى لخصومه إلى يومنا هذا إلا معارك فاشلة وحججاً متهاوية وكلاماً فارغاً إلا من المغالطات التي لا تنطلي إلا على الأغبياء.</p>
<p>ومن علامات هزائمهم أن كثيراً منهم يتظاهرون بمدحه واحترامه، ثم يكيدون لدعوته إلى التوحيد بنقل ما يزعمون أنه يؤيد باطلهم من كلامه بعد بتره وتشويهه.</p>
<p>هذا ما يقال بصفة إجمالية بالنسبة لجهوده في مؤلفاته الجليلة.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 25</h4>
<p>50 -</p>
<p>فهذه الأنواع من خطاب الملائكة والأنبياء والصالحين بعد موتهم عند قبورهم وفي مغيبهم، وخطاب تماثيلهم، هو من (1) أعظم أنواع الشرك الموجود في المشركين من غير أهل الكتاب، وفي مبتدعة أهل الكتاب والمسلمين الذين أحدثوا من الشرك والعبادات ما لم يأذن به الله تعالى، قال الله تعالى (2) (42: 21) : {أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَاءُ شَرَعُوا لَهُمْ مِنْ الدِّينِ مَا لَمْ يَأْذَنْ بِهِ اللَّهُ} . فإن دعاء الملائكة والأنبياء بعد موتهم وفي مغيبهم وسؤالهم والاستغاثة بهم والاستشفاع بهم في هذه الحال - و [نصب] تماثيلهم بمعنى طلب الشفاعة منهم - هو من الدين الذي لم يشرعه الله ولا ابتعث به رسولاً ولا أنزل به كتاباً، وليس هو واجباً ولا مستحباً باتفاق المسلمين، ولا فعله أحد من الصحابة والتابعين/ لهم بإحسان، ولا أمر به إمام من أئمة المسلمين، وإن كان ذلك مما يفعله كثير من الناس ممن له عبادة وزهد، ويذكرون فيه حكايات ومنامات، فهذا كله من الشيطان. وفيهم من ينظم القصائد في دعاء الميت والاستشفاع به والاستغاثة، أو يذكر ذلك في ضمن مديح الأنبياء والصالحين، فهذا كله ليس بمشروع لا واجب ولا مستحب باتفاق أئمة المسلمين.</p>
<p>51 -</p>
<p>ومن تعبد بعبادة ليست واجبة ولا مستحبة وهو يعتقدها واجبة أو مستحبة فهو ضال مبتدع بدعةً سيئة لا بدعة حسنة باتفاق أئمة الدين، فإن الله لا يُعبد إلا بما هو واجب أو مستحب (3) . وكثير من</p>
<p>(1) كلمة &quot;من&quot; سقطت من: ز، ب.</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>&quot;قال الله تعالى&quot; سقطت من: ز.</p>
<p>(3)</p>
<p>في خ: &quot;واجبا أو مستحبا&quot;.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 25</h4>
<p>أَمَّا منهجه في هذا الكتاب فإنه يعرض القضية من القضايا ويدرسها من كل النواحي التي تتطلبها الدراسات العلمية؛ من الناحية اللغوية والتفسيرية والحديثية والتأريخية والأصولية والفقهية، ويضرب الأمثال، ويقرب النظير من الأمور إلى نظيره بطريقة فذة تدل على غزارة علمه وقوة استحضاره وقدرته على استحضار الأمثال والأشباه من المسائل وهذا شأنه في جميع مؤلفاته رحمه الله.</p>
<p>وإنني لأعترف أنني لم أوف هذا الكتاب حقه من الدراسة لأسباب منها؛ خوف الإطالة وضيق وقتي، فأجتزئ بنماذج من منهجه الفذ في هذا الكتاب القيم.</p>
<p>قال رحمه الله فيما يتعلق بلفظ التوسل فقرة (236) : &quot;إذا عرف هذا فقد تبين أن لفظ الوسيلة والتوسل فيه إجمال واشتباه يجب أن تعرف معانيه ويعطى كل ذي حق حقه، فيعرف ما ورد به الكتاب والسنة من ذلك ومعناه، وما كان يتكلم به الصحابة، ويفعلونه ومعنى ذلك، ويعرف ما أحدثه المحدثون في هذا اللفظ ومعناه. فإن كثيراً من اضطراب الناس في هذا الباب هو بسبب ما وقع فيه من الإجمال والاشتراك في الألفاظ ومعانيها حتى تجد أكثرهم لا يعرف في هذا الباب فصل الخطاب&quot;.</p>
<p>ثم بين معاني التوسل والوسيلة في لغة القرآن والسنة وكلام الصحابة وأن من أعظم معاني التوسل التقرب إلى الله بالإيمان بالله ورسله وكتبه واليوم الآخر والقيام بكل واجب ومستحب أمر الله به ورسله، وطاعة الرسول في كل ما أمر به ونهى عنه، وأن من معانيه: التوسل إلى الله بدعائه وشفاعته في حياته في الدنيا وبدعائه وشفاعته في</p>
</div>
</details>

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said:

So this intercession (ash-shafāʿah) which the Qur’an negated includes the negation of what the mushrikūn of the Arabs used to say, and those similar to them from the other mushrikīn.

And it is of the same type as the shirk of the Christians and those like them among the misguided who affiliate themselves with Islam, where they believe regarding the angels or the prophets or the shuyūkh that they are intercessors for them with Allāh — just as the intercessors intercede with the kings of the world.

And they strike for Allāh an analogy and say: whoever wants to draw near to a great king should not come to him first, but rather draw near to those close to him, who then raise his needs and bring him near to him.

Allāh the Exalted said: “And those who take Awliyâ’ besides Him (say): "We worship them only that they may bring us near to Allâh."” [az-Zumar: 3] That is, they say: “We do not worship them except that they may bring us near to Allāh.”

He mentioned this after His saying: "The revelation of the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] is from Allāh, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book, [O Muḥammad], in truth. So worship Allāh, [being] sincere to Him in religion. Unquestionably, for Allāh is the pure religion.

And those who take Awliyâ’ besides Him (say): "We worship them only that they may bring us near to Allâh. Indeed, Allāh will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allāh does not guide he who is a liar and disbeliever." [az-Zumar :3]

Source: al-Radd ʿalā al-Manṭiqiyyīn by Ibn Taymiyyah p.571-572

Shaykh Muḥammad Ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said:

It is said to this ignorant person: if you know that the ilāh is the one who is worshipped, and you know that duʿāʾ is from ʿibādah (worship), then how do you call upon a created being, a dead one, one who is incapable? And you leave the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, the Present, the Compassionate, the Merciful, the All-Powerful?

So this mushrik may say: “The matter is in the hand of Allah, but this righteous servant will intercede for me with Allah, and his intercession and rank will benefit me,” and he thinks that this saves him from shirk.

Source: ad-Durar as-Saniyyah 2/104

<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: الدرر السنية في الأجوبة النجدية</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 104</h4>
<p>واعلم أن من ذبح لغير الله، من جني أو قبر، فكما لو سجد له; وقد لعنه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحديث الصحيح، قال: &quot; لعن الله من ذبح لغير الله &quot;1.</p>
<p>ومن أنواع العبادة: الدعاء؛ كما كان المؤمنون، يدعون الله وحده، ليلا ونهارا، في الشدة والرخاء، لا يشك أحد، أن هذا من أنواع العبادة، فتفكر&quot; رحمك الله&quot; فيما حدث في الناس اليوم، من دعاء غير الله في الشدة والرخاء; هذا يريد سفرا، فيأتي عند قبر أو غيره، فيدخل عليه بما له، عمن ينهبه، وهذا تلحقه الشدة، في البر، أو البحر، فيستغيث بعبد القادر، أو شمسان، أو نبي من الأنبياء، أو ولي من الأولياء، أن ينجيه من هذه الشدة.</p>
<p>فيقال لهذا الجاهل: إن كنت تعرف أن الإله هو: المعبود، وتعرف أن الدعاء من العبادة، فكيف تدعو مخلوقا، ميتا، عاجزا؟! وتترك الحي، القيوم، الحاضر، الرؤوف، الرحيم، القدير؟! فقد يقول&quot; هذا المشرك&quot;: إن الأمر بيد الله، ولكن هذا العبد الصالح يشفع لي عند الله، وتنفعني شفاعته وجاهه; ويظن أن ذلك يسلمه من الشرك.</p>
<p>فيقال لهذا الجاهل: المشركون عباد الأصنام، الذين قاتلهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وغنم أموالهم وأبناءهم ونساءهم، كلهم يعتقدون أن الله هو النافع، الضار، الذي يدبر الأمر، وإنما أرادوا ما أردت من الشفاعة عند الله، كما قال</p>
<p>1 مسلم: الأضاحي (1978) ، والنسائي: الضحايا (4422) ، وأحمد (1/108 ،1/118 ،1/152) .</p>
</div>

<!-- evidence-id: 000687 -->
Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said:

It is said that this report is itself a proof against the disputant. When that man made his request of the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet did not say, “I will supplicate for you.” Rather, he instructed them to do what he had legislated and established for them: that they themselves call upon Allāh and seek rain from Him. The report states that he told the man, “Tell ʿUmar to be prudent,” meaning to remain upright. When this was conveyed to ʿUmar, he said, “I spare no effort.”

Thus, the report contains an instruction to obey Allāh and His Messenger and to seek rain from Allāh. This was the same law the Messenger established for them during his life. After his death he instructed them only with what he had instructed them during his life. The man who said to him, “Supplicate for your nation,” is unknown and was not among the Emigrants or the Helpers whose example is followed. It is sufficient that not one of them went to his grave to request supplication from him. The most knowledgeable people concerning his religion and those who followed him most closely, the Emigrants and the Helpers, did not go to him or request supplication from him.

Moreover, the person who requested the supplication was not granted his request, nor was he told, “I will supplicate for you.” Rather, he was told in effect: obey my command and call upon Allāh yourselves, and He will answer you.

This is the truth with which Allāh sent him. Happiness in this world and the Hereafter lies in obeying him, following him, taking him as one’s example, doing what he commanded, leaving what he prohibited, taking his allies as allies, opposing his enemies, treating as lawful what he declared lawful, treating as unlawful what he declared unlawful, and believing everything he reported concerning Allāh, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the other matters of the unseen. He is truthful and confirmed in everything he reports. “He does not speak from his own desire. It is only revelation revealed.” [An-Najm 53:3-4]

Had the Messenger ﷺ legislated that Muslims request from him forgiveness, victory, rain, and other forms of supplication and desire after his death, just as they requested these things from him during his life and as the creation will request him to intercede on the Day of Resurrection, his command to do so would have been well known and transmitted from him, just as the rest of what he commanded was transmitted. He said: “I have left nothing that brings you closer to Paradise except that I have informed you of it, and nothing that takes you farther from the Fire except that I have informed you of it.” He also said: “I have left you upon a clear path whose night is like its day; none deviates from it after me except one who is destroyed.”

Abū Dharr said: “The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ died, and there was not even a bird turning its wings in the sky except that he had mentioned knowledge of it to us.”

If he had established for them the practice of requesting supplications from him after his death, it would have been known to them and transmitted from him. His Companions would have known it better than anyone else, and they were the most obedient to him and the closest followers of his Sunnah. They would therefore have gone to his grave after his death and asked him to supplicate for their forgiveness, guidance, victory, provision, the payment of their debts, the removal of their afflictions, and other matters, just as some of them requested his supplication during his life.

Yet their leading figures, such as Abū Bakr and those like him, had learned from him to ask none but Allāh and to call upon none but Allāh. When the whip fell from the hand of al-Ṣiddīq, he would not say to anyone, “Hand it to me,” and he would say, “My intimate friend instructed me not to ask people for anything.” Aḥmad narrated this in the Musnad.

The Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn ʿAbbās: “When you ask, ask Allāh; and when you seek aid, seek aid from Allāh.” In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, ʿAwf ibn Mālik related that the Prophet took a pledge from a group of his Companions and privately instructed them “not to ask people for anything.” ʿAwf said: “I later saw one of those men drop his whip from his hand and not ask anyone to hand it to him.”

It is also established in an agreed-upon authentic ḥadīth that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning. They are those who do not request ruqyah, do not cauterize, do not regard omens, and rely upon their Lord.” These people do not say to anyone, “Perform ruqyah for us.” Although some people came to the Prophet ﷺ and requested ruqyah from him or from some of his Companions, and although doing so is permissible, those seventy thousand ask none but Allāh and therefore possess a higher rank.

After the Prophet’s death, the Companions did not ask him for anything they had asked him for during his life, neither supplication nor anything else whatsoever. Nor did the predecessors of the first three generations go to the grave of any prophet or righteous person to request from him a need, a supplication, or anything else. They did not travel to his grave. When they visited the graves of the believers, their purpose was to supplicate for the deceased, as they did in the funeral prayer. Their purpose was not to call upon them or to call upon Allāh through them.

It is therefore clear that the position of the majority of scholars, who do not recommend requesting forgiveness or anything else from the Prophet ﷺ after his death, is the legislated position practiced by the Companions.

Furthermore, if it were legislated to request supplication and intercession from a dead person just as they were requested from him during his life, this would be legislated with respect to every prophet and righteous person. A man would then be encouraged to go to the grave of a righteous person, whether a prophet or otherwise, and say: “Supplicate for my forgiveness, victory, guidance, and provision. Intercede for me with your Lord.” He would thereby take the righteous person as an intercessor after death, as the Christians and many Muslim innovators do.

If it were permissible to make this request of the dead, it would also be permissible to request it from the angels by saying, “O Jibrīl, O Mīkāʾīl, intercede for us with your Lord and supplicate for us.”

It is known that this is not part of the religion of the Muslims or the religion of any messenger. No prophet ever legislated for people that they request supplication or intercession from dead or absent righteous people or from angels. Rather, this is the foundation of shirk, for the polytheists took them only as intercessors. Allāh says: “They worship besides Allāh that which neither harms nor benefits them, and they say, ‘These are our intercessors with Allāh.’ Say, ‘Are you informing Allāh of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?’” [Yūnus 10:18]

Source: Qāʿidah ʿAẓīmah fī al-Farq bayna ʿIbādāt Ahl al-Islām wa-al-Īmān wa ʿIbādāt Ahl al-Shirk wa-al-Nifāq by Ibn Taymiyyah, pp. 117-121

<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: قاعدة عظيمة في الفرق بين العبادات</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 117</h4>
<p>قيل: هذه الحكاية حجّة على المنازع، فإن هذا الرجل لما طلب منه، ما قال له: أنا أدعو لكم، بل أمرهم بما شرعه لهم، وسنه لهم، وهو أنهم يدعون الله، ويستسقون به. وفي الحكاية أنه قال /48أ/ له: قل لعمر: عليك بالكيس، أي بالاستقامة، فلما قال لعمر قال: ما آلو جهدي.</p>
<p>فهذا فيه أنه أمرهم بطاعة الله ورسوله وأمرهم بالاستسقاء، وهذا هو شرعه الذي شرعه لهم في حياته، فلم يأمرهم بعد الموت إلا بما أمرهم في حياته، وهذا الرجل الذي قال له: ادع لأمتك، مجهول، ما هو من المهاجرين، والأنصار، الذين يقتدى بهم، ويكفيك أنه لم يأت أحد منهم إلى قبره يطلب منه الدعاء إلا رجل مجهول، لا يُعرف، فأما المهاجرون والأنصار الذين هم أعلم الناس بدينه، وأتبعهم له، فلم يأت أحد إليه، ولم يطلب منه الدعاء، ثم هذا الطالب للدعاء لم يُعط طلبته (1) ، ولا قال: أنا أدعو لكم، بل قال: أطيعوا أمري، وادعوا أنتم الله يجيبكم.</p>
<p>وهذا هو الحق الذي بعثه الله به، فإن سعادة الدنيا والآخرة في طاعته، واتباعه، والاقتداء به، وفعل ما أمر، وترك ما حظر، وموالاة أوليائه، ومعاداة أعدائه، وتحليل ما حلّل، وتحريم ما حرّم، وتصديقه في كل ما أخبر به عن الله، وملائكته، وكتبه، ورسله، واليوم الآخر، وغير ذلك من أنباء</p>
<p>(1) غيرت في المطبوع إلى: (طلبه) .</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 118</h4>
<p>الغيب، بل هو الصادق المصدوق في كل ما يخبر به، وهو الذي لا {يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَى • إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَى} ، وقد استأذنه عبد الله بن عمرو في أن يكتب ما يسمع منه، وقال له بعض قريش: إن رسول الله /48ب/ صلى الله عليه وسلم يتكلم في الغضب والرضا، فقال: «اكْتُبْ فَوَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ مَا خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمَا إِلَّا حَقٌّ (1) » .</p>
<p>ولو كان قد شرع للمسلمين أن يطلبوا منه الاستغفار، والاستنصار، والاستسقاء، وغير ذلك من أنواع الأدعية، والرغبات، كما كانوا يطلبون ذلك منه في حياته، وكما يطلب منه الخلق يوم القيامة أن يشفع لهم، لكان أمره بذلك معروفًا، منقولاً عنه، كما نقل سائر ما أمرهم به، فإنه قد قال: «مَا تَرَكْتُ شَيْئًا يُقَرِّبُكُمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ إِلَّا وَقَدْ حَدَّثْتُكُمْ بِهِ، وَلَا شَيْئًا يُبْعِدُكُمْ مِنَ النَّارِ إِلَّا وَقَدْ حَدَّثْتُكُمْ بِهِ (2) » وقال: «تَرَكْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْبَيْضَاءِ لَيْلُهَا كَنَهَارِهَا لَا يَزِيغُ عَنْهَا بَعْدِي إِلَّا هَالِكٌ» .</p>
<p>(1) غيرت في المطبوع إلى: (الحق) .</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>في الأصل: (حذرتكم منه) وهو خطأ، وقد صححها المحقق في المطبوع إلى: (حدثتكم عنه) ، ثم عدلتها أنا إلى ما يوافق معظم روايات شيخ الإسلام لهذا الحديث في كتبه الأخرى، وهو: (حدثتكم به) .</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 119</h4>
<p>وقال أبو ذر: لقد توفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما طائر يقلب جناحيه في السماء إلا ذكر لنا (1) منه علمًا.</p>
<p>فلو كان سنّ لهم أن يطلبوا منه الأدعية بعد موته لكان هذا معروفًا عندهم منقولاً عنه، ولكان أصحابه أعلم بذلك من غيرهم، وهم أطوع له، وأتبع لسنته، فكانوا بعد موته يأتون قبره فيطلبون منه أن يدعو لهم بالمغفرة، ويدعو لهم بالهداية، ويدعو لهم بالنصر، ويدعو لهم بالرزق، ويدعو لهم بقضاء الديون، ويدعو لهم بكشف الضُّر، وغير ذلك كما كان بعضهم /49أ/ يطلب منه الدعاء في حياته، مع أن أجِلائهم كأبي بكر وأمثاله قد تعلموا منه أنهم لا يسألون إلا الله، ولا يدعون إلا الله، فكان الصديق يسقط السوط من يده فلا يقول لأحد: ناولني إياه، ويقول: إِنَّ خَلِيلِي أَمَرَنِي أَنْ لَا أَسْأَلَ النَّاسَ شَيْئًا. رواه أحمد في المسند.</p>
<p>وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لابن عباس: «إِذَا سَأَلْتَ فَاسْأَلِ اللَّهَ، وَإِذَا اسْتَعَنْتَ فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ» . وفي صحيح مسلم عن عوف بن مالك: أَنَّهُ بَايَعَ رَهْطًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ، وَأَسَرَّ إِلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَةً خَفِيَّةً: «أَنْ لَا (2) تَسْأَلُوا النَّاسَ شَيْئًا» . قَالَ: فَلَقَدْ</p>
<p>(1) في الأصل: (ذكرنا) ، والتصويب من المحقق.</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>غيرت في المطبوع إلى: (ألا) .</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 120</h4>
<p>رَأَيْتُ بَعْضَ أُولَئِكَ النَّفَرِ يَسْقُطُ السَّوْطُ مِنْ يَدِهِ فَلَا يَقُولُ لِأَحَدٍ: نَاوِلْنِي إِيَّاهُ.</p>
<p>وقد ثبت في الحديث المتفق على صحته أنه قال: «يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مِنْ أُمَّتِي سَبْعُونَ أَلْفًا بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ؛ هُمُ الَّذِينَ لَا يَسْتَرْقُونَ، وَلَا يَكْتَوُونَ، وَلَا يَتَطَيَّرُونَ، وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ» . فهؤلاء لا يقولون لأحد: ارقنا، وقد كان جماعة يأتون إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويطلبون منه الرقية ويطلبون ذلك من بعض أصحابه، وهذا وإن كان جائزًا لكن أولئك لا يسألون إلا الله، فدرجتهم أعلى، وأما بعد موته، فلم يكن الصحابة يطلبون منه ما كانوا يطلبون منه في حياته، لا من دعاء، ولا من غير دعاء البتة، ولا كان السلف في القرون الثلاثة يأتون إلى قبر أحدٍ من الأنبياء، والصالحين، يطلبون منه حاجة، ولا دعاء، ولا غيره، ولا يسافرون إلى قبره، بل إذا /49ب/ زاروا قبور المؤمنين كان مقصودهم الدعاء لهم كالصلاة على جنائزهم، لا دعاؤهم، ولا الدعاء بهم.</p>
<p>فتبين أن قول جمهور العلماء الذين لا يستحبون أن يطلب منه بعد موته استغفار، ولا غيره، هو المشروع الذي كان عليه الصحابة.</p>
<p>وأيضًا فلو شرع أن يطلب من الميت الدعاء، والشفاعة، كما كان يطلب منه في حياته؛ كان ذلك مشروعًا في حق الأنبياء، والصالحين، فكان يسنّ أن يأتي الرجل قبر الرجل الصالح، نبيًّا كان، أو غيره، فيقول</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 121</h4>
<p>ادع لي بالمغفرة، والنصر، والهدى، والرزق، اشفع لي إلى ربك، فيتخذ الرجل الصالح شفيعًا بعد الموت، كما يفعل ذلك النصارى، وكما تفعل كثير من مبتدعة المسلمين، وإذا جاز طلب هذا منه، جاز أن يطلب ذلك من الملائكة، فيقال: يا جبريل، يا ميكائيل، اشفع لنا إلى ربك، ادع لنا.</p>
<p>ومعلوم أن هذا ليس من دين المسلمين، ولا دين أحد من الرسل، لم يسنّ أحد من الأنبياء للخلق أن يطلبوا من الصالحين الموتى، والغائبين، والملائكة، دعاء، ولا شفاعة، بل هذا أصل الشرك، فإن المشركين إنما اتخذوهم شفعاء، قال تعالى: {وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ هَؤُلَاءِ شُفَعَاؤُنَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قُلْ أَتُنَبِّئُونَ اللَّهَ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ /50أ/ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ} [يونس: 18] .</p>
<p>وقال: {وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَى كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَتَرَكْتُمْ مَا خَوَّلْنَاكُمْ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِكُمْ وَمَا نَرَى مَعَكُمْ شُفَعَاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّهُمْ فِيكُمْ شُرَكَاءُ لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْكُمْ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ} [الأنعام: 94] .</p>
<p>وقال تعالى: {وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لَا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَرْضَى} [النجم: 26] .</p>
<p>وقال تعالى: {قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا لَهُمْ فِيهِمَا مِنْ شِرْكٍ وَمَا لَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ ظَهِيرٍ • وَلَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ حَتَّى إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ قَالُوا مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُوا الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ} [سبأ: 22-23] .</p>
<p>وقال: {وَأَنْذِرْ بِهِ الَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنْ يُحْشَرُوا إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ وَلِيٌّ وَلَا شَفِيعٌ} [الأنعام: 51] .</p>
</div>
</details>

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message1535 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000688 -->

Sheikh ’Abd ar-Raḥmān ash-Shaykh said:

The Author (Sheikh Muhammad Ibn Abdul Wahhab) رحمه الله said: On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever dies while calling upon a rival to Allah besides Him will enter the Fire. ” Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

Explanation:

Ibn al-Qayyim said: Al-nidd (الند) means a counterpart or equal. It is said: “So-and-so is the nidd of so-and-so” or his equivalent, meaning his equal and counterpart. End quote. Allah Almighty said:

“So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know [the truth].” (Al-Baqarah: 22)

His statement: (Whoever dies while calling upon a rival to Allah besides Him) —meaning: he assigns a rival to Allah in worship, calling upon him, asking him, and seeking his aid— “will enter the Fire.”

Al-ʿAllāmah Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Beware of shirk, for it is evident and clear, This type shall never be forgiven.

It is to set up a rival to the Most Merciful, regardless of who it may be—whether a stone or a human being.

He calls upon it, hopes for it, then fears it, and loves it, just as the love of the Sustainer.

And know that setting up a rival to Allah is of two types:

The first: To make that rival a partner with Allah in any type of worship, or in some of it, as previously mentioned. This is major shirk.

The second: It is the type of minor shirk, such as saying: “What Allah wills and you wills,” or “If it weren’t for Allah and you.” Also, slight showing off (riya). It is confirmed that when a man said to the Prophet ﷺ, “What Allah wills and you wills,” he replied, “Did you make me a partner with Allah? Rather, what Allah alone wills.” This was narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah, al-Bukhārī in his Al-Adab al-Mufrad , al-Nasā’ī, and Ibn Mājah.

In this, it is evident that calling upon others besides Allah for something that only Allah can do is clear shirk, such as seeking intercession from the dead. The right of intercession belongs to Allah alone, and He has control over it, while no one else holds any part of it. It is He who permits the intercessor to intercede for those who meet Allah with sincerity and monotheism, from among the people of major sins.

Source: Fatḥ al-Majīd by Sheikh ’Abd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥasan ibn ash-Shaykh p.65-66

<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: فتح المجيد شرح كتاب التوحيد</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 65</h4>
<p>قوله: &quot;إذ رفع لي سواد عظيم&quot; المراد هنا الشخص الذي يرى من بعيد.</p>
<p>قوله: &quot;فظننت أنهم أمتي&quot;؛ لأن الأشخاص التي ترى في الأفق لا يدرك منها إلا الصورة. وفي صحيح مسلم: &quot;ولكن انظر إلى الأفق&quot; ولم يذكره المصنف; فلعله سقط في الأصل الذي نقل الحديث منه. والله أعلم.</p>
<p>قوله: &quot;فقيل له: هذا موسى وقومه&quot; أي موسى بن عمران كليم الرحمن، وقومه: اتباعه على دينه من بني إسرائيل1.</p>
<p>فنظرت فإذا سواد عظيم، فقيل لي: هذه أمتك ومعهم سبعون ألفا يدخلون</p>
<p>1 في قرة العيون: فيه فضيلة اتباع موسى من بني إسرائيل ممن آمن منهم بالرسل. والكتب التي أنزلها الله: التوراة، والإنجيل، والزبور، والفرقان وغيرها. وكانت بنو إسرائيل قبل التفرق كثيرين وفيهم الأنبياء، ثم بعد ذلك حدث ما حدث من اليهود، وهذا الحديث يدل على أن التابع لموسى عليه السلام كثيرون جدا، وقد قال تعالى: 45: 16 (وفضلناهم على العالمين) ، أي في زمانهم. وذلك أن في زمانهم وقبله ممن كفر بالله خلقا لا يحصون، كحزب جالوت وبختنصر وأمثالهم. ففضل الله بني إسرائيل بالإيمان فصاروا أفضل أهل زمانهم، وحدث فيهم ما ذكر الله في سورة البقرة وغيرها من معصيتهم لأنبيائهم واختلافهم في دينهم، وقد ذكره الله تعالى محتجا به على اليهود الذين كفروا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فتدبر ما ذكره الله تعالى من أحوالهم بعد الاختلاف.</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 66</h4>
<p>قوله: &quot;فنظرت فإذا سواد عظيم، فقيل لي: هذه أمتك ومعهم سبعون ألفا يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب ولا عذاب&quot;، أي لتحقيقهم التوحيد، وفي رواية ابن فضيل: &quot;ويدخل الجنة من هؤلاء من أمتك سبعون ألفا&quot;. وفي حديث أبي هريرة في الصحيحين: &quot;أنهم تضيء وجوههم إضاءة القمر ليلة البدر&quot;. وروى الإمام أحمد والبيهقي في حديث أبي هريرة: &quot;فاستزدت ربي فزادني مع كل ألف سبعين ألفا&quot;. قال الحافظ: وسنده جيد12.</p>
<p>قوله: &quot;ثم نهض&quot; أي قام. قوله: &quot;فخاض الناس في أولئك&quot; خاض بالخاء والضاد المعجمتين. وفي هذا إباحة المناظرة والمباحثة في نصوص الشرع على وجه</p>
<p>صحبوا رسول الله صلي الله عليه وسلم. وقال بعضهم: فلعلهم الذين ولدوا في الإسلام، فلم يشركوا بالله شيئا، وذكروا أشياء. فخرج عليهم رسول الله صلي الله عليه وسلم فأخبروه، فقال: هم الذين لا يسترقون،</p>
<p>الاستفادة وبيان الحق، وفيه عمق علم السلف لمعرفتهم أنهم لم ينالوا ذلك إلا بعمل. وفيه حرصهم على الخير. ذكره المصنف3.</p>
<p>قوله: &quot;فقال: هم الذين لا يسترقون&quot; هكذا ثبت في الصحيحين وهو كذلك في حديث ابن مسعود في مسند أحمد. وفي رواية لمسلم:</p>
<p>&quot;ولا يرقون&quot; قال شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية:</p>
<p>1 صحيح: أحمد (2/359) : وقال الحافظ في الفتح (11/410) : &quot;وسنده جيد&quot; ا. هـ وصححه الألباني في الصحيحة (1486) لشواهده.</p>
<p>2 في قرة العيون: فيه فضيلة هذه الأمة وأنهم أكثر الأمم تابعا لنبيهم صلى الله عليه وسلم، وقد كثروا في عهد الصحابة رضي الله عنهم، وفي وقت الخلفاء الراشدين ومن بعدهم، فملأوا القرى والأمصار والقفار، وكثر فيهم العلم، واجتمعت لهم الفنون في العلوم النافعة، فما زالت هذه الأمة على السنة في القرون الثلاثة المفضلة، وقد قلوا في آخر الزمان. قال شيخنا - رحمه الله تعالى - في مسائله: ((وفيه فضيلة هذه الأمة بالكمية والكيفية، فالكمية الكثرة والعدد، والكيفية فضيلتهم في صفاتهم)) .</p>
<p>3 في قرة العيون: وفيه أيضا فضل الصحابة رضي الله عنهم في مذاكرتهم العلم وحرصهم على فهم ما حدثهم به نبيهم صلى الله عليه وسلم حرصا على العمل به، وفيه جواز الاجتهاد فيما لم يكن فيه دليل؛ لأنهم قالوا ما قالوا باجتهادهم، ولم ينكر صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك عليهم، لكن المجتهد إذا لم يكن معه دليل لا يجوز له أن يجزم بصواب نفسه، بل يقول: لعل الحكم كذا وكذا كقول الصحابة رضي الله عنهم في هذا الحديث.</p>

Shaykh ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ash-Shaykh said:

What has already been established clarifies that asking the dead or the absent, and seeking intercession through them to Allāh, is exactly the religion of the mushrikūn among the Arabs and those before them. For Allāh sent His Messengers only to oppose this, as has been established in the verses on al-shafāʿah and those similar to them, and in what came from the Master of the Messengers:

"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I call only upon my Lord, associating none with Him ˹in worship˺.” Say, “It is not in my power to harm or benefit you.” ˹My duty is˺ only to convey ˹the truth˺ from Allah and ˹deliver˺ His messages.” And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger will certainly be in the Fire of Hell, to stay there for ever and ever." [al-Jinn: 20-23]

So reflect on what is in these verses, and what the Exalted has arranged as a consequence for opposing the Messenger ﷺ in what he commanded towards and conveyed from Allāh regarding His tawḥīd, namely the threat of the Fire and eternal residence therein. And the Qurʾān, from beginning to end, establishes this call, directs to it, forbids everything that contradicts it—whether in speech, deed, or belief—and warns them of Himself and cautions them about His punishment.

Source: Kashf mā Alqāh Iblīs min al-Bahraj wa-al-Talbīs ʿalā Qalb Dāwūd ibn Jirjīs by Shaykh ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ash-Shaykh p.219

Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī said:

Allāh declared disbelievers those who spoke a word of disbelief in jest and mockery while traveling, even though they testified that lā ilāha illā Allāh and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah. They came apologizing to the Rasūl ﷺ and swearing oaths, yet Allah revealed about them: “Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after your īmān.” And the inner states are left to Allāh.

The explicit wording of one who calls upon other than Allah, seeks refuge in him, do istaghātha with him, or requests his shafā‘a (intercession) after his death, is greater in kufr than that of one who uttered such words concerning the Rasūl ﷺ and his companions in jest or mockery. For supplication to other than Allah and asking for what only Allah can do is the very foundation of the world’s shirk — none who has even smelled the fragrance of dīn would doubt this. The proof is clear, and the sign is evident.

And whoever says that the one who does such a thing is still a Muslim is among those who have fabricated lies against Allāh. For Allah has declared disbelievers those who made with Him another god, and He has stated explicitly that a person does not enter Islām except by worshipping Allah alone with no partner and by disavowing everything that is worshipped besides Him, as mentioned previously.

However, this objector is either among the most foolish of people, the dullest of mind, and the most ignorant of Allāh, His dīn, and His shar‘ (law); or else he deliberately lies and cares nothing for it.

Source: as-Sayf al-Maslūl ʿalā ʿĀbid ar-Rasūl by Shaykh ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Qāsim an-Najdī p.126

Shaykh Ibn Bāz was asked:

Question: May Allah reward you well, Shaykh! What about someone who goes to a grave and asks the deceased to make Duʿāʾ for them with Allah?

Answer: This is also shirk, because the dead have no power to do that. If one says to the deceased: “Intercede for me, make Duʿāʾ to Allah for me,” they are committing shirk according to the correct view, because they are asking for something beyond the person’s ability.

Question: Some people claim that this is the view of Ibn Taymiyyah [i.e it is a innovation]. Is that correct?

Answer: No, this is not correct about Ibn Taymiyyah. Ibn Taymiyyah explicitly stated that this is shirk al-akbar.

Source: Sharḥ Kashf ash-Shubuhāt by Shaykh Ibn Bāz p.59

Is talab ad-du‘āʾ (requesting du‘āʾ) from the dead, shirk?

Shaykh al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: If a person goes to the occupant of a grave and asks him to make duʿāʾ to Allāh for him, is that considered shirk, since some people have reported from Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah that this action is a bidʿah?

A: This is shirk. Seeking needs from the dead is shirk—whether duʿāʾ or anything else. The one who makes an exception for duʿāʾ and says it is not shirk—he must bring the evidence.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: Is there a difference between asking a dead person for duʿāʾ and asking him for shafāʿah? Because I heard some people say that asking for duʿāʾ is an innovation, while asking for shafāʿah is shirk. Is this distinction correct?

A : Duʿāʾ is shafāʿah. What is the meaning of shafāʿah? Its meaning is that he supplicates for you, and Allāh responds to his supplication. That is shafāʿah. Shafāʿah is supplication on behalf of another. So there is no difference between them.

Shaykh Ṣāliḥ al-Fawzān was asked:

Q: Noble shaykh, may Allāh grant you success. If I see a person committing acts of shirk, such as calling upon the dead and seeking intercession from them, how should I treat him—do I treat him as a Muslim or as a kāfir?

A: You treat him as a Muslim while he is committing shirk and you can hear him committing shirk and calling upon other than Allāh?!!! Treat him as a mushrik, but call him to Islam. Explain to him that this is major shirk, and clarify the danger of shirk, from the angle of calling to Allāh and offering sincere advice. Yes.

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān said:

The sixth point: the major issue is that worship of Allāh is not achieved except through kufr biṭ-ṭāghūt (disbelief in false deities). In this lies the meaning of the statement of Allāh: “So whoever disbelieves in ṭāghūt and believes in Allāh has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it.” (al-Baqarah: 256)

The shaykh explains that Allāh forbids matters that were actually occurring among people in his time. Among people are those who, according to their claim, worship Allāh, while they also worship the ṭāghūt, and they believe that they are Muslims. The ṭāghūt has already been defined as everything that is worshipped besides Allāh. If it is living and rational, then it must be qualified by being pleased with that worship. As for if it is dead, or an inanimate object, or something else, then it is known that it has no command and no choice, yet it may still be worshipped.

Its worship consists of performing tabarruk (seeking blessings) from it, turning toward it with duʿāʾ, seeking the removal of calamities and the relief of distresses, or ṭawāf around the graves of those who are called awliyāʾ, sitting devotedly at their graves seeking blessing, or seeking intercession, saying: intercede for me, or the like. All of this is worship of the ṭāghūt.

Kufr biṭ-ṭāghūt is a condition for the existence of īmān, because kufr biṭ-ṭāghūt is avoidance of shirk. This is like the statement of Allāh: “Worship Allāh and associate nothing with Him.” (al-Nisāʾ: 36) Therefore, duʿāʾ, ṭawāf, and all worship must be purely for Allāh alone; no part of it belongs to any created being whatsoever.

Source: Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghunaymān 1/70

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

Al-shafā‘ah (intercession) only occurs under two conditions:

First: permission from Allāh for the shāfi‘ (intercessor).

Second: approval for the one for whom intercession is sought. Allāh does not permit anyone to be taken out of the Fire except for the sinful muwaḥḥidīn, and Allāh only approves of those upon tawḥīd and sincerity.

As for the kāfir, Allāh does not approve of him, and no one can intercede for him. Whoever dies upon shirk without dying upon tawḥīd has no share in al-shafā‘ah. Allāh says: “So no intercession of intercessors will be of any use to them.” [al-Muddaththir: 48].

Source: Shurūḥ Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Mujaddid Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb by Shaykh ar-Rājihī 2/327

Shaykh Ayman al-ʿAnqarī said:

We hear from some who claim to be Muslims the phrase: “O Messenger of Allah, intercede for me” or “Intercession, O Muhammad.” This phrase is not permissible; asking for intercession from the Prophet ﷺ is major shirk because intercession belongs to Allah alone. Allah, the Exalted, says: “Say, ‘To Allah belongs [all] intercession’”. The Prophet ﷺ and other deceased people have no power over anything—not intercession nor supplication—because he ﷺ said: “When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three…” Since intercession is among matters that only Allah can grant, the dead have no power over it. Therefore, beware of this phrase.


---

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message735 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000698 -->

Shaykh Ayman al-ʿAnqarī said:

Ibn Taymiyyah transmitted the consensus of the Companions that requesting intercession from the dead is shirk without qualification, whether one is at the deceased person's grave or away from it. This is because legal responsibility has ceased for the deceased. He is not like a living person from whom one requests something that Allāh has commanded him to do, such as an act of worship, obedience, or benefiting another person.

This refutes those who claim that doing so at the grave is merely a bidʿah while doing so from afar is shirk. It also refutes those who attribute this distinction to Ibn Taymiyyah.

Dr. Ayman al-ʿAnqarī said:

The Intended Meaning of the One Who Abandons Tawḥīd

He is the one who falls into a nullifier from the nullifiers of the statement of tawḥīd: Lā ilāha illa Allāh, whether that nullifier is in the domain of rubūbiyyah—such as believing in a god, creator alongside Allāh, or denying the existence of Allāh, or believing that among the awliyāʾ and imāms are those who control the universe, or that Allāh has delegated the management of the affairs of the world to the saints and imāms.

And among that: to believe that the one who brought this child into being is such-and-such saint or the occupant of such-and-such shrine—because in this is attributing creation to other than Allāh, exalted is He.

And among that: the statement of the doctrine of waḥdat al-wujūd—that Allāh and the universe are one entity, and that Allāh—exalted and far above that—is this very universe in itself, with everything in it from among the created beings. Or if it is in the domain of ulūhiyyah — such as calling upon and istighāthah from the Prophet ﷺ or from the saints in matters that no one is capable of except Allāh—such as fulfilling needs, removing hardships, and guiding hearts. Or requesting intercession from the Prophet ﷺ by saying: “O Messenger of Allāh, intercede for me with Allāh.”

Or approaching al-Badawī or al-Dusūqī or al-Ḥusayn or ʿAlī and saying: “Madad, madad” or “Rescue me” or “Cure me of my illness,” or offering a sacrifice to the occupant of the grave out of veneration for him. Or a woman who cannot conceive goes to those called awliyāʾ and requests from them to become pregnant, saying: “O Master so-and-so, grant me a child.” Or seeking blessings from the graves of the saints with the belief that they elevate needs to Allāh, exalted is He, Or performing ṭawāf around the graves of the awliyāʾ out of glorification and drawing near to them, Or making a vow to other than Allāh. This is what is meant here by abandoning tawḥīd.

Source: Taḥrīr qawl al-shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿUthaymīn fī tārik al-tawḥīd by Dr. Ayman al-ʿAnqarī p.16-17

Fatawa of Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Jarbūʿ on ṭalab al-du‘ā’

I asked: As-salāmu ‘alaykum wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh.

Our respected Shaykh, I hope you are well. I have a question: We know that whoever excuses the mushrik and calls him a Muslim is undoubtedly among the ghulāt al-murji’ah. However, some people have confusion regarding the issue of ṭalab al-du‘ā’ due to a misunderstanding of Ibn Taymiyyah’s words when he referred to it as a bid‘ah. How should we deal with them? Should they be treated the same as in the first issue, or is this dealt with differently?

We know that if something is a bid‘ah, it can lead to excusing the mushrik in his shirk, and this is one of the doubts used by the murji’ah to justify excusing the mushrik. But how do we deal with those who fell into this doubt because of some statements from the scholars on this matter, where they claim that there is khilāf (difference of opinion) about it?

Shaykh ʿAbd Allāh al-Jarbūʿ responded:

Wa ‘alaykum as-salām wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh.

It is a bid‘ah and it is shirk — it is both a bid‘ah and shirk. When speaking with people who claim it is obligatory and legislated, the response is: it is not legislated, but rather a bid‘ah. When Shaykh al-Islām discussed the rulings concerning it, he said: such a person is a kāfir, and if he repents, then it is accepted, but if not, he is to be executed. At another time, he said: it is kufr by the consensus of the Muslims. So it is both a bid‘ah and kufr.

As for those people, they should be taught. Tell them to learn and to gather the strongest statements of Shaykh al-Islām on the issue.

Saying it is a bid‘ah does not mean it is not shirk. No—it is a bid‘ah that is shirk.

Shaykh Abdullah Ibn Zayd said:

These two great verses, or this great verse, indicate a profound matter, which is exactly what the author—who speaks the truth—intends to clarify and explain. It contains a response to the doubt raised by those mushrikīn , the worshippers of graves and saints, who are many in our time. We see them performing pilgrimage and ʿumrah , yet they say: “O so-and-so, heal me. O so-and-so, grant me health. O so-and-so, remove this from me. I come to you in supplication, fearful and anxious; remove the affliction and disease from me.”

This is a greater shirk because they call upon and seek help from other than Allah. Even if they perform Hajj, fast, and give zakah, it benefits them nothing, because they have associated others with Allah, the Most High. Whoever associates anyone with Allah, Allah does not forgive him; He will nullify all his deeds of prayer and worship: “But if you associate others with Me, surely your deeds will become worthless, and you will surely be among the losers.” [Quran 39:65]

This verse and the following one are perfectly suited to refute this great doubt and misguidance of these people, because the strongest doubt they hold onto is this one. You always find those who worship graves nowadays—those who visit saints, light candles by their graves, circumambulate them, seek help from them, and slaughter for them. If you ask them why they do this, they say: “They are intermediaries with Allah, interceding for us; we have sins and faults, and we cannot reach the door of Allah, so we make them intercessors to intercede on our behalf.”

This response firmly closes the door on this great doubt. The verses respond strongly to this great doubt which these people cling to. True shafāʿah (intercession) is only for those who are from the people of tawḥīd , from the people of faith, whose deeds please Allah. Allah only accepts the deeds of the muwaḥḥidīn (monotheists), the believers, the Muslims. As for the mushrik , Allah does not accept his deeds: “They do not intercede except for one whom He approves.” [Quran 2:255]

Those servants, those graves, those idols, those prophets, angels, righteous people, and others do not benefit or harm, do not intercede, and do not possess any intercession. They cannot benefit themselves nor intercede for others. All intercession belongs to Allah alone, and they only intercede by His permission. This verse, as mentioned earlier, refutes the mushrikīn who think that intercession is taken from creatures or sought from these saints, righteous people, angels, or others. It clearly indicates that intercession is for Allah alone, and if it is for Allah, then one should ask only Him.

### Tawassul: meanings and distinctions
<!-- evidence-id: 000702 -->

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message2047 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000703 -->

what is Wasīlah?

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

If it is asked, “What is the meaning of wasīlah in the statement of Allah, the Exalted: ‘And seek nearness (wasīlah) to Him’ [Al-Māʾidah: 35], the answer is: The intended meaning of wasīlah is drawing near to Allah, the Exalted, through doing what He has commanded and avoiding what He has forbidden.

Al-Baghawī said: “Wasīlah means nearness.” Al-Bayḍāwī said: “It means that by which you seek closeness to His reward and nearness to Him, through acts of obedience and refraining from sins.” Ibn Kathīr said: “It means to draw near to Him through obedience and doing what pleases Him.” He also stated, “This is the consensus of the commentators.”

Similarly, in another verse: “They seek nearness to their Lord.” [Al-Isrāʾ: 57] Al-Baghawī said: “Wasīlah means nearness.” It has also been said: “Wasīlah is everything by which one draws near to Allah.” Al-Bayḍāwī commented: “They seek to their Lord wasīlah through obedience.” Ibn Kathīr said: “It means that they strive to be closer to Allah through obedience and increasing in goodness.”

Regarding Al-Baghawī’s statement: “They seek out whoever is closer to Allah and use him as a means,” this is his own wording, not from Ibn ʿAbbās. The one who misattributed it to Ibn ʿAbbās has erred. If the meaning of wasīlah is as Al-Baghawī mentioned, then it refers to what the Ṣaḥābah did with the Prophet ﷺ during his lifetime—such as asking him to supplicate for them or seeking rain through him, as reported in many aḥādīth.

This is also what ʿUmar did after the Prophet’s death, when he sought rain through Al-ʿAbbās, saying: “O Allah, we used to seek rain through our Prophet, and You would provide for us. Now, we seek rain through the uncle of our Prophet, so grant us rain!”

Similarly, Muʿāwiyah did this with Yazīd ibn Al-Aswad Al-Jurashī when he sought rain, saying: “O Allah, we seek intercession through our best ones. O Yazīd, raise your hands to Allah!” So Yazīd raised his hands, supplicated, and they were given rain.

This is the correct understanding of wasīlah.

Source: Ta'sīs al-Taqdīs fī Kashf Talbīs Dāwūd bin Jirjīs wa Yalīhi Daḥḍ Shubuhāt ʿalā al-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn p.119-120
