<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4373 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000704 -->

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ibrahim said:

“The Islām of the majority is nominal Islam, for most of those affiliated with it in this time are called ‘Muslims’ only by name, in contrast to the Jews and Christians. Whoever is found to have something that nullifies it, then his Islam is merely Islam-in-name, with no love and no honor.

Is it imagined that those who were pleased with idols, worshipped them, protected them, collected levies for them, and enforced al-qawānīn (man-made laws)—is there, after this, any Islām? What is this except the kufr that the Prophet ﷺ was sent to demolish? And even the smallest among you knows that whoever enters Islām remains upon it only as long as he maintains it; rather, if he nullifies it, he exits it. And the chapter on the ruling of the apostasy is well known and explained—there is ijmāʿ among the people of knowledge that apostasy is of two types.”

“But what the Prophet ﷺ informed of has occurred, in his saying: ‘A people will come who will regard wine as permissible, calling it by other than its name.’ It has happened: they regarded shirk as permissible and called it by other than its name, saying: ‘tawassul’ and ‘tashaffuʿ.’ But it is the very tawassul and tashaffuʿ of the mushrikīn.”

Source: Fatāwā wa Rasāʾil by Shaykh Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm 1/77

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages5.html#message4347 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000705 -->

Shaykh ʿAbdullāh Al-Ghunaymān said:

The meaning of the verse is that Allāh informed that He does not forgive the mushrik. Therefore, since shirk is unforgivable, it becomes obligatory for the servant to research its types, causes, and means, and to avoid them so that he does not fall into it unknowingly.

Many people, including the intelligent and even scholars, have fallen into shirk al-akbar because of ignorance, carelessness, and leniency, as is still occurring in many Muslim lands. People go to graves, ask their occupants, and think this is not shirk, but rather permissible tawassul. This is among the calamities.

Shirk that Allāh does not forgive may, in some cases, be treated by some people as an act of obedience to draw near to Allāh but the verse indicates that sins other than shirk do not render a Muslim a kāfir.

The verse also shows that if a mushrik dies upon his shirk, he is not forgiven. However, if he repents, Allāh may accept his repentance if He wills. Confidence in Allāh and hope in His acceptance is encouraged; He rejoices most at the repentance of the one who turns back.

Allāh does not benefit from the obedience of the obedient nor from the repentance of the repentant, for He is self-sufficient over all else. Yet, due to His generosity and bounty, He does not wish to punish His servants, and when a servant repents, He rejoices.

This is why Allāh sent the messengers and revealed the books, so that no one has an excuse before Him. The sending of the messengers and revelation of the books is sufficient as guidance. Allāh has given humans reason and thought to discern benefit; thus, if a person  knows that the Messenger came with the truth and guidance from Allāh, it is obligatory for him to seek what the Messenger ﷺ brought.

If he does not, he is blameworthy, and the proof stands against him. There is no excuse for saying, “I was ignorant and did not know,” because that will not help him. Once he knows that Allāh sent His Messenger and revealed His Book, it is incumbent upon him to seek the truth himself.

Source: Sharḥ Kitāb at-Tawḥīd by Shaykh ʿAbdullāh al-Ghunaymān 1/157-158

### What may be requested from a living, present, capable person
<!-- evidence-id: 000706 -->

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message758 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000707 -->

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (رحمه الله) said:

"...we seek intercession, or we use as a means, or we turn to; for he will not intercede for them in that, rather one uses him as a means, seeks intercession through him, and turns to him, in that which he (peace be upon him) was an intercessor for. Nor did they ask him after his death to intercede for them and supplicate for them, as the Christians do, for they seek intercession from the dead, whether prophets or others. For the dead person has had all obligation severed from him; he is not like the living person from whom one asks what he is commanded to do of worship, obedience, and benefiting others. For when the living person is asked to assist another through supplication, intercession, benefit, or charity, he has been asked to do what Allah commands him of doing good. But the dead person is not commanded with anything by way of binding obligation, for obligation is severed by death. Rather he is in the position of the people of Paradise and the angels: he does what is willed of him, so whatever Allah willed of him comes to pass, whether the living person asked it of him or not, and what He did not will of him does not come to pass. So there is no benefit in the living asking the dead , neither for the living nor for the dead. Rather in it is shirk with the dead and harming him, for supplicating to him harms him, and there is no benefit in it for the living. Rather in it is his wronging of himself, his associating partners with his Lord, and his harming of the dead. So it contains all three types of wrongdoing.

And those who visit with the visitation of the people of polytheism and innovation are those who travel to their graves for that purpose, and it is a pilgrimage to them. Allah the Exalted forbids that pilgrimage be made to any house other than His. Nor is pilgrimage made to all of His houses; rather one does not travel except to three mosques. Travel to the Sacred Mosque for Hajj is obligatory, and to each one of the three..."

[A Great Principle on the Difference Between the Worship of the People of Islam and Faith and the Worship of the People of Polytheism and Hypocrisy, pg. 74]

---

<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages2.html#message2110 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000708 -->

al-‘Allāmah ‘Abdullāh Abā Butayn said:

Since it is well established among scholars that seeking refuge (istiʿādhah) in Allah is an act of worship, they have ruled that seeking refuge in a created being is impermissible. Based on this principle, they used it as evidence that the Speech of Allah is uncreated, because it is authentically reported that the Prophet ﷺ sought refuge in the perfect words of Allah, both in action and in speech. This is an argument used by Ahl al-Sunnah against the Jahmiyyah, who claim that the Qurʾān is created. They argue that if the Qurʾān were created, it would not be permissible to seek refuge in it.

Since istiʿādhah (seeking refuge) is a form of supplication (duʿāʾ), as explained by Shaykh al-Islām Taqī al-Dīn (Ibn Taymiyyah), this matter is clear. The scholars who prohibited seeking refuge in created beings also maintain that it is impermissible to supplicate to them, since istiʿādhah is, in reality, a type of duʿāʾ. The one seeking refuge in his Lord is, in essence, asking Him to avert or remove harm, and this is the very definition of duʿāʾ.

Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said: “Seeking refuge (istiʿādhah), seeking protection (istijārah), and seeking aid (istighāthah) are all forms of supplication (duʿāʾ), and these terms are closely related. The Prophet ﷺ himself referred to istiʿādhah as duʿāʾ, as recorded in the Sunan where a man asked him: ‘O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication I can make.’ The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, from the evil of my sight, from the evil of my tongue, from the evil of my heart, and from the evil of my desires.’” (Sunan Abī Dāwūd)

Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate, saying: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is a terrible companion, and I seek refuge in You from betrayal, for it is a terrible inner trait.” (Abū Dāwūd, with a ṣaḥīḥ chain).

In the Sunan, ʿĀʾishah (رضي الله عنها) reported that the Prophet ﷺ would supplicate using these words: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Fire and the punishment of the Fire, and from the evil of wealth and poverty.”

In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ would supplicate: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the removal of Your blessing, the loss of Your protection, the sudden onset of Your punishment, and anything that incurs Your displeasure.”

The purpose of citing these aḥādīth is to establish that the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions referred to istiʿādhah as duʿāʾ. Thus, when the scholars ruled that istiʿādhah is not permissible with a created being and is exclusively for Allah, because it is a form of duʿāʾ, then the same applies to all other forms of duʿāʾ. If this is firmly established, it becomes clear that if a person fears an enemy and seeks protection from a living, present person to shield him from harm, this is permissible according to all Muslims. This does not fall under the scholars’ ruling that istiʿādhah with a created being is prohibited.

This is an example of a single act whose ruling changes based on its recipient: Seeking help from a living, present person is permissible, whereas seeking help from anyone else is forbidden. Likewise, supplicating to anyone other than Allah to fulfill needs is impermissible, as Allah says: “So do not call upon anyone along with Allah.” (Sūrat al-Jinn: 18). However, this does not include asking a living, present person for assistance in matters within human capability.

Source: Ta'sīs al-Taqdīs fī Kashf Talbīs Dāwūd bin Jirjīs wa Yalīhi Daḥḍ Shubuhāt ʿalā al-Tawḥīd by al-ʿAllāmah ʿAbdullāh Abā Buṭayn p.87-88

<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 87</h4>
<p>فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَعْرِفُ العِبَادَةَ وَلَا أَنْوَاعَهَا؛ فَبَيِّنْهَا بِقَوْلِكَ: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى</p>
<p>(1)</p>
<p>: {ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً}</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>(3)</p>
<p>.</p>
<p>فَإِذَا أَعْلَمْتَهُ</p>
<p>(4)</p>
<p>بِهَذَا</p>
<p>(5)</p>
<p>؛ فَقُلْ لَهُ: هَلْ هُوَ عِبَادَةٌ لِلَّهِ</p>
<p>(6)</p>
<p>؟</p>
<p>فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَقُولَ</p>
<p>(7)</p>
<p>: نَعَمْ، وَ «الدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ</p>
<p>(8)</p>
<p>العِبَادَةِ»</p>
<p>(9)</p>
<p>.</p>
<p>فَقُلْ لَهُ: إِذَا</p>
<p>(10)</p>
<p>أَقْرَرْتَ أَنَّهُ</p>
<p>(11)</p>
<p>عِبَادَةٌ، وَدَعَوْتَ اللَّهَ لَيْلاً وَنَهَاراً، خَوْفاً</p>
<p>(1)</p>
<p>في ب: «قوله تعالى»، وفي د: «قول اللَّه»، وفي هـ: «قول اللَّه تعالى»، وفي و: «بينها بقول اللَّه تعالى»، وفي ز: «فبينها له بقولك: قال اللَّه تعالى»، وفي ح: «قال اللَّه»، وفي ط: «فبينها بقول اللَّه»، وفي ي: «قال اللَّه بقوله»، وفي م: «يقول اللَّه تعالى».</p>
<p>(2)</p>
<p>{تضرعاً}؛ أَيْ: تَذَلُّلاً وَاسْتِكَانَةً لِطَاعَتِهِ، {وخفيةً}؛ أَيْ: بِخُشُوعِ قُلُوبِكُمْ، وَصِحَّةِ اليَقِينِ مِنْكُمْ بِوَحْدَانِيَّتِهِ فِيمَا بِيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ، لَا جِهَاراً وَمُرَاءَاةً. تفسير الطَّبريّ (10/ 247).</p>
<p>(3)</p>
<p>في أ، ج، ز، ك، ل، م زيادة: {إنه لا يحب المعتدين}.</p>
<p>(4)</p>
<p>في أ، ج: «عملت»، وفي ب: «إذا أعلمته»، وفي د، ز، ط: «إذا علمت»، وفي هـ، ح، ي: «إذا عملت»، وفي ك، م: «علَّمته».</p>
<p>(5)</p>
<p>في و: «علمت هذا».</p>
<p>(6)</p>
<p>في ب: «فهل هو عبادة اللَّه»، وفي د، ي: «هل هو عبادة اللَّه»، وفي و: «قل: هل هو عبادة اللَّه»، وفي ز: «هل هذا عبادة للَّه تعالى أوْ لا» وفي ك: «ثم قلت له: هل هي عبادة اللَّه» بدل: «فَقُلْ لَهُ: هَلْ هُوَ عِبَادَةٌ لِلَّهِ»، و «لِلَّهِ» ليست في هـ.</p>
<p>(7)</p>
<p>في ي: «يقرَّ ويقول».</p>
<p>(8)</p>
<p>في و: «من» بدل: «مُخُّ».</p>
<p>(9)</p>
<p>هذا لفظُ حديثٍ أَخْرَجهُ التِّرمذيُّ (3371) منْ حَديثِ أَنَسٍ رضي الله عنه، وقال: «هَذَا حَدِيثٌ غَرِيبٌ مِنْ هَذَا الوَجْهِ، لَا نَعْرِفُهُ إِلَّا مِنْ حَدِيثِ ابْنِ لَهِيعَةَ»، وفي الباب: حَديثُ النُّعْمَان بن بَشِيرٍ رضي الله عنهما: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إِنَّ الدُّعَاءَ هُوَ العِبَادَةُ» أَخْرَجهُ أَحْمَدُ (18352)، وأَبُو دَاوُد (1479)، والتِّرمذيُّ (3372)، وقال: «حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ».</p>
<p>(10)</p>
<p>في ب: «إنما» بدل: «إِذَا».</p>
<p>(11)</p>
<p>في أ، ب، ج، د، هـ، و، ح، ط، ي، ك: «أنها».</p>

<p>(8)</p>

<p>(9)</p>

<p>(10)</p>
<p>؟</p>

<p>(12)</p>
<p>.</p>

<p>(13)</p>
<p>نَحَرْتَ لِمَخْلُوقٍ - نَبِيٍّ، أَوْ جِنِّيٍّ، أَوْ غَيْرِهِمَا -؛ هَلْ أَشْرَكْتَ فِي هَذِهِ العِبَادَةِ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ</p>

<p>؟</p>
<p>فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ يُقِرَّ وَيَقُولَ</p>
<p>(15)</p>
<p>: نَعَمْ</p>
<p>(16)</p>
<p>.</p>
<p>(1)</p>
<p>في ب زيادة: «اللَّه» وهو وهم، وفي ز زيادة: «مع اللَّه تعالى».</p>
<p>(2)</p>

<p>(5)</p>

<p>(7)</p>
<p>في أ: «فإذا قال اللَّه»، وفي ب، ي: «إذ قال اللَّه تعالى»، وفي ج، و، ح، ط: «إذا قال اللَّه»، وفي د، هـ: «إذ قال اللَّه»، وفي ك: «قال اللَّه تعالى» بدل: «فَقُلْ لَهُ: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى».</p>

<!-- evidence-id: 000709 -->
Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah said:

Whoever denies what has been established by mass transmission and consensus is a disbeliever after the proof has been established against him, whether or not he calls the established meaning “istighāthah.”

As for one who acknowledges the Prophet’s intercession but denies what the Companions practiced of tawassul through him and seeking his intercession, such as what al-Bukhārī narrated from Anas that when the people suffered drought, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb sought rain through al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and said, “O Allāh, we used to seek a means to You through our Prophet and You would give us rain. Now we seek a means to You through our Prophet’s uncle, so give us rain,” after which they were given rain; and such as the report in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and elsewhere that a Bedouin said to the Prophet ﷺ, “The people are exhausted, the children are hungry, and the property has perished, so call upon Allāh for us. We seek your intercession with Allāh, and we seek Allāh’s intercession with you.” The Messenger ﷺ glorified Allāh until this became apparent in the faces of his Companions, and said, “Woe to you! Allāh is not made an intercessor with any of His creation. Allāh’s station is greater than that.” He then completed the ḥadīth. The Prophet objected to the man’s statement, “We seek Allāh’s intercession with you,” but did not object to his statement, “We seek your intercession with Allāh.” Rather, he approved it. Its permissibility is therefore known. One who denies this is astray, mistaken, and an innovator; regarding declaring him a disbeliever, there is detail and disagreement.

As for one who affirms what is established by the Book, the Sunnah, and consensus concerning the Prophet’s intercession, tawassul through him, and similar matters, but says that none is to be called upon except Allāh and that matters which none but Allāh can accomplish are to be requested from none but Him, such as forgiving sins, guiding hearts, sending down rain, causing vegetation to grow, and the like, then this person is correct. Indeed, this is also a matter concerning which there is no disagreement among the Muslims.

Allāh says: “Who forgives sins except Allāh?” [Āl ʿImrān 3:135] He says: “You do not guide whom you love, but Allāh guides whom He wills.” [Al-Qaṣaṣ 28:56] He says: “O humanity, remember Allāh’s favor upon you. Is there any creator other than Allāh who provides for you from the sky and the earth?” [Fāṭir 35:3] He says: “Allāh made it only as good news for you and so that your hearts might be reassured by it. Victory comes only from Allāh.” [Āl ʿImrān 3:126] And He says: “If you do not aid him, Allāh has already aided him when the disbelievers drove him out as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; Allāh is with us.’” [At-Tawbah 9:40]

Meanings established by the Book and the Sunnah must be affirmed, and meanings negated by the Book and the Sunnah must be negated. If the expression indicating affirmation or negation occurs in the speech of Allāh or His Messenger ﷺ, it must be accepted. If it occurs in someone else’s speech and his intended meaning is clear, he is judged according to that intended meaning; otherwise, he is asked what he means. An expression occurring in the speech of Allāh or His Messenger may possess a correct meaning while some people understand from it something other than what Allāh and His Messenger intended. That person’s mistaken understanding must be rejected.

Al-Ṭabarānī narrated in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr that during the Prophet’s lifetime there was a hypocrite who harmed the believers. Abū Bakr said, “Come with us so that we may seek the aid of the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ against this hypocrite.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Aid is not sought from me; aid is sought only from Allāh.” By this, the Prophet intended the second meaning: requesting from him something none but Allāh can accomplish. Otherwise, the Companions used to request supplication from him and seek rain through him. Thus the scholars who wrote concerning the names of Allāh said that every legally responsible person must know that, in the absolute sense, there is no relief and no bringer of relief except Allāh. Every relief comes from Him, even if He brings it about at the hands of another. In reality it belongs to Allāh, while its attribution to another is figurative.

They said that among His names are al-Mughīth, the Bringer of Relief, and al-Ghiyāth, the source of relief. The meaning is that He reaches His servants amid hardships when they call upon Him, answers them, and delivers them. In the authentic rain-seeking report, the supplication is: “O Allāh, bring us relief. O Allāh, bring us relief.” Allāh says: “When you sought relief from your Lord and He answered you.” [Al-Anfāl 8:9] Relief is more properly associated with actions and response with words, though each may be used in the place of the other.

Seeking relief through Allāh’s mercy is, in reality, seeking relief through Him, just as seeking refuge through His attributes is seeking refuge through Him, and swearing by His attributes is swearing by Him. The transmitted supplications include: “I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allāh from the evil of what He created,” and: “I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in You from You. I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself.”

Source: Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā by Ibn Taymiyyah, 1/109-111

<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: مجموع الفتاوى</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 109</h4>
<p>وَأَمَّا مَنْ أَنْكَرَ مَا ثَبَتَ بِالتَّوَاتُرِ وَالْإِجْمَاعِ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ بَعْدَ قِيَامِ الْحُجَّةِ وَسَوَاءٌ سَمَّى هَذَا الْمَعْنَى اسْتِغَاثَةً أَوْ لَمْ يُسَمِّهِ. وَأَمَّا مَنْ أَقَرَّ بِشَفَاعَتِهِ وَأَنْكَرَ مَا كَانَ الصَّحَابَةُ يَفْعَلُونَهُ مِنْ التَّوَسُّلِ بِهِ وَالِاسْتِشْفَاعِ بِهِ؛ كَمَا رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ فِي صَحِيحِهِ عَنْ أَنَسٍ أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ كَانَ إذَا قَحَطُوا اسْتَسْقَى بِالْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ وَقَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ إنَّا كُنَّا نَتَوَسَّلُ إلَيْك بِنَبِيِّنَا فَتَسْقِينَا وَإِنَّا نَتَوَسَّلُ إلَيْك بِعَمِّ نَبِيِّنَا فَاسْقِنَا فَيُسْقَوْنَ. وَفِي سُنَنِ أَبِي دَاوُد وَغَيْرِهِ {أَنَّ أَعْرَابِيًّا قَالَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَهَدَتْ الْأَنْفُسُ وَجَاعَ الْعِيَالُ وَهَلَكَ الْمَالُ فَادْعُ اللَّهَ لَنَا فَإِنَّا نَسْتَشْفِعُ بِك عَلَى اللَّهِ وَنَسْتَشْفِعُ بِاَللَّهِ عَلَيْك. فَسَبَّحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى عُرِفَ ذَلِكَ فِي وُجُوهِ أَصْحَابِهِ وَقَالَ: وَيْحَك إنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُسْتَشْفَعُ بِهِ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ شَأْنُ اللَّهِ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ} وَذَكَرَ تَمَامَ الْحَدِيثِ فَأَنْكَرَ قَوْلَهُ نَسْتَشْفِعُ بِاَللَّهِ عَلَيْك وَلَمْ يُنْكِرْ قَوْلَهُ نَسْتَشْفِعُ بِك عَلَى اللَّهِ بَلْ أَقَرَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَعُلِمَ جَوَازُهُ فَمَنْ أَنْكَرَ هَذَا فَهُوَ ضَالٌّ مُخْطِئٌ مُبْتَدِعٌ؛ وَفِي تَكْفِيرِهِ نِزَاعٌ وَتَفْصِيلٌ. وَأَمَّا مَنْ أَقَرَّ بِمَا ثَبَتَ بِالْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ وَالْإِجْمَاعِ مِنْ شَفَاعَتِهِ وَالتَّوَسُّلِ بِهِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ وَلَكِنْ قَالَ لَا يُدْعَى إلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ الْأُمُورَ الَّتِي لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهَا إلَّا اللَّهُ لَا تُطْلَبُ إلَّا مِنْهُ مِثْلَ غُفْرَانِ الذُّنُوبِ وَهِدَايَةِ الْقُلُوبِ وَإِنْزَالِ الْمَطَرِ وَإِنْبَاتِ النَّبَاتِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ: فَهَذَا مُصِيبٌ فِي ذَلِكَ بَلْ هَذَا مِمَّا لَا نِزَاعَ فِيهِ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَيْضًا. كَمَا قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: {وَمَنْ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إلَّا اللَّهُ} وَقَالَ: {إنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ} وَكَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: {يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ هَلْ مِنْ خَالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 110</h4>
<p>وَالْأَرْضِ} وَكَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: {وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إلَّا بُشْرَى لَكُمْ وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُمْ بِهِ وَمَا النَّصْرُ إلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ} وَقَالَ: {إلَّا تَنْصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ إذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا} . فَالْمَعَانِي الثَّابِتَةُ بِالْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ: يَجِبُ إثْبَاتُهَا وَالْمَعَانِي الْمَنْفِيَّةُ بِالْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ؛ يَجِبُ نَفْيُهَا وَالْعِبَارَةُ الدَّالَّةُ عَلَى الْمَعَانِي نَفْيًا وَإِثْبَاتًا إنْ وُجِدَتْ فِي كَلَامِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَبَ إقْرَارُهَا. وَإِنْ وُجِدَتْ فِي كَلَامِ أَحَدٍ وَظَهَرَ مُرَادُهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ رُتِّبَ عَلَيْهِ حُكْمُهُ وَإِلَّا رُجِعَ فِيهِ إلَيْهِ. وَقَدْ يَكُونُ فِي كَلَامِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عِبَارَةٌ لَهَا مَعْنًى صَحِيحٌ لَكِنَّ بَعْضَ النَّاسِ يَفْهَمُ مِنْ تِلْكَ غَيْرَ مُرَادِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَهَذَا يُرَدُّ عَلَيْهِ فَهْمُهُ. كَمَا رَوَى الطَّبَرَانِي فِي مُعْجَمِهِ الْكَبِيرِ {أَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي زَمَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُنَافِقٌ يُؤْذِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ: قُومُوا بِنَا لِنَسْتَغِيثَ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ هَذَا الْمُنَافِقِ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إنَّهُ لَا يُسْتَغَاثُ بِي وَإِنَّمَا يُسْتَغَاثُ بِاَللَّهِ} فَهَذَا إنَّمَا أَرَادَ بِهِ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمَعْنَى الثَّانِيَ وَهُوَ أَنْ يُطْلَبَ مِنْهُ مَا لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَإِلَّا فَالصَّحَابَةُ كَانُوا يَطْلُبُونَ مِنْهُ الدُّعَاءَ وَيَسْتَسْقُونَ بِهِ كَمَا فِي صَحِيحِ الْبُخَارِيِّ عَنْ ابْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ: رُبَّمَا ذَكَرْت قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ وَأَنَا أَنْظُرُ إلَى وَجْهِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَسْتَسْقِي فَمَا يَنْزِلُ حَتَّى يَجِيشَ لَهُ مِيزَابٌ: وَأَبْيَضَ يُسْتَسْقَى الْغَمَامُ بِوَجْهِهِ ثِمَالُ الْيَتَامَى عِصْمَةٌ لِلْأَرَامِلِ وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ وَلِهَذَا قَالَ الْعُلَمَاءُ الْمُصَنِّفُونَ فِي أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: يَجِبُ عَلَى كُلِّ مُكَلَّفٍ أَنْ يَعْلَمَ أَنْ لَا غِيَاثَ وَلَا مُغِيثَ عَلَى الْإِطْلَاقِ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ كُلَّ</p>
<h4 dir="rtl">ص. 111</h4>
<p>غَوْثٍ فَمِنْ عِنْدِهِ وَإِنْ كَانَ جَعَلَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى يَدَيْ غَيْرِهِ فَالْحَقِيقَةُ لَهُ سبحانه وتعالى وَلِغَيْرِهِ مَجَازٌ. قَالُوا: مِنْ أَسْمَائِهِ تَعَالَى الْمُغِيثُ وَالْغِيَاثُ وَجَاءَ ذِكْرُ الْمُغِيثِ فِي حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالُوا وَاجْتَمَعَتْ الْأُمَّةُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ. وَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الحليمي: الْغِيَاثُ هُوَ الْمُغِيثُ وَأَكْثَرُ مَا يُقَالُ غِيَاثُ الْمُسْتَغِيثِينَ وَمَعْنَاهُ الْمُدْرِكُ عِبَادَهُ فِي الشَّدَائِدِ إذَا دَعَوْهُ وَمُجِيبُهُمْ وَمُخَلِّصُهُمْ وَفِي خَبَرِ الِاسْتِسْقَاءِ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ: {اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا} يُقَالُ أَغَاثَهُ إغَاثَةً وَغِيَاثًا وَغَوْثًا وَهَذَا الِاسْمُ فِي مَعْنَى الْمُجِيبِ وَالْمُسْتَجِيبِ قَالَ تَعَالَى: {إذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ} إلَّا أَنَّ الْإِغَاثَةَ أَحَقُّ بِالْأَفْعَالِ وَالِاسْتِجَابَةَ أَحَقُّ بِالْأَقْوَالِ وَقَدْ يَقَعُ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا مَوْقِعَ الْآخَرِ. قَالُوا الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَ الْمُسْتَغِيثِ وَالدَّاعِي أَنَّ الْمُسْتَغِيثَ يُنَادِي بِالْغَوْثِ. وَالدَّاعِيَ يُنَادِي بِالْمَدْعُوِّ وَالْمُغِيثِ. وَهَذَا فِيهِ نَظَرٌ فَإِنَّ مِنْ صِيغَةِ الِاسْتِغَاثَةِ يَا لَلَّهِ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَقَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ مَعْرُوفٍ الْكَرْخِي أَنَّهُ كَانَ يُكْثِرُ أَنْ يَقُولَ وَا غَوْثَاهُ وَيَقُولَ إنِّي سَمِعْت اللَّهَ يَقُولُ: {إذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ} وَفِي الدُّعَاءِ الْمَأْثُورِ {: يَا حَيُّ يَا قَيُّومُ لَا إلَهَ إلَّا أَنْتَ بِرَحْمَتِك أَسْتَغِيثُ أَصْلِحْ لِي شَأْنِي كُلَّهُ وَلَا تَكِلْنِي إلَى نَفْسِي طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ وَلَا إلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِك} . وَالِاسْتِغَاثَةُ بِرَحْمَتِهِ اسْتِغَاثَةٌ بِهِ فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ كَمَا أَنَّ الِاسْتِعَاذَةَ بِصِفَاتِهِ اسْتِعَاذَةٌ بِهِ فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ وَكَمَا أَنَّ الْقَسَمَ بِصِفَاتِهِ قَسَمٌ بِهِ فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ فَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: {أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ} وَفِيهِ {أَعُوذُ بِرِضَاك مِنْ سَخَطِك وَبِمُعَافَاتِك مِنْ عُقُوبَتِك وَبِك مِنْك لَا أُحْصِي ثَنَاءً عَلَيْك أَنْتَ كَمَا أَثْنَيْت عَلَى نَفْسِك} .</p>
</div>
</details>

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message913 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000710 -->

Shaykh ar-Rājihī said:

So whoever places an intermediary between himself and Allah, whether living or dead, is a mushrik.

A living person is only to be asked for something that he is capable of doing. So you may say, “O so-and-so, help me repair my car,” “O so-and-so, lend me some money,” or “O so-and-so, help me repair my farm.”

But as for asking a living person to forgive your sin, save you from the Fire, provide for you, grant you victory over your enemy, or not deprive you of entering Paradise, these are things that he neither has the ability nor the power to do, and this is shirk.

Therefore, if a person places intermediaries between himself and Allah, making du‘āʾ to them besides Allah, asking them for intercession, or placing tawakkul upon them, meaning that he depends upon them and entrusts his affairs to them in obtaining what he seeks, then he commits kufr by the ijmāʿ of the Muslims.

For this reason, the author said: “He commits kufr by ijmāʿ.”

The evidences for this are the evidences which establish that shirk in worship is kufr that expels one from the religion, that is, the evidences prohibiting shirk, prohibiting making du‘āʾ to other than Allah, and prohibiting asking from other than Allah that which none is able to do except Allah.

Source: Shurūḥ Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Mujaddid Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb by Shaykh ar-Rājihī 1/173

### Grave visitation and the pathways leading to shirk
<!-- evidence-id: 000711 -->

<!-- telegram-source: personal/messages.html#message587 -->
<!-- evidence-id: 000712 -->

Ibn Qayyim said:

Among them: that which the Messenger ﷺ legislated regarding visiting graves is only to remember the Hereafter, and to show iḥsān (goodness) to the deceased by making duʿāʾ for him, and praying for mercy upon him, and istighfār (seeking forgiveness) for him, and asking for well-being for him, so the visitor is a doer of iḥsān to himself and to the dead.

But these mushrikūn reversed the matter, and inverted the religion, and made the purpose of visiting the grave, shirk with the dead, and making duʿāʾ to him and through him, and asking him for their needs, and seeking blessings from him, and victory for them over the enemies, and the like.

Source: Ighāthat al-Lahfān fī Maṣāyid ash-Shayṭān 1/359

## 12. Methodology concerning the divine attributes

### Imām Aḥmad: transmitted reports are accepted with submission rather than speculative dispute
<!-- evidence-id: 000731 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->

Imām Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said:

“The foundations of the Sunnah with us are adherence to what the Companions of the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ were upon, taking them as an example, abandoning innovations, and abandoning disputation in religion. The Sunnah explains the Qurʾān and consists of the indications of the Qurʾān. There is no analogy in the Sunnah, examples are not coined for it, and it is not grasped through intellects or desires. It is only following and abandoning desire.

Belief in the reports concerning divine decree and faith in them is required. It is not said, ‘Why?’ or ‘How?’ Rather, it is affirmation and faith. Whoever does not know the explanation of a report and whose intellect does not reach it has been sufficed by it and the matter has been made decisive for him. He must believe in it and submit to it. The same applies to all the reports concerning the vision, even if they are unfamiliar to the ears and the listener feels uneasy about them. He is only required to believe in them and not reject a single letter of them, as with the other transmitted reports from trustworthy narrators.”

Source: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, *Uṣūl al-Sunnah*, pp. 14-21, Dār al-Manār edition.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">This copy transmits the treatise through a chain ending with ʿAbdūs ibn Mālik al-ʿAṭṭār from Imām Aḥmad. No named overall authentication judgment for the transmission was found in the consulted edition.</p>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَالَ عَبْدُوسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ الْعَطَّارُ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ أَحْمَدَ بْنَ حَنْبَلٍ يَقُولُ: أُصُولُ السُّنَّةِ عِنْدَنَا التَّمَسُّكُ بِمَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِ أَصْحَابُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَالِاقْتِدَاءُ بِهِمْ، وَتَرْكُ الْبِدَعِ، وَكُلُّ بِدْعَةٍ فَهِيَ ضَلَالَةٌ، وَتَرْكُ الْخُصُومَاتِ فِي الدِّينِ. وَالسُّنَّةُ تُفَسِّرُ الْقُرْآنَ، وَهِيَ دَلَائِلُ الْقُرْآنِ، وَلَيْسَ فِي السُّنَّةِ قِيَاسٌ، وَلَا تُضْرَبُ لَهَا الْأَمْثَالُ، وَلَا تُدْرَكُ بِالْعُقُولِ وَلَا الْأَهْوَاءِ، إِنَّمَا هُوَ الِاتِّبَاعُ وَتَرْكُ الْهَوَى.</p>
<p>وَالْإِيمَانُ بِالْأَحَادِيثِ فِيهِ وَالْإِيمَانُ بِهَا، لَا يُقَالُ: لِمَ؟ وَلَا كَيْفَ؟ إِنَّمَا هُوَ التَّصْدِيقُ وَالْإِيمَانُ بِهَا. وَمَنْ لَمْ يَعْرِفْ تَفْسِيرَ الْحَدِيثِ وَيَبْلُغْهُ عَقْلُهُ فَقَدْ كُفِيَ ذَلِكَ وَأُحْكِمَ لَهُ، فَعَلَيْهِ الْإِيمَانُ بِهِ وَالتَّسْلِيمُ. وَمِثْلُ أَحَادِيثِ الرُّؤْيَةِ كُلِّهَا، وَإِنْ نَبَتْ عَنِ الْأَسْمَاعِ وَاسْتَوْحَشَ مِنْهَا الْمُسْتَمِعُ، وَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْهِ الْإِيمَانُ بِهَا، وَأَنْ لَا يَرُدَّ مِنْهَا حَرْفًا وَاحِدًا، وَغَيْرُهَا مِنَ الْأَحَادِيثِ الْمَأْثُورَاتِ عَنِ الثِّقَاتِ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: أحمد بن حنبل، <em>أصول السنة</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">14-21</bdi>، طبعة دار المنار.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Bukhārī: none of Allāh’s attributes resembles creation
<!-- evidence-id: 000715 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->

Imām al-Bukhārī said:

“In this is evidence that the voice of Allāh does not resemble the voices of creation, because the voice of Allāh, majestic is His mention, is heard from afar just as it is heard from nearby, and because the angels fall unconscious from His voice. When the angels call to one another, they do not fall unconscious. Allāh, mighty and majestic, said: ‘So do not set up rivals to Allāh.’ There is no rival or likeness to the attributes of Allāh, and nothing from His attributes is found among created beings.”

Source: al-Bukhārī, *Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād*, p. 98, ed. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿUmayrah.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: «وَفِي هَذَا دَلِيلٌ أَنَّ صَوْتَ اللَّهِ لَا يُشْبِهُ أَصْوَاتَ الْخَلْقِ، لِأَنَّ صَوْتَ اللَّهِ جَلَّ ذِكْرُهُ يُسْمَعُ مِنْ بُعْدٍ كَمَا يُسْمَعُ مِنْ قُرْبٍ، وَأَنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ يُصْعَقُونَ مِنْ صَوْتِهِ، فَإِذَا تَنَادَى الْمَلَائِكَةُ لَمْ يُصْعَقُوا، وَقَالَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: {فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا}، فَلَيْسَ لِصِفَةِ اللَّهِ نِدٌّ، وَلَا مِثْلٌ، وَلَا يُوجَدُ شَيْءٌ مِنْ صِفَاتِهِ فِي الْمَخْلُوقِينَ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: البخاري، <em>خلق أفعال العباد</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">98</bdi>، تحقيق عبد الرحمن عميرة.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Ṭabarī: affirm the realities of the attributes without resemblance
<!-- evidence-id: 000713 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī said:

“The correct position concerning the meanings of these attributes which we have mentioned, some of which came in the Book of Allāh and His revelation and some of which came from the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ, is that we affirm their realities according to what is known from the standpoint of affirmation, while negating resemblance, just as He, exalted is His praise, negated it from Himself when He said: ‘There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.’

Thus it is said that Allāh is Hearing and Seeing, and that He has hearing and sight. We affirm all these meanings which the reports, the Book, and the revelation have brought according to the reality of affirmation that is understood, while negating resemblance from Him.

We say that He hears voices, not through an opening in an ear and not through an organ like the organs of the children of Ādam. Likewise, He sees persons with a sight that does not resemble the sight of the children of Ādam, which consists of organs. He has two Hands, a Right Hand, and Fingers. They are not bodily organs. Rather, they are two Hands outstretched with blessings to the creation and not withheld from goodness. He has a Face, unlike the bodily organs of the creation which consist of flesh and blood. We say that He laughs toward whomever He wills among His creation, but we do not say that this means baring teeth. He descends every night to the lowest heaven.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *al-Tabṣīr fī Maʿālim al-Dīn*, pp. 140-143, ed. ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Shibl, Dār al-ʿĀṣimah.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>فَإِنْ قَالَ لَنَا قَائِلٌ: فَمَا الصَّوَابُ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ فِي مَعَانِي هَذِهِ الصِّفَاتِ الَّتِي ذَكَرْتَ، وَجَاءَ بِبَعْضِهَا كِتَابُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَوَحْيُهُ، وَجَاءَ بِبَعْضِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ؟ قِيلَ: الصَّوَابُ مِنْ هَذَا الْقَوْلِ عِنْدَنَا أَنْ نُثْبِتَ حَقَائِقَهَا عَلَى مَا نَعْرِفُ مِنْ جِهَةِ الْإِثْبَاتِ وَنَفْيِ التَّشْبِيهِ، كَمَا نَفَى ذَلِكَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُهُ فَقَالَ: {لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ}.</p>
<p>فَيُقَالُ: اللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ، لَهُ سَمْعٌ وَبَصَرٌ. فَنُثْبِتُ كُلَّ هَذِهِ الْمَعَانِي الَّتِي ذَكَرْنَا أَنَّهَا جَاءَتْ بِهَا الْأَخْبَارُ وَالْكِتَابُ وَالتَّنْزِيلُ عَلَى مَا يُعْقَلُ مِنْ حَقِيقَةِ الْإِثْبَاتِ، وَنَنْفِي عَنْهُ التَّشْبِيهَ.</p>
<p>فَنَقُولُ: يَسْمَعُ جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُهُ الْأَصْوَاتَ، لَا بِخَرْقٍ فِي أُذُنٍ، وَلَا جَارِحَةٍ كَجَوَارِحِ بَنِي آدَمَ. وَكَذَلِكَ يُبْصِرُ الْأَشْخَاصَ بِبَصَرٍ لَا يُشْبِهُ أَبْصَارَ بَنِي آدَمَ الَّتِي هِيَ جَوَارِحٌ لَهُمْ. وَلَهُ يَدَانِ وَيَمِينٌ وَأَصَابِعُ، وَلَيْسَتْ جَارِحَةً، وَلَكِنْ يَدَانِ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ بِالنِّعَمِ عَلَى الْخَلْقِ، لَا مَقْبُوضَتَانِ عَنِ الْخَيْرِ. وَوَجْهٌ لَا كَجَوَارِحِ الْخَلْقِ الَّتِي مِنْ لَحْمٍ وَدَمٍ. وَنَقُولُ: يَضْحَكُ إِلَى مَنْ شَاءَ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ، وَلَا نَقُولُ: إِنَّ ذَلِكَ كَشَرٌّ عَنْ أَسْنَانٍ. وَيَهْبِطُ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>التبصير في معالم الدين</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">140-143</bdi>، تحقيق علي بن عبد العزيز الشبل، دار العاصمة.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Ṭabarī: submit to the apparent meaning of the transmitted report
<!-- evidence-id: 000714 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī said concerning the divine coming and descent:

“Its meaning is what the apparent wording of the report indicates. With us there is nothing regarding the report except submission to it and belief in it. We therefore say: Our Lord, majestic is His majesty, comes on the Day of Resurrection while the angels are row upon row, and He descends to the lowest heaven every night. We do not say that this means His command descends, for His command descends to it and to the rest of His existing creation at every moment and hour.

The correct position concerning every report transmitted about the attributes and names of Allāh, mighty and majestic, is like what we have stated concerning these meanings.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *al-Tabṣīr fī Maʿālim al-Dīn*, pp. 146-147, ed. ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Shibl, Dār al-ʿĀṣimah.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قِيلَ لَهُ: مَعْنَى ذَلِكَ مَا دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ ظَاهِرُ الْخَبَرِ، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا لِلْخَبَرِ إِلَّا التَّسْلِيمُ وَالْإِيمَانُ بِهِ، فَنَقُولُ: يَجِيءُ رَبُّنَا جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا، وَيَهْبِطُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا وَيَنْزِلُ إِلَيْهَا فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ، وَلَا نَقُولُ: مَعْنَى ذَلِكَ يَنْزِلُ أَمْرُهُ؛ بَلْ نَقُولُ: أَمْرُهُ نَازِلٌ إِلَيْهَا كُلَّ لَحْظَةٍ وَسَاعَةٍ وَإِلَى غَيْرِهَا مِنْ جَمِيعِ خَلْقِهِ الْمَوْجُودِينَ مَا دَامَتْ مَوْجُودَةً.</p>
<p>وَكَالَّذِي قُلْنَا فِي هَذِهِ الْمَعَانِي مِنَ الْقَوْلِ، الصَّوَابُ مِنَ الْقِيلِ فِي كُلِّ مَا وَرَدَ بِهِ الْخَبَرُ فِي صِفَاتِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَأَسْمَائِهِ تَعَالَى ذِكْرُهُ بِنَحْوِ مَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>التبصير في معالم الدين</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">146-147</bdi>، تحقيق علي بن عبد العزيز الشبل، دار العاصمة.</p>
</div>
</details>

## 13. Divine highness and istiwāʾ

### Ibn al-Mubārak: Allāh is above His heavens upon His Throne
<!-- evidence-id: 000716 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak said:

“We do not say as the Jahmiyyah say, that He is here on the earth. Rather, He rose over the Throne.”

He was asked, “How do we know our Lord?” He replied:

“Above His heavens, upon His Throne.”

Source: al-Bukhārī, *Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād*, pp. 31-32, ed. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿUmayrah.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">No named authentication judgment was found in the consulted edition. Al-Bukhārī cites this wording without a complete chain at this location.</p>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْمُبَارَكِ: «لَا نَقُولُ كَمَا قَالَتِ الْجَهْمِيَّةُ إِنَّهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ هَهُنَا، بَلْ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى».</p>
<p>وَقِيلَ لَهُ: كَيْفَ تَعْرِفُ رَبَّنَا؟ قَالَ: «فَوْقَ سَمَاوَاتِهِ عَلَى عَرْشِهِ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: البخاري، <em>خلق أفعال العباد</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">31-32</bdi>، تحقيق عبد الرحمن عميرة.</p>
</div>
</details>

### A report rejecting the claim that istawā means istawlā
<!-- evidence-id: 000718 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->
<!-- authority-name: Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aʿrābī -->
<!-- authority-death: 231 -->
<!-- provenance: telegram-supplied -->
<!-- telegram-source: dar/messages.html#message988 -->

Al-Lālakāʾī reported from Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, the grandson of Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr, that he said:

“Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Aʿrābī was our neighbor, and his night was the finest of nights.” He then mentioned that Ibn Abī Duʾād asked him, “Do you know in the Arabic language that istawā means istawlā?” He replied, “I do not know that.”

Source: al-Lālakāʾī, *Sharḥ Uṣūl Iʿtiqād Ahl al-Sunnah wa-al-Jamāʿah*, 2/38. Supplied through the Dār al-Salafiyyah Telegram export, message 988.

### Al-Ṭabarī: the Lord is the One who rose over the Throne
<!-- evidence-id: 000717 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī said:

“A person should know that his Lord is the One who rose over the Throne. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens, whatever is on the earth, whatever is between them, and whatever is beneath the soil. Whoever goes beyond that has failed, lost, strayed, and perished.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *Ṣarīḥ al-Sunnah*, pp. 26-27, ed. Badr Yūsuf al-Maʿtūq.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَيَعْلَمَ أَنَّ رَبَّهُ هُوَ الَّذِي عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى، {لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ الثَّرَى}، فَمَنْ تَجَاوَزَ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ خَابَ وَخَسِرَ وَضَلَّ وَهَلَكَ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>صريح السنة</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">26-27</bdi>، تحقيق بدر يوسف المعتوق.</p>
</div>
</details>

## 14. The Qurʾān is the uncreated speech of Allāh

### ʿAmr ibn Dīnār: the scholars maintained for seventy years that the Qurʾān is uncreated
<!-- evidence-id: 000721 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->

Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah said:

“I met our shaykhs over the course of seventy years, among them ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, and they would say: ‘The Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh and is not created.’”

Source: al-Bukhārī, *Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād*, p. 29, ed. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿUmayrah.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">No named authentication judgment was found in the consulted edition.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Full chain</summary>
<p>Al-Bukhārī → al-Ḥakam ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭabarī → Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah → the shaykhs he met over seventy years, including ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>حَدَّثَنِي الْحَكَمُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الطَّبَرِيُّ، كَتَبْتُ عَنْهُ بِمَكَّةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، قَالَ: أَدْرَكْتُ مَشَائِخَنَا مُنْذُ سَبْعِينَ سَنَةً، مِنْهُمْ عَمْرُو بْنُ دِينَارٍ، يَقُولُونَ: «الْقُرْآنُ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ وَلَيْسَ بِمَخْلُوقٍ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: البخاري، <em>خلق أفعال العباد</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">29</bdi>، تحقيق عبد الرحمن عميرة.</p>

### Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq: the Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh
<!-- evidence-id: 000720 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->

Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār al-Duhnī said that he asked Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq whether the Qurʾān was created or a creator. Jaʿfar replied:

“It is neither a creator nor created. Rather, it is the speech of Allāh, mighty and majestic.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *Ṣarīḥ al-Sunnah*, p. 19, report 15, ed. Badr Yūsuf al-Maʿtūq.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">No named authentication judgment was found in the consulted edition.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Full chain</summary>
<p>Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī → Mūsā ibn Sahl al-Ramlī → Mūsā ibn Dāwūd → Maʿbad Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān → Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār al-Duhnī → Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ سَهْلٍ الرَّمْلِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ دَاوُدَ، حَدَّثَنَا مَعْبَدٌ أَبُو عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ الدُّهْنِيِّ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِجَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: إِنَّهُمْ يَسْأَلُونَ عَنِ الْقُرْآنِ: مَخْلُوقٌ أَوْ خَالِقٌ؟ فَقَالَ: «إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ بِخَالِقٍ وَلَا مَخْلُوقٍ، وَلَكِنَّهُ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>صريح السنة</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">19</bdi>، الأثر رقم <bdi dir="ltr">15</bdi>، تحقيق بدر يوسف المعتوق.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Ṭabarī: the Qurʾān remains the uncreated speech of Allāh wherever it is recited or written
<!-- evidence-id: 000722 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī said:

“The Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh and His revelation. Since this is among the meanings of affirming His oneness, the correct position with us is that it is the speech of Allāh, uncreated, however it is written, wherever it is recited, and in whatever place it is read. It is the same Qurʾān whether found in heaven, preserved on earth, written in the Preserved Tablet, inscribed on the tablets of children in the schools, engraved in stone, written on paper, preserved in the heart, or pronounced by the tongue.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *Ṣarīḥ al-Sunnah*, pp. 18-19, ed. Badr Yūsuf al-Maʿtūq.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>الْقُرْآنُ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ وَتَنْزِيلُهُ؛ إِذْ كَانَ مِنْ مَعَانِي تَوْحِيدِهِ، فَالصَّوَابُ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ فِي ذَلِكَ عِنْدَنَا أَنَّهُ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ غَيْرُ مَخْلُوقٍ كَيْفَ كُتِبَ وَحَيْثُ تُلِيَ وَفِي أَيِّ مَوْضِعٍ قُرِئَ، فِي السَّمَاءِ وُجِدَ، وَفِي الْأَرْضِ حَيْثُ حُفِظَ، فِي اللَّوْحِ الْمَحْفُوظِ كَانَ مَكْتُوبًا، وَفِي أَلْوَاحِ صِبْيَانِ الْكُتَّابِ مَرْسُومًا، فِي حَجَرٍ نُقِشَ، أَوْ فِي وَرَقٍ خُطَّ، أَوْ فِي الْقَلْبِ حُفِظَ، وَبِلِسَانٍ لُفِظَ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>صريح السنة</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">18-19</bdi>، تحقيق بدر يوسف المعتوق.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Ājurrī: the Qurʾān is uncreated and the contrary positions are rejected
<!-- evidence-id: 000738 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->
<!-- authority-name: Abū Bakr al-Ājurrī -->
<!-- authority-death: 360 -->
<!-- provenance: external-primary-text -->

Abū Bakr al-Ājurrī said:

“Beware, may Allāh have mercy upon you, of those who say that a person’s utterance of the Qurʾān is created. This was, according to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and those who followed his path, a grave objectionable doctrine. Its proponent is an innovator who is to be avoided, neither spoken to nor sat with, and the people are to be warned against him.

The scholars recognize nothing other than what we previously mentioned: the Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh and is not created. Whoever says that it is created has disbelieved. Whoever says, ‘The Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh,’ and then stops without saying that it is uncreated is a Jahmī. Whoever says, ‘My utterance of the Qurʾān is created,’ is likewise a Jahmī. This is what Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said, and he spoke very sternly concerning it.”

Source: Abū Bakr al-Ājurrī, *al-Sharīʿah*, 1/533-535, chapter on the Lafẓiyyah. [Read the source online](https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/1006/196/%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%A8-%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%84%D9%81%D8%B8%D9%8A%D8%A9).

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="external-primary-text">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ: احْذَرُوا رَحِمَكُمُ اللَّهُ هَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ: إِنَّ لَفْظَهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَخْلُوقٌ، وَهَذَا عِنْدَ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ حَنْبَلٍ وَمَنْ كَانَ عَلَى طَرِيقَتِهِ مُنْكَرٌ عَظِيمٌ، وَقَائِلُ هَذَا مُبْتَدِعٌ، يُجْتَنَبُ وَلَا يُكَلَّمُ وَلَا يُجَالَسُ، وَيُحَذَّرُ مِنْهُ النَّاسُ.</p>
<p>لَا يَعْرِفُ الْعُلَمَاءُ غَيْرَ مَا تَقَدَّمَ ذِكْرُنَا لَهُ، وَهُوَ أَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ غَيْرُ مَخْلُوقٍ، وَمَنْ قَالَ: مَخْلُوقٌ فَقَدْ كَفَرَ، وَمَنْ قَالَ: الْقُرْآنُ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ وَوَقَفَ فَهُوَ جَهْمِيٌّ، وَمَنْ قَالَ: لَفْظِي بِالْقُرْآنِ مَخْلُوقٌ فَهُوَ جَهْمِيٌّ أَيْضًا، كَذَا قَالَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ حَنْبَلٍ، وَغَلَّظَ فِيهِ الْقَوْلَ جِدًّا.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: أبو بكر الآجري، <em>الشريعة</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">1/533-535</bdi>، باب ذكر اللفظية.</p>
</div>
</details>

## 15. The believers’ vision of Allāh

### Hadith: the believers will see their Lord as they see the full moon
<!-- evidence-id: 000724 -->
<!-- record-type: hadith -->
<!-- report-status: authenticated-in-primary-collection -->

Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh reported that the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ looked at the moon on the night when it was full and said:

“You will certainly see your Lord, mighty and majestic, just as you see this moon, without crowding one another in seeing Him. If you are able not to be overcome concerning a prayer before sunrise and a prayer before sunset, then do so.”

He then recited: “And glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset.” [Qāf 50:39]

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *Ṣarīḥ al-Sunnah*, p. 20, report 18. The hadith is also recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

<p class="verification-note authenticated">Hadith. Al-Ṭabarī introduces this doctrine as established by authentic reports. This hadith is also transmitted in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Chains recorded by al-Ṭabarī</summary>
<p>Al-Ṭabarī → Abū al-Sāʾib Salm ibn Junādah → Ibn Fuḍayl → Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid → Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim → Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh → the Prophet ﷺ.</p>
<p>Al-Ṭabarī → Tamīm ibn al-Muntaṣir → Yazīd ibn Hārūn → Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid → Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim → Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh → the Prophet ﷺ.</p>
<p>Al-Ṭabarī → Mujāhid ibn Mūsā → Yazīd ibn Hārūn → Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid → Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim → Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh → the Prophet ﷺ.</p>
<p>Al-Ṭabarī → Ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ → Sufyān, Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah, and Yazīd ibn Hārūn → Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid → Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim → Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh → the Prophet ﷺ.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو السَّائِبِ سَلْمُ بْنُ جُنَادَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ فُضَيْلٍ، وَحَدَّثَنَا تَمِيمُ بْنُ الْمُنْتَصِرِ، وَمُجَاهِدُ بْنُ مُوسَى، قَالَ تَمِيمٌ: أَنْبَأَنَا يَزِيدُ، وَقَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ هَارُونَ، وَحَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ الصَّبَّاحِ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، وَمَرْوَانُ بْنُ مُعَاوِيَةَ، وَيَزِيدُ بْنُ هَارُونَ، جَمِيعًا عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي خَالِدٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: كُنَّا جُلُوسًا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، فَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْقَمَرِ لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ فَقَالَ: «إِنَّكُمْ رَاءُونَ رَبَّكُمْ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ كَمَا تَرَوْنَ هَذَا الْقَمَرَ، لَا تُضَامُّونَ فِي رُؤْيَتِهِ، فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ لَا تُغْلَبُوا عَلَى صَلَاةٍ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا فَافْعَلُوا» ثُمَّ تَلَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: {وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ}.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>صريح السنة</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">20</bdi>، الحديث رقم <bdi dir="ltr">18</bdi>.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Ṭabarī: the people of Paradise will see their Lord
<!-- evidence-id: 000723 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī said:

“As for the correct position concerning the believers seeing their Lord, mighty and majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, which is the religion by which we worship Allāh and upon which we found Ahl al-Sunnah wa-al-Jamāʿah, it is that the people of Paradise will see Him according to what the authentic reports from the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ establish.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *Ṣarīḥ al-Sunnah*, p. 20, ed. Badr Yūsuf al-Maʿtūq.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَأَمَّا الصَّوَابُ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ فِي رُؤْيَةِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَبَّهُمْ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَهُوَ دِينُنَا الَّذِي نَدِينُ اللَّهَ بِهِ، وَأَدْرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ أَهْلَ السُّنَّةِ وَالْجَمَاعَةِ، فَهُوَ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْجَنَّةِ يَرَوْنَهُ عَلَى مَا صَحَّتْ بِهِ الْأَخْبَارُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>صريح السنة</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">20</bdi>، تحقيق بدر يوسف المعتوق.</p>
</div>
</details>

## 16. Statements concerning the Jahmiyyah and sectarian disbelief

### Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān disavows the religion of one who says the Qurʾān is created
<!-- evidence-id: 000725 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->

Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān told Sufyān al-Thawrī:

“Convey to that mushrik that I am free of his religion.”

The person in question used to say that the Qurʾān was created.

Source: al-Bukhārī, *Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād*, p. 29, ed. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿUmayrah.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">No named authentication judgment was found in the consulted edition.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Full chain</summary>
<p>Al-Bukhārī transmits from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan → Abū Nuʿaym → Sulaymān al-Qāriʾ → Sufyān al-Thawrī → Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ الْقَارِئُ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ سُفْيَانَ الثَّوْرِيَّ يَقُولُ: قَالَ لِي حَمَّادُ بْنُ أَبِي سُلَيْمَانَ: «أَبْلِغْ أَبَا فُلَانٍ الْمُشْرِكَ أَنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنْ دِينِهِ»، وَكَانَ يَقُولُ: «الْقُرْآنُ مَخْلُوقٌ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: البخاري، <em>خلق أفعال العباد</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">29</bdi>، تحقيق عبد الرحمن عميرة.</p>
</div>
</details>

### ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs: those who say the Qurʾān is created are not people of tawḥīd
<!-- evidence-id: 000726 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs was asked about people who said that the Qurʾān was created. When the questioner claimed that they were among the people of tawḥīd, he replied:

“These are not among the people of tawḥīd. They are heretics. Whoever claims that the Qurʾān is created has claimed that Allāh is created. Allāh says: ‘In the name of Allāh, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.’ Allāh is not created, the Most Merciful is not created, and the Especially Merciful is not created. This is the foundation of heresy. Whoever says this is under the curse of Allāh. Do not sit with them and do not marry them.”

Source: al-Bukhārī, *Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād*, p. 30, ed. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿUmayrah.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">No named authentication judgment was found in the consulted edition.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Full chain</summary>
<p>Al-Bukhārī → Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh Abū Jaʿfar al-Baghdādī → Abū Zakariyyā Yaḥyā ibn Yūsuf al-Zimmī → ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الْبَغْدَادِيُّ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا زَكَرِيَّا يَحْيَى بْنَ يُوسُفَ الزِّمِّيَّ، قَالَ: كُنَّا عِنْدَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ، فَجَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ، مَا تَقُولُ فِي قَوْمٍ يَقُولُونَ: الْقُرْآنُ مَخْلُوقٌ؟ فَقَالَ: «أَمِنَ الْيَهُودِ؟» قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «فَمِنَ النَّصَارَى؟» قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «فَمِنَ الْمَجُوسِ؟» قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «فَمِمَّنْ؟» قَالَ: مِنْ أَهْلِ التَّوْحِيدِ، قَالَ: «لَيْسَ هَؤُلَاءِ مِنْ أَهْلِ التَّوْحِيدِ، هَؤُلَاءِ الزَّنَادِقَةُ. مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ مَخْلُوقٌ فَقَدْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَخْلُوقٌ. يَقُولُ اللَّهُ: {بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ}، فَاللَّهُ لَا يَكُونُ مَخْلُوقًا، وَالرَّحْمَنُ لَا يَكُونُ مَخْلُوقًا، وَالرَّحِيمُ لَا يَكُونُ مَخْلُوقًا. وَهَذَا أَصْلُ الزَّنَادِقَةِ. مَنْ قَالَ هَذَا فَعَلَيْهِ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ، لَا تُجَالِسُوهُمْ وَلَا تُنَاكِحُوهُمْ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: البخاري، <em>خلق أفعال العباد</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">30</bdi>، تحقيق عبد الرحمن عميرة.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Bukhārī: the Jahmiyyah are deeply astray in disbelief
<!-- evidence-id: 000727 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->

Imām al-Bukhārī said concerning the Jahmiyyah:

“I examined the speech of the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians, and I did not see anyone more astray in their disbelief than them. I consider ignorant the one who does not declare them disbelievers, except for a person who does not know their disbelief.”

Source: al-Bukhārī, *Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād*, p. 33, ed. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿUmayrah.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: «نَظَرْتُ فِي كَلَامِ الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى وَالْمَجُوسِ فَمَا رَأَيْتُ أَضَلَّ فِي كُفْرِهِمْ مِنْهُمْ، وَإِنِّي لَأَسْتَجْهِلُ مَنْ لَا يُكَفِّرُهُمْ إِلَّا مَنْ لَا يَعْرِفُ كُفْرَهُمْ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: البخاري، <em>خلق أفعال العباد</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">33</bdi>، تحقيق عبد الرحمن عميرة.</p>
</div>
</details>

## 17. Early explanations of ṭāghūt and disbelief in it

### ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: the ṭāghūt is Satan
<!-- evidence-id: 000728 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->

ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said:

“The ṭāghūt is Satan.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *Jāmiʿ al-Bayān*, 5/417, reports 5834-5835, commentary on al-Baqarah 2:256, Dār al-Tarbiyah wa-al-Turāth edition.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">Al-Ṭabarī records two chains for this wording. The consulted edition discusses Ḥassān ibn Fāʾid and notes that Abū Ḥātim called him a shaykh and Ibn Ḥibbān included him among the trustworthy Followers, but it does not give an overall grade for either chain.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Chains recorded by al-Ṭabarī</summary>
<p>Al-Ṭabarī → Muḥammad ibn Bashshār → ʿAbd al-Raḥmān → Sufyān → Abū Isḥāq → Ḥassān ibn Fāʾid al-ʿAbsī → ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.</p>
<p>Al-Ṭabarī → Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā → Ibn Abī ʿAdī → Shuʿbah → Abū Isḥāq → Ḥassān ibn Fāʾid → ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ حَسَّانَ بْنِ فَائِدٍ الْعَبْسِيِّ، قَالَ: قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ: الطَّاغُوتُ الشَّيْطَانُ.</p>
<p>وَحَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي عَدِيٍّ، عَنْ شُعْبَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ حَسَّانَ بْنِ فَائِدٍ، عَنْ عُمَرَ، مِثْلَهُ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>جامع البيان</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">5/417</bdi>، الأثران <bdi dir="ltr">5834-5835</bdi>، عند تفسير البقرة: <bdi dir="ltr">256</bdi>، طبعة دار التربية والتراث.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Mujāhid: the ṭāghūt may be a human figure to whom people refer judgment
<!-- evidence-id: 000729 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->

Mujāhid ibn Jabr said:

“The jibt is sorcery, and the ṭāghūt is Satan in human form. They refer judgment to him, and he is the leader of their affair.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *Jāmiʿ al-Bayān*, 8/462, report 9770, commentary on al-Nisāʾ 4:51, Dār al-Tarbiyah wa-al-Turāth edition.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">No named authentication judgment was found in the consulted edition.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Full chain</summary>
<p>Al-Ṭabarī → Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr → Abū ʿĀṣim → ʿĪsā → Ibn Abī Najīḥ → Mujāhid ibn Jabr.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَاصِمٍ، عَنْ عِيسَى، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي نَجِيحٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ: {يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْجِبْتِ وَالطَّاغُوتِ}، قَالَ: «الْجِبْتُ السِّحْرُ، وَالطَّاغُوتُ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي صُورَةِ إِنْسَانٍ يَتَحَاكَمُونَ إِلَيْهِ، وَهُوَ صَاحِبُ أَمْرِهِمْ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>جامع البيان</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">8/462</bdi>، الأثر رقم <bdi dir="ltr">9770</bdi>، عند تفسير النساء: <bdi dir="ltr">51</bdi>، طبعة دار التربية والتراث.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Ṭabarī: ṭāghūt includes every being exalted through worship, obedience, or submission besides Allāh
<!-- evidence-id: 000730 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī said:

“The correct view with me concerning the ṭāghūt is that it is every possessor of transgression against Allāh who is worshipped besides Him, whether he compels those who worship him or they obey him willingly, and whether that object of worship is a human being, a devil, an idol, an image, or anything else.

Thus the meaning is: whoever rejects the lordship of every object worshipped besides Allāh, disbelieves in it, and believes in Allāh, affirming that He is his deity, Lord, and object of worship, has grasped the firmest handhold.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *Jāmiʿ al-Bayān*, 5/419, commentary on al-Baqarah 2:256, Dār al-Tarbiyah wa-al-Turāth edition.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: وَالصَّوَابُ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ عِنْدِي فِي «الطَّاغُوتِ» أَنَّهُ كُلُّ ذِي طُغْيَانٍ عَلَى اللَّهِ، فَعُبِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ، إِمَّا بِقَهْرٍ مِنْهُ لِمَنْ عَبَدَهُ، وَإِمَّا بِطَاعَةٍ مِمَّنْ عَبَدَهُ لَهُ، إِنْسَانًا كَانَ ذَلِكَ الْمَعْبُودُ، أَوْ شَيْطَانًا، أَوْ وَثَنًا، أَوْ صَنَمًا، أَوْ كَائِنًا مَا كَانَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ.</p>
<p>فَتَأْوِيلُ الْكَلَامِ إِذًا: فَمَنْ يَجْحَدْ رُبُوبِيَّةَ كُلِّ مَعْبُودٍ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ، فَيَكْفُرْ بِهِ، وَيُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ، يَقُولُ: وَيُصَدِّقْ بِاللَّهِ أَنَّهُ إِلَهُهُ وَرَبُّهُ وَمَعْبُودُهُ، فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَى.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>جامع البيان</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">5/419</bdi>، عند تفسير البقرة: <bdi dir="ltr">256</bdi>، طبعة دار التربية والتراث.</p>
</div>
</details>

## 18. Takfīr of sects and of one who does not declare them disbelievers

### Yazīd ibn Hārūn: ruling on the one who says the Qurʾān is created and the one who does not declare him a disbeliever
<!-- evidence-id: 000732 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->
<!-- authority-name: Yazīd ibn Hārūn -->
<!-- authority-death: 206 -->

Ibn Baṭṭah reported that Yazīd ibn Hārūn said:

“Whoever says that the Qurʾān is created is a disbeliever. Whoever does not declare him a disbeliever is himself a disbeliever. Whoever doubts his disbelief is a disbeliever.”

Source: Ibn Baṭṭah, *al-Ibānah al-Kubrā*, 6/57, report 257.

<p class="verification-note unresolved">This is a transmitted report with a complete chain in the cited source. No named authentication judgment for this exact chain was found during the present review, so the archive does not grade it.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Full chain</summary>
<p>Ibn Baṭṭah → Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Khalaf → Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdān al-ʿAskarī → Muḥammad ibn Mujāhid → Yazīd ibn Hārūn.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="online-primary-text">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو حَفْصٍ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ خَلَفٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ حَمْدَانَ الْعَسْكَرِيُّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُجَاهِدٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ يَزِيدَ بْنَ هَارُونَ، يَقُولُ: «مَنْ قَالَ: الْقُرْآنُ مَخْلُوقٌ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ، وَمَنْ لَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ، وَمَنْ شَكَّ فِي كُفْرِهِ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ».</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن بطة، <em>الإبانة الكبرى</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">6/57</bdi>، الأثر رقم <bdi dir="ltr">257</bdi>.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal: ruling on the one who says the Qurʾān is created and the one who does not declare him a disbeliever
<!-- evidence-id: 000733 -->
<!-- record-type: transmitted-report -->
<!-- report-status: unresolved -->
<!-- authority-name: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal -->
<!-- authority-death: 241 -->

In the letter attributed to Imām Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and addressed to Musaddad ibn Musarhad, it states:

“The Qurʾān is the speech of Allāh, mighty and majestic. Whoever says that it is created is a disbeliever in Allāh the Magnificent, and whoever does not declare him a disbeliever is himself a disbeliever.”

Source: Ibn Abī Yaʿlā, *Ṭabaqāt al-Ḥanābilah*, 2/428, in the biography of Musaddad ibn Musarhad. [Open the passage in Shamela](https://shamela.ws/book/1520/1003#p1).

<p class="verification-note unresolved">The cited passage reproduces a letter attributed to Imām Aḥmad. The linked location does not provide a complete transmission chain for the letter, and no named authentication judgment for this exact wording was found during the present review. The archive therefore leaves its transmission status unresolved.</p>

<details class="source-panel chain-source">
<summary>Transmission information</summary>
<p>Ibn Abī Yaʿlā reproduces the statement as part of the letter attributed to Imām Aḥmad and addressed to Musaddad ibn Musarhad. A complete chain for the letter is not displayed at the cited passage.</p>
</details>

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="online-primary-text">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>وَالْقُرْآنُ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، فَمَنْ قَالَ: مَخْلُوقٌ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ، وَمَنْ لَمْ يُكَفِّرْهُ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن أبي يعلى، <em>طبقات الحنابلة</em>، <bdi dir="ltr">2/428</bdi>، في ترجمة مسدد بن مسرهد.</p>
</div>
</details>

### Al-Ṭabarī: disbelief of one who holds that the speech of Allāh is created or doubts that it is uncreated
<!-- evidence-id: 000737 -->
<!-- record-type: direct-authorial-statement -->
<!-- authority-name: Al-Ṭabarī -->
<!-- authority-death: 310 -->

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī said:

“We have previously demonstrated that no accountable person may remain ignorant that Allāh is knowing with knowledge, powerful with power, speaking with speech, mighty with might, and the Creator, and that every originated thing is fashioned and created. We stated that whoever is ignorant of this is a disbeliever in Allāh.

Accordingly, whoever claims that the speech of Allāh is created and that He once had no speech is more deserving of disbelief and of losing the name of faith. There is likewise no doubt that whoever claims that the speech of Allāh becomes originated and created when it is recited, memorized, or written is a disbeliever in Allāh. The same ruling applies if he doubts that it is uncreated, whether it is recited, memorized, or written.”

Source: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, *al-Tabṣīr fī Maʿālim al-Dīn*, pp. 149-151, ed. ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Shibl.

<details class="source-panel arabic-source" data-origin="local-library">
<summary>Arabic text</summary>
<div class="arabic-text" dir="rtl" lang="ar">
<p>قَدْ دَلَّلْنَا فِيمَا مَضَى قَبْلُ مِنْ كِتَابِنَا هَذَا أَنَّهُ لَا يَسَعُ أَحَدًا بَلَغَ حَدَّ التَّكْلِيفِ الْجَهْلُ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ جَلَّ ذِكْرُهُ عَالِمٌ لَهُ عِلْمٌ، وَقَادِرٌ لَهُ قُدْرَةٌ، وَمُتَكَلِّمٌ لَهُ كَلَامٌ، وَعَزِيزٌ لَهُ عِزَّةٌ، وَأَنَّهُ خَالِقٌ، وَأَنَّهُ لَا مُحْدَثٌ إِلَّا مَصْنُوعٌ مَخْلُوقٌ. وَقُلْنَا: مَنْ جَهِلَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ بِاللَّهِ كَافِرٌ.</p>
<p>فَلَا شَكَّ أَنَّ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ كَلَامَهُ مَخْلُوقٌ، وَأَنَّهُ قَدْ كَانَ وَلَا كَلَامَ لَهُ، فَإِنَّهُ أَوْلَى بِالْكُفْرِ وَبِزَوَالِ اسْمِ الْإِيمَانِ عَنْهُ. فَلَا شَكَّ أَنَّ مَنْ يَزْعُمُ أَنَّ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ يَتَحَوَّلُ بِتِلَاوَتِهِ إِذَا تَلَاهُ، وَبِحِفْظِهِ إِذَا حَفِظَهُ، أَوْ بِكِتَابَتِهِ إِذْ كَتَبَهُ مُحْدَثًا مَخْلُوقًا، فَبِاللَّهِ تَعَالَى ذِكْرُهُ كَافِرٌ. وَكَذَلِكَ الْقَوْلُ فِيهِ إِنْ شَكَّ أَنَّهُ غَيْرُ مَخْلُوقٍ، مَقْرُوءًا كَانَ، أَوْ مَحْفُوظًا، أَوْ مَكْتُوبًا.</p>
<p class="arabic-citation">المصدر: ابن جرير الطبري، <em>التبصير في معالم الدين</em>، ص. <bdi dir="ltr">149-151</bdi>، تحقيق علي بن عبد العزيز الشبل.</p>
</div>
</details>
